ܝܕ ܙ × ܰ‫ ܡܳܐܡܪܳܐ ܕܐܪܒܰܥܬ݁ܰܥܣܰܪ ܕܥܰܠ ܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ ܘܥܰܠ ܓܡܺܝܪ̈ܶܐ ܨ < ܀
FOURTEENTH SERMON ON THE RIGHTEOUS AND THE PERFECT
ܟ݁ܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܓ݁ܳܝܪܺܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܚܰܝܒܺܝܢ: ܓܡܺܝܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܪܳܓܺܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܒܰܨܪܺܝܢ. ܟ݁ܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܒ݂ܳܙܝܺܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܛܳܠܡܺܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܥܳܠܒܝܺܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܒܳܥܶܝܢ ܠܰܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܕܝܳܠܗܘܽܢ: ܓܡܺܝܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܩܳܢܶܝܢ݂ ܘܠܳܐ ܒܳܢܶܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܢܳܨܒܝܺܢ: ܘܠܳܐ ܝܳܪܬܝܺܢ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܦܳܠܚܝܢ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܣܰܝܒܳܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܠܒܘܽܫܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܚܳܐܶܝܢ ܒܛܰܝܒܘܽܬܳܐ ܡܶܣܟܺܢܳܐܝܺܬ. ܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܝܳܡܝܢ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܨܒܽܘ: ܓܡܺܝܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܨܳܒܶܐ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܐܳܡܪܝܺܢ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܒܐܶܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܢܶܬܥܰܒܪܽܘܢ ܘܢܶܬܒܰܕܪܽܘܢ. ܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ ܩܰܕ݂ܝܺܫܝܺܢ ܡܶܢ ܒܺܝܫܬܳܗ ܕܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܠܰܘ ܡܶܢ ܩܶܢܝܢܶܗ ܘܛܳܒ݁ܳܬܳܗ ܘܫܰܘܬܳܦܘܽܬܳܗ: ܓܡܺܝܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܥܰܠܶܝܢ ܡܶܢ ܟ݁ܽܠܳܗ ܝܳܪܬܘܽܬܳܗ ܕܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܕܡܶܬܚܰܙܝ݂ܳܐ ܘܡܶܢ ܟ݁ܽܠܗܶܝܢ ܒܺܝܫ̈ܳܬܳܗ ܘܡܶܢ ܟ݁ܽܠܶܗ ܩܶܢܝܢܳܗ ܘܡܶܢ ܟܽܠܗܘ̇ܢ ܢܶܟܣܶܐ ܘܡܶܢ ܙܘܽܘܳܓ݁ܳܐ ܕܙܰܒܢܳܝܐ ܘܡܶܢ ܟܽܠܗܶܝܢ ܪ̈ܓܺܝܓܳܬܳܗ. ܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ ܦܳܪܫܺܝܢ ܚܰܝܘܳܬܳܐ ܛܰܡ̈ܐܳܬܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܕ݁ܰܟܝ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܘܐܳܟܠܺܝܢ ܡܶܢܗܶܝܢ: ܓܡܺܝܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܥܰܠܺܝܢ ܡܶܢ ܕܰܟܝ̈ܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܡܶܢ ܛܰܡ̈ܐܳܬ݂ܳܐ. ܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ ܒܳܢܶܝܢ ܘܩܳܢܶܝܢ ܠܰܘ ܐܰܝܟ ܕ݁ܰܠܥܳܠܰܡ܂ ܘܗܳܘܺܝܢ ܒܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܢܘܽܟ݁ܪܳܝ̈ܶܐ: ܓܡܺܝܪ̈ܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܒܳܢܶܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܩܳܢܶܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܩܰܝܡܶܐ ܪܶܥܝܢܗܘܽܢ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ ܦܳܪܫܝܺܢ ܛܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܒܺܝܫ̈ܶܐ ܘܡܶܬܪܰܚܡܝܺܢ ܥܠܰܝܗܘ̇ܢ: ܓ݁ܡܺܝܪ̈ܶܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܡܚܰܬܪܝܺܢ ܡܶܢܗܘܽܢ ܣܳܝܡܝܺܢ ܠܗܘܿܢ. ܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ ܥܳܩܪܝܺܢ ܚܶܡܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܡܶܬܬܢܺܝܚܝܺܢ ܡܶܢܳܗ: ܓܡܺܝܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܰܘ ܡܶܢ ܚܶܡܬ݁ܳܐ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ ܡܶܬܬܢܺܝܚܝܺܢ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܳܦ݂ ܠܩܳܝܛܘܽܠܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ ܪܳܚܡܝܺܢ ܘܰܠܟ݁ܽܠܢܳܫ ܘܰܡܨܰܠܶܝܢ ܥܠܰܝ̈ܗܘܿܢ. ܟ݁ܺܐܢܶܐ ܐܰܒܥܝܺܢ ܕܝܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܐܝܒܐ ܕܐܘܙ̈ܦܘ ܐܘ ܙܒܰܢܘ: ܕܠܳܐ ܪܶܒܝܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܩܝܨܳܬ݂ܳܐ: ܓܡܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܝܳܙܦܝܺܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܩܳܢܶܝܢ: ܝܰܬܝܺܪ ܡܶܢ ܣܰܒܪܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܬܳܐ ܠ ܐ ܝ
1. The righteous do not commit adultery, nor are they condemned; but the perfect do not covet nor do they contract any defect. The righteous do not plunder, do not commit injury, do not oppress, do not seek what is not their own; but the perfect do not possess, do not build, do not plant, do not inherit on earth, do not work for the sake of food and clothing, but live most poorly by the grace [of others]. The righteous do not swear, except by yes and no concerning any matter; but the perfect, as the Lord wishes, speak only, lest by 'yes' and 'no' they transgress and contract a defect. The righteous are sanctified from the malice of the earth, not from its riches and goods and fellowship; but the perfect are exalted above the whole visible inheritance of the earth and above all its malices and above all possessions and above all riches and temporal marriage and its delights. The righteous separate unclean animals from clean and eat of these; the perfect transcend the clean and the unclean. The righteous build and possess, not as if for eternity, and live in the world as strangers; the perfect neither build, nor possess, nor does their mind dwell on the earth. The righteous separate the good from the wicked and have mercy on them; the perfect think them better than themselves. The righteous eradicate anger and find rest from it; the perfect not only enjoy leisure from anger, but also love their murderers and all men and pray for them. The righteous demand their own from those to whom they have lent, or sold, without interest and usury; but the perfect neither accept a loan, nor possess more than the most poor food and a modest garment.


[p. 324] {#po.0.p324}


[p. 325] {#po.0.p325}


[p. 326] {#po.0.p326}


[p. 327] {#po.0.p327}
ܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܪܳܫܶܝܢ ܘܠܐ ܪܶܓ݂ܙܝܺܢ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܐܰܪܬܚܽܘ ܒܡܰܟܝܺܟܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܐܰܠܶܦܘ ܒܚܘ̈ܒܳܐ. ܟܺܐܢܶܐ
2. The righteous admonish and do not get angry, but exhort with humility and teach with charity. The righteous satisfy the hungry, clothe the naked, redeem the oppressed
ܦܳܪܩܝܺܢ ܠܰܐܠܺܝܨܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܩܶܢܝܳܢܗܘܽܢ ܘܡܶܢ ܢܶܟܣܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ: ܓܡܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܕܶܝܢ ܝܳܗܒܝܺܢ ܠܗ
with their riches and wealth; but the perfect give all their substance in one day to the needy and oppressed and take up their cross and follow their Lord in the Spirit and in the Spirit serve Him, loving all men and praying for
ܘܠܐܠܝ̈ܺܨܶܐ ܘܫܳܩܠܝܳܢ ܨܠܝܼܒܗܘܿܢ ܘܐܺܙܠ̱ܝܢ ܒܳܬ݂ܰܪ ܡܳܪܗܘܽܢ ܒܪܘܽܚ: ܘܰܒܪܘܰܚ ܡܫܰܡܫܝܺܢ ܠܶܗ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܪܳܚܡܝܺܢ ܠܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܘܰܡܨܰܠܶܝܢ ܥܠܰܝ̈ܗܘܿܢ. ܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܐܝܺܬ ܠܗ̱ܘܿܢ ܚܰܕ ܬ݁ܰܪܥܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܬܪܶܝܢ ܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ: ܘܢܳܩܫܝܺܢ ܒܙܰܒܢܳܐ ܚܰܡܫ ܙܰܒܢܺܝܢ ܒܝܰܘܡܳܐ: ܓܡܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܟ݁ܽܠܳܗ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܬ݁ܰܪ̈ܥܶܐ ܗ̱ܝ ܩܕܳܡܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ ܘܟܽܠܶܗ ܝܰܘܡܳܐ ܚܳܝܪܝܺܢ ܬܰܡܳܢ: ܘܡܰܘܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܘܰܡܫܰܒܚܝܺܢ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܡܶܢ ܫܘܽܒܚܳܐ ܠܫܘܽܒܚܳܐ ܡܗܰܠܟܝܺܢ ܒܪܘܽܚ: ܘܚܳܙܶܝܢ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ ܐܝܟ ܕܰܒܡܰܚܙܝܺܬ݁ܳܐ ܒܠܒܗܘܿܢ. ܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܠܒܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܡܕܺܝܢ̱ܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܓܡܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܝܳܪܬܝܺܢ: ܓܡܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܒܰܥܕܶܝܢ ܘܒܐܘܽܪܺܫܠܶܡ ܥܶܠܳܝܬܳܐ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܥܰܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܐܶܬ݁ܕ݂ܰܡܝܽܘ ܒܶܝܗ. ܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܡܨܶܝܢ ܥܳܒܕ݂ܝܺܢ ܟ݁ܽܠܶܗ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܐܳܬܰܘ ܠܩܰܕܝܺܫܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܐܶܣܬܰܪܰܩܘ: ܓܡܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܗܶܢܘܽܢ ܥܳܒܕܝܺܢ ܘܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܥܰܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ. ܟ݁ܺܐܢܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܝܳܕ݂ܥܝܢ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܕܘܰܒܳܪ̈ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܝܰܘܡܳܢ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܐܶܬ݂ܰܘ ܠܩܰܕ݂ܝܺܫܘܽܬ݂ܳܐ ܘܐܶܣܬܰܪܰܩܘ: ܓܡܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܥܳܒܕ݂ܝܺܢ ܘܩܳܒܠܝܺܢ ܩܳܠܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܥܳܢܺܝ ܩܳܠܝ ܫܳܡܥܳܐ ܘܒܳܬܰܪܝ ܐܳܬܝܳܐ: ܘܠܐ ܝܺܕ݂ܥܳܐ ܩܳܠܶܗ ܕܢܘܽܟܪܳܝܳܐ. ܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܒܐܵܪܬܝܺܬܳܐ ܡܫܰܒܚܝܺܢ ܠܰܐܠܳܗܳܐ ܘܡܰܣܛܠܝܺܢ ܡܶܢ ܒܝܺܫܬܳܐ: ܓܡܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܰܕܪܟܝܺܢ ܪܰܘܡܳܐ ܘܥܘܽܡܩܳܐ ܘܐܘܰܪܟܳܐ ܘܰܦܬܳܝܳܐ: ܥܰܡ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܩܰܕ݁̈ܝܺܫܶܐ ܕܐܶܬܓܡܰܪܘ ܐܰܕ݂ܪܶܟܘ ܘܰܙܟܰܘ ܘܰܣܠܳܩܘ ܠܐܘܽܪܺܫܠܶܡ ܥܶܠܳܝܬܳܐ. ܓ݁ܡܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܡܳܛܶܝܢ ܠܨܶܗܝܘܽܢ ܘܠܐܘܽܪܺܫܠܶܡ ܕܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܘܰܠܦܰܪܕ݁ܰܝܣܳܐ ܪܘܽܚܳܢܳܐ: ܘܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܠܟܐ ܡܶܢܗܘܽܢ ܣܰܓܝܿ ܠܡܰܚܣܶܢ
them. The righteous have one or two doors to heaven, which they knock five times a day; but for the perfect the whole heaven is a door before them and throughout the whole day they aspire thither and, confessing, they praise the Lord and from glory to glory they tend in the Spirit and see the Lord as in a mirror in their hearts. The righteous will inherit on this side of the city of the perfect; but the perfect will be in Eden and in the heavenly Jerusalem with the Lord, because they have imitated Him. The righteous cannot do the whole will of the Lord, unless they have arrived at holiness and have emptied themselves; the perfect do it and become with the Lord. The righteous do not know today the whole conversation of the Lord, unless they have arrived at holiness and have emptied themselves; but the perfect do it and hear the voice of the Lord, as He said: My sheep hear my voice and follow me and do not know the voice of a stranger. The righteous with trembling glorify God and recede from evils; but the perfect comprehend the height and the depth and the length and the breadth with all the saints, who are perfect and, having carried off the victory, have ascended to the heavenly Jerusalem. The perfect arrive at Sion and the heavenly Jerusalem and the spiritual Paradise and the righteous will barely and not even barely arrive on this side of them and will be much inferior to the perfect.


[p. 328] {#po.0.p328}


[p. 329] {#po.0.p329}


[p. 330] {#po.0.p330}
ܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܓܫܝܺܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܛܳܥܶܝܢ ܡܶܢ ܦܘܰܩܕܳܢܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܰܒܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܓܡܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܝܰܬܪܝܺܢ ܘܰܡܥܰܠܺܝܢ
3. The righteous are not perturbed nor do they wander from the precepts of the Lord constituting justice; but the perfect are more excellent and more sublime than them and convert all who wander. Whose heart is clean, he will see the Lord; and whose
ܘܕ݂ܰܕܟ݂ܶܐ ܠܶܒܶܗ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ ܚܳܙܶܐ: ܘܐܰܝܢܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܕܟܶܐ ܠܶܒܶܗ ܠܳܐ ܡܨܶܐ ܕܢܶܚܙܶܝܘܗ̱ܝ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܚܳܪܶܐ ܐܰܬܪܳܐ ܕܙܳܕܶܩ ܠܶܗ. ܟ݁ܺܐܢܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܠܺܝܛܝܺܢ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܘܠܳܐ ܩܳܪܶܝܢ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܪܰܩܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܣܰܟܠܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܟܝܺܬܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܕܰܓܠܝܺܢ ܒܐ݈ܢܳܫ:ܓܡܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܚܰܩܪܝܺܢ ܘܰܡܟܰܪܟ݁ܝܺܝܢ ܠܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܘܡܰܠܦܝܺܢ ܠܟ݁ܽܠܢܳܫ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܕ݂ܰܓ݁ܶܠ ܒܚܰܒܪܶܗ. ܘܟܽܠ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ
heart is not clean, he cannot see Him, but will inherit a place convenient for himself. The righteous curse no one, call no one a fool, stupid, contemptible, defraud no one; but the perfect honor everyone, bless everyone,


[p. 331] {#po.0.p331}
ܐܰܝܟ ܪܶܗܛܶܗ ܘܐܰܝܟ ܡܫܘܽܚܬܳܗ ܘܐܰܝܟ ܕ݁ܰܫܚܶܩ ܪܶܥܝܳܢܶܗ ܘܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܡܡܰܟܶܟ݂ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ: ܗܳܟܰܢ ܡܶܬܬܪܝܶܡ. ܘܫܰܪܟܳܐ ܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܡܶܬܦ݂ܪܰܥ ܐܰܝܟ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܰܥܒܰܕ ܠܶܗ ܘܐܶܢ ܕܛܳܒ ܘܐܶܢ ܕܒܺܝܫ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܢܳܝܳܐ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܒܗܰܘ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܫܠܺܝܚܳܝܐ: ܕܟܽܠܰܢ ܠܰܡܩܳܡ ܐܺܝܬ ܠܰܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܒܶܡ ܕܰܡܫܺܝܚܳܐ: ܕܢܶܬܦ݂ܪܰܥ ܐ̱ܢܶܫ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܡܶܢܰܢ ܒܦܰܓܪܶܗ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܰܥܒܰܕ ܠܶܗ. ܐܝܺܬ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܕܰܩܫܳܐ ܬܰܫܢܺܝܩܶܝܗܶܝܢ ܡܶܢ ܕܚܰܒܪܶܗ: ܘܐܝܺܬ ܕ݁ܘܳܠܶܐ ܕܢܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܥܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܪ̈ܰܚܡܶܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܐܶܬ݂ܪܰܚܰܡ ܘܡܶܢ ܬܰܫܢܺܝܩܳܝܐ ܡܶܬܦܰܠܰܛ. ܡܰܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܫܳܡܰܥ ܡܰܠܬ݁ܳܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܐܰܘ ܕܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܕܰܓܡܺܝܪܘܳܬܳܐ: ܠܕ݂ܝܰܢܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܐܳܬܶܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܐܳܬܶܐ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܢܶܫܬ݁ܰܒ݁ܰܚ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܒܶܡ ܕܰܡܫܝܺܚܳܐ ܠܥܰܝܢ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܟ݀ܽܠܶܗ: ܐܰܘ ܕܰܢܕܘܳܢ ܠܚܰܛܳܝ̈ܶܐ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕ݁ܡܰܢ ܕܫܳܡܰܥ ܠܡܶܠܬܳܝ ܘܡܗܰܝܡܶܢ ܒܗܰܘ
and teach everyone, so that they do not defraud their companions in any matter. And each one according to his course and measure and, as he has worn down his mind and humbled his soul, will be exalted. Otherwise each one according to what he has done, will receive retribution, whether good or evil from this age into another age, as the Apostle said: We must all stand before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each of us may receive retribution in his body for those things which he has done. There are men, whose torments will be harder than others; and there are those, whom it is just to obtain mercy, because they have had mercy, and to be freed from torments. But he who has heard the word of the Lord, whether of justice or of perfection, will not go to judgment; if, however, he comes, so that he may be glorified before the judgment seat of Christ before the whole world, or so that he may judge sinners, as the Lord said: He who hears my words, passes from death to life. But the spiritual man (that is: who is perfect, the truth having been known) judges all and he himself is judged by no one.


[p. 332] {#po.0.p332}


[p. 333] {#po.0.p333}
ܕܫܰܕܪܰܢܝ ܐܺܝܬ ܠܶܗ ܚܰܝܶܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܳܝܬܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܐܳܬܶܐ ܠܕ݂ܝܳܢܳܐ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܫܰܢܺܝ ܠܶܗ ܡܰܢ ܡܰܘܬܳܐ ܠܚܰܝ̈ܶܐ. ܓܰܒ݂ܪܳܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܰܒܪܘܰܚ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܫܪܳܪܳܐ ܘܐܶܬܓܡܰܪ: ܠܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܕܳܐܶܢ ܘܡܶܢ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܕܝܺܢ܀ ܒܪܝܺܟ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܡܳܪܳܐ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܡܫܺܝܚܳܐ ܟܡܐ ܬܪܝܺܨ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܘܰܟܡܳܐ ܛܳܒ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ: ܕܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܬܟܺܝܠܳܐ ܪܰܒ݂ܘܽܬܳܟ݂: ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܡܰܫܚܳܐ ܛܰܝܒܘܽܬܳܟ݂. ܘܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܒܳܥܶܐ ܠܳܟ: ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ
4. Blessed art Thou Lord Jesus Christ! How upright and how good Thou art, so that Thy majesty cannot be measured and no one can measure Thy goodness! And each one as he seeks Thee, finds Thee; and as he compels himself to keep Thy law, so he progresses; and the more he will have been humbled, the more he will be glorified.


[p. 334] {#po.0.p334}
ܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܠܳܟ. ܘܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܳܠܶܨ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܕ݁ܢܶܛܰܪ ܦܽܘܩܕܳܢܰܝܟ: ܗܳܟ̣ܰܢ ܢܶܫܬܒܰܚ܀ ܫܠܺܝܡ ܡܺܐܡܪܳܐ ܕܐܰܪܒܰܬܰܥܣܰܪ ܕܥܰܠ
The fourteenth sermon on the righteous and the perfect ends.


[p. 335] {#po.0.p335}
ܝܗ ܡܺܐܡܪܳܐ ܕܚܰܡܶܫܬܥܣܰܪ ܕܥܰܠ ܀ ܀
FIFTEENTH SERMON ON THE INSTINCT OF COITUS, WHICH WAS IN ADAM
ܡܰܪܕܝܳܬܐ ܕܙܘܳܘܓܳܐ ܕܰܗܘܳܐ ܒܐܳܕܳܡ ܡܶܟܝܺܠ ܢܦܰܫܶܩ ܥܰܠ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܡܰܪܕ݂ܝܰܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܙܘܳܘܓ݁ܳܝܐ ܕܰܗܘܳܬ ܒܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܗܘܳܬ ܒܳܗ ܘܐܳܡܰܬܝ ܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܩܠܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܝܰܠܺܕܰܘܗ̱ܝ. ܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܕܐܰܣܟ݁ܶܠ ܘܐܶܬܪܫܝܺ ܘܐܶܬܬܣܺܝܡ ܠܶܗ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܕܰܡܬܰܚܬܰܝ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܳܐ: ܒܰܗ ܟܰܝܕ݂ ܒܰܝܙܳܐ ܒܚܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܝܐ ܐܰܦ݁ܺܝܣ ܠܶܗ ܕܢܶܙܕܰܘܰܓ. ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܰܪܚܶܡ ܕܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܦ݁ܰܓ݁ܪܳܢܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܪܘܰܚܳܢܳܝܐ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕܶܝܢ ܐܰܪܥܳܢܳܫܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܐ: ܗܳܝܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܗܘܳܬ ܒܶܗ ܡܰܒܪܕ݂ܝܺܬܳܐ ܕܪܶܓܬܳܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܰܨܒܳܐ ܐܳܕ݁ܶܡ ܒܫܰܘܬܳܦܘܽܬܳܐ܆ ܒܝܘܽܠܦܳܢܶܗ ܕܒܺܝܫܳܚܐ ܕܐܶܨܛܰܢܰܥ ܕܢܰܚܬ݁ܶܗ ܡܶܢ ܩܰܕܝܺܫܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܡܰܠܰܐܟܳܝܶܐ: ܘܢܶܬ݁ܕ݁ܰܡܶܐ ܒܚܰܝܘܽܬܳܐ. ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܝܕ݂ܰܥ ܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ ܕܢܰܦ݁ܺܝܣ ܠܗ ܕܢܶܙܕ݂ܰܘܰܓ: ܐܶܬܪܰܥܝܰܢ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܕܐܰܠܦܶܗ ܒܺܝܫܳܝܐ: ܟܰܕ ܠܝܬ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܒܶܗ ܪܶܓܬܳܐ: ܘܰܣܒܰܝܪܘ ܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ ܘܚܰܘܳܐ ܕܗܳܘܶܐ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܐܰܠܶܦ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܒܝܺܫܳܐ: ܐܶܠܘ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܳܐ
1. Therefore we will explain about the instinct of coitus, which was in Adam, in what manner it was in him and when it is taken away from his progeny. After he had sinned and had been rebuked and a law inferior to the first law had been imposed upon him, by this very law it was permitted to him to enter into marriage. And because he preferred to become corporeal and not spiritual, that is, earthly and not heavenly, then there arose in him the instinct of concupiscence, because Adam desired coitus by the doctrine of the Evil One plotting, so that he might cast him down from the holiness of the angels and that he might become like the brutes. But this, before God had permitted him to have intercourse, Adam was meditating, taught by the Evil One, while as yet concupiscence was not in him; and Adam and Eve thought that all things would happen, which the Evil One taught them; for unless God had had mercy on Adam, by the blow, with which the Evil One struck him, so that he might become Satan in his likeness, he wished to subject him to himself. Blessed is the Good One, who opened the door to every penitent!


[p. 336] {#po.0.p336}
ܪܚܡ ܥܠ ܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ: ܒܫܶܕ݂ܝܳܐ ܕܰܫܕܺܝܗ̱ܝ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܒܺܝܫܳܐ: ܕܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܶܗ ܨܳܒܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܘܕܰܢܫܰܥܒܕ݁ܶܗ ܬܚܶܝܬ ܐܝܺܕܶܗ. ܒܪܝܺܟ ܗ̱ܘ ܛܳܒܳܝܐ ܕܰܦܬܰܚ ܬܰܪܥܳܐ ܠܟ݁ܽܠ ܕܬܳܐܶܒ܀ ܒܩܰܕܡܳܐ ܗܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܡܰܚܫܰܒܬ݁ܳܐ ܒܝܺܫܬܳܐ ܩܰܒ݁ܶܠܘ ܕܒܰܝܬ ܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ܂ ܘܰܠܫܘܽܦܝܪܳܗ ܕܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܐܶܬ݁ܪܰܓܪܰܓܘ. ܘܰܚܙܳܬ݁ܶܗ ܠܰܡ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܬܳܐ ܠܐܝܺܠܳܢܳܐ ܕܰܪܓܝܰܓ݂ ܠܡܶܐܟ݂ܰܠ ܡܶܢܶܗ: ܘܪܶܓܬܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ ܠܥܰܝܢܰܝ̈ܐ: ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢ ܕܝܰܘܡܳܢ ܝܺܕ݂ܥܺܝܢܰܢ ܕܰܪܓܝܺܓ ܗ̱ܘ̈ ܕܰܗܒܳܐ ܘܣܺܐܡܳܐ ܘܩܶܢܝܳܢܳܐ ܘܰܠܒ̈ܘܽܫܶܐ ܘܦܘܽܢܳܩ̈ܶܐ ܕܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܘܰܠܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܪܰܓܘ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܶܐ ܥܰܠ ܣܰܒܪܳܐ ܕܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܒܳܪܘܽܝܗܘܽܢ: ܒܛܰܥܡܳܐ ܕܡܰܘܬܳܐ ܕܐܰܪܡܝܳ ܒܺܝܫܳܝܐ ܒܐܶܕܢܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ: ܘܒܳܬܰܪ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܪܳܗܶܛ ܪܶܥܝܢܗܘܽܢ. ܠܝܬ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܒܗܘܢ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܪܶܓܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܢܶܪܓ݁ܘܽܢ ܠܥܰܝܘܬܳܦ݂ܘܽܬܳܐ: ܨܒܰܝܘ ܒܗ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܶܨܒ݂ܳܐ ܕܐܰܚܙܰܪ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܒܝܺܫܳܐ ܒܰܒܥܺܝܪܳܐ: ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܕܰܘܝܺܕ݂: ܕܒ݁ܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܕܒܐܺܝܩܳܪܶܗ ܠܳܐ ܐܶܬܒ݁ܰܚܰܢ ܕܐܝܺܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܩܰܕܝܺܫ ܐܰܝܟ ܡܰܠܰܐܟ݁ܶܐ ܘܰܡܫܰܚܠܰܦ ܐܰܝܟ ܫܡܰܝܳܢܶܐ: ܘܚܳܪ ܒܚܰܝܘܽܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܨܒܳܐ ܕܢܶܬ݁ܕܰܡܶܐ ܒܳܗ ܒܙܘܽܘܳܓ݁ܳܐ ܕܫܰܘܬܳܦܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܠܰܝܬ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܒܗܘܢ ܪܶܓܬ݁ܳܐ
2. In the beginning therefore the house of Adam conceived an evil thought and coveted the beauty of the earth. And the woman saw, he says, the tree, that it was delightful to eat from it, which was the concupiscence of the eyes, as today we know gold and silver and riches and clothes and the delights of the earth to be covetable, which once they coveted for the hope, that they would be in the likeness of their creator, by the taste of death, which the Evil One suggested to their ears, which their mind was following. For there was no concupiscence in them to desire coitus; but this they were wanting, because the Evil One showed them the beast; for which reason David says: Man did not understand his honor, for he was holy, like the angels and quiet, like the heavenly ones; and he looked at the brute, which he wished to imitate by the coitus of fellowship; nor was there in them the concupiscence


[p. 337] {#po.0.p337}


[p. 338] {#po.0.p338}
ܕܡܰܪܕܝܺܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܢܶܫܬܰܘܬܦܘܽܢ ܥܕܡܐ ܕܐܿܬܛܦܝّܣܘ ܠܒܺܝܫܳܐ ܕܢܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܐܰܪ̈ܥܳܢܳܝܶܐ ܘܢܶܩܢܘܽܢ ܥܰܡܠܳܐ ܘܥܘܺܐܪܳܐ ܐܰܪ̈ܥܳܢܳܝܳܐ. ܘܐܰܦܶܣ ܠܗܘܿܢ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܢܶܙܕܰܘܓܘܽܢ ܘܢܶܥܡܠܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܕܠܳܛ ܐܰܢܘܽܢ: ܘܰܗܘܳܐ ܒܗܘܽܢ ܪܶܓܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܡܰܪܕܝܺܬ݁ܳܐ ܕ݂ܙܰܪܥܳܐ:
instinctual to have intercourse, until they obeyed the Evil One, so that having become earthly they might possess labor and earthly riches; and God permitted them to have intercourse and to work, after He had cursed them and concupiscence and the flow of seed had arisen in them, because they sinned and transgressed His law, hating holiness and loving coitus. Nor did they covet this, coveting, except for the hope, that they would be


[p. 339] {#po.0.p339}
ܘܰܣܢܰܝܘ ܩܰܕܝܺܫܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܰܪܚܶܡܘ ܫܰܘܐܳܦ݂ܘܽܬܳܐ. ܘܠܰܘ ܡܶܢ ܪܰܓܘܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܗܰܘ ܣܰܒܪܳܐ ܕܚܳܪܒܝܺܢ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܐܝܟ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ. ܢܚܰܘܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ
magnified like God. Hence we will demonstrate that there was no concupiscence in Adam and Eve, before they had sinned.
ܡܶܢ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܕܠܰܝܬ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܒܝܗܘܿܢ ܪܶܓܬ݁ܳܐ ܒܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ ܘܰܒ݁ܚܰܘܳܐ ܥܰܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܢܶܚܛܘܽܢ܀ ܟܬܝܒ ܓܶܝܪ ܕ݁ܰܗܘܳܐ ܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ ܘܚܰܘܳܐ ܥܰܪܛܶܠܳܝܺܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܚܰܙܝܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܥܰܪܛܳܠܳܝܘܽܬܗܘܽܢ ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܛܠܳ̈ܝܶܐ ܕܚܰܠܒܳܐ ܕܰܠܝܬܝܺܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܝܳܕܥܝܺܢ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ ܥܰܪܛܶܠܳܝܘܽܬܳܐ: ܒܗܳܕ݁ܶܐ ܕܠܐ ܒܳܗܬܝܺܢ ܒ݁ܚܰܫܳܒܬ݁ܳܐ ܣܢܝܺܬܳܐ: ܐܶܠܘܽ
3. For it is written: Adam and Eve were naked, nor did their nakedness appear; that is, they were like suckling infants, who are naked, nor do they know, what nakedness is, in that they do not blush because of an obscene thought; for if they had known, they would have covered themselves. Who is therefore a man or a woman, in whose hearts concupiscence does not arise, while they stand naked one before the other, seeing themselves to be naked,


[p. 340] {#po.0.p340}
ܗܳܟܝܶܠ ܓܰܒܪܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܩܳܝܡܝܺܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܚܕܼܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܟܕ ܫܠܝܚܝܺܢ: ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܬܥܺܝܪܳܐ ܪܶܓܬܗܘܽܢ ܒܠܶܒܗܘܽܢ: ܘܚܳܙܶܝܢ ܕܥܰܪܛܶܠܳܝܝܢ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܰܕ݂ܟ݂ܶܝܐ ܠܶܒܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܪܳܓܬܳܐ ܩܰܕܝܺܫܝܺܢ ܒܠܶܒܗܘ̇ܢ ܘܰܒܦܰܓܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܺܝܬܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܕܒܶܝܬ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܥܰܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܢܶܚܛܘܽܢ܆ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕܐܳܠܳܐ ܬܶܐܗܰܦܟܘܽܢ ܘܬܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܝܰܠܽܘܕ݂ܶܐ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ: ܠܳܐ ܐܝܺܬܰܝܟ݂ܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܗܳܝ ܒܪܝܺܬܶܗ ܕܐܳܕܳܡ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܬ݁ܳܐ: ܕܥܰܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܢܶܥܒܰܪ ܥܰܠ ܦܘܰܩܕ݁ܳܢܳܐ ܕܓܰܒܘܽܠܶܗ. ܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ ܕܶܝܢ ܘܚܰܘܳܐ ܥܰܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܢܶܚܛܘܽܢ ܫܠܝܚܝܺܢ ܗ݈ܘܰܘ ܐܝܟ ܝܰܠܽܘܕ݂ܶܐ ܕܚܰܠܒܳܐ: ܘܰܕ݂ܗܳܝ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܬܥܺܝܪܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܪܶܓܬ݁ܳܐ ܒܠܶܒܗܘܽܢ: ܠܳܐ ܒܳܗܬܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܠܳܐ ܒܳܗܬܝܺܢ ܛܠܳ̈ܝܶܐ ܕܚܰܠܒܳܐ. ܡܶܢ ܕ݁ܰܚܛܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܘܰܗܘܳܐ ܚܛܺܝܬܳܐ ܒܠܶܒܗܘܽܢ: ܘܐܰܬܥܺܝܪܰܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܕܢܶܕܒܘܽܢ ܒܫܰܘܬܳܦܘܽܬ݁ܳܐ: ܚܙܰܘ ܕܥܰܪܛܶܠܳܝܝܢ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕܶܝܢ: ܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܘ ܒܳܗܬܬ݁ܳܐ ܗܳܝ ܕ݁ܠܳܐ ܝܰܕ݂ܥܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ. ܘܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܕܡܶܢ ܕܰܗܘܳܐ ܚܛܺܝܬܳܐ ܒܠܶܒܗܘܿܢ: ܕܒܶܝܬ ܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ܂ ܟ݁ܶܢ ܨܒܰܘ ܒܫܰܘܬܳܦܘܽܬ݂ܳܐ ܘܐܰܦܶܣ ܠܗܘܢ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܢܶܝܙܕܰܘܓܘܽܢ: ܘܰܗܘܳܐ ܒܗܘܢ ܡܰܪܕ݂ܝܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܪܶܓ݂ܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܫܰܘܐܳܦܘܽܬܳܐ: ܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ ܡܳܐ ܕܐܬܟܰܬܰܪܘ ܝܰܘܡܳܢ ܕܒܶܝܬ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܐܰܝܠܺܝܢ ܕ݂ܪܳܚܡܝܺܢ ܩܰܕ݂ܝܺܫܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܩܰܛܠܘܽܗ ܠܰܚܛܺܝܬܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܠ̈ܒܳܘܬܳܐ ܒܡܰܟܝܺܟܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܰܒܚܘܽܒܳܐ: ܟܶܢ ܫܳܒܩܺܝܢ ܠܳܗ ܠܪܶܓܬܳܐ ܕܦܰܓ݁ܪܳܐ ܘܢܳܕ݂ܳܐ ܠܗܘ̇ܢ ܡܢܳܗ: ܘܡܶܬܥܰܠܶܝܢ ܠܪܶܓܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܘܗܳܚܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܦܳܩܶܕ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܬܶܫܬܩܶܠ ܪܶܓܬܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܠܶܒܳܐ ܘܡܰܒܪܕܝܺܬ݁ܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܦ݁ܰܓ݁ܪܳܐ ܓܡܝܪܳܐܝܺܬ. ܘܗܳܚܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܩܰܕ̈ܝ̈ܫܶܐ ܐܝܟ ܝܰܠܽܘܕ݂ܶܐ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕܐܶܠܳܐ ܬܶܬܗܰܦܟܘܽܢ ܘܬܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܐܰܟ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܛܠܳܝ̈ܶܐ: ܠܳܐ ܬܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܚܺܝܬܘܽܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܝܬܘܽܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܕܠܳܐ ܬܶܚܛܘܽܢ: ܒܗܳܝ ܕܰܟܚܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܰܒܪܝܺܬ ܒܳܗ ܐܰܒ݂ܘܽܟܘܽܢ: ܥܰܕ݂ ܠܳܐ ܢܶܥܒܰܪ ܥܰܠ ܦܘܽܩܕ̈ܳܢܰܝ. ܘܐܶܢ ܗܳܟܘܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܗܘܘܽܢ: ܠܳܐ ܫܳܘܶܝܢ ܐܰܢ݈ܬܘܽܢ
unless whose heart is clean from concupiscence and they are holy in heart and body, as the house of Adam was before they had sinned? Therefore the Lord said: Unless you have been converted and become like these little ones, you will not be like the pristine creature of Adam, before he had transgressed the law of his creator. But Adam and Eve before they had sinned, were naked, like suckling infants; and because concupiscence did not arise in their hearts, they did not blush, just as suckling infants do not blush. But when they had sinned and sin had arisen in their heart, and it solicited them so that they wanted coitus: they saw that they were naked; that is, they knew shame, which they had been ignorant of. And just as sin having arisen in the heart of the house of Adam, then they wanted coitus and God permitted them to have intercourse and the instinct and appetite of coitus arose in them: so today those from the house of Adam, who struggling love holiness and kill sin from the heart by humility and charity: then concupiscence of the flesh having been left, they abhor it and are elevated to the desire of God; and then God commands concupiscence to recede from the heart and the instinct entirely from the body and they become holy like little ones, as the Lord said: Unless you have been converted and become like these little ones, you will not be, as you were, before you sinned, in that purity, in which I created your father, before he had transgressed my law. And unless you are such, He says, you will not be worthy of me, so that


[p. 341] {#po.0.p341}


[p. 342] {#po.0.p342}


[p. 343] {#po.0.p343}
ܠܝ ܕܐܶܬܓܰܡܪܘܽܢ ܘܐܶܫܬܰܒ݂ܚܘܽܢ ܥܰܡܝ. ܛܠܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܚܰܠܒܿܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܪܳܓܝܺܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܕܳܝܢܝܺܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܝܳܨܦܝܺܢ ܘܫܰܠܝܛܝܺܢ ܕܢܶܒܟܘܽܢ ܟ݁ܽܠܥܳܕ݂ܳܢ܂ ܚܢܰܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܐܶܬ݁ܕ݁ܰܟܝܺܢ ܕܳܝܢܝܺܢܰܢ ܘܝܳܨܦܝܢܰܢ: ܘܠܳܐ ܟܰܠܝܺܢܰܢ ܕܢܶܒܟܶܐ ܒܟܽܠܥܺܕ݂ܳܢ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܥܰܠ ܕܦܳܝܫܝܺܢܰܢ ܡܶܢܶܗ. ܐܶܡܰܪ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܰܠܗܳܝ ܩܝܳܡܬܳܐ ܬ݁ܘܰܘ: ܐܰܝܟ ܡܰܠܰܐܟ݁ܶܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܘܠܰܡܡܳܬ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܟܚܝ̈ܢ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܰܡ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܝܳܕܥܝܺܢ ܡܶܠܰܘ̈ܗܝ ܘܢܳܛܪܝܺܢ ܠܗܶܝܢ: ܐܰܝܟ ܡܰܠܰܐܟ݁ܶܐ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ. ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܗܰܟܺܝܠ ܐܳܡܪܝܺܢܰܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܩܠܳܐ
you may be perfected and glorified with me. 4. But suckling infants do not covet, do not judge, do not have care, they can cry at any time. We indeed, who have been purified, judge, have care, nor can we cry at any time for the sake of the Lord, because we have receded from Him. For the Lord said: Those who will be worthy of that resurrection, will be like the angels of God and cannot die; that is: those who know my words and observe them, will be like the angels. Therefore in what manner do we assert that concupiscence will not be taken away from men? Is it perhaps that concupiscence is in the angels, the Lord saying: 'you will be like them'? And if you say that in that age we will be in the likeness of the angels, let us hear now, what the Lord said: As you will be found you will be taken. How much more excellent you will be in this
ܐܝܺܬ ܒܡܰܠܰܐܟ݁ܶܐ: ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܐܰܟܘܳܬܗܘܽܢ ܬܶܗܘܘܽܢ܆ ܘܐܶܢ ܬܺܐܡܰܪ ܕܰܒܗܰܘ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܗܳܘܶܝܢܰܢ
age, you will be that much greater in that new age. And if you say that there are men in whom concupiscence persists until they depart from this world: does concupiscence therefore remain in them until the day of judgment? I do not say so; but unless one
ܕܬܶܫܬܰܟܚܘܽܢ ܬܶܬܕܰܒܪܘܽܢ. ܐܝܟ ܟ݁ܡܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܰܡܝܰܬܪܝܺܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܒܗܳܢܳܐ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ: ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܝܰܬܝܪܝܺܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܒܗܰܘ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܚܰܕܬܳܐ. ܘܐܶܢ ܬܺܐܡܰܪ ܕܐܝܺܬ ܐ݈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܕܩܺܝܡܳܐ ܒܗܘܢ ܪܶܓܬܳܐ: ܥܕ݂ܳܡܳܐ ܕܢܳܦܩܝܺܢ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ: ܐܶܢܬܳܐ ܡܳܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܩܳܝܡܳܐ ܒܗܘܢ ܒܗܰܘ ܝܰܘܡܳܐ ܕܕܝܺܢܳܐ~ ܠܰܝܬ ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܕܐܶܢ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܠܶܐ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܡܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܡܰܠܰܐܟ̈ܶܐ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܠܰܝܬ ܒܗܘܽܢ ܪ̈ܓܝ̈ܓ݁ܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܒܰܒܣܰܪ ܘܪܶܓܬܳܐ ܕܦ݁ܰܓ݂ܪܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܒܗܰܘ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܗܘܽܢ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ܀
has been as the angels, in whom carnal desires and the concupiscence of the body are absent from this age: he will not be in that age as they are, as the Lord said.


[p. 344] {#po.0.p344}


[p. 345] {#po.0.p345}
ܡܳܪܰܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܐܰܫܬܰܘܕܝܿ: ܕܟ݁ܽܠܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܬ݂ܶܫܶܐܠܘܽܢ ܬܶܣܒܘܽܢ: ܘܠܰܝܬ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܬܶܫܐܠܘܽܢ ܕܡܗܰܝܡܢܝܿܢ ܐܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܒܝ: ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܠܟܘܽܢ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܗܳܟ݂ܶܝܠ ܠܳܐ ܫܳܐܠܝܺܢܰܢ ܠܶܗ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ ܗܝܺ ܗܳܕܶܐ: ܕܐܰܝܟ ܡܰܠܰܐܟ݂ܶܐ ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܓܝܰܓ݂ܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܪܶܓܰܬ ܦܰܓܪܳܐ. ܘܗܳܘܶܝܢܰܢ ܐܝܟ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ ܓܡܝܺܪܳܐ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ̈. ܘܰܟܒܰܪ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܝ ܕܚܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܕܐܶܫܰܐܠܝܽܘܗ̱ܝ ܘܢܶܬܶܠ ܠܝ ܗܝ݇ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܫܶܐܠܬܳܐ: ܕܐܝܺܬܶܝܗ ܡܰܘܗܰܒܬܳܐ ܪܰܒ݂ܬܳܐ ܕܡܶܬܝܰܗܒܿܳܐ ܒܚܘܽܒܳܐ: ܘܒܰܨܠܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܰܒܨܰܘܡܳܐ ܘܰܒܡܘܽܟܳܟܳܐ. ܫܳܐܠܝܺܢܰܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܢܳܣܒܝܺܢܰܢ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܥܳܒܕ݁ܝܺܢܰܢ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ ܕ݂ܡܳܪܰܢ ܓܡܝܺܪܳܐ: ܒܗܳܝ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܳܛܪܝܺܢܰܢ ܦܘܿܩܕܳܢܵܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܪܰܘܪ̈ܒܿܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܰܚܒܝܺܢܰܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܡܰܟܟ݁ܝܺܢܰܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܬܡܰܟܰܟ݂ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܝܳܗܶܒ ܠܰܢ ܫܶܐܠܶܬ݂ܰܢ ܗܳܝ ܓܡܝܺܪܬܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܡܝܺܬܶܐ ܠܥܳܠܡܳܐ: ܘܰܢܕܘܽܢ ܦܰܓܪ̈ܰܝܢ ܘܢܶܩܛܘܽܠ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ: ܡܶܛܽܠܳܬ݂ܳܗ ܕܐܝܺܬܶܝܗ ܕ݁ܰܚܛܝܳܬܳܐ ܕܥܳܡܪܳܐ ܒܰܢ: ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܩܳܛܠܝܺܢܰܢ ܠܳܗ. ܐܰܝܠܺܝܢ ܠܰܡ ܕ݁ܰܠܒܶܫܘ ܠܰܡܫܝܺܚܳܐ ܒܶܣܪܗܘܽܢ ܨܠܰܒܘ ܠܘܰܩܒܰܠ ܟܽܠܗܺܝܢ ܫܶܐܠܳܬ݂ܗܘܽܢ ܘܰܪ̈ܓܝܺܓܳܬܵܗܘܽܢ
5. The Lord indeed promised: Whatever you ask, you shall receive; and there is nothing that you ask, believing in me, that shall not be done for you. Why then do we not ask of the Lord that we may be as the angels, without desire and without the concupiscence of the body, made according to the perfect will of the Lord? And perhaps you will say to me: «I will gladly ask that he may grant me this request, which is the greatest charisma, which is imparted through charity, prayer, fasting, and humility»! But we ask and do not receive, because we do not perform the perfect will of the Lord, in that we do not observe his great commandments, nor do we love, nor do we humble ourselves after the likeness of the Lord: therefore he does not grant us this perfect request of ours, unless, dead to the age, we judge and mortify our body on account of the sin dwelling in us, until we kill it. Those who have put on Christ, he says, have crucified their flesh against all their desires and lusts, and then they have put him on. You see how those who have put on Christ judged their bodies, and did not grant themselves to rejoice and enjoy the rest and delights and desires


[p. 346] {#po.0.p346}
ܘܟܶܢ ܠܰܒܫܘܽܗ̱ܝ. ܚܳܙܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢ ܕܳܢܘ ܦܰܓܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܕܰܠܒܶܫܘ ܠܰܡܫܝܺܚܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܝܰܗ̱ܒܘ ܠܗܘܿܢ ܕܢܶܚܕܘܽܢ ܘܢܶܬܬܢܝܺܚܘܽܢ ܒܰܬܚܺܝܘܗ̱ܝ ܕ݁ܗܳܢܳܐ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܘܰܒܦܘܰܢܳܩܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܘܒܰܪ̈ܓܝܺܓ݂ܳܬܶܗ: ܘܟܶܢ ܡܝܺܬܘ ܦܰܓܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܚܛܝܳܬܳܐ: ܘܠܰܒܫܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܠܰܡܫܝܺܚܳܐ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܐܶܢ ܡܰܫܝܺܚܳܐ ܒܟܘܽܢ ܦ݁ܰܓ݁ܪܳܐ ܡܝܬ ܗ̱ܘܵ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܚܛܝܳܬܳܐ: ܪܘܽܚܳܐ
of this world, and then, their body being dead to sin, they put on Christ. Therefore he said: If Christ is in you, the body is dead because of sin, but the spirit lives because of righteousness.


[p. 347] {#po.0.p347}
ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܚܰܝܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܙܰܕܝܺܩܘܽܬܳܐ܀ ܡܶܐܟ݂ܠܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܦ݁ܰܘܠܳܘܣ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܩܝܰܡܶܢ ܠܰܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܐܶܬܥܰܕ݂ܰܪܘ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܗܰܠܶܟܘ ܒܗܶܝܢ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܛܥܰܘ ܠܰܐܠܳܗܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܕܐܶܟܰܠܘ ܘܐܶܬܦܰܢܰܩܘ: ܘܰܣܠܶܩ ܒܗܘܢ ܪܘܰܓ݂ܙܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܝܳܐ. ܚܳܙܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܠܳܐ ܫܳܒܺܩܳܢ ܠܰܢ ܡܶܐܟ݂ܠܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܦܘܰܢܳܩܶܐ ܕܰܢܩܘܽܡ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ. ܥܰܠ ܗܰܘ ܗܳܟ݂ܝܶܠ ܣܰܒܪܳܐ ܐܰܠܶܦ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܒܺܝܫܳܐ ܠܰܒ݂ܶܝܬ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܕܗܳܟܰܢ ܠܰܡ ܝܳܪܒܝܺܢ ܐܰܢ݈ܬܘܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܘܟܶܢ ܗ̱ܘܵ ܠܰܡ ܐܝܺܬ ܠܳܗ ܦܘܽܪܣܳܐ ܕܬܶܦܪܘܽܢ ܘܬܶܣܓܘܽܢ: ܘܬܶܥܒܕܘܽܢ ܟܠ ܕܳܒ݂ܶܝܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܥܒܰܕ݂ ܒܳܪܘܺܝܳܐ. ܘܰܨܒܿܳܐ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܕܢܶܡܪܰܕ݂ ܘܢܶܬܛܦܝ̈ܣ: ܕܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܒܰܕܡܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܫܰܘܬܳܦ݂ܘܽܬ݂ܳܐ ܕܚܰܝ̈ܘܳܬܳܐ. ܘܠܳܐ ܝܺܕ݂ܰܥ ܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ ܕܦܳܪܶܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܵܘ ܘܣܳܓ݁ܶܝܢ ܐܶܠܽܘܽ ܢܛܰܪܘ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ܰܢ ܕܐܰܦ݂ܪܝܺ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܚܰܘܳܐ ܒܥܰܠܰܬ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܪܶܓܬܳܐ. ܐܳܦܶܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܗܳܢܘܽܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܶܠܬܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܟܚܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܥܳܒܕ݂ܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܣܒܰܪܘ ܕܗܳܘܶܐ ܒܶܠܥܳܕ݂ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܡܶܕ݁ܡ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܒܺܝܫܳܐ ܒܝܳܕܶܗ ܚܛܳܐ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܘܐܰܣܒ݁ܶܠ ܕܐܶܬܛܦܝܺܣ ܠܘܰܒܠܟ݁ܶܝܗ ܕܒܺܝܫܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܐܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܕܢܶܣܥܘܽܪ ܒܰܥܒܳܕ݂ܳܐ: ܒ݁ܶܠܥܳܕ݂ ܡܶܢ ܒܳܪܘܺܝܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܫܬܰܦܰܠ ܘܰܢܦ݁ܰܩ ܡܶܢ ܦܰܪܕ݁ܰܝܣܳܐ ܕܡܰܡܠܟܘܳܬܳܐ ܘܰܟܒܰܪ ܬ݁ܺܐܡܰܪ ܕܡܶܟ݂ܝܶܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܐܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܕܢܶܣܥܘܽܪ ܒܰܥܒܿܳܕ݂ܳܐ ܡܶܕ݁ܳܡ ܒܶܠܥܺܕ݂ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܕܒܳܪܘܺܝܰܐ: ܥܰܠ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܐܰܦܩܶܗ ܘܐܶܚܰܕ݂ ܬܰܪܥܶܗ ܕܦܰܪܕ݁ܰܝܣܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܥܘܽܠ ܠܶܗ܆ ܗܳܝ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܣܰܝܟܠܘܽܬܶܗ ܙܥܘܽܪܝܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ: ܕܰܨܒܿܳܐ ܕܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܣܰܩܘܽܒܝܳܐ ܠܒܳܪܘܳܢܶܗ: ܘܢܺܬ݁ܶܒ ܠܩܘܽܒܠܶܗ ܘܢܶܠܕ݁ܺܝܘܗ̱ܝ:
6. Foods, says Paul, do not commend us before God, because they profited nothing those who walked in them, but they forgot God after they had eaten, and they were delighted, and the anger of the Lord rose against them. You see how foods and delights do not allow us to stand before God. Concerning this hope, therefore, the Evil One instructed the house of Adam: thus, he said, you will be magnified, as God; and then, he said, a way will be given so that you may grow and multiply and do whatever you wish, as the Creator did. And Adam, about to rebel, was led to become in the likeness of the association of animals, nor did Adam know that he would be multiplied by observing the commandment, just as he procreated Eve without concupiscence. For although they could do nothing without the word of the Lord, they thought nevertheless that what the Evil One said would come to pass against the will of the Lord, in which Adam sinned and transgressed, because he obeyed the counsel of the Evil One: in truth, he could effect nothing without the Creator, but he went out of the paradise of the kingdom prostrate. And perhaps you might say: Since therefore he could in truth effect nothing without the Creator, why, when he was cast out, did he close the gates of paradise, lest he should enter? For the sin was less, that he wished to resist his Creator and sit opposite him and rebel against him, than that he thought he would be like him and that he opposed force to him; for unless he had thought: «I will hold him as nothing,» he would have feared his commandments and listened to him. Nevertheless, he was defiled even without concupiscence; and they contrived that which the Evil One instilled into their ears. For immediately, when they lent obedient ears, the evil thought, the taste of death, entered and was fixed in their hearts. And if you say: «Behold, those members were destined as if for association»: you indeed, if you do not wish for carnal association, the Creator made them so that you might emit urine from them.


[p. 348] {#po.0.p348}


[p. 349] {#po.0.p349}
ܐܰܟ ܕܐܰܣܒܰܪ ܕܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܰܟܘܳܐܶܗ: ܘܐܰܪܰܥ ܠܶܗ ܒܚܰܝܠܳܐ: ܐܶܠܘܽ ܠܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕ݁ܰܪܢܳܐ ܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܚܳܫܶܒ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܠܶܗ: ܕܳܚܶܠ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܦܘܽܩܕ݂ܳܢܶܗ: ܘܐܳܦ ܫܳܡܰܥ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܳܦ ܕܠܳܐ ܪܶܓ݁ܬ݁ܳܐ ܐܶܬܛܰܝܡܰܬ ܘܰܗܘܰܘ ܒܘܽܕ݂ܩܶܐ ܕܐܰܪܡܝܽ ܒܚܺܫܳܐ ܒܐܶܕܢܵܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ. ܡܶܚܕ݂ܳܐ ܓܶܝܪ ܕܐܶܬܛܦܺܝܣܘ ܘܝܰܗ̱ܒܘ ܡܰܫܡܰܥܬܗܘܽܢ ܥܶܠܰܬ ܡܰܚܫܰܝܒܬ݁ܳܐ ܒܺܝܫܬܳܐ ܛܥܳܡܬ݁ܶܗ ܕܡܰܘܬܳܐ: ܘܐܶܬܩܰܒܥܰܬ ܒܠܶܒܗܘܽܢ. ܘܐܶܢ ܬܺܐܡܰܪ ܕܗܳܐ ܗܰܕ݁ܳܡܶܐ ܐܝܺܬܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕ݁ܠܳܗ ܠܫܰܘܬܳܦܘܽܬܳܐ: ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܐܶܢ ܠܳܐ ܨܳܒܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܒܳܗ ܒܫܰܘܬܳܦܘܽܬܳܐ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܬܶܦܫܘܽܪ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܡܶܢܗܘܽܢ: ܥܒܰܕ݂ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܒܳܪܘܳܝܳܐ܀ ܡܳܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܛܰܪ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܵܘܗ̱ܝ ܝܰܘܡܳܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܳܟ ܘܰܐܬܳܐ ܠܘܳܬ ܡܚܰܪܘܽܬܳܐ ܗܳܝ ܕܐܰܘܒ݁ܶܕ݂ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܘܗܳܐ ܫܳܩܠܳܗ ܡܳܢܳܟ ܠܪܶܓܬܳܐ: ܡܳܐ ܕܐܶܬܰܝܬ ܠܗܰܘ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܰܢܦܰܠ ܡܶܢܶܝܗ ܐܳܕܳܡ܂ ܘܡܳܐ ܕܰܗܘܰܝܬ ܩܰܕ݂ܝܺܫܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܪܶܓܬܳܐ: ܚܳܙܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܕ݂ܰܦܫܳܪܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܗܰܕ̈ܳܡܶܐ ܘܠܳܐܘ ܕܫܰܘܬܳܦܘܽܬܳܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܬܘܒ ܣܳܠܩܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܒܳܠܳܟ
7. Therefore observe his commandments today, as he told you, and tend toward the perfection which Adam lost, and behold, he will take away from you concupiscence when you arrive at that from which Adam fell. And after you have become holy and without concupiscence, you will see that those members are for urination, not [instruments] of coitus,


[p. 350] {#po.0.p350}


[p. 351] {#po.0.p351}
ܪܶܓ݂ܬ݁ܳܐ ܡܳܐ ܕܗܳܘܶܝܬ ܩܰܕ݂ܝܺܫܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܪܳܐܶܓ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܳܗ ܠܫܰܘܬܳܦܘܽܬܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ ܠܳܐ ܪܳܐܶܓ ܠܳܗ ܡܝܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܰܫܩܺܝܠܳܐ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܗܳܟܘܳܐ: ܐܳܦ݂ ܚܺܐܪܘܳܬܳܟ݂ ܐܶܫܬܰܡܥܰܬ ܠܒܺܝܫܳܐ ܘܰܨܒܰܝܬ ܒܳܗ ܐܰܝܟ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܘܝܳܗܶܒ ܠܳܟ ܒܳܪܘܳܝܳܟ݂ ܒܚܺܝܡܬ݁ܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܠܳܐܕܳܡ: ܘܪܳܓ݁ܶܙ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܰܡܪܦܶܝܢܰܢ ܩܰܕܝܺܫܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܡܰܠܰܐܟܶܐ ܘܡܶܬ݁ܕ݁ܰܡܶܝܢܰܢ ܒܰܒܥܝܺܪܳܐ. ܘܡܶܬܪܰܚܰܡ ܥܠܰܝܟ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܥܰܠ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܘܢܳܛܰܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܚܳܝܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܒܫܰܘܬܳܦܘܽܬܳܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ. ܘܐܶܢ ܬ݁ܺܐܡܰܪ ܕܥܰܠ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܥܒܰܕ݂ ܕ݁ܶܟܪܳܐ ܘܢܶܩܒܬܳܐܢ ܙܶܠ ܪܰܫܚܶܝܗܝ ܕܥܰܠ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܠܒܰܕ݂ ܕ݁ܰܟܪܳܐ ܘܢܶܩܒܬܳܐ. ܘܗܘܽ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܠܳܟ: ܕܠܳܐ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܡܣܰܓܦܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܳܟ݂: ܐܰܠܘܽ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܳܐ ܨܒܰܝܬ ܕܐܰܝܟ ܒܥܺܝܪܳܐ ܬ݁ܶܗܘܶܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܡܰܠܰܐܟܶܐ. ܚܳܪ ܠܶܗ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܒ݁ܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܒܰܒܥܺܝܪܳܐ ܘܰܪܚܶܡ ܕܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܐܰܟܘܳܐܶܗ ܘܰܣܢܳܐ ܩܰܕܝܺܫܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܡܰܠܰܐܟܶܐ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܥܰܠ ܣܰܒܪܳܐ ܕܝܺܪܶܒ ܡܶܢ ܡܰܠܰܐܟ݂ܳܝܶܐ ܘܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܡܳܪܗܘܽܢ. ܘܰܗܘܰܘ ܥܰܠܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܒܥܳܩܬ݁ܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܡܰܦܘܽܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܐܳܕܳܡ ܘܥܰܠ ܪܘܰܓ݂ܙܳܐ ܕܩܰܒ݁ܶܠ ܡܶܢ ܒܺܝܫܳܝܐ: ܘܰܗܘܳܬ ܒܗܰܘ ܙܰܒ݂ܢܳܐ ܒܥܶܠܕܒܳܒܘܽܬܳܐ ܠܥܶܠܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܥܰܡ ܬܰܚܬܳ̈ܶܐ: ܥܰܠ ܕܫܳܛ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܒܳܪܝ̈ܗ. ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ
because when you are holy, concupiscence will no longer rise to your mind, nor will you any longer desire association, just as a dead, lifeless person does not crave it; unless you are such, even your freedom will obey the evil one and you will crave it, like Adam, and your Creator will grant it to you with fury, as he did to Adam, and he is angry because, having abandoned the holiness of the angels, we are assimilated to the beast, and he will have mercy on you, as he did on Adam, and having observed justice you will live while you are in marriage. Even if you say: «Why did he make male and female»? Go, rebuke him, «why did he make male and female», and he himself will say to you: «This would have harmed you nothing, if you had not wished to be like a beast and not like the angels». For he looked, he says, at the beast and wished to become like it and hated the holiness of the angels, namely when he hoped that he would become greater than the angels and as if he were their master. And the angels were made in sadness because of the fall of Adam and because of the anger which he contracted from the Evil One, and at that time enmity arose between the heavenly and the earthly, because Adam despised the word of his Creator. For a similar reason, therefore, by observing the words of the Lord today, we are reconciled with the heavenly ones. After Jesus appeared, however, he reveals to whom he wills that he wishes him to become in the likeness of the first creation of Adam. Before the advent of the Lord, indeed, the kingdom of heaven was narrow, because it was not manifest to everyone, and a few certain ones afflicted and humbled themselves and, doing the will of God, grasped it; this, however, is manifest today to everyone who loves it.


[p. 352] {#po.0.p352}
ܗܳܟ݂ܽܠ ܝܰܘܡܳܢ: ܡܳܝܐ ܕܰܢܛܰܪܢ ܡܶܝܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܡܶܬܪܰܥܺܝܢ ܥܰܡܰܢ ܥܶܠܳܫ̈ܶܐ. ܡܶܢ ܕܐܬܓܠܝ̇ ܕ݁ܺܝܢ ܝܽܘܠܦܳܢܳܐ ܓ݁ܠܳܐ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܨܳܒܶܐ ܕ݁ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܒܪܝܺܬܶܗ ܕܐܳܕܳܡ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܺܝܬܳܐ. ܡܶܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܡܶܐܬ݂ܝܺܬ݁ܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ: ܐܰܠܺܝܨܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܬ ܡܰܠܟ݁ܘܽܬܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܒܗܳܝ ܕܠܳܐ ܓܰܠܝܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܟܽܠ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ. ܘܚܰܕܚܕ݁ܳܢܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܐܰܠܶܨܘ ܢܰܦܫܗܘܽܢ ܘܐܶܬܡܰܟܰܟܘ ܘܰܥܒܰܕ݂ܘ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܘܐܰܕܪܟܘܽܗ̱ܝ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ: ܗܳܐ ܓܰܠܝܳܐ ܝܰܘܡܳܢܳܐ ܠܟܠ ܕܪܳܚܶܡ ܠܳܗ܀ ܡܶܢ ܕܰܒܩܰܝܘ ܗܳܟ݂ܽܠ ܕܒܶܝܬ ܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܦܰܚܳܐ: ܘܰܪܚܶܡܘ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܘܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܡܶܬܚܰܙܝܳܢ: ܘܰܥܒܰܪܘ ܥܰܠ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܕܒܳܪܘܺܝܳܐ ܘܐܶܬܿܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܪܫܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܘܐܶܬ݂ܪܰܚܰܡ ܥܠܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܘܣܳܡ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܺܢܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܕܰܥܒܰܪܘ ܥܰܠ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܳܐ ܘܐܰܦܶܣ ܠܗܘܢ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܢܶܫܬܰܘܬܦܘܽܢ: ܟܶܢ ܗܘܳܬ ܡܪܕ݂ܝܺܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܪܶܓܬܳܐ ܕܙܘܽܘܳܓ݂ܳܐ ܒܐܳܕܳܡ ܘܰܒܚܰܘܳܐ: ܘܟܶܢ ܒܚܰܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܟܽܠܳܗ ܣܰܟܠܘܽܬܶܗ ܐܶܫܬܰܘܬܰܦ. ܟܬܝܺܒ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܕܰܪܫܺܝܗ̱ܝ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܳܐܕܳܡ ܘܐܰܦ݁ܶܣ ܠܶܗ ܕܢܶܩܢܶܐ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܰܪܚܶܡ: ܢܦܰܩ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܡܶܢ ܦܰܪܕ݁ܰܝܣܳܐ ܘܰܦܠܰܚ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܕܐܬܢܣܺܝܒ ܡܶܢܳܗ: ܘܰܚܟܰܡ ܠܚܰܘܳܐ ܘܝܶܠܕ݂ܰܬ ܠܩܳܝܐܶܝܢ. ܐܝܺܬ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܪܶܓ݁ܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܐܝܺܬ ܪܶܓܬ݁ܳܐ. ܪܶܓ݂ܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܫܰܘܬܳܦܘܽܬܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܺܬܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ: ܘܪܶܓܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܬܶܪܰܓ݂ ܡܶܕ݁ܳܡ ܕܐܺܝܬ ܠܚܰܒܪܳܟ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܬܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ܂ ܗܳܟ݂ܰܢ ܐܳܦ ܝܰܘܡܳܢ: ܡܳܐ ܕܰܪܚܶܡܘ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܘܰܦܒܰܩܘ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܟܽܠ ܕܐܝܺܬ ܒܳܗ: ܘܰܐܠܰܝܘ ܪܶܥܝܳܢܗܘܽܢ ܘܦܰܓܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܝܘܽܬܪܳܢܳܐ
8. After, therefore, the house of Adam had left heaven and loved the earth, and had transgressed the visible things and the law of the Creator, and God came rebuking them and had mercy on them and set another law for them, after they had transgressed the first, and God had permitted them to cohabit; then the instinct of the concupiscence of coitus arose in Adam and Eve, and finally, at the end of the whole transgression, he cohabited. For it is written, after God rebuked Adam and permitted him to possess what he might love, that Adam went out of paradise and tilled the earth from which he was taken and knew Eve, who bore Cain. But there is concupiscence and there is concupiscence. One is the concupiscence of coitus and another is the concupiscence of «do not covet what is your neighbor's». So also today; when the sons of Adam, loving heaven, leave the earth and all that is in it


[p. 353] {#po.0.p353}


[p. 354] {#po.0.p354}


[p. 355] {#po.0.p355}
ܥܳܒܘܽܪܳܐ ܘܐܶܬܡܰܟܰܟ݂ ܪܶܥܫܳܢܗܘܽܢ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕ݁ܝܺܕ݂ܰܥ ܕܢܶܬܬܪܝܰܡ ܘܢܶܫܒܘܽܩ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܘܢܺܐܪܰܬ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ܀
and suspend their mind from fleeting gain and their mind is humbled, just as it knows how to be exalted, having left heaven to inherit the earth.
ܡܳܐ ܗܳܝܶܠ ܕܐܶܣܬ݁ܰܪܰܩܘ ܘܐܶܬܡܰܟܟܘ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܐܶܬܬܪܝܡܝܘ ܡܶܢ ܒܪܝܫܝܬ: ܟܶܢ ܡܶܬܥܰܩܪܳܐ ܡܰܪܕ݂ܝܳܢܽܘܬܳܐ ܕܪܰܓܬ݁ܳܐ ܡܶܢܗܘܿܢ. ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܡܶܢ ܕܰܪܚܺܝܡ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܟ݁ܽܠ ܕܒܳܗ̇: ܟܶܢ ܐܰܦܶܣ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܬܶܗܘܶܐ ܒܗܘܽܢ ܪܰܓܬܳܐ: ܗܳܟܰܢ ܐܳܦ ܝܰܘܡܳܢ: ܡܳܐ ܕܰܫܒܰܩܘ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܟ݁ܽܠ ܕܒܳܗ̇: ܘܚܺܝܪܘ ܒܫܡܰܝܳܐ: ܘܐܰܕܪܶܟܘ ܗܰܘ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܐܰܘܒܶܕ݂ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܘܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܘ ܡܳܢܰܘ ܫܪܳܪܳܐ: ܘܪܰܘܡܳܐ ܘܥܘܽܡܩܳܐ ܘܐܘܰܪܟ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܦܬܳܝܳܐ: ܟܶܢ ܡܶܬܚܰܝܪܝܺܢ ܡܶܢ ܡܰܪܕ݂ܝܳܢܽܘܬܳܐ ܕܪܶܓܬܳܐ: ܘܦܳܣܶܩ ܠܳܗ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܡܶܢܗܘܽܢ ܘܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܡܰܠܰܐܟ݂ܶܐ ܕܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܪܳܓܚܢ. ܐܳܡܰܪ ܓܶܝܪ ܫܠܺܝܚܳܐ ܕ݁ܗܳܠܺܝܢ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ: ܕܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢ ܕܛܰܝܒܬܘܽܢ ܗܰܕܳܡܰܝܟܘܽܢ ܙܰܝܢܳܐ ܠܰܚܛܺܝܬܳܐ: ܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ ܐܶܬܛܰܝܒܘ ܠܶܡܫܡܰܥ ܐܶܕܢܳܐ ܕܟܰܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ. ܘܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܝܳܕ݂ܥܝܺܢܰܢ ܕܢܶܫܒܘܽܩ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܘܢܺܐܪܰܬ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ ܢܰܫܒܘܽܩ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܢܺܐܪܰܬ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ: ܘܗܳܐ ܙܳܟ݂ܶܝܢܰܢ ܡܶܢ ܚܘܽܦܳܝܛܳܐ ܕܒܺܝܫܬܳܐ. ܡܶܛܺܝܠ ܕܐܳܦ ܒܥܰܝܘܬ݁ܳܢܽܘܬܳܐ ܕܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܚܶܠܛܰܬ ܒܺܝܫܬܳܐ. ܡܶܢ ܕܚܺܠܳܗ ܓܰܘܪܳܐ ܘܪܰܒܝܰܬ ܙܳܢܝܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܒܬܪ ܬܘܽܒ ܡܶܢ ܙܳܢܝܘܽܬܳܐ: ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܰܣܢܳܝܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܕܐܰܝܟܰܝܢ ܢܶܦܠܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܐܳܦ ܡܶܢ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ. ܐܰܝܠܺܝܢ ܗܽܘܟܝܺܠ ܕܡܶܣܬ݁ܰܪܩܺܝܢ ܡܶܢ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܘܚܳܝܪܝܺܢ ܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܒܡܳܪܗܘܽܢ ܘܣܳܓܕ݂ܝܺܢ ܠܰܐܠܳܗܗܘܽܢ: ܘܰܠܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܪܳܚܡܺܝܢ: ܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܩܰܕ݁ܺܝܫܺܝܢ ܘܥܳܡܪܝܺܢ ܥܰܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܒܪܰܘܡܳܐ ܥܶܠܳܝܳܐ. ܘܐܺܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܫܳܩܠܺܝܢ ܘܢܳܬܠܺܝܢ ܒ݂ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܘܙܳܒܢܺܝܢ ܘܰܡܙܰܒܢܺܝܢ: ܘܩܳܢܶܝܢ ܒܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܡܰܛܶܝܒܺܝܢ ܠܰܣܟ̈ܺܝܢܶܐ: ܟܰܕ ܠܚܕ݂ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܠܳܐ ܡܰܒܶܐܫܝܢ: ܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܕܒܳܬ݂ܰܪ ܓܡܝܪ̈ܶܐ. ܟܰܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܰܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܡܰܒܶܐܫܳܐ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܡܰܡܒܶܐܫ ܠܳܗ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܰܡܘܒ݁ܕ݂ܳܐ ܕܶܒܝܳܫܬܳܐ ܘܥܳܪܩܳܐ
9. Therefore, when they have emptied themselves and humbled themselves, just as from the beginning they were exalted, then the instinct of concupiscence is rooted out from them. For just as after their mind had loved the earth and all that is in it, God permitted concupiscence to come to be in them: so also today, after they have left the earth and all that is in it and have looked at the Lord in heaven and grasped what Adam lost, and have known the whole truth and height and depth and length and breadth: they will be freed from the instinct of concupiscence, which God will cut off from them, and they will be as the Angels in heaven, who do not covet. For the Apostle says: I say this: as you prepared your members as instruments for sin, so be prepared to hear the ear of justice. And now, as we know that having left heaven we inherit the earth, so having left the earth we will inherit heaven and behold, we will carry off the victory over the solicitation of iniquity. For even in just marriage iniquity is mixed. From it comes adultery and [it] added fornication and what is still worse than fornication, which displeases God; for how the sons of Adam have fallen even from justice! Those, therefore, who have renounced the earth and looked to heaven, to their Lord, and have adored their God and loved everyone, will be holy and will dwell with the Lord in the supernal height. And those who in the age are occupied with leisure and business and sell and buy and possess justly and do no evil to the needy: they are just, inferior to the perfect. For human justice does not do evil to one who does evil to it, but, its own things being lost, it flees evil, just as Isaac left the wells of water of his father when he was litigated with, and he called their names Satan and Burden, because he was litigated with and difficulties were placed upon him and he went away from there; and just as Abraham and Isaac surrendered their wives and did not contend nor quarrel, but God judged their contention.


[p. 356] {#po.0.p356}


[p. 357] {#po.0.p357}
ܡܢ ܒܚܺܫܬܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܰܒܰܩ ܐܝܼܣܚܳܩ ܟܺܝ̈ܶܐ ܕܡܰܝ̈ܳܐ ܕܐܰܒܝܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܟܰܝܕ݂ ܢܕ݂ܰܘ ܥܰܩܒܶܗ: ܘܰܩܪܳܐ ܫܡܳܗܰܝ̈ܗܶܝܢ ܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ ܘܰܥܝܼܣܳܩܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܕܰܢܨܰܘ ܘܐܶܬܥܰܣܰܩܘ ܥܰܡܶܗ: ܘܟܰܢܝܼ ܡܶܢ ܬܰܡܳܢ: ܘܐܰܝܟ ܕܝܰܙܒܶܢܘ ܢܶܫܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ ܐܰܒܪܳܗܳܡ ܘܐܝܼܣܚܳܩ ܘܠܳܐ ܕܳܢܘ ܘܠܳܐ ܢܨܰܚ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܳܢ ܕܝܳܢܗܘܽܢ܀ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܗܳܟܝܺܠ ܕܡܰܛܶܐܒ݁ܝܺܢ ܘܰܐܪܝܺܨܝܺܢ ܒܕܘܳܡ ܕܘܳܟ: ܘܒܰܙܒܰܢ ܡܰܒܶܐܘܝܺܝܢ ܠܐ̱ܢܳܫ: ܠܳܐ ܠܘܳܬ ܟܺܐܢܝܘܽܬܳܐ ܩܰܘܝܽܘ ܘܠܳܐ ܠܘܳܬ ܒܚܽܫܘܽܬܳܐ: ܒܬܰܪ̈ܬܰܝܗܶܝܢ ܡܶܬܚܰܫܚܝܺܢ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܝܰܘܡܳܢ ܚܳܙܶܝܢܰܢ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܕܥܳܒܕܝܰܢ ܕ݁ܰܠܬܰܚܬ ܡܶܢ ܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕ݁ܰܡܬ݁ܰܚܬ݁ܺܝܢ ܡܶܢ ܓܡܝܳܪ̈ܶܐ. ܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܕܡܶܬܚܰܫܚܝܺܢ ܒܛܳܒ̈ܳܬܳܐ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܠܳܐ ܡܰܒܶܐܝܺܢ. ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܦ݂ܶܠܓ݁ܳܐ ܛܳܒ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܥܳܒܕܝܺܢ ܘܦ݁ܶܠܓܿܳܐ ܒܚܺܫ̈ܳܬ݁ܳܐ: ܐܳܦܶܢ ܡܶܬܪܕ݁ܺܝܢ: ܥܳܒܶܕ݂
10. Therefore, those who do good here and there and show themselves sincere and sometimes do evil to some, remain neither with justice nor with wickedness: they use both; just as we see today men who do things inferior to the just, inferior to the perfect. But the just are those who use good things and do no evil to anyone. Those, however, who do half good [works] and half evil, although they will be punished,


[p. 358] {#po.0.p358}


[p. 359] {#po.0.p359}
ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܪ̈ܰܚܡܐ ܥܠܰܝܗܘܽܢ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܰܥܒ݁ܰܕ݂ܘ ܗܶܢܘܽܢ ܪ̈ܰܚܡܐ ܥܰܠ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ. ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܰܙܥܘܽܪ̈ܝܳܢ ܐܶܢܺܝܢ ܛܳܒ̈ܳܬܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܒܝܼܫ̈ܳܬܗܘܽܢ: ܠܳܐ ܥܰܘܿܠ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܢܰܛܥܶܐ ܥܒܳܕܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ: ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܕܦܳܪܰܥ ܠܗܘܢ ܒܝܼܫ̈ܳܬܗܘܽܢ: ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܐܳܦ ܛܳܒܿܳܬܗܘܽܢ. ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܰܗܘܰܘ ܕܠܳܐ ܛܳܒܿܳܬܳܐ ܘܰܕܠܳܐ ܒܚܺܫ̈ܳܬ݁ܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܐܰܛܶܐܒ݂ܘ ܠܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܘܠܳܐ ܐܰܒܶܐܫܘ: ܠܳܐ ܠܓ݂ܺܗܰܢܳܐ ܢܳܚܬܝܺܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܰܠܟܘܽܬܳܐ ܝܳܪܬܝܺܢ: ܡܶܬܝܰܩܪܝܺܢ ܡܶܢ ܓ݁ܺܗܰܢܳܐ ܘܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܒܐܰܬ݁ܪܳܐ ܕܘܳܠܶܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܘܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܨܳܒܶܐ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܥܳܒܶܕܠܗܘܿܢ. ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܐܰܒܺܐܫܘ ܠܐ̱ܢܳܫ: ܗܳܟ݂ܰܢ ܐܶܚܰܕܘ ܪ̈ܰܚܡܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܟܽܠܢܳܫ. ܢܛܰܪܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܗܳܝ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܡܰܢ ܕܡܰܟܺܐܦ ܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܢܰܩ: ܘܫܰܒܩܘܽܗ ܠܥܰܒܕܽܘܬܳܐ ܗܳܝ ܕܡܰܢ ܕ݁ܡܰܡܛܶܐܒ݂ ܝܳܪܶܬ ܚܰܫ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܰܠܥܳܠܰܡ: ܡܶܟܝܺܠ ܓܠܰܙܘ ܢܰܦܫܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܒܘܽܣܳܡܳܐ ܘܰܢܛܰܪܘ ܢܰܦܫܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܦܘܽܢܳܩܳܐ. ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܝܢ ܗܳܕܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ ܕܰܬܪܝܺܨܳܐ ܒܕܝܺܠܳܗ ܘܡܰܛܶܐܒ݂ܳܐ ܠܟ݁ܽܠܢܳܫ ܒ݁ܰܕ݂ܡܳܛܚܳܐ ܒܐܝܰܕܼܶܝܗ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܠܳܐ ܡܰܒ݁ܶܐܫܳܐ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ: ܗܳܕܶܐ ܒܳܬ݂ܰܪ ܓܡܝܼܪܘܽܬܳܐ ܐܝܺܬܶܝܗ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܐܶܣܬܰܪܩܰܬ ܡܶܢ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܐܰܕܪܟܰܬ ܪܰܘܡܳܐ ܘܥܘܽܡܩܳܐ ܘܐܘܽܪܟܳܐ ܘܰܦܬܳܝܳܐ. ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܐܰܛܺܐܒܘ ܘܠܳܐ ܐܰܒܶܐܫܘ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ: ܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܒܶܝܬ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܢܩܝܺܢ ܠܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܐܝܼܬܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܒܐܰܬܪܳܐ ܕܚܰܝ̈ܶܐ: ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢ ܕܰܗܘܰܘ ܒܗܳܢ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ
God will show mercy to them, because they had mercy on men; but those whose good works are less than their evil ones, God is not unjust to forget their works; just as he will repay them for their evil works, so also for the good. Those, however, who are destitute of both good and evil works, doing good to no one and evil to no one, do not descend into Gehenna, nor will they inherit the kingdom: they are valued as more than Gehenna and are placed in a place convenient for them, and the Lord will do what he wills with them. But just as they did no evil to anyone: so they closed their charity to all; they observed the saying: he who does evil will be tortured, and they omitted that: he who does good will inherit eternal life; consequently, they deprived themselves of delights and preserved themselves from torture. But justice is that which is upright in its own affairs and does good to each one as is the measure for itself, harming no one; this is inferior to perfection, because it is not emptied from the earth nor does it grasp the height and depth and length and breadth. Those, however, who do good to no one and evil to no one, will be in the middle between those who are tortured and those who hold the place of life, just as in this life they were in the middle between those doing good and those doing evil: not doing good with these nor doing evil with those. But these things are so, for there are many mansions with the Father.


[p. 360] {#po.0.p360}
ܒܰܝܢܳܬ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܥܳܒܕܝܺܢ ܫܰܦܝܼܪܳܬܳܐ ܠܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܥܳܒܕܝܺܢ ܒܝܼܫ̈ܳܬ݁ܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܥܒܰܕ݂ܘ ܛܳܒ̈ܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܥܒܰܕ݂ܘ ܒܝܼܫ̈ܳܬܳܐ. ܘܰܕ݂ܗܳܟܰܢ ܐܝܺܬܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ: ܕ݂ܰܕ݂ܝܳܪ̈ܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܣܰܓ̈ܺܝܶܐܐ ܐܝܺܬ ܒܶܝܬ ܐܰܒܳܐ܀ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܐܡܰܪ: ܕܡܰܢ ܕܰܒܩܰܠܝܺܠ ܥܰܘܰܠ ܒܣܰܓܺܝ ܥܰܘܳܠ: ܘܡܰܢ ܕܰܒܩܰܠܝܺܠ ܡܗܰܝܡܰܢ ܒܣܰܓܺܝ ܡܗܰܝܡܰܢ. ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܶܠܬܳܐ ܡܰܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܦܳܪܶܫ ܠܳܗ: ܐܰܘ ܙܰܟܝܼ ܒܳܗ ܟ݀ܽܠܳܗ ܒܪܝܺܬܳܐ: ܐܰܘ ܚܰܫܶܒ ܒܳܙܘ ܟܽܠܳܗ ܒܪܝܺܬܳܐ: ܠܒܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܡܶܬܓܰܡܪܝܺܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܚܰܫܒܝܺܢ ܬܚܘܽܬܶܝܗ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܰܫܠܚܽܘ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܘܰܨܳܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ. ܘܠܳܐ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕ݁ܡܰܪܫܥܝܺܢ ܘܰܓܠܝܼܙܝܺܢ ܡܶܢ ܟܽܠܗܶܝܢ ܛܳܒܿ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܡܶܬܚܰܫܒܝܺܢ ܬܚܘܽܬܶܝܗ: ܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܡܶܬܚܰܫܒܝܺܢ ܬܚܶܝܬ ܥܰܘܠܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܶܒܕܨܰܪ ܒܨܝܼܪܝܺܢ ܡܶܢ ܓܡܝܳܪ̈ܶܐ. ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܐܶܣܬ݁ܰܪܰܩܘ ܘܐܶܬܩܰܕ݂ܰܫܘ: ܠܳܐ ܐܶܫܟ݁ܰܚܘ ܕܢܶܥܒܕܘܽܢ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܓܡܝܼܪܳܐ ܘܰܡܩܰܒܠܳܐ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܚܶܢܢ ܕܰܓܡܝܼܪ̈ܶܐ ܘܒܫܺܝܘܠܝܼܢ ܐܲܢܘܽܢ: ܘܠܰܝܬ ܒܗܘܽܢ ܒܘܽܨܳܪܶܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܩܰܠܝܺܠ ܡܶܢ ܕܐܶܬܓܡܰܪܘ: ܘܪ̈ܰܫܝܼܥܶܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܩܰܠܝܺܠ ܐܶܙܕ݂ܰܕ݁ܰܩܘ ܡܶܢ ܕܐܰܪܫܰܥܘ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܠܒ݂ܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܪܶܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܶܠܬܳܐ. ܟ݁ܽܠ ܕܝܢ ܕܐܚܺܬ ܠܶܗ ܩܰܠܺܝܠ ܙܰܕ݁ܺܝܩܽܘܬܳܐ ܘܩܰܠܺܝܠ ܥܰܘܠܳܐ: ܚܒܰܫܝܬ݁ܶܗ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܡܶܠܬܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܠܥܶܠ ܝܳܗܒܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܕ݁ܢܶܬܥܰܠܶܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܠܘܳܬ ܪ̈ܰܝܳܥܶܐ ܝܽܘܒ݁ܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܕ݁ܢܳܚܘܽܐ. ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܗܳܟ݂ܽܝܠ ܕ݁ܪܳܚܫܺܝܢ: ܕܚܰܕ݂ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܐܰܬܪܳܐ ܕܚܰܫ̈ܶܐ ܐܝܺܬ ܠܳܗ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܰܚܕ݂ܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ ܓܺܗܰܢܳܐ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܕܥܰܘܳܠܝܺܢ ܩܰܠܺܝܠ ܘܙܰܕ݁ܺܝܩܝܺܢ ܩܰܠܺܝܠ: ܒܐܺܝܢܳܐ ܐܰܬ݂ܪܳܐ ܡܩܝܡܝܢ
11. For the Lord said: He who is unjust in a little is unjust in much; and he who is faithful in a little is faithful in much. But by this word, unless one discerns it rightly, he either justifies the whole creation or condemns the whole creation except those who have escaped perfect and are not reckoned to the same, for they have put off all their defects. Nor are those who, acting unjustly, are destitute of all good things, reckoned to the same, nor are the just included under iniquity, except that they are lesser than the perfect; and because they did not empty themselves nor sanctify themselves, they could not do the perfect and acceptable will of God. But because the perfect are consummated and have no defect, not even the slightest, after they have escaped perfect, and the impious are not justified even a little after they have become unjust: these are outside this saying. But all who have moderate justice or moderate iniquity, this saying includes, and it neither allows them to be exalted upward nor suffers them to descend to the impious. Those, therefore, who contend that the Lord has a single mansion of life and a single Gehenna: where do they place men who are little unjust and little just, when behold, the sentence of the Lord neither allows them to ascend to

[p. 363] {#po.0.p363}
ܠܗܘܽܢ: ܕܗܳܐ ܡܶܠܬܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ: ܠܳܐ ܠܪܰܘܡܳܐ ܥܶܠܳܝܳܐ ܐܰܬ݂ܪܳܐ ܕܠܰܝܬ ܒܘܽܨܳܪ̈ܶܐ ܫܳܒܩܳܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܕܢܶܣܩܘܽܢ: ܘܠܳܐ ܠܓ݂ܺܗܰܢܳܐ ܐܰܬ݂ܪܳܐ ܕܠܰܝܬ ܚܰܝ̈ܶܐ ܝܽܘܒ݁ܳܐ ܠܗܘܢ ܕܢܶܚܬܘܽܢ܆ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܡܰܢ ܕ݁ܶܠܰܚ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܘܽܨܳܪܶܐ: ܘܡܰܢ ܕܰܚܶܝܒ ܠܟܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܛܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܘܒܺܝ̈ܫܶܐ: ܠܕ݂ܰܪܓ݁ܳܐ ܕܰܓܡܝܳܪܘܬܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܡܳܛܳܐ. ܡܰܢ ܕܚܰܣܰܪ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܚܕܳܐ: ܙܥܘܽܪ ܗ̱ܘ̈ ܡܶܢ ܓܡܝܳܪ̈ܶܐ. ܟܽܠ ܐܢܫ ܗܳܟ݂ܽܝܠ ܐܰܝܟ ܥܒܳܝܕ݂ܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܡܶܬܦܪܰܥ. ܠܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܫܘܶܐ ܩܳܛܶܠ ܡܳܐܐ ܩܶܛܠܺܝܢ ܥܰܡ ܗܰܘ ܕ݁ܩܳܛܶܠ ܚܰܕ݂ ܩܶܛܠܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܝܳܗܶܒ݂ ܗܰܘ ܚܕ݂ܳܐ ܢܰܦܫܳܐ: ܗܰܘ ܡܳܐܐ ܝܳܗܶܒ: ܘܐܶܢ ܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܢܰܩ ܗܰܘ ܚܰܕ݂ ܬܰܫܢܝܺܩܳܐ: ܥܰܡ ܡܳܐܐ ܡܶܫܬܰܢܰܩ. ܘܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܺܐܡܰܪ ܕܐܰܝܟ ܚܕ݂ܳܐ
the supernal height, where no defect is given, nor suffers them to descend into Gehenna, where there is no life? For unless one lays aside all his defects and loves all men, good and bad, he does not arrive at the degree of perfection; for he who lacks one thing is lesser than the perfect. Therefore, each one will receive retribution according to his works. For he who commits a hundred homicides is not equal to him who commits a single homicide, but if the latter gives his soul once, the former will give it a hundred times; and if the latter is tortured with a single torture, the former will be tortured a hundred times. Nor should you say that they are to be tortured as if with a single torture: but the torture of him who committed a single homicide being finished, the other will be tortured after him with a hundred other torments.


[p. 364] {#po.0.p364}
ܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܢܩܝܺܢ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܳܐ ܕܪܰܓܡܰܪ ܬܰܫܢܝܺܩܶܗ ܕܗܰܘ ܕ݁ܰܩܛܰܠ ܚܰܕ݂ ܩܶܛܠܳܐ: ܗܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܪܶܗ ܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܢܰܩ ܗܰܘ ܡܳܐܐ ܐܰܝܟܰܢܳܝܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܢܝܺܢ܀ ܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܟ݁ܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܘܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܘܙܰܕ݁ܺܝܩ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܰܡܛܰܘ ܠܰܓ݂ܡܝܳܪܘܳܬܳܐ ܘܰܫܟܶܒܘ ܡܶܢܩܕܳܡ ܡܶܐܬ݂ܝܺܬܶܗ ܕ݁ܡܳܪܰܢ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܠܳܐ ܓܡܝܳܪܝܺܢ: ܠܥܝ̈ܢ ܫܠܝ̈ܚܶܐ ܓ݁ܡܰܪ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܦ݁ܰܘܠܳܘܣ: ܕܒܶܠܥܳܕ݂ܰܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܢܶܬܓܰܡܪܘܽܢ. ܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܦܰܪܰܩܠܺܝܛܳܐ ܗܰܘ ܕܡܰܠܶܦ݂ ܡܘܰܟܳܟܳܐ ܕܰܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܟܽܠܢܳܫ: ܘܚܘܽܒܳܐ ܕܰܠܘܳܬ ܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܐܶܫܬ݁ܰܕ݁ܰܪ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܫܬܰܕܰܪ ܠܰܫܠܝ̈ܚܶܐ: ܘܣܰܟܝܽܘ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܝܰܘ̈ܡܳܬܗܘܽܢ ܕܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܫܰܝܢܳܐ ܒܚܰܝ̈ܘܳܬܗܘܽܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܗܘܳܐ: ܝܳܕ݂ܥܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܐܳܬܶܐ ܦܳܪܘܺܩܳܐ ܠܥܳܠܡܳܐ: ܒܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܕܐܝܺܬ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܒܗܘܽܢ ܘܰܡܫܰܝܢ ܟ݇ܠ. ܐܳܦ݂ ܠܳܐܕ݂ܳܡ ܟܰܕ݂ ܒܟܳܐ ܘܰܒܥܳܐ ܘܐܶܬܚܰܢܰܢ: ܐܶܫܬܰܘܕܝܽ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܕܐܳܬܶܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܘܓ݂ܳܡܰܪ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܠܰܐܝܠܶܝܢ ܕ݁ܪܳܕ݂ܝܺܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܚܘܽܒܳܐ ܘܒܳܬܰܪ ܓܡܝܳܪܘܳܬܳܐ: ܗܳܝ ܕܰܢܦ݁ܰܠ ܡܶܢܳܗ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܗܳܟ݂ܽܝܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܗܘܳܐ ܫܰܝܢܳܐ ܒܚܰܝ̈ܘܳܬܗܘܽܢ: ܠܳܐ ܐܶܬܓܡܰܪܘ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕ݁ܰܒ݁ܚܰܫܳܐ ܘܒܰܙܩܝܳܦܳܐ ܕܰܒܪܶܗ: ܨܒܳܐ ܐܰܒܳܐ ܘܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܕܢܶܥܒܶܕ݂ ܬܰܪܥܘܽܬܳܐ. ܘܐܶܠܘܽ ܨܒܳܐ ܟ݁ܽܠܳܗ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܕܡܶܢܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܡܶܐܬ݂ܝܺܬ݂ܶܗ ܕܢܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܡܘܽܫܳܐ ܘܐܰܝܟ ܐܶܠܺܝܐ: ܡܰܥܦܶܣ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܢܶܬܓܰܡܪܘܽܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܒܥܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܕܢܺܐܬ݁ܶܐ ܠܚܰܠܕ݂ܳܐ ܘܰܠܨܰܥܪܳܐ ܕܰܙܩܝܳܦܳܐ: ܘܐܰܪܥܶܕ݂ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܣܳܓ݂ܳܐ ܕܰܒܥܶܠܕܒܳܒܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܡܶܛܽܠ ܥܒܳܪ ܦܘܰܩܕ݂ܳܢܳܐ: ܟ݁ܰܕ ܝܳܬܶܒ ܒ݁ܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܒܐܝܰܩܳܪ ܪܰܒܘܽܬ݂ܶܗ ܘܫܳܠܶܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܚܰܪܒ݁ܳܐ ܕܟܳܦܘܽܪܶܐ ܘܰܕ݂ܙܰܝ̈ܥܶܐ ܘܡܶܬܓܰܡܪܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ. ܐܶܠܘܽ ܠܰܡ ܐܝܺܬܶܝܗ ܗ̱ܘܳܬ ܕܺܝܰܬܝܽܩܝ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܪܶܫܝܳܢ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܓܡܝܳܪܬ݂ܳܐ܆ ܠܡܳܢܳܐ ܡܶܬܒܰܠܝܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܕܺܝܰܬܝܺܩܳܐ ܕܐܰܚܪܳܝܬܳܐ ܒܕܺܝܰܬܝܺܩܺܝܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܝܬܳܐ ܬ݁ܪܰܥ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܣܝܳܓܳܐ ܕܰܒܥܶܠܕܒܳܒܽܘܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܡܶܢ ܩܕ݂ܝܰܡ: ܐܚܺܝܕܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܕܝܢ ܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܪܶܫܝܳܢ: ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܰܒܡܶܠܬ݁ܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ
12. But all the prophets and the upright and the just who had arrived at perfection and had fallen asleep before the advent of the Lord and did not attain perfection, he perfected in the sight of the apostles, as Paul said: Without us they will not be consummated. For neither was the Paraclete sent to them, who would teach humility and charity toward all, as he was sent to the apostles; and all their days they were expecting that there would be peace in their days, and it did not happen; for through the Spirit that was in them, they knew that the Redeemer would come to pacify all things into the world. He even promised to Adam, weeping and beseeching and sighing: I will come and I will perfect those who have followed charity and perfection, from which he fell. Therefore, because there was no peace in their days, they were not perfected, because the Father and the Lord wished to effect reconciliation through the passion and cross of his Son. Even if the whole world before his advent had wished to become like Moses and Elijah, the Lord would have permitted them to be perfected, nor would it have been necessary for him to come to birth and the ignominy of the cross; and he would have pierced the wall of enmity arisen because of the transgression of the commandment, sitting in heaven in the glory of his majesty, and the prophets would have omitted the impugning of the infidels and the impious and would have escaped perfect. Nevertheless, if the first Testament had been irreprehensible, that is, perfect, why would there have been need for a second Testament? For in the newest Testament the Lord pierced the wall of ancient enmity; the ancient just indeed are irreprehensible, who walked in the word of the Lord.


[p. 365] {#po.0.p365}


[p. 366] {#po.0.p366}
ܡܗܰܠܟ݁ܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ܀ ܓܡܝܰܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܫܳܩܠܺܝܢ ܢܶܫ̈ܶܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܦܳܠܚܝܺܢ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܩܳܢܶܝܢ ܩܶܢܝܳܢܳܐ ܘܠܰܝܬ
13. But the perfect do not take wives, nor do they work on the earth, nor do they possess


[p. 367] {#po.0.p367}
ܠܗܘܢ ܡܰܥܪܳܣܳܐ ܠܪܺܝܫܳܐ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܡܰܠܦܳܢܗܘܿܢ. ܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ ܕܶܝܢ ܘܙܰܕܺܝ̈ܩܶܐ ܐܶܬ݂ܚܰܫ݁ܰܚܘ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܐܝܺܬ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕ݁ܰܡܛܰܘ ܠܰܓܡܝܳܪܘܬܳܐ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܐܶܣܬ݁ܰܪܰܩܘ ܘܐܶܬܩܰܕܰܫܘ: ܘܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܗܰܠܶܟܘ ܡܶܢܗܘܽܢ ܒܰܒܬܘܽܠܘܽܬܳܐ: ܝܰܪܰܒ݂ܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܺܐܪܰܒ݂ ܣܰܓܺܝ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܐܶܬܓܡܰܪܘ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܐܳܦ ܡܶܢ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܟܠܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܡܫܰܕܰܪ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܕܢܶܩܛܠܘܽܢ ܠܒܥܶܠܕ݁ܒܳܒܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܒܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܰܒܗܰܝܡܳܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܫܟܶܒܘ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܟ݀ܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܝܩܰܠܘ ܡܘܽܠܟܳܢܗܘܽܢ: ܘܠܰܫܠܺܝܚܶܐ ܕ݁ܝܰܬܺܝܪ ܡܶܢܗܘܿܢ ܩܰܕܶܡ ܚܙܳܐ. ܐܶܡܰܪ
wealth, nor do they have a place to rest their head on the earth, like their Doctor. But the upright and the just enjoyed the earth and sometimes arrived at perfection; when they emptied and sanctified themselves and when some of them walked in virginity, they progressed indeed exceedingly, yet they did not escape perfect; for the Lord even restrained them from justice, sending them to kill their enemies; nevertheless, all these fell asleep in justice and faith, nor did they receive their promises; and he provided for the apostles, because it is better for them. The Apostle says: Without them [the apostles], he says, they are not to be perfected. These, therefore, who died imperfect, the Lord perfected in the sight of the Apostles, because he himself restrained them from perfection. Hence, without respect of persons, he perfected them in the sight of the Apostles, and God, after they were perfect, assumed them and they appeared with him in the supernal cities,
ܟܰܕ݂ ܠܳܐ ܓܰܡܝܰܪܺܝܢ ܓܡܰܪ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܳܕ݂ܶܝܢ ܠܠܰܝܗܽܘܢ ܫܠܺܝܚܶܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܗܘ ܟܠܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܓܡܝܳܪܘܬܳܐ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܗܳܢܐ ܠܳܐ ܢܣܰܒ ܟܺܝܦܳܐ ܘܰܓܡܰܪ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܠܥܰܝܢ ܫܠܺܝܚܶܐ ܘܐܰܣܶܩ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܕܰܓܡܰܪ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ: ܘܐܶܬܚܙܺܝܘ ܥܰܡܶܗ ܒܟܰܪ̈ܟ݁ܶܐ ܥܶܠܳܝ̈ܶܐ: ܗܶܢܘܽܢ ܘܰܫܠܺܝܚܶܐ. ܫܰܪܟ݁ܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܙܰܕܺܝ̈ܩܶܐ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܟܠܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܓܡܝܰܪܘܳܬܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܕܰܟܠܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܰܢ̈ܒܺܝܶܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܗܶܢܘܽܢ ܨܒܰܝܘ ܕܰܢܩܰܘܘܽܢ ܒܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܕ݁ܝܰܘܡܳܢ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ: ܘܠܰܘ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܓܡܝܰܪ̈ܶܐ: ܕܠܳܐ ܐܶܬܓܡܰܪܘ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ ܕܰܓܡܰܪ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܫܠ̈ܝܺܚܶܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܪܳܕ݂ܶܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܗܘܽܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܚܘܽܒܳܐ ܘܒܳܬ݂ܰܪ ܓܡܝܳܪܘܽܬܳܐ܀
they and the apostles. But to the other just ones, whom the Lord did not restrain from perfection, as he restrained the prophets, but who of their own accord wished to persevere in justice, as happened to the just of today, not as to the perfect; for they are not perfect, like the prophets whom the Lord perfected together with the apostles, for they did not follow charity and perfection after their likeness.


[p. 368] {#po.0.p368}


[p. 369] {#po.0.p369}
ܫܠܺܝܚܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܟܰܕ݂ ܥܢܰܕܘ ܡܶܢ ܦܰܓܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ:ܥܰܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܗܘܰܘ: ܘܰܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܓ݁ܡܰܪ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܠܥܝ̈ܢ ܫܠܺܝܚܶܐ ܥܰܠܘ ܘܰܥܡܰܪܘ ܥܰܡܗܘܿܢ ܒܟܰܪ̈ܟܶܐ ܥܶܠܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܘܰܚܕ݂ܝܽܘ ܥܰܡ ܫܠܺܝܚܶܐ ܥܰܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܗܘ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܟܠܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܓܡܝܰܪܘܬܳܐ: ܕܗܳܟܘܳܬ݂ ܐܳܐܶܩ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܒܗܰܘ ܙܰܒܢܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܕܰܟܬܝܺܒ: ܕܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܩܝܳܡܬܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ: ܣܠܶܩܘ ܡܶܢ ܙܰܕܝܺܩܶܐ ܕܰܫܟܝܰܒܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ: ܘܐܶܬܚܙܝܽܘ ܒܥܰܪ̈ܟ݁ܶܐ ܥܶܠܳܝ̈ܶܐ. ܝܰܘܡܳܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܘܰܢ ܕ݁ܨܳܒܶܐ ܕܢܺܐܙܰܠ ܠܘܳܬ ܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܕ݁ܰܒ݁ܰܪ ܒܕܘܰܒܳܪ̈ܶܐ ܕܰܫܠܺܝܚܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܰܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ ܘܙܰܕܝܺܩ̈ܶܐ: ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܪܳܗܛܝܳܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܒܳܬ݂ܰܪ ܓܡܝܳܪܘܳܬܳܐ: ܥܰܠܝ̈ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܣܰܓܝܽ: ܡܶܢ ܕܰܓܡܰܪ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܐܰܦ݁ܶܣ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܦܳܠܚܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܝܰܘܡܳܢ ܕܐܰܝܟ ܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ ܢܶܬܕܰܒܪܘܽܢ. ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܟܬܝܺܒܳܐ ܒܐܶܘܰܢܓ݁ܶܠܰܝܘܢ: ܕܡܶܢܗܘܽܢ ܕܙܰܕ݂ܝܺܩ̈ܶܐ ܕܰܫܟܝܰܒܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܩܳܡܘ ܘܐܶܬܚܙܝܽܘ ܒܟܰܪ̈ܟ݁ܶܐ ܥܶܠܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܥܰܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ. ܘܠܳܐ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܕܟ݂ܽܠܗܘܽܢ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܦܰܓܪ̈ܶܐ ܕܟܽܠܗܘܿܢ ܙܰܕ݂ܝܺܩ݁ܶܐ ܐܰܩܝܶܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܥܶܡܗ ܡܶܢ ܒܶܝܬ ܡܝ̈ܺܬܶܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܪܳܗܛܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܓܡܝܺܪܘܽܬܳܐ: ܐܰܣܶܩ ܠܰܡܗ ܕܰܢܚܰܘܶܐ
14. But the apostles, after they had gone out from their bodies from this world, were with the Lord; and the prophets, after Jesus had perfected them in the sight of the apostles, entered and dwelt with them in the supernal cities and rejoiced with the apostles with the Lord; for the Lord himself restrained them from perfection, for at that time it was fitting, as it is written: After the resurrection of the Lord, there arose from the just who had fallen asleep, and they appeared in the supernal cities. Today, however, he who wishes to arrive at the prophets, unless he has been occupied in the conversation of the apostles, will not be as the prophets; for the Lord greatly exalted the prophets and the just who followed perfection, after he had perfected them; nor did God permit those who worship him today to converse in the manner of the prophets. But in the Gospel it is written: From the just who had fallen asleep, they arose and appeared in the supernal cities with the Lord. He does not say «all», because the Lord did not raise the bodies of all the just with him from the dead, but he assumed with him [the bodies of] those who followed perfection, about to demonstrate to the heavenly and the earthly the future resurrection and the glory prepared for the bodies and souls of all those who fell asleep in the charity of the Lord


[p. 370] {#po.0.p370}
ܠܥܶܠܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܘܰܠܬܰܚ̈ܬܳܝܶܐ ܩܝܳܡܬܳܐ ܕܰܥܬܝܺܕ݂ܳܐ: ܘܐܶܫܒܘܽܚܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܰܡܛܰܝܒܳܐ ܠܦܰܓܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܘܰܠܢܰܦ̈ܫܳܬܗܘܽܢ: ܕܟܽܠ ܕܰܫܟܶܒܘ ܘܰܕܫܳܟܟܝܺܢ ܒܚܘܽܒܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܰܕܟܽܠܗܘܿܢ ܟܳܪ̈ܘܽܙܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܩܰܕ݁̈ܡܳܝܶܐ ܘܰܐܚܪ̈ܳܝܶܐ: ܡܶܛܠ ܕܐܳܐܶܩ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܕܦܰܓܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܘܰܕ݂ܢܰܦ̈ܫܳܬܗܘܽܢ ܐܰܟܚܕ݂ܳܐ ܢܶܬܓܰܡܪܘܿܢ: ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܕܐܶܬܓܡܰܪܘ ܫܠܺܝܚܶܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܠܒܝܺܫܝܺܢ ܦܰܓܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ܀
and are falling asleep, and the glory of his first and last heralds; for it was just that their bodies and souls should be perfected together, just as the Apostles were perfected while still clothed in the body.


[p. 371] {#po.0.p371}
ܘܰܕܬܶܕ݁ܰܥ ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܐܰܡܰܪ ܦܰܘܠܘܳܣ ܕܰܠܥܺܝܢܰܝܺܢ ܡܶܬܓܰܡܪܝܺܢ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ ܘܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ ܘܙܰܕܝܺܩ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܰܥܒܰܕ݂ܘ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ ܓܡܝܳܪܳܐ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ: ܘܠܳܐ ܥܩܰܠܘ ܡܘܽܠܟܳܢܗܘܽܢ: ܐܶܡܰܪ ܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ: ܕܐܰܢܬܘܽܢ ܓܡܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܡܛܰܝܬܘܽܢ ܠܛܘܽܪܳܐ ܕܨܗܝܘܽܢ ܘܠܰܡܕܝܺܢ̱ܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܚܰܝܳܐ: ܠܐܘܪܶܫܠܶܝܡ ܕܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ: ܘܰܠܡܰܫܪ݁̈ܝܳܬܳܐ ܕܪܶܒܘܳܬܳܐ ܕܡܰܠܰܐܟ݁ܶܐ ܘܰܠܥܺܕ݂ܬܳܐ ܕܒܘܽܟܪ̈ܶܐ ܕܡܶܬܟܰܬܒܝܺܢ ܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ: ܘܠܰܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܝܳܢܳܐ ܕܟ݁ܰܠ: ܘܰܠܪ̈ܽܘܚܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ ܕܐܶܬܓܡܰܪܘ ܘܰܠܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܡܶܨܥܳܝܳܐ ܕܕܰܝܰܬܝܺܩܝܽ ܚܕ݂ܰܬܳܐ: ܘܚܰܘܝܺ ܒ݁ܝܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܕܬܳܚܠܘܽܦܳܐ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܳܦ ܠܢܰܦ̈ܫܳܬܗܘܽܢ: ܒܝܗܳܝ ܕܚܰܘܝܺ ܕܐܶܬܓܡܰܪܘ. ܘܕܥܰܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܐܝܺܬܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ ܘܰܫܠܺܝܚܶܐ ܝܰܘܡ̈ܳܢܳܝܐ. ܦ݁ܰܘܠܳܘܣ ܬܘّܒ ܐܰܘܕܰܥ: ܒܗܳܝ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܐܶܡܰܬܝ ܕܢܶܥܢܰܕ݂ ܡܶܢ ܦ݁ܰܓ݁ܪܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܢܶܗܘܶܐ: ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܐܳܬܶܐ ܗܰܘ ܝܰܘܡܳܐ ܕܕܺܝܢܳܐ: ܘܩܳܝܡܝܺܢ ܦܰܓܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܕܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܓܡܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܒܦܘܽܒܚܳܐ: ܘܡܶܬܒܰܠܥܝܺܢ ܒܢܘܽܗܪܳܐ
15. And so that it may be known to you for what reason Paul said that all the prophets and the just were perfected before our eyes, and the just who did the perfect will of God without having received their promise, he asserts thus: You, perfect ones, have arrived at Mount Sion and the city of the living God, at the heavenly Jerusalem and at the camps of myriads of angels and at the church of the firstborn, who are enrolled in the heavens, and at God, the judge of all, and the spirits of the just who are perfected, and Jesus, the mediator of the new Testament, showing that a change has been made even in their souls, in that he shows them to have been made perfect. And the same Paul indicated that the prophets and apostles are today with the Lord, saying: When we have departed from the body, we will be with the Lord, until, the day of judgment coming, the bodies of all the perfect will stand in glory and their spirits will be absorbed by their light and they will be glorified with the Lord for age upon age; for just as they suffered with him, so they will be glorified with him: if anyone, he says, suffers with him, Paul says, he will also be glorified with him, just as he was affected with contumely with him


[p. 372] {#po.0.p372}
ܕܪܘܽܚܬܗܘܿܢ. ܘܡܶܫܬܰܒ݁ܚܺܝܢ ܥܰܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܠܥܳܠܰܡ܂ ܥܳܠܡܝܢ. ܐܰܝܟ ܕ݁ܚܰܫܘ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܥܰܡܗ: ܗܳܟܰܢ ܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܒܚܝܺܢ ܥܶܡܗ: ܐܢ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܠܰܡ ܢܶܚܫܰܝܫ ܥܰܡܶܗ: ܐܶܡܺܝܪ ܦ݁ܰܘܠܳܘܣ: ܐܳܦ ܥܰܡܶܗ ܢܶܫܬܰܒ݁ܰܚ ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܕܥܰܡܶܗ ܐܶܨܛܰܥܰܪ܀ ܐܶܢ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܢܳܛܺܝܪ ܝܰܘܡܳܢ ܟܺܐܢܘܳܬܳܐ ܘܡܰܕ݂ܪܶܟ ܠܳܗ: ܡܶܬܓܰܠܝܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܡܶܐܬ݂ܝܺܬܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܗܘܳܬ: ܘܕܘܰܒܳܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܕܰܫܠܺܝܚܶܐ ܘܦܳܪܶܫ ܗܘ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܶܐ ܕܐܶܬܓܡܺܝܪܘ ܒܗܘܢ ܫܠܺܝܚܶܐ: ܘܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܐܳܦ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕ݁ܢܺܐܚܶܐ ܒܗܘܢ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ. ܘܐܶܢ ܬܘܽܒ ܐܳܬܶܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܠܗܳܠܶܝܢ
16. If anyone, however, today observes justice and has attained it, the advent of the Lord will be revealed to him, in what manner it was, and the conversation of the apostles; and the commandments being discerned by which the Apostles are perfect, he knows also those by which the world is saved. But if he still approaches those apostolic manners, he receives the Paraclete and is perfected and will go to the prophets and apostles and there will be magnified, just as here he diminished himself; and if he humbles himself still more, the Lord will appear


[p. 373] {#po.0.p373}
ܘܡܶܬܓܡܰܪ: ܘܐܳܙܶܠ ܠܘܳܬ ܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ ܘܰܫܠܺܝܚ̈ܶܐ ܘܝܳܪܶܒ݂ ܬܰܡܳܢ: ܐܰܝܟ ܡܳܐ ܕܐܰܙܥܰܪ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܗܳܪܟܳܐ: ܘܐܶܢ ܡܰܣܓܶܐ ܡܶܬܡܰܟܰܟ: ܡܶܬܓܠܶܐ ܥܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܒܗܳܢ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ. ܘܫܳܡܰܥ ܩܳܠܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܘܦܳܪܶܫ ܩܳܠܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܕܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ. ܘܡܳܐ ܕܝܺܕ݂ܰܥ ܟ݁ܽܠܶܗ ܫܪܳܪܳܐ: ܡܶܬܝܺܕ݂ܰܥ ܠܶܗ ܩܳܠܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܡܶܢ ܕܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ. ܐܶܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܡܩܰܘܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܒܗܳܝ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܩܰܕ݁̈ܡܳܝܶܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܫܳܒܶܩ ܠܳܗ ܠܰܐܪܥܳܐ ܐܰܝܟܰܢܳܐ ܕܫܰܒܩܘܽܗ ܫܠܺܝܚ̈ܶܐ ܘܨܳܡܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܠܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܟܽܠܶܗ: ܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܡܩܰܒ݁ܶܠ ܦܰܪܰܩܠܺܝܛܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬ݂ܓ݁ܠܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܟ݁ܽܠܶܗ ܫܪܳܪܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܩܳܠܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܫܳܡܰܥ ܐܰܝܟ ܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܗܘܐ ܒܶܗ ܥܘܽܪܒܳܢܳܐ ܕܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܕܩܘܽܕ݂ܫܳܐ: ܘܝܺܕ݂ܰܥ ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢ ܫܰܒܩܘܽܗ ܫܠܺܝܚܶܐ ܐܰܐܪܥܳܐ ܘܨܰܡܝܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܠܥܳܠܡܳܐ: ܘܟܶܢ ܩܰܒܶܠܘ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܦܰܪܰܩܠܺܝܛܳܐ: ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܰܓ݂ܠܳܐ ܠܗܘܿܢ ܕܶܝܢ ܦܰܪܰܩܠܺܝܛܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܕܢܰܕ݂ܪܳܟ݂. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܝܺܕ݂ܰܥ ܚܰܝܠܶܐ ܕܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܶܐ ܕܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܕܰܪܚܰܡ ܠܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܟ݂ ܡܶܢ
to him in this age; and the voice of God being heard, he distinguishes the voice of God from the voice of Satan and, the whole truth being known, he discerns the voice of the Lord from the [voice] of Satan. Nevertheless, if anyone has persevered in the justice of the ancients and has not left the earth, as the Apostles left it, fasting from the whole world, he will not be able to receive the Paraclete, nor will the whole truth be manifest to him, nor will he hear the voice of God, as the prophets, but a mixture of the holy Spirit comes to be in him, and he knows how the Apostles left the earth and fasted from the world and then received the Paraclete; but what the Paraclete revealed to them, he cannot grasp, but he knows the power of the commandments of justice: Love the Lord your God


[p. 374] {#po.0.p374}


[p. 375] {#po.0.p375}
ܟ݁ܽܠܶܗ ܠܶܒܳܟ ܘܠܰܒܢܰܚ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܢܰܦܫܳܟ: ܘܗܳܝ ܕ݁ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܰܣܢܶܐ ܥܠܰܝܟ ܠܚܰܒܪܳܟ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܥܒܶܕ݂: ܘܐܰܝܟ ܕ݁ܨܳܒܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܢܰܥܒܕܘܽܢ ܠܳܟ ܒܢܰܚ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ: ܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ ܐܳܦ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܥܒܶܕ ܠܗܘܽܢ: ܘܝܺܕ݂ܰܥ ܕܰܒ݂ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐܰܪܒ݁ܥܳܐ ܦܘܽܩܕܲܢܺܝܢ ܐܝܺܬܶܝܗ ܟ݁ܽܠܳܗ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܬܘܒ ܕܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܥܶܝܢܳܐ ܚܠܳܦ ܥܰܝܢܳܐ: ܘܒܝܺܫܬܳܐ ܚܠܳܦ ܒܝܺܫܬܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܐܶܬ݂ܡܰܪܕ݁ܳܢ:
with all your heart and men, as yourself; and what is hateful to you, do not do to your neighbor; and just as you wish that men should do to you, so also do you to them; and he knows that in these four commandments consists the whole justice; and he still knows those: an eye for an eye, evil for evil, are not said to him, nor does he do them; and having gone out in the state of justice from the world, he will be gathered to the mansion of the just.
ܘܠܳܐ ܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܠܗܶܝܢ ܘܢܳܦܶܩ ܡܶܢ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܒܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܡܶܬܟܰܢܰܫ ܠܰܐܰܬܪܳܐ ܕܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ܀ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܬܘܒ ܢܶܕ݂ܥܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ: ܕܟܽܠܶܗ ܕܰܡܡܰܠܶܠ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܥܰܡܗܘ̇ܢ ܕܰܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ ܒܗܰܘ ܙܰܒ݂ܢܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܠܳܐ ܓܡܝܺܪܝܺܢ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܗܘ ܟܠܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܓܡܝܺܪܘܽܬܳܐ ܒܗܰܘ ܙܰܒ݂ܢܳܐ: ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܕ݁ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܕܰܥܬܝܰܕܝܺܢ ܕܢܶܬܓܰܡܪܘܽܢ: ܘܥܰܡ ܫܰܪܟ݁ܳܐ ܕܙܰܕ݂ܝܺܩ̈ܶܐ. ܘܝܰܘܡܳܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܡܰܠܰܠ ܥܰܡ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܓܰܠܝܳܐܝܺܬ: ܥܰܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܓܡܝܺܪ: ܘܰܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܐܳܬܶܐ ܠܰܓ݂ܡܝܰܪܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܝܺܕ݂ܰܥ ܕܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܫܳܡܰܥ ܠܶܗ ܠܳܐ ܡܡܰܠܶܠ ܥܰܡܗ. ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܳܡܰܪ: ܕܡܰܢ ܕ݂ܪܳܚܺܝܡ ܠܺܝ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܰܝ ܢܳܛܰܪ ܘܐܶܪܚܡܝܽܘܗ̱ܝ ܕܐܶܚܰܘܶܝܘܗ̱ܝ ܢܰܦܫܝ ܘܐܶܓ݁ܠܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܥܠܺܝ ܘܢܰܕ݂ܪܶܟ ܚܰܝܠܳܐ ܕܪܳܙܰܝ ܒܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܰܢ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ ܥܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ. ܘܥܰܡ ܙܰܕ݂ܝܺܩܶܐ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܥܬܝܳܕ݂ܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܕܢܶܬܓܰܡܪܘܽܢ ܕܡܰܠܶܠ ܥܰܡܗܘܽܢ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܥܕ݂ܰܟܝܺܠ ܕ݂ܪܝܺܫܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܬ ܐܘܽܪ̈ܚܳܬܳܐ ܒܥܶܩܒܳܬܶܗ ܕ݂ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܡܶܛܽܠܗܳܢܳܐ ܡܰܠܶܠ ܥܰܡܗܘܽܢ ܒܗܰܘ ܙܰܒܢܳܐ: ܕܰܢܚܰܘܶܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܕܢܺܐܒ݂ܕܘܽܢ ܘܢܶܛܥܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕ݁ܘܳܠܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܕܰܢܗܰܠܟܘܽܢ ܒܶܗ ܒܗܰܘ ܙܰܒ݂ܢܳܐ. ܝܰܘܡܳܢ ܕܶܝܢ: ܟܬܝܺܒܝܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܕܘܰܒܳܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܕܙܰܕܝܺܩ̈ܶܐ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܥܰܝܢܰܝܢ: ܘܰܕ݂ܪܝܺܫܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ ܠܰܢ ܐܘܽܪܚܳܐ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܕܰܫܠܺܝܚܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܰܡܬܒܰܥܝܳܐ ܕܰܢܡܰܠܶܠ
17. Let this also be known to all men, that the fact that the Lord spoke at that time with the prophets, still imperfect, happened because at that time he himself restrained them from perfection, although he knew them to be ready to be perfected and with the rest of the just. And that today he speaks with no one openly: because he is not perfect; and until he arrives at perfection, knowing that he cannot hear him, he does not speak with him, as he said: He who loves me, keeps my commandments; and I will love him and I will manifest myself to him and I will reveal to him about me and he will grasp the power of my mysteries, because I will appear to him. But that he spoke with the just, who were not ready to be perfected: because the way was not yet manifest in the footsteps of the Lord; wherefore at that time he spoke with them, so that he might show them, lest they should perish or wander from the way in which it behooved them to walk at that time. Today, however, the conversation of the just is written before our eyes and the way of the Lord and the apostles is manifest, nor is it necessary for God to speak openly with anyone, unless it be just that God should call him to his way. Otherwise, until one coming enters into the commandments of the Lord and walks in them and, going, arrives at the house of the Lord, like the son who dissipated his substance: then going out to meet him, he receives him as the clement father received his repentant son.


[p. 376] {#po.0.p376}


[p. 377] {#po.0.p377}
ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܓ݁ܰܠܝܳܐܝܺܬ ܥܳܐܶܠ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܢܗܘ ܕܙܳܪܶܩ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܢܶܩܪܶܝܘܗ̱ܝ ܠܐܘܽܪܚܶܗ. ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܶܝܢ: ܕܐܳܬܶܐ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܥܳܐܶܠ ܠܦܘܽܩܕ݂ܳܢܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܪܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܒܗܽܘܢ ܘܰܡܡܰܢܰܥ ܕܢܶܡܛܶܐ ܠܒܺܝܬ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܗܰܘ ܒܪܳܐ ܕܦܰܚܙܰܚ ܢܶܟܣܰܝܘܽܗ̱ܝ: ܗܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܢܳܦܶܩ ܠܐܘܽܪܥܶܗ ܘܰܡܩܰܒܶܠ ܠܶܗ: ܐܰܝܟ ܐܰܒ݁ܳܐ ܒ݁ܰܣܚܺܝܡܳܐ ܕܩܰܒܶܠ ܠܰܒܪܶܗ ܐܰܝܳܒܳܐ܀ ܡܢ ܕܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܢܶܫܡܰܥ ܡܶܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܗܘ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܩܳܪܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܕܢܶܥܘܽܠ ܠܐܘܽܪܚܶܗ: ܘܡܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܨܶܐ ܕܢܶܫܡܰܥ ܡܶܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܒ݁ܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܰܓܡܺܝܪ ܡܚܰܘܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܐܘܽܪܚܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ. ܐܶܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܨܶܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܕܢܶܫܡܰܥ ܡܶܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܡܶܢ ܪܺܝܫ ܬܘܽܠܡܳܕ݁ܶܗ ܓ݁ܳܠܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܪܳܙܶܗ: ܘܐܶܢ ܐܰܘܚܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܐܶܬܓܠܝّ ܠܶܗ: ܢܺܕ݂ܰܥ ܕܡܶܢ ܒ݁ܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܕܰܡܫܰܡܠܰܝ ܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܕܢܶܫܡܰܥ ܫܪܳܪܳܐ. ܘܐܝܺܬ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܕܗܘ ܡܶܢ ܨܒܘܽܬ ܢܰܦ݂ܫܶܗ ܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܫܳܡܰܥ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܡܶܢ ܨܘܳܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܰܕ݂ܝܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܡܶܬܡܰܟܰܟ ܘܩܳܪܶܐ ܠܳܗ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ: ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܥܳܢܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܘܰܡܚܰܘܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ ܓܡܺܝܪܳܐ ܘܰܡܩܰܒܠܳܐ. ܠܰܘ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ
18. But he who can hear the Lord, the Lord himself calls him, so that he may enter his way; but he who cannot hear the Lord, the perfect man of the Lord shows him the way of the Lord. If, however, he can hear the Lord, from the beginning of his discipleship he shows him his truth; but if he makes delay and does not appear to him: let it be known to him that he can hear the truth from a perfect man. There is one who of his own accord can hear the words of the Lord from the characters of ink and, humbled, invokes the Lord Jesus, until the Lord answers him and shows what his perfect and acceptable will is. For not everyone is capable of being called by God, nor can everyone

[p. 379] {#po.0.p379}
ܟ݁ܽܠܢܳܫ ܣܳܦܶܩ ܕܡܶܢ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܢܶܬܩܪܶܐ: ܘܠܰܘ ܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܕ݁ܡܶܢ ܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܢܶܫܡܰܥ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܟܬܝܺܒ: ܕܐܝܺܬ ܡܗܰܝܡܰܢܶܐ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܩܪܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܘܰܥܒܰܕ݂ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ. ܘܐܝܺܬ ܕܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܩܪܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܐܝܺܬ ܕܗܳܢܘܽܢ ܐܶܬܡܰܟ݁ܰܟܘ ܘܰܒܥܰܘ ܘܐܶܬܚܰܕ݂ܰܬܘ ܒܡܘܽܟܳܟܗܘܽܢ: ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܣܦ݁ܰܩܘ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܐܬܓܠܝّ ܥܠܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܘܚܰܘܝܽ ܠܗܘܢ ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ ܡܩܰܒܠܳܐ ܘܰܓܡܺܝܪܳܐ. ܘܰܕܗܳܟ݁ܰܢ ܙܕ݁ܶܩ ܕܒܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܪܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝ ܒܐܘܽܪܚܳܐ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ: ܐܰܘ ܒܚܰܕ݂ ܩܪܳܝܬܳܐ ܕܒܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܒܝܰܕ݂ ܡܘܽܟܳܟܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܩܢܘܽܡܶܗ ܕܒܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܘܟܶܢ ܡܶܬ݂ܓ݁ܠܶܐ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܥܠܰܝܘܗ̱ܝ: ܓܰܠܝܳܐܝܺܬ ܕܰܘܝܺܕ݂ ܦܰܫܶܩ: ܕܐܶܗܰܠܶܟ݂ ܒܐܘܽܪܚܳܟ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܘܽܡ ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܬ݂ܺܐܬܶܐ ܠܘܳܬܝ܆ ܘܐܘܰܒ ܐܳܡܰܪ: ܕ݁ܨܰܗܝܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ ܠܳܟ݂ ܢܰܦܫܝ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܚܰܝܳܐ. ܕܐܶܡܰܬܝ ܐܬܶܐ ܘܐܶܚܙܶܐ ܐܰܦܰܝ̈ܟ݁. ܘܡܢ ܕܪܳܚܺܝܡ ܠܝ ܦܘܽܩܕ݂ܳܢܰܝ̈ ܢܳܛܰܪ ܘܐܳܬܶܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܨܶܐܕ݁ܰܘܗ̱ܝ: ܐܳܢܳܐ ܘܐܰܒܳܐ ܘܪܘܽܚ ܩܘܽܕܫܳܐ. ܚܳܙܶܐ ܐ݇ܢܬ ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢ ܐܳܙܠ̱ܝܢ ܬܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܓܰܕ̈ܶܫܐ ܚܰܕ݂ ܠܘܳܬ ܚܰܕ: ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܥܳܒܰܪ ܪܶܥܝܳܢܶܗ ܕܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܡܶܢ ܐܰܬܪܳܐ ܕܒܝܺܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܡܳܛܶܐ ܠܰܐܰܬ݂ܪܳܐ ܕܫ̈ܰܝܢܳܐ ܕܰܪܶܐ ܒܶܗ ܡܳܪܰܢ. ܘܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܕܰܫܒܰܩ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܒܪܳܐ ܠܗܰܘ ܐܰܬܪܳܐ ܕ݂ܪܳܥܶܐ ܙܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܒܶܗ ܚܙܝܰܪ̈ܶܐ: ܘܟܶܢ ܟܰܕ݂ ܡܛܳܐ ܒܶܝܬ ܐܰܒ݂ܘܽܗ̱ܝ: ܢܦܰܩ ܐܰܒܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܠܐܘܽܪܥܶܗ ܘܩܰܒܠܶܗ: ܗܳܟܰܢ ܡܳܐ ܕܫܰܒܩܳܗ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܠܰܐܪܥܳܐ ܒܪܶܥܝܳܢܶܗ ܕܐܝܺܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܐܰܬܪܳܐ ܕ݂ܪܳܥܶܐ ܒܶܝܗ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܒܚܺܦ̈ܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܒܰܕ̈ܓܝܺܓ݂ܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܣܳܥܰܪ ܘܟܳܦܶܢ ܠܰܡ ܠܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܰܠܩܰܕ݂ܝܺܫܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܝܳܗܶܒ ܠܶܗ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܪܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܪܶܥܝܳܢܶܗ ܣܳܠܳܩ ܠܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ: ܐܰܬ݁ܪܳܐ ܡܫܰܝܢܐ ܕܒܶܝܬ ܐܰܒܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܕܐܰܓܝܪ̈ܶܐ ܡܰܘܬܪܝܺܢ ܬܰܡܳܢ ܟܰܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܫܰܦܝܳܪ̈ܬܳܐ. ܗܳܟܰܢ ܡܳܐ ܕܰܪܕܳܐ ܘܰܡܛܳܐ ܬܰܡܳܢ ܬܰܝܳܒܳܐ ܒܪܶܥܝܳܢܶܗ: ܢܳܦ݁ܶܩ ܠܐܘܽܪܥܶܗ ܚܢܳܢܳܐ ܘܐܳܡܰܪ: ܗܳܢܳܐ ܒ̇ܪܝ ܢܦ݁ܰܩ ܡܶܢ ܠܘܳܬܝ ܘܰܛܥܶܡ ܘܰܡܘܬܳܐ ܘܗܳܦܶܟ݂ ܚܰܝܳܐ ܘܐܶܬܳܐ. ܗܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܣܰܒܰܥ ܠܶܗ ܩܰܕ݂ܝܺܫܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܰܟ݂ܦܶܢ ܠܳܗ: ܘܰܡܥܰܛܶܦ݂ ܠܶܗ ܓܡܺܝܪܘܳܬܳܐ ܐܶܣܛܳܠܳܐ ܪܝܺܫܳܝܬ݁ܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܪܓ݁ܳܐ ܥܶܠܳܝܳܐ: ܘܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܩܳܐܶܡ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܒܰܦܔܰܪ: ܘܰܡܡܰܠܶܠ ܐܳܡܳܢ ܥܰܡܶܗ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܗܘ ܐܰܒ݁ܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܒܪܶܗ ܘܗܳܘܶܐ ܡܦܰܪܢܳܣ ܠܰܐ݇ܚܪ̈ܳܢܶܐ ܥܘܺܬܪܳܐ ܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܐ ܡܶܐܟܘܽܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܕ݂ܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܚܠܳܦ ܕܚܳܡܶܡܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܗܳܪܟܳܐ ܠܟܰܦܢܶܗ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܒܚܕ ܒܶܣܪܳܢܳܐ ܘܚܳܐܰܪ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܒܠܳܐ ܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܦܪܳܪܳܐ ܕܒܳܥܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܕܢܽܘܒܠܶܐ ܟܰܪܣܺܝܗ ܗܳܪܟܳܐ ܚܰܝ̈ܫܶܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܝܳܗܶܒ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕܶܝܢ ܒܺܝܥܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܕܢܺܝܕ݂ܰܥ: ܐܳܦܶܢ ܬܪܺܝܨܽܘܬܶܗ ܕܗܳܢܳܐ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ: ܐܰܘ ܕܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܒܳܥܶܐ: ܘܥܰܠ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܐܶܬܒܪܺܝ ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܥܒܶܕ ܥܰܒܕ݂ܳܐ ܠܰܚܛܺܝܬܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܓ݁ܳܠܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ. ܘܗܰܘ ܕܗܳܝܕ݂ܶܝܢ ܟܰܦܶܢ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܫܳܬܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܡܶܕ݂ܶܡ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ: ܗܳܐ ܡܰܠܶܦ ܠܰܐܚܪ̈ܳܢܐ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܠܳܐ
hear the Spirit: therefore it is written: There are eunuchs, whom the Lord has called and made, and there are those whom the man of the Lord calls, and there are those who have humbled themselves and boldly asked in their humility, until they have become fit for the Lord and he has revealed himself to them and shown what his well-pleasing and perfect will is. And that this is so, that the man first runs in the way of the Lord, whether through the invitation of a man, or through the humiliation of his human hypostasis, and then the Lord manifests himself to him, David clearly explained: I will walk in your way blameless: until when will you come to me? And again he said: My soul has thirsted for you, the living God: when shall I come and see your face? And, he who loves me, keeps my commandments; and I will come to him, I and the Father and the holy Spirit. You see for what reason one part approaches the other, until the mind of man departs from the place of iniquity and arrives at the mansion of peace, where the Lord dwells. And just as the son left the place where he was feeding pigs and then, after he had arrived at the house of his father, the Father meeting him embraced him: so man, having left the earth with his mind (that place where man feeds evil things through desires, which he delivers to effect), hungers, he says, for justice and holiness and no one gives to him, unless his mind sets out and ascends to heaven, the peaceful place, the house of the Father, where the hired laborers earn justice and decorations. Similarly, after the penitent has set out with his mind and arrived there, mercy meets him saying: This son of mine went out from me and tasted death and now he has come alive. Then he satisfies him with the holiness for which he hungered, and puts on him perfection, the best robe of a sublime degree, and, while he remains in the body on the earth, his mind daily dwells spiritually in heaven and there the Lord speaks with him, just as that father with his son, and he [also] ministers to others heavenly riches, spiritual food, as his hunger has heated up here, while, having become carnal due to the defect of knowledge and truth, he was looking at the earth, and wishing to fill his belly with life, nor did anyone give to him; this is: he wished to know at least the right reason of this world, or how it was created and why it was created and why he was made a servant of sin, nor did anyone reveal it to him. And this one, who afterwards was hungry and had nothing (this is: he knew nothing), behold, he teaches others what they did not perceive,
