[p. 381] {#po.0.p381}


[p. 382] {#po.0.p382}


[p. 383] {#po.0.p383}
ܪܓܺܝܫܺܝܢ: ܘܡܰܡܦܶܐ ܠܗܘܿܢ ܠܒܺܝܫܰܝ̈ ܚܰܝ̈ܶܐ܀
and leads them back to the house of life.
ܐܶܢ ܗܳܟܝܺܠ ܐܝܺܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܒܙܘܽܘܳܓ݂ܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܐܝܺܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܒܟܺܐܢܘܽܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܟܺܐ̈ܢܶܐ: ܗܳܘܶܐ ܒܗ ܥܘܽܪܒ݁ܳܢܳܐ ܕܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܕܩܘܽܕ݂ܫܳܐ: ܘܐܶܢ ܡܶܬܥܰܠܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܙܘܽܘܳܓܿܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܐܝܺܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܒܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܬܘܒ ܝܳܬܶܪ ܡܶܢ ܙܘܽܘܳܓ݁ܳܐ. ܘܐܶܢܗܘ̈ ܕܐܶܬܥܰܠܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܙܘܽܘܳܓܿܳܐ ܢܶܬܥܰܠܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܫܰܘܬܳܦܘܽܬܳܐ ܠܕܘܽܒܳܪ̈ܶܐ ܕܰܫܠܺܝ̈ܚܶܐ: ܣܰܓܝܺ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܡܶܬܓ݂ܰܡܪܰ ܘܰܡܩܰܒܶܠ ܦܰܪܰܩܠܺܝܛܳܐ ܘܫܳܡܰܥ ܩܳܠܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ. ܘܐܶܢ ܒܬܘܽܠܘܽܬܳܐ ܬ݁ܺܐܬ݁ܶܐ ܠܕܘܽܒܳܪ̈ܶܐ ܕܰܫܠܺܝ̈ܚܶܐ: ܣܰܓܝܽ ܡܝܰܬܪܳܐ ܘܰܡܩܰܒܠܳܐ ܦܰܪܰܩܠܺܝܛܳܐ ܘܡܶܬܓ݂ܰܡܪܳܐ ܘܫܳܡܥܳܐ ܩܳܠܶܗ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ. ܘܐܶܢ ܡܶܬܩܰܕ݂ܰܫ ܙܘܽܘܳܓ݂ܳܐ ܘܡܶܬܡܰܟ݁ܰܟ݂ ܣܰܓܝܰ ܡܶܢ ܒܬܘܽܠܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܦܰܓ݁ܪܳܐ: ܝܳܬܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܡܶܢܳܗ: ܘܐܳܢܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܩܰܠܺܝܠ ܩܳܕ݁ܶܡ ܠܳܗ ܒܚܕܳܐ: ܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܳܗ. ܐܶܢܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܒܬܘܽܠܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܦܰܓ݁ܪܳܐ ܬܶܗܘܶܐ ܒܪܘܰܚ ܘܐܶܣܬ݁ܰܪܰܩ ܘܐܶܬܡܰܟ݁ܰܟ݂ ܝܰܬܝܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܟ݁ܽܠ: ܠܰܝܬ ܕܩܳܕ݁ܶܡ ܠܳܗ ܡܶܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܙܘܽܘܳܓܿܳܐ ܕܐܰܟ݂ܘܳܬܳܗ ܐܶܬܡܰܟ݁ܰܟ݂ ܘܐܶܬܩܰܕ݂ܰܫ ܒܪܘܰܚ ܐܳܙܶܠ ܨܶܐܕܶܝܗ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܡܳܐܶܟ݂ ܡܶܢܳܗ܀
19. If anyone, therefore, joined in marriage, dwells in the justice of the just, a mixture of the holy Spirit comes to be in him; and if he transcends marriage, remaining in the justice of the just, he will be still greater than marriage. But if anyone, receding from marriage, raises himself to the conversation of the Apostles, he is greatly perfected and, the Paraclete being received, he hears the voice of God. And if virginity has arrived at the apostolic conversation, it excels greatly and, the Paraclete being received, it is perfected and hears the voice of God. And if marriage has been sanctified and has humbled itself more than bodily virginity, the former will be greater; but if it has preceded it somewhat in humility, it will be as the latter. If, however, bodily virginity has become spiritual and has emptied and humbled itself below all things, no one will precede it among men, but marriage, humbled after its likeness and sanctified by the spirit, approaches it, although it is inferior to it.


[p. 384] {#po.0.p384}


[p. 385] {#po.0.p385}
ܐܶܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܶܬܚܙܶܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܡܶܢ ܕ݁ܰܪܓ݁ܳܐ ܥܶܠܳܝܳܐ ܒܗܰܘ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ: ܒܶܝܬ ܕ݁ܳܪ̈ܓ݁ܶܐ ܕܰܠܬܰܚܬ ܡܶܢܶܗ: ܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܒܥܰܝܢܰܘܗ̱ܝ. ܘܐܶܢ ܡܶܢ ܙܥܘܽܪܶܐ ܢܶܬܚܙܶܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܠܘܳܬ ܥܶܠܳܝ̈ܶܐ: ܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܒܰܝܢ̈ܳܬܗܘܽܢ. ܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܒܐܰܬܪܳܐ ܕܛܰܝܶܒ ܠܶܗ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܐܰܟ ܡܰܫܘܽܚܬܶܗ ܦܰܩܳܚ ܠܶܗ ܕܢܶܬܟܰܬܰܫ ܠܡܰܛܰܪ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܶܐ: ܕܢܺܐܪܰܒ݂ ܒܥܰܝܢܰܝ ܪܰܘܪ̈ܒ݁ܶܐ ܒܥܳܠܡܶܗ
20. If anyone, however, in that age were to appear from a more sublime degree among the inferior degrees, it would be as if they were nothing in comparison to him. And if anyone from the lesser were to appear among the more sublime, it would be as if he were nothing among them. It is expedient for each one that, in the place prepared for him by the Lord according to his measure, he should strive to observe the commandments, so that he may grow in the eyes of the greater in the new age of the Lord Jesus Christ, the king of all ages. To him be glory. Amen.


[p. 386] {#po.0.p386}
ܚܰܕ݂ܬܳܐ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܡܫܺܝܚܳܐ ܡܰܠܟܳܐ ܕ݁ܟܽܠ ܥܳܠܡ̈ܶܝܢ. ܠܶܗ ܬܶܫܒܘܽܚܬܳܐ ܐܰܡܺܝܢ܀ ܫܠܶܡ ܡܐܡܪܳܐ ܕܚܰܡܫܰܬܥܣܰܪ: ܕܥܰܠ ܘܰܪܕܝܺܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܙܘܽܘܳܓ݂ܳܐ܀
The fifteenth discourse on the instinct of coitus ends.


[p. 387] {#po.0.p387}

### SIXTEENTH DISCOURSE
ܡܐܡܪܳܐ ܕܬܰܫܬܰܥܣܰܪ: ܕܥܰܠ ܕ݁ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܝܳܪܶܒ݂ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܡܶܢ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܶܐ ܪܰܘܪ̈ܒ݁ܶܐ. ܥܰܠ ܕܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢ ܝܳܪܶܒ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܡܶܢ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܶܐ ܪܰܘܪ̈ܒ݁ܶܐ ܒܚܘܰܒܳܐ: ܐܶܢ ܨܳܒܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕ݁ܬܶܫܡܰܥܰܝܢܝ: ܘܐܶܢܳܐ ܡܚܰܘܶܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܠܳܟ ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܝܳܪܶܒ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܘܡܶܬܡܰܠܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܐܳܦ݂ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܶܐ ܪܰܘܪ̈ܒܳܐ. ܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܳܟ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕܡܰܢ ܕܡܳܚܶܐ ܠܳܟ ܥܰܠ ܦܰܟܳܟ: ܩܰܪܶܒ ܠܶܗ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܢܳܐ: ܗܰܒ ܠܶܗ ܬܘܒ ܟܠܶܗ ܓܘܽܫܡܳܟ ܘܗܳܐ ܝܺܪܰܒܬ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܕܦܰܟܶܗ ܗܘܽ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܝܳܗܶܒ. ܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܳܟ ܕܡܰܢ ܕ݁ܰܡܫܰܚܰܪ ܠܳܟ ܡܺܝܠ ܚܰܕ݂: ܙܶܠ ܥܶܡܗ ܬܪ̈ܶܝܢ ܐ̱ܚܪ̈ܳܢܺܝ̈ܢ: ܙܶܠ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܚܰܬܝܺܪ ܥܰܠ ܕܐ݀ܡܰܪ ܠܳܟ: ܘܗܳܐ ܝܺܪܶܒܬ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܕ݁ܐܳܙܶܠ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܬܦܰܩܰܕ݂. ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܳܟ ܕܰܢܒܘܽܩ ܠܶܗ ܫܰܒܥܺܝܢ ܥܰܠ ܫܒܰܥ ܠܡܰܣܟܠܳܢܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܶܬܒ݂ܰܥ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܣܰܟܠܘܽܬܳܐ ܟܽܠ ܟ݁ܽܠܳܗ ܘܗܳܐ ܝܺܪܰܒܬ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܕܫܰܒܥܺܝܢ ܥܰܠ ܫܒܰܥ ܫܒܰܩ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂. ܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܳܟ ܕܠܳܐ ܬܕܘܽܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܬܶܬܕܺܝܢ: ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܦ݁ܰܪܣܶܐ ܠܰܐܚܘܽܟ: ܘܗܳܐ ܝܺܪܰܒܬ ܐܳܦ݂ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܕܦܰܟܶܗ ܗܘܽ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܝܳܗܶܒ. ܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܳܟ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܶܩܪܶܐ ܪܰܝܩܳܐ ܘܫܳܛܝܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܣܰܢܝܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܣܰܟܠܳܐ: ܕܠܳܐ ܐܶܬܚܰܝܰܒ ܠܓ݂ܺܗܰܢܳܐ. ܡܰܢ ܕܩܳܪܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܪܰܝܩܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܪܰܩܳܐ ܡܚܰܝܰܒ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܝܰܘܡܳܐ ܟ݁ܽܠܶܗ ܠܰܟܢܘܽܫܬܳܐ. ܥܰܠ ܕܰܩܪܳܐ ܪܰܝܩܳܐ ܠܰܐܚܘܽܗ̱ܝ: ܗܘܳܐ ܪܰܝܩܳܐ ܟ݁ܽܠܳܗ ܚܰܝܘܽܬܳܐ. ܒܗܰܘ ܕܕܺܝܢܳܐ ܕܕܳܝܰܢ ܐ݇ܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ: ܡܶܬܬܕܝܺܢܝܺܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ. ܘܐܶܢ ܩܳܪܶܐ ܠܰܡܚܳܪ: ܗܳܟܰܢ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܪܰܝܩܳܐ: ܘܐܶܢ ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܢܳܦܶܩ ܡܶܢ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܩܳܪܶܐ: ܚܰܣܺܝܪ ܪܶܥܝܳܢܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ: ܘܠܳܐ ܩܳܢܶܐ ܪܶܥܝܳܢܳܐ ܡܰܠܝܳܐ ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܢܶܥܩܘܽܪ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܒܘܽܨܳܪܶܐ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ܀
ON THE MANNER BY WHICH A MAN BECOMES GREATER THAN THE GREAT COMMANDMENTS. 1. As regards the question of how one might become greater than the great commandments, if you are willing to listen to me, I will show you how you may become greater and more sublime than the great commandments themselves. The Lord said to you: 'Whoever strikes you on your cheek, offer him the other': give him your whole body, and behold, you will be greater than he who offers only the cheek. He said to you: 'Whoever compels you to go a thousand paces, go with him another two'; go further than He told you, and behold, you have become greater than he who goes as he is commanded. And He said to you: 'Forgive the one who sins seventy times seven'; do not seek retribution for the offense at all, and behold, you have become greater than he who forgives only seventy times seven. He said to you: 'Do not judge, so that you may not be judged'; but you, do not slander your brother, and behold, you have become greater than he [who judges his brother and slanders him]. For He said to you: 'Do not call anyone a fool, a blockhead, an abominable one, or a simpleton, lest you be condemned to Gehenna'; but whoever calls someone 'fool' or 'blockhead' will be liable to the council all day long. Whoever calls his brother 'empty' will be empty all day long. With the same judgment with which you judge, you will be judged. And if he calls him so on the morrow, he will be empty in the same way; and if he continues to call him so until he departs from the world, he is mindless, nor will he possess full reason until he eradicates those defects, as the Lord said.


[p. 388] {#po.0.p388}


[p. 389] {#po.0.p389}


[p. 390] {#po.0.p390}
ܦܫܚܺܚܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܣܰܟܠܘܽܬܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܣܰܟܠܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܓ݁ܺܗܰܢܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܓ݁ܺܗܰܢܳܐ. ܟ݁ܽܠ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܐܰܝܟ ܥܒܳܕ݂ܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܡܶܬܬܕܝܺܢ. ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܩܪܝܿ ܠܰܐܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܰܟܘܳܝ̈ܟ: ܐܚܝ ܘܚܳܬܝ: ܘܠܰܐܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܰܛܠܶܝܢ ܡܶܢܳܟ: ܒܶܪܝ ܘܒܰܪܬܝ: ܘܠܰܐܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܩܰܫܝܺܫܺܝܢ ܡܶܢܳܟ: ܐܳܒ݂ܝܿ ܘܐܶܡܝ: ܘܠܰܐܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܟܳܗ̈ܢܶܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ: ܡܳܪ̈ܰܝ ܘܦܰܛܪ̈ܘܳܢܰܝ: ܘܰܠܩܰܕ̈ܝܺܫܶܐ ܘܰܠܩܰܕ̈ܝܺܫܳܬ݁ܳܐ: ܡܳܪ̈ܰܝ ܘܡܳܪ̈ܳܬܝ. ܘܰܠܡܰܢ ܕ݁ܐܝܺܩܳܪܳܐ ܐܝܺܩܳܪܳܐ: ܘܰܠܡܰܢ ܕܚܘܽܒܳܐ ܚܘܽܒܳܐ: ܘܰܠܡܰܢ ܕܕ݂ܶܚܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܶܚܠܬܳܐ:
2. One offense is lighter than another, and one Gehenna than another. Each is judged according to his works. But you, call your equals 'brother' and 'sister', those younger than you in age 'son' and 'daughter', those older than you 'father' and 'mother', and those who are priests 'my lords and patrons', and the holy men and women 'my masters and mistresses'. And to whom honor is due, give honor; and to whom love is due, give love;


[p. 391] {#po.0.p391}
ܒܐܝܺܩܳܪܳܐ ܘܒܰܚܦܝܺܛܘܽܬܳܐ. ܘܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܥܶܠ ܡܶܢ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܳܐ ܘܰܐܚܪܳܝܳܐ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕܶܝܢ ܥܰܡ ܡܳܪܗܘܽܢ ܕܢܳܡܘ̈ܣܶܐ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ. ܐܶܢ ܕܶܝܢ ܩܳܪܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܐܳܚܝ ܘܚܳܬܝ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕ݁ܰܒܐܰܚܳܐ ܘܰܒܚܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܚܘܽܪ ܒܶܗ: ܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܕ݂ܰܓ݁ܶܠ ܒܡܶܠܬܳܟ݂. ܠܳܐ ܫܰܠܝܶܛ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܬܰܒܶܐܫ ܠܶܗ ܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܡܰܒܶܐܫ ܠܳܟ. ܘܐܶܢ ܛܳܥܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܗܽܘ: ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܛܥܶܐ ܕܐܳܚܘܽܟ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܒܚܘܽܒܳܐ. ܘܗܰܘ ܕܩܳܪܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܶܗ ܡܳܪܝ ܘܡܳܪܬ݁ܝ: ܐܶܬܕܰܟܪ ܕܥܰܒܕ݁ܶܗ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܒܨܶܒܝܳܢܳܟ: ܐܶܢ ܡܰܒ݁ܶܐܫ ܠܳܟ݂: ܠܳܐ ܬܩܘܽܡ ܠܩܘܽܒܠܶܗ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕ݁ܰܠܡܳܪܳܐ ܣܰܝܒܪܳܝܗ̱ܝ. ܘܗܰܘ ܡܰܢ ܕ݁ܩܳܪܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܶܗ ܒܪܝ ܘܒܰܪܬܝ: ܐܶܬܕܰܟܪ ܕܰܒܢܰܝ̈ܟ݂ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܒܪ̈ܰܚܡܶܐ: ܪܰܒܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܘܐܰܟܶܦ ܥܠܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܘܰܪܚܶܡ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܟܡܐ ܕܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ: ܘܐܶܢ ܛܳܥܶܝܢ ܗܶܢܘܽܢ ܕܰܒ̈ܢܰܝܟ݂ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ: ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܛܥܶܐ ܕܰܒܢܰܝ̈ܟ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܬܰܗܡܶܐ ܡܶܢܗܘܽܢ. ܘܗܰܘ ܕܩܳܪܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܶܗ ܡܳܪܝ ܘܦܰܛܪܘܽܢܝ: ܐܶܬܕܰܟܪ ܕܰܡܩܰܪܶܒ ܩܘܽܪ̈ܒܳܢܶܐ ܘܰܨܠܰܘܳܬܳܐ ܚܠܳܦܰܝܟ ܘܰܚܠܳܦ ܟ݁ܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ: ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܥܒܳܕܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ ܐܶܫܬܰܝܰܬ݁ܘ ܥܰܡܗܘܽܢ ܘܐܶܫܬ݁ܰܥܒ݁ܰܕ݂ܘ ܠܗܘܽܢ܀
and to whom fear is due, give fear, with the honor and solicitude by which you will be above the first and the last law; that is, you will be with the Lord of the laws. But if you call someone brother and sister, consider him as a brother and sister; do not refute your own words: it is not permitted for you to do evil, even if he has done evil to you! And if he forgets, do not you forget that he is your brother by the power of charity. And whom you call 'lord' or 'lady', remember that you have voluntarily become their servant; if they do evil to you, do not resist them, but endure them as your lord. And those whom you call 'son' or 'daughter', remember that they are your children by the power of love; educate them and attend to them and love them as you are able; and if they forget that they are your children, do not you forget that they are children to you, nor neglect them. And whom you call 'my lord and patron', remember that he offers oblations and prayers for you and for all men; and because of their works, have peace with them and be subject to them.


[p. 392] {#po.0.p392}
ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܬܘܽܒ: ܕܐܶܡܰܬܝ ܕ݁ܰܡܨܰܠܶܝܢ ܐܵܢ̱ܬܘܵܢ ܐܶܡܰܪܘ: ܐܰܒܘܽܢ ܕܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ: ܢܫܒܘܽܩ ܠܰܢ ܚܰܘܒܰܝ̈ܢ ܐܵܦ ܚܢܵܢ ܫܒܰܩܢ ܠܚܰܝܳܒܰܝ̈ܢ. ܫܒܘܽܩ ܠܶܗ ܠܚܘܽܟ݂ ܘܟܶܢ ܬܰܠܶܐ: ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܒܰܨܠܘܽܬܳܟ: ܫܒܘܽܩ ܠܝ ܡܳܪܝ: ܕܐܶܢܳܐ ܫܰܒܩܶܬ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܚܰܝܳܒ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܝ ܘܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܫܒܘܽܩ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܕܐ݂ܰܣܟ݁ܶܠܘ ܒܝ: ܘܒܳܥܳܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܡܳܢܳܟ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܒܰܪܝܺܬ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܕܪܶܓ݂ܙܶܬ݂ ܡܶܪܓܰܙ: ܘܗܳܟܰܢ ܗܳܘܳܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܥܶܠ ܡܶܢ ܦܘܽܩܕܳܢܶܐ ܪܰܘܪ̈ܒ݁ܶܐ ܘܕܰܩܕ݁̈ܩܶܐ ܘܰܠܥܶܠ ܡܶܢ ܐ݈ܘܳܪܺܝܬܳܐ ܘܰܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ: ܘܡܰܕܪܶܟ݂ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܕ݂ܘܰܒܳܪ̈ܰܘܗ̱ܝ: ܕܰܒܗܘܽܢ ܐܳܙܶܠ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܘܳܬܶܗ ܘܰܠܘܳܬ ܫܠܺܝܚܰܘܽܗ̱ܝ. ܐܶܢܬ ܕܶܝܢ: ܐܶܢ ܡܳܛܶܐ ܐܰܢ݈ܬ݁ ܠܗܘܢ ܠܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܶܐ ܪܰܘܪ̈ܒܿܶܐ: ܦܫܺܝܩ ܗ̱ܘ ܠܳܟ ܕܬܶܥܒܰܪ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܠܥܶܠ. ܐܶܢ ܕܝܢ ܟܳܠܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܗܳܝ ܕܙܰܩܳܐ: ܒܰܪ ܫܳܥܬ݂ܶܗ ܩܳܪܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܐܳܚܝ: ܘܐܶܢ ܟܳܠܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܗܳܝ ܕܣܰܟܠܳܐ ܒܰܪ ܫܳܥܬ݁ܶܗ ܩܳܪܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܒܶܪܝ: ܘܐܶܢ ܟܳܠܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܗܳܝ ܕ݂ܫܶܛܝܳܐ: ܦܫܺܝܩ ܠܟ ܕܬ݂ܶܩܪܶܐ ܚܰܒܝܒܝ: ܘܐܶܢ ܫܳܒܶܩ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܫܰܒܥܝܺܢ ܥܰܠ ܫܰܒܥ: ܦܫܺܝܩ ܠܳܟ ܕܟܠ ܘܽܠܳܗ ܬܶܫܒܘܽܩ: ܘܐܶܢ ܡܶܬܪܰܥܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܘܟܶܢ ܡܨܰܠܶܐ ܐܰܢ݈ܬ: ܦܫܺܝܩ ܠܳܟ ܕܠܳܐ ܬܘܒ ܬܶܪܔ݁ܰܝܙ: ܘܐܶܢ ܡܫܺܝܓ ܐܰܢܬ ܪ̈ܶܓܠܶܐ ܕܰܒܥܶܠܕܒܳܒܰܝ̈ܟ݂: ܦܫܺܝܩ ܠܳܟ ܕܰܬܢܰܫܶܩ ܐܶܢܶܝܢ: ܘܐܶܢ ܝܳܗܶܒ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܦܰܟܳܟ: ܦܫܺܝܩ ܠܳܟ ܕ݁ܬ݂ܶܬܶܠ ܟ݁ܽܠܶܗ ܓܘܽܫܡܳܟ: ܘܐܶܢ ܐܳܙܶܠ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܬܪܶܝܢ ܡܝܠܺܝܢ: ܐܳܦ݂ ܟ݁ܡܳܐ ܕܨܳܒܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܐܳܙܶܠ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ: ܘܐܶܢ ܝܳܗܶܒ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܟܘܰܬܺܝܢܳܟ: ܡܨܿܝܬ ܝܳܗܶܒ݂ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܐܳܦ ܰܡܪܛܘܽܛܳܟ. ܘܐܶܢ ܠܗܘܢ ܠܦܘܿܩܕܿܳܢܶܐ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܡܳܛܶܐ ܐܰܢ݈ܬ: ܠܥܶܠ ܡܶܢܗܘܽܢ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܘܰܦܫܺܝܩ ܠܟ ܕܬܶܗܘܶܐ ܘܬܺܐܪܰܒ ܒܙܰܒܢܳܐ ܗܰܘ܀݂
3. And again He said: 'When you pray, say: Our Father, who art in heaven, forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors.' Forgive your brother, and then in your prayer you will say: 'Forgive me, Lord, because I have forgiven my debtor, and forgive those who have sinned against me; and I beseech you, confused that I have been angry in my anger': by this way you will be above the great and small commandments and above the Law and the Prophets, and you will attain the Lord, that is, His conversation, by which you will arrive at Him and His apostles. But if you have arrived at those great commandments, it will be easy for you to exceed them. If you abstain from the [name of] fool, you will immediately call him 'my brother'; and if you abstain from the [name of] simpleton, you will immediately call [him] 'my son'; and if you abstain from the [epithet of] senseless, it will be easy for you to call him 'beloved'; and if you forgive seventy times seven, it will be easy for you to forgive altogether; and if you pray reconciled, it will be easy for you not to be angry anymore; and if you wash the feet of your enemies, it will be easy for you to kiss them; and if you give your cheek, it will be easy for you to give your whole body; and if you have gone two thousand paces, you will go as much as you wish; and if you have given your tunic, you will be able to give your cloak as well. And if you have arrived at those commandments, you will be above them and it will be easy for you to progress at this time.


[p. 393] {#po.0.p393}


[p. 394] {#po.0.p394}


[p. 395] {#po.0.p395}
ܩܰܕܡܳܐܝܺܬ ܐܰܠܝܨ ܐܰܢܬ: ܘܰܠܚܰܕ݁ܬ݁ܳܐ ܡܶܬ݁ܪܰܟܰܚ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܳܟ. ܐܶܡܰܪ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕ݁ܐܶܛܰܪ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܟ݂ ܠܥܳܠܰܡ ܥܳܠܡܺܝܢ ܘܐܺܗܰܠܶܟ݂ ܒܐܰܪܘܰܚܬܳܐ. ܐܰܡܰܪ ܠܟ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ: ܐܰܚܶܒ ܠܰܐܚܘܽܟ݂ ܛܳܒ ܡܶܢ ܢܰܦܫܳܟ. ܡܶܢ ܗܳܪܟ݁ܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܬ݁ܶܕ݂ܥܘܽܢ ܡܳܢܰܘ ܚܘܽܒܿܳܐ: ܡܰܢܽܘ ܠܰܡ ܕܣܳܐܶܡ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܚܠܦ ܪܳܚܡܶܗ. ܘܐܶܢ ܫܰܪܝܰܪ ܠܟܘܽܢ ܠܰܡ܂ ܚܘܽܒܝ: ܣܝܡܘ ܢܰܦܫܟܘܽܢ ܚܠܳܦ ܐܰܚܰܝ̈ܟܘܽܢ. ܐܶܢ ܕܝܢ ܪܳܚܶܡ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܒܰܥܠܶܐ ܣܳܢܰܝ̈ܟ݂ ܝܰܬܝܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܢܰܦܫܳܟ݂: ܣܰܓܝّ ܪܰܒ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܝܰܬܝّܪ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܕܰܠܚܰܒܪܶܗ ܪܳܚܶܡ ܝܰܬܝܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܘܰܠܣܳܢܶܐܗ ܐܰܝܟ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ: ܘܗܳܟܰܢ ܝܳܪܶܒ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܐܳܦ ܝܰܬܝܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܳܐ ܪܰܘܪ̈ܒ݁ܺܝܐ ܘܡܶܫܬܰܒܚܰܬ ܥܰܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ܂ ܐܰܝܢܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܶܐ ܪܰܘܪ̈ܒ݁ܶܐ ܗ݀ܳܘܶܐ ܓܡܺܝܪܳܐ: ܘܐܶܢ ܥܳܒܶܝܕ݂ ܝܰܬܝܰܪ ܥܰܠ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܶܐ ܪܰܘܪ̈ܒ݁ܶܐ ܘܡܰܚܶܒ ܐܳܦ ܡܶܬܡܰܟ݁ܰܟ݂
4. At the beginning you will be afflicted, in the end you will be refreshed. For He said: 'I will keep your law for ever and ever, and I will walk in refreshment.' But He said to you: 'Love your brother more than yourself.' Hence, He says, you will know what charity is: 'He who lays down his life,' He says, 'for his friend.' And if my love for you is truthful, lay down your life for your brothers. But if you love the wicked, your haters, more than yourself: you will be greater than he who loves his companion more than himself, and his enemy as himself; by this way you will be greater than the great commandments and will be glorified with the Lord. For he who has done these great commandments will be perfect, and if he has surpassed the great commandments by loving and greatly humbling himself and sympathizing with the Lord, he will be glorified with Him, since he spiritually beholds Him and sympathizes with Him, as He said: 'I have set this example for you, that you may wash the feet of your brothers and your betrayers': you, kiss the feet of your betrayers, and behold, you will be greater than he who washes the feet of his betrayers.


[p. 396] {#po.0.p396}
ܣܰܓܝܽ ܘܚܳܐܶܫ ܥܰܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܡܶܫܬ݁ܳܒ݂ܰܚ ܠܰܡܺܝܡܶܗ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܚܳܐܰܪ ܒܶܗ ܒܪܘܰܚ ܘܚܳܐܶܫ ܥܰܡܶܗ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܗܳܢܳܐ ܛܘܽܦܣܳܐ ܣܳܡܶܬ ܠܟܘܽܢ ܕܰܐܦܝܺܓܘܽܢ ܪ̈ܶܓܠܶܐ ܕܐܰܚܰܝ̈ܟܘܽܢ ܘܰܕܡܰܫܠܡܳܢܰܝܟܘܽܢ. ܢܰܫܰܩ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܪ̈ܶܓ݂ܠܶܐ ܕܡܰܡܫܠܡܳܢܰܝܟ: ܘܗܳܐ ܝܺܪܰܒܬ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܕܰܡܫܝܿܓ݂ ܪ̈ܶܓ݂ܠܶܐ ܕܡܰܡܟܠܡܳܢܰܘܗ̱ܝ܀ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܩܪܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܪ̈ܶܚܡܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܠܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ: ܠܣܳܢܰܐܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܘܰܠܪ̈ܳܚܝܡܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܘܰܪܚܶܡ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܝܰܬܝܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ: ܐܰܝܢܳܐ ܕܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܣܳܡ ܚܠܳܦܰܝܗܘܽܢ. ܘܡܰܢ ܕܗܳܘܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܬܰܠܡܝܺܕ݂ܳܐ: ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܢܶܥܒܶܕ݂ ܐܶܟܘܳܬܶܗ: ܘܐܶܢ ܪܰܒܳܟ݂ ܕܠܳܐ ܚܳܛܶܐ: ܠܳܗ ܥܒܰܕ݂ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܚܛܝܳܬܳܐ: ܗܳܝ ܕܥܳܒܕ݂ܳܐ ܚ̈ܛܳܗܶܐ ܕܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܚܰܛܳܝ̈ܶܐ: ܚܫܘܿܒ ܢܰܦܫܳܟ݂ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܒܝܺܫ ܡܶܢ ܚܛܝܳܬܳܐ: ܘܗܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܕܳܐܶܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܐ̱ܢܳܫ. ܐܶܢ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܠܝܬ ܚܰܕ݂ ܡܶܢܝ: ܘܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܟ݂ܚܰܬ݀ ܕ݁ܳܐܶܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܐܰܘ ܡܚܰܣܶܕ݂ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܶܗ: ܐܰܘܪܰܒܬ ܠܳܟ݂
5. The Lord called all men His friends: those who hated Him and those who loved Him, and He loved them more than Himself, so that He laid down His life for them. And he who becomes a disciple to Him should do as He did; and if your Master, who was without sin, made Himself sin (which makes the sins of all sinners): you, consider yourself something that is worse than sin: and behold, you will judge no one. For if you say: 'No one is more guilty than I' and you are caught judging another or reproaching him: you make yourself greater than him, nor are your words consistent with your works. Do this and you will be found with the Lord; and because you consider yourself sin, do not judge sinners; and because the sin of the creature makes all sins: your sins are immense: and because your sins


[p. 397] {#po.0.p397}
ܢܰܦܫܳܟ݂ ܡܶܢܶܗ: ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܬܰܐܡܢܳܢ ܡܶܠܰܝ̈ܟ݂ ܥܰܡ ܥܒܳܕܰܝ̈ܟ݂. ܗܳܟ݂ܰܢܳܐ ܥܒܶܕ݂ ܘܡܶܫܬܟܰܚ ܐܢ̱ܬ ܥܰܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܰܚܫܰܒܬ ܠܳܟ ܢܰܦܫܳܟ݂ ܚܛܝܳܬܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܕܳܐܳܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܚܰܛܳܝ̈ܶܐ: ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܰܚܛܝܳܬܳܐ ܕܒܪܝܺܬ݁ܳܐ ܥܳܒܕ݂ܳܐ ܚ̈ܛܳܗܶܐ: ܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܬܟܝܠܝܳܢ ܚܰܛܳܗܰܝ̈ܟ݂: ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܬܟܝܠܝܳܢ ܚܰܛܳܗܰܝ̈ܟ݂: ܠܳܐ ܬܕܘܽܢ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܡܶܬܬܘܚܠܝܢ ܚܛܳܗܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ. ܐܶܢ ܐܶܢܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܡܳܪܟܘܽܢ ܘܪܰܒܟܘܽܢ ܥܶܒܕ݁ܶܬ ܢܰܦܫܝ ܚܛܝܳܬܳܐ ܒܡܘܽܟܳܟܝ: ܚܰܕ݂ ܟܡܳܐ ܝܰܬܝܰܪ ܘܳܠܶܐ ܠܟܘܽܢ ܕܬܶܬܡܰܟܟܘܽܢ܆ ܗܰܘ ܠܰܡ ܓܶܝܪ ܕܠܳܐ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܚܛܝܳܬܳܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠܳܬܟܘܽܢ ܚܛܝܳܬܳܐ ܥܰܒܕ݁ܶܗ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܥܒܰܕ݂ ܗܽܘ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܘܐܶܬܡܰܟܰܟ: ܕܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܠܰܢ ܚܰܘܪܳܐ ܕ݁ܢܶܬܕ݁ܰܡܶܐ ܒܶܗ. ܘܐܶܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܒ݁ܰܫܠܳܡܳܐ
are immense: do not judge him whose sins are measurable. If I, He says, who am your Lord and Master, made Myself sin in My humiliation: how much more does it behoove you to be humbled? 'Him,' He says, 'who knew no sin, He made sin for your sake,' that is: He made Himself and humbled


[p. 398] {#po.0.p398}


[p. 399] {#po.0.p399}
ܕܢܶܫ̈ܶܝܐ ܒܡܘܽܟܳܟܶܗ: ܚܢܰܝܢ ܕܢܶܣܓܽܘܕ ܠܓ݂ܰܒܪܶܐ ܘܰܠܢܶܫ̈ܶܐ ܙܿܕܩ ܠܰܢ. ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܓܶܝܪ ܕܗܰܘ ܝܰܠܘܽܕ݂ܳܐ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܰܢ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܕܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܶܗ: ܐܰܝܟ ܝܰܠܘܽܕ݁ܳܐ ܕܝܳܢܺܝܩ ܚܰܠܒܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܚܝܺܠܳܐ ܡܝܰܬܪܳܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܕ݁ܢܶܗܘܶܐ. ܐܰܝܟܳܐ ܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܝܰܠܘܽܕܳܐ ܕܕܳܐܲܢ ܒܰܩܪܝܺܬ݁ܳܐ: ܐܰܘ ܕܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܓܰܝܳܪ̈ܶܐ ܘܓܰܢܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܕܐܚܺܝܕ݂ ܒܳܗ̇: ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܕܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܡܶܛܠܳܐ ܛܫܶܝܢ ܓܰܝܳܪ̈ܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܛܠܝܐ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܰܗܘܰܘ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܗܘܽܢ܆ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܝܳܕܥܺܝܢ ܕܰܢܦܰܪܣܘܽܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ: ܘܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܛܡܐܘܽܬܳܐ ܓܰܠܝܳܐ ܠܪܶܥܝܳܢܗܘܿܢ. ܘܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܰܥܶܠ ܚܰܠܘܽܕܳܐ ܠܒܰܝܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܐܚܺܝܕ݂ ܒܳܗ̇ ܓܰܝܳܪ̈ܶܐ ܘܓܰܢܳܒ̈ܶܐ: ܘܐܳܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ: ܥܘܽܠ ܚܙܝܺ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܐܝܺܬ ܠܓܰܘ: ܘܰܚܙܝܺ ܕܠܳܐ ܚܳܪܶܐ ܠܗܘܢ ܒܚܳܫܳܐܝܺܬ ܘܠܳܐ ܕܐܶܢ ܢܰܥܪܺܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܕܐܶܢ
Himself, so that He might become an example to us, that we might imitate Him. And if the Lord in His humility greeted women: it behooves us to adore men and women. For like the infant, whom the Lord said we should be like, so that we might be like a nursing or weaned infant, humble, the Lord said. Where will you find an infant in the village judging or knowing who among them are adulterers or thieves, even if the adulterers do not hide themselves even from the children, to whom the Lord said: 'Be like them?' because they do not know how to slander them, nor is impurity manifest to their minds; but if you bring a little child into some house in which there are adulterers and thieves, and say to him: 'Enter and see what is inside,' you will see that he will not look at them malignantly, not even then, if they are naked, nor if they are committing adultery. Let us also be infants in these wickednesses, and in knowledge and charity and humility let us be perfect.


[p. 400] {#po.0.p400}
ܓܳܝܪܺܝܢ. ܘܐܳܦ݂ ܚܢܰܝܢ ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܝܰܠܽܘܕ݂ܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܒܚܳܫ̈ܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܒܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܬܳܐ ܘܰܒܚܘܽܒܳܐ ܘܰܒܡܰܟܝܺܟܘܽܬܳܐ ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܓܡܝܳܪ̈ܶܐ܀ ܐܶܟܰܪܶܟ ܠܳܟ ܗܳܟܽܠ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܬܶܣܰܒ ܡܶܢ ܛܠܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܘܡܳܢܳܐ ܫܳܒܶܩ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ: ܡܳܐ ܕܰܚܙܰܝܬ ܗܳܟ݂ܰܢܳܐ ܛܰܠܝܳܐ ܕ݁ܠܳܐ ܚܳܨܶܦ ܕܰܠܒܘܽܫ݁ܶܗ ܘܰܕܬܰܪܒܝܳܬܶܗ: ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܗܳܕ݁ܶܐ ܕܝܺܠܝ ܗܹܝ. ܘܡܳܐ ܕܚܳܙܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܶܗ ܕܠܳܐ ܪܳܐܶܓ݂ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ݁ܬܳܐ ܘܫܳܠܶܛ ܠܶܗ ܕ݁ܢܶܒܟܶܐ ܒܟ݁ܽܠ ܥܶܕ݂ܳܢ: ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕ݁ܝܺܠܝ ܐܶܢܶܝܢ: ܐܶܗܘܶܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܪܶܓܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܐܳܒܟܶܐ ܒܟܽܠ ܥܶܕ݂ܳܢ. ܘܡܳܐ ܕܚܳܙܶܝܬ ܠܶܗ ܕܠܳܐ ܕܳܐܲܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܚܙܶܝܢ ܠܶܗ ܒܺܝ̈ܫܶܐ ܘܓܰܝܳܪ̈ܶܐ: ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܝܺܠܝ ܐܶܢܶܝܢ. ܐܶܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܚܳܙܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܶܗ ܕܠܳܐܶܛ ܐܰܘ ܪܳܓܶܙ ܐܰܘ ܡܰܒܶܐܫ ܐܰܘ ܡܳܚܶܐ: ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܗܘܰܘ ܕܝܺܠܝ: ܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܶܕ݂ܡܶܐ ܒܗܳܠܺܝܢ. ܠܰܘ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܗܳܟܰܢ ܫܒܺܝܪ ܪܶܥܝܳܢܳܟ݂ ܕܢܺܐܙܰܠ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܒܺܝ̈ܫܳܬܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܗܰܘ ܝܰܠܘܽܕ݂ܳܐ: ܕ݁ܡܳܐ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܠܘܽܛ: ܠܳܐܶܛ: ܐܳܦ݂ ܡܳܐ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܡܚܝ: ܡܳܚܶܐ ܘܪܳܓܶܙ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܥܶܡܗ ܡܶܬܝܰܠܕ݂ܳܐ ܚܛܺܝܬܳܐ: ܘܗܝ ܨܢܺܝܥܳܐ ܘܗܘ ܦܫܺܝܛ. ܐܰܢ݈ܬ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܙܟܶܝܗ ܘܰܥܩܘܽܪܶܝܗ ܘܰܗܘܝܺ ܝܰܠܘܽܕ݂ܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܢܶܩܦܳܗ ܕܒܺܝܫܬܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܡܶܢ ܒܺܝ̈ܫܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܗܘܰܘ ܝܰܠܽܘܕ݂ܶܐ: ܘܒܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܬ݁ܳܐ
6. Therefore I will explain to you what you should receive from children and what you should omit. When you see a child who has no care for his clothing and food, say: 'This is mine.' And when you see him not coveting a woman and being able to weep at any time, say: 'These are mine; I will be without concupiscence and I will weep at all times.' And when you see him not judging nor looking at the wicked and adulterers, say: 'These are mine.' But if you see him cursing, or getting angry, or doing evil, or striking, say: 'These are not mine': do not imitate these. For your mind is not so simple that you should follow evil, like a little child, to whom if someone says: 'Curse!' he curses, or if someone says to him: 'Strike!' he strikes and gets angry, because sin is innate with him: that is cunning, he himself is simple. But you, overcome sin and root it out and be an infant in obedience to evil, as He said: 'Be infants in evil and in knowledge be perfect.'


[p. 401] {#po.0.p401}


[p. 402] {#po.0.p402}
ܗ݇ܘܰܘ ܓܡܝܳܪ̈ܶܐ܀ ܬܘܽܒ ܐܶܦܪܽܘܫ ܠܳܟ ܥܰܠ ܫܳܛܝܳܐ: ܕܡܳܐ ܕܰܚܙܰܝܬܳܝܗ̱ܝ ܠܫܳܛܝܳܐ ܕܡܫܳܐܶܛ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ: ܘܠܳܐ ܩܢܶܐ ܒ݁ܰܝܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ݁ܬ݁ܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܩܶܢܝܳܢܳܐ ܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܚܰܝܬ݂ܶܐ ܠܒܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܠܒܘܽܫܶܗ: ܘܠܳܐ ܣܰܝܒܳܪܬ݁ܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܕܝܘܽܡ ܒܫܰܘܡܶܗ: ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܝܺܠܝ ܐܶܢܶܝܢ ܘܐܶܬܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܒܗܶܝܢ. ܘܡܳܐ ܕܰܚܙܰܝܬܳܝܗ̱ܝ ܕ݁ܰܡܡܰܠܶܠ ܒܫܳܛܝܘܽܬܶܗ ܥܰܡ ܟܽܠܢܳܫ: ܘܣܳܐܶܡ ܠܶܗ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܕ݁ܠܳܐ ܢܶܬܚܰܡܰܬ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕ݁ܠܳܐ ܢܶܙܕ݂ܰܥܰܡ:
7. I will still explain to you about the fool. But if you see a fool despising himself, having neither house, nor wife, nor substance, but not even clothes, except for his garment, nor food, except for the daily, say: 'These are mine,' imitate these. And when you see him conversing with everyone because of his foolishness and setting a law for himself


[p. 403] {#po.0.p403}
ܘܚܰܟܝܺܡܳܐ ܕ݁ܥܳܠܡܳܝܐ ܕܰܢܛܺܝܠ ܒܚܶܟܡܬܳܐ: ܘܦܺܝܠܳܣܘܽܦܳܐ ܕܫܳܛ ܠܶܗ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܡܶܬܚܙܶܐ: ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܝܺܠܝ ܐܶܢܶܝܢ: ܗܳܕܶܐ ܫܳܛܝܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܰܫܠܺܝܚܶܐ. ܡܳܐ ܕܚܳܙܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܶܗ ܕܰܡܚܰܪܶܫ ܐܰܘ ܕܰܡܢܰܓܶܫ: ܐܰܘ ܕ݁ܰܡܙܰܢܶܐ ܐܰܘ ܕܩܳܨܶܡ܂ ܐܰܘ ܕܣܳܓܶܕ݂ ܠܰܦܬܰܟܪ̈ܶܐ: ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܠܰܝܬ ܕܝܺܠܝ ܐܶܢ̈ܝܼܢ. ܘܐܳܦ݂ ܣܰܟ݁ܺܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܕ݁ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܒܣܰܟ݁̈ܠܘܳܬܗܘܽܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܦܳܪܫܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܡܰܢ ܕ݁ܰܡܨܰܥܰܪ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܰܡܚܰܝܩܺܝܪ ܠܗܘܽܢ: ܘܥܰܡ ܗܰܘ ܕܰܡܚܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܒܪܰܡܫܳܐ: ܡܩܰܕ݂ܡܝܺܢ ܡܡܰܠܠܝܺܢ ܥܰܡܶܗ ܒܨܰܦܪܳܐ. ܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ ܐܶܬܕܰܡܳܐ ܒܗܘܽܢ: ܐܰܝܟ ܣܰܟܠܳܐ ܥܘܽܠ ܠܘܳܬ ܡܨܰܥܪܳܢܰܝܟ ܘܡܰܡܠܶܠ ܥܰܡܗܘܽܢ ܘܠܰܡܚܰܩܪܳܢܰܝܟ ܝܰܩܰܪ. ܘܚܘܽܪ ܒܣܰܟܠܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ
that he will not be angered by wrath, lest he be rebuked, and the wise man of the world despised for his wisdom, and the philosopher, to whom visible things become vile, say: 'These are mine,' this is the foolishness of the apostles. But if you see him practicing magic or fortune-telling, or fornicating, or divining, or adoring idols, say: 'These are not mine.' And they become a laughingstock to the world because of their foolishness, when they do not discern who is mocking them and who is honoring them, and they address in the morning him who struck them in the evening. Imitate them in this way; enter as a fool to those who mock you, and speak with them and honor those who honor you, and look at the fool, who because of his folly does not discern the good from the bad. You, in like manner, love the good and the bad even if you know them. Even if you see him being directed by his folly and when another says to him: 'Go, commit adultery' or 'steal' or 'curse,' he does so because of his folly, do not become like him, for He says to you about the cunning of earthly wisdom: 'Be a fool,' not about heavenly wisdom, nor like the cunning wise men


[p. 404] {#po.0.p404}
ܦܳܪܶܫ ܒܣܰܟܠܘܽܬܶܗ ܛܳܒܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܒܺܝܫ̈ܶܐ. ܘܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ ܐܰܚܶܒ ܐܰܢܬ ܠܛܳܒܶܐ ܘܰܠܒܺܝܫ̈ܶܐ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܗܘܽܢ. ܘܡܳܐ ܕܰܚܙܰܝܬܳܝܗ̱ܝ ܕܡܶܬܕܰܒܰܪ ܒܣܰܟܠܘܽܬܶܗ: ܐܶܢ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܕܙܶܠ ܓܘܽܪ ܐܰܘ ܓܢܽܘܒ ܐܰܘ ܠܘܽܛ: ܘܥܰܒܶܕ݂ ܗܳܟܰܢ ܒܣܰܟܠܘܽܬܶܗ: ܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܶܬܕ݁ܰܡܶܐ ܒܶܗ: ܡܶܛܰܠ ܕܡܶܢ ܚܰܪܝܨܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܚܶܟܡܬܳܐ ܐܰܪܥܳܢܳܝܬ݁ܳܐ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܠܳܟ ܕܰܗܘܺܝ ܣܰܟܠܳܐ: ܠܰܘ ܡܶܢ ܚܶܟܡܬܳܐ ܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܝܬܳܐ: ܘܠܰܘ ܐܰܝܟ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܚܰܟܝ̈ܡܶܐ ܚܰܪ̈ܝܨܶܐ ܬ݁ܶܗܘܶܐ ܚܳܙܶܐ ܒܚܰܫ̈ܶܐ ܘܕܳܐܳܢ ܠܗܘܽܢ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܣܰܟ݁ܺܠܶܐ ܗܘܰܝܬ ܚܳܙܶܐ ܘܡܰܪܦܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܣܰܟܠܘܳܬܗܘܽܢ: ܘܐܰܝܟ ܚܰܟܝܺܡܳܐ ܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܐ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܕܰܢܬܘܽܒܘܽܢ: ܘܠܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܚܰܟܝܺܡܳܐ ܐܰܪܥܳܢܳܐ ܬܕܘܽܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܕܰܢܡܘܽܬܘܽܢ ܒܝܰܕ݂ ܒܺܝܫ̈ܶܐ. ܘܐܶܬܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܒܛܰܝܒܘܽܬܶܗ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܘܐܰܛܶܐܒ ܠܟܽܠ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܘܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܕ݂ܰܡܶܐ ܒܶܗ ܕܦܳܪܰܥ ܠܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܐܰܝܟ ܥܒܳܕ݂ܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܗܘܰܝܬ ܐܝܺܬܝܳܐ ܘܰܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܶܗ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܐܶܢ ܗܽܘ ܠܳܐ ܥܳܒ݂ܶܕ݂ ܕ݁ܝܺܢܶܐ ܠܰܛܠܺܝܡܶܐ: ܡܰܢܘܽ ܥܰܒ݁ܶܕ݂ ܠܶܗ܆ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܶܗ ܒܳܥܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܬܿܶܗܘܶܐܢ ܥܒܕ ܠܳܟ ܒܪܝܺܬܳܐ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܶܗ. ܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܶܗܘܶܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܒܓ݂ܰܘ ܒܪܝܺܬܶܗ: ܕܠܳܐ ܢܣܰܚܘܳܟ݂ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܠܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ܀
look at the wicked and judge them, but like those fools, having seen their sins, neglect them and as a heavenly wise man exhort them to do penance, nor condemn them as an earthly wise man, so that they may die through the wicked. Imitate the grace of God by doing good to all, nor imitate Him who renders to each according to his works, for you are not an Aeon, nor are you without law, like Him. For if He does not do judgment for the oppressed, who will? Do you want to become like Him? Make a creature for yourself in His likeness! Do not become God among His creatures, lest He consume you, like Satan!


[p. 405] {#po.0.p405}
ܥܰܠ ܓ݁ܰܒܪܳܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܰܒܪܘܽܚ ܪܳܗܶܛ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܚܘܽܒܿܳܐ: ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܫܰܠܺܛ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܠܥܶܠ ܡܶܢ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ. ܨܳܒܶܐ ܐܰܢ݈ܬ ܗܳܟܝܶܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܕ݂ܘܽܢܳܟ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܶܚܛܶܐ ܒܦܰܓܪܳܟ: ܘܐܶܢ ܨܳܒܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܪ݁ܶܝܟ݂ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܝܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܶܚܛܶܐ ܒܠܶܒܳܟ ܒܡܰܪܢܺܝܬܳܐ ܣܢܝܺܬܳܐ ܕܥܰܠ ܒܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ: ܘܐܶܢ ܨܳܒܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܬܶܗܘܶܐ ܥܰܡ ܡܳܪܗܘܽܢ ܕܰܟܬܳܒܿ̈ܶܐ: ܪܚܰܡ ܠܡܳܪܳܟ ܘܐܰܚܺܝܒ ܠܟܽܠ
8. But over the man who follows charity in the spirit, the law does not rule, but he is above the law. If you wish, therefore, that the first law may not condemn you, do not sin with your body; and if you wish that the last law may not reproach you, do not sin in your heart by thinking shameful things about men; and if you wish to become with the Lord of the Scriptures, love your Lord and love all men from the progeny of Adam: and behold, you have comprehended the law.


[p. 406] {#po.0.p406}
ܒ݁ܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܗܰܘ ܕܡܶܢ ܝܰܠܕܰܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܕܐܳܕܳܡ ܘܗܳܐ ܣܰܟܶܠܬ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ܀ ܣܳܟ݁ܶܗ ܠܰܡ ܕܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܚܘܽܒܰܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܡܶܢ ܬ݁ܶܐܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܟܝܳܬܳܐ ܘܗܰܝܡܳܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܫܓܘܽܫܝܳܐ: ܕܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܦܘܽܩܕ̈ܳܢܶܐ ܐܰܪܦܺܝܘ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܘܰܛܥܰܘ ܫܪܳܪܳܐ ܘܕܰܟܝܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܠܶܒܳܐ. ܟܬܳܒܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܩܳܛܶܠ ܠܳܟ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܚܳܕ݂ܰܩ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܐܶܦܪܘܺܫ ܦܘܽܩܕ݂ܳܢܵܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܘܐܶܣܰܒ ܠܳܟ ܡܶܢܗܘܽܢ ܚܘܽܒܳܐ
9. For the end of the law is charity [proceeding] from a pure conscience and unperturbed faith, which men who have forgotten the truth and the purity of the heart have abandoned as precepts. The letter, He says, kills you, because you do not know how to discern its commandments and derive charity from them, and the Lord Jesus saves you,


[p. 407] {#po.0.p407}
ܘܡܳܪܰܢ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܡܰܚܺܝܐ ܠܳܟ ܕܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܘܬܰܦ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܶܗ. ܒܡܰܟܺܝܟܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܰܒܚܘܽܒܿܳܐ ܕܡܰܟ݁ܺܝ̈ܟ݁ܶܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܥܳܡܰܪ ܡܫܺܝܚܳܐ ܘܰܠܗܘܽܢ ܓ݁ܳܠܶܐ ܪܳܐܙܰܘܗ̱ܝ. ܘܐܶܢ ܨܳܒ݂ܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܬ݁ܳܐ ܠܗܳܢܳܐ ܢܝܳܚܳܐ ܘܛܰܥܶܡܝܗ ܠܗܳܕ݁ܶܐ ܚܰܠܝܘܽܬ݂ܳܐ. ܘܰܚܙܝܺ ܐܶܡܰܬܝ ܡܢܺܝܚ ܗ̱ܘܰܝܬ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܕܳܐܶܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܝܬ ܠܟܽܠܢܳܫ: ܐܰܘ ܗܳܫܳܐ ܕ݁ܩܰܒܶܠܬ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܘܡܰܚܶܝܒ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܗܘܽܢ܆ ܚܙܝܺ ܐܰܡܰܬܝ ܡܥܰܪܶܐ ܕܢܶܬܬܒܰܪ ܚܰܝܠܳܗ ܕܰܚܛܺܝܬܳܐ ܡܶܢܳܟ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܐܝܬ ܠܳܟ ܒܥܶܠܕܒܳܒܝܘܽܬܳܐ ܥܡ ܒܢܰܝ݁ ܗܰܝܡܳܢܘܽܬ݂ܳܟ܂ ܘܥܰܡ ܦܶܠ̈ܚܳܬ݂ܳܐ: ܐܰܘ ܗܳܫܳܐ ܕ݁ܡܰܚܶܝܒ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܟܽܠܗܘ̇ܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܛܳܒܶܐ ܘܒܺܝ̈ܫܶܐ: ܘܠܰܝܬ ܠܳܟ ܒܥܶܠܕ݂ܒܳܒܳܐ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ: ܘܠܰܝܬ ܠܳܟ݂ ܬܰܟܬܘܽܫܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܒܶܣܪܳܐ ܘܰܕ݂ܡܳܐ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܥܳܒܕܰܬ ܩܪܳܒܿܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܙ̈ܘܺܥܶܐ ܒܺܝ̈ܫܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܚܰܝ̈ܠܰܘܳܬܳܗ ܕܰܚܛܺܝܬܳܐ܆ ܘܡܳܡܘܽܢܳܐ ܘܥܰܘܠܳܐ ܘܟ݁ܽܠ ܕܥܳܒܰܪ: ܫܒܘܽܩ ܘܐܰܪܚܶܩ ܡܶܢܶܗ ܐܰܝܟ ܒܥܶܠܕܒܳܒܳܐ: ܘܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܘܡܳܪܰܢ ܢܶܬܚܙܘܽܢ ܠܳܟ݂ ܐܰܝܟ ܪܳܚܶܡܐ ܚܰܒ̈ܝܒ݁ܶܐ ܩܰܪ̈ܝܺܒܶܐ ܘܐܰܒܳܗܶܐ ܘܡܳܪܰܝܳܐ ܘܐܰܢ݈ܬ ܥܰܒܕ݂ܳܐ ܗܰܘܺܝ ܠܗܘܢ ܒܚܘܽܒܳܟ ܘܰܒܪܳܐ ܘܐܰܚܳܐ ܘܪܳܚܡܳܐ ܘܝܳܪܬܳܐ܀
as you associate yourself with Him. In the humility and charity of the humble, Christ dwells and reveals His mysteries to them. And if you wish, enter into this rest and taste this sweetness. And see, when you were content: when you judged everyone, or now, after you have forgiven everyone and loved them? See, when the power of sin began to be broken in you: when you had enmity with the followers of your faith and sects, or now, when you love everyone, good and bad, and have no enemy, except Satan, nor is there a struggle there with flesh and blood, the sons of Adam, but you enter into battle with evil spirits, the armies of sin? And leave mammon and iniquity and all fleeting things and distance yourself from them, as from enemies, and all men and the Lord will seem to you dear friends and relatives and parents and masters: you be their servant through charity and son and brother and friend and heir.


[p. 408] {#po.0.p408}
ܢܶܙܗܘܶܐ ܗܳܟܝܶܠ ܗܳܟܰܢ: ܘܰܢܨܰܠܶܐ ܥܰܠ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܫ̈ܐ ܕ݁ܡܶܢ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܘܰܕ݂ܡܳܐ ܠܚܰܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܢܺܚܘܽܢ ܘܰܢܫܰܒܚܘܽܢ ܠܰܐܒ݂ܳܐ ܘܠܰܒ݁ܪܳܐ ܘܰܠܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܕܩܘܽܕ݂ܫܳܐ ܬܠܝܳܬܳܝܘܽܬܳܐ ܡܫܰܡܠܳܝܬܳܐ܀
10. Let us therefore be such and pray for all men from Adam to the last, that they may live and glorify the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit, the perfect Trinity.
ܣܳܗܶܕ݂ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܠܝ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ: ܕܐܶܢ ܚܳܫܶܝܢ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܫ̈ܐ ܕܰܗܘܰܘ ܘܰܕܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܡܶܢ ܝܰܠܺܕ݂ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܕܐܳܕܳܡ: ܡܶܢ ܪܺܫܺܝܬܳܐ ܘܰܕ݂ܡܳܐ ܠܚܰܪܬ݁ܳܐ: ܐܶܢ ܢܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܠܚܰܕ݂ ܚܰܕ݂ ܡܶܢܗܘܽܢ ܪܶܒܘܽ ܦܘܽܡ̈ܡܺܝܢ: ܘܰܠܚܰܕ݂ ܚܰܕ݂ ܦܘܽܡܳܐ ܪܶܒܘܽ ܠܶܫܳܢܶܬܝܢ: ܘܰܠܚܰܕ݂ ܚܰܕ݂ ܠܶܫܳܢܳܐ ܪܶܒܘܽ ܡܶܠܝܺܢ: ܘܠܰܚܕ݂ܳܐ ܚܕ݂ܳܐ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܪܶܒܘܽ ܫܘܽܒ̈ܚܺܝܢ: ܘܰܠܚܰܕ݂ ܚܰܕ݂ ܫܘܽܒܚܳܐ ܪܶܒܘܽ ܩܘܽܠܳܣ̈ܝܢ: ܙܥܘܽܪܝܺܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܕܢܰܘܕܘܽܢ ܘܰܢܫܰܒܚܘܽܢ ܠܒܰܣܺܝܡܘܽܬܶܗ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܰܗܘܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܒܢܰܫ̈ܐ: ܐܶܢ ܒܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܬܳܐ ܘܐܶܢ ܒ݁ܰܡܨܰܥܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܐܶܢ ܒܰܐ̱ܚܪܺܝܬܳܐ. ܘܰܙܥܘܽܪܝܺܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܫ̈ܐ ܠܰܐܬܪ̈ܘܳܬܳܐ ܕܰܢܝܳܚܬܳܐ ܕܰܡܛܰܝܒܺܝܢ ܠܶܗ ܠܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܐܰܝܟ ܡܰܥܒܰܕ݂̈ܘܗ̱ܝ ܘܐܰܝܟ ܡܫܘܽܚܬܶܗ: ܘܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܰܠܶܨ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܘܐܶܬܰܠܟܰܥ ܘܐܶܫܬܰܢܰܩ. ܘܐܶܢ ܝܳܬܪܺܝܢ ܬܘܰܒ ܝܰܬܝܺܪ ܡܶܢ ܫܠܺܝܚܶܐ ܘܡܶܢ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܚܰܘܝܺ ܠܗܘܿܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܛܘܰܦܣܳܐ ܕܡܰܟܝܺܟܘܽܬܳܐ: ܣܰܓܝܰ ܙܥܘܿܪܝܺܢ ܡܶܢ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܛܰܝܶܒ ܠܗܘܿܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ. ܡܶܬܪܰܥܶܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܕܠܳܐ ܫܳܘܶܝܢ ܚܰܫܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܕܗܳܢܳܐ ܙܰܒ݂ܢܳܐ ܘܪܶܗܛܳܐ ܕܪܳܗܛܺܝܢ ܓܡܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ: ܠܬܶܫܒܘܽܚܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܠܘܽܦܪܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܥܬܝܰܕ݂ܝܺܢ ܕܰܢܩܰܒܠܘܽܢ: ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܥܰܝܢܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܚܙܳܬ ܘܐܶܕ݂ܢܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܫܶܡܥܰܬ: ܘܥܰܠ ܠܶܒܳܐ ܕܒܰܪ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܣܠܶܩ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܛܰܝܶܒ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܒܕ݂ܰܪ̈ܓ݁ܶܐ ܥܶܠܳܝܶܐ ܠܰܐܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܪܰܚܡܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܘܰܫܒܰܩܘ ܟܽܠ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܥܳܒܰܪ ܘܰܪܚܶܡܘ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܠܗܰܘ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ܂ ܕܠܳܐ ܥܳܒܰܪ: ܕܥܰܡܶܗ ܒܡܰܠܟܘܽܬܳܐ ܢܶܗܘܘܽܢ
11. For the Lord testifies to me that if all men who were and are from the sons of Adam were alive, from the beginning to the end, if each of them had myriads of mouths and each mouth myriads of tongues and each tongue myriads of words and each word myriads of hymns and each hymn myriads of doxologies: they would be unequal to praising the sweetness of God toward men, whether in the first [things], or in the middle, or in the last, and they would be unequal to the mansions of rest, which are prepared for each one according to his works and according to his capacity and according to how he afflicted and humbled and tormented himself. And if they progressed more than the apostles and more than the example of humility, which the Lord Himself set for them: they would be most unequal to that which the Lord Himself prepared for them. I think, He says, that the sufferings of this time and course, in which the perfect run, are not worthy of the glory and beauty which they are about to receive: what eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has it ascended to the heart of man, is that which God has prepared in the higher degrees for those who loved Him, and left all fleeting things and loved the eternal, because they will be with Him in the kingdom and will be glorified with Him,


[p. 409] {#po.0.p409}


[p. 410] {#po.0.p410}


[p. 411] {#po.0.p411}
ܘܥܰܡܶܗ ܢܶܫܬܰܒܚܘܽܢ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܚܰܫܘ ܥܰܡܶܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܩܢܰܘ ܡܶܕ݁̇ܡ ܕܥܳܒܰܪ ܠܰܡܕܶܡ: ܕܠܳܐ ܬܶܒܛܰܠ ܡܶܢ ܢܰܦܫܗܘܽܢ ܬܶܫܡܶܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܦܠܚܘ ܦܘܽܠܚܳܢܳܐ ܕܰܐܪܥܳܐ: ܘܰܫܒܰܩܘ
for they sympathized with Him, nor did they possess fleeting things with Him, lest their soul should fail from spiritual ministry, nor did they work earthly work, having left heavenly work from the day they knew it.
ܦܘܽܠܚܝܢܳܐ ܫܡܰܚܳܢܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܝܰܘܡܳܐ ܕܝܰܕܥܘܽܗ̱ܝ܀ ܘܐܳܦ ܠܟܺܐܢܳܐ ܘܰܠܥܰܒ̈ܕ݂ܰܝ ܛܰܒ݁ܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܟܝܼܢ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܰܡܛܰܝܰܒ: ܘܟܽܠܶܗ ܗܰܘ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܫܒܺܝܚ ܘܰܡܫܰܬܰܪ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܥܳܐܶܠ ܠܶܗ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܝܰܬܰܪ ܫܘܽܒܚܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܫܘܽܒܚܳܐ: ܐܝܺܬ ܐܝܟ ܫܘܽܒܚܳܐ ܕܫܶܡܫܳܐ ܝܳܪܶܒ ܘܐܝܺܬ ܕܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܣܰܗܪܳܐ ܘܐܝܺܬ ܕܰܐܝܟ ܕܟܰܘܟܒ̈ܶܐ. ܘܐܝܺܬ ܕܫܘܽܒܚܳܐ ܕܪܰܒ ܘܰܟܣܶܐ ܝܳܪܶܬ: ܕ݁ܰܡܝܰܬܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܕܫܶܡܫܳܐ ܘܰܕܣܰܗܪܳܐ ܘܰܕܟܰܘܟܒ̈ܶܐ. ܐ̱ܚܪܺܢܳܐ ܓܶܝܪ ܠܰܡ ܬܘܽܒ ܫܘܽܒܚܳܐ ܕܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܘܰܐܚܪܺܢܳܐ ܕܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܘܰܐܚܪܺܢܳܐ ܕ݂ܫܶܡܫܳܐ ܘܰܐܚܪܺܢܳܐ ܕܣܰܗܪܳܐ: ܘܰܐܚܪܺܢܳܐ ܕܟܰܘܟܒ̈ܶܐ. ܘܟܰܘܟܒܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܡܶܢ ܟܰܘܟܒܳܐ ܡܝܰܬܰܪ ܒܢܘܽܗܪܶܗ. ܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܒܚܰܝܳܬ݁ ܡܝܺܬܶܐ: ܡܝܰܬܰܪ ܫܘܽܒܚܳܐ ܘܢܘܽܗܪܳܐ ܕܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܡܶܢ ܕܚܰܒܪܶܗ. ܘܗܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܫܘܽܒܚܳܐ ܕܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܗܘܰܝܘܽ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܐܳܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕܥܰܝܢܳܐ ܕܒ݁ܶܣܪܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܚܙܳܬ ܘܥܰܠ ܠܶܒܳܐ ܕܒ݁ܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܣܠܶܩ: ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܛܰܝܶܒ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܰܐܝ݂ܠܶܝܢ ܕܪܰܚܡܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܘܰܢܛܺܝܪܘ ܡܶܠܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܕܣܰܓܝܼ ܡܝܰܬܰܪ ܘܰܡܫܰܒܰܚ ܡܶܢ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܬܘܽܒܚ̈ܬܳܢ. ܡܶܬܓܰܡܪܝܺܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܘܡܰܕܪܟܝܢ ܠܶܗ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܡܶܬܡܰܟܟܝܿܢ ܘܡܶܬܩܰܕ݂ܫܝܺܢ
12. It is also glorious what is prepared for the just and those who do good; and that whole world is glorious and it is expedient for him who enters there. Nevertheless, there is glory and glory: there are those who are to be magnified like the glory of the sun, and there are those who are to be like the moon and the stars. And there are those who are to inherit a great and hidden glory, more excellent than the sun, moon, and stars. For one is the glory of the celestial and another of the terrestrial, and another is the [glory] of the sun and another of the moon and another of the stars. And star, He says, is more excellent than star in its light. Similarly, in the resurrection of the dead, the glory and light of each [will be] more excellent than that of his neighbor. That celestial glory is the one of which the Lord said: The eye of the flesh has not seen and it has not ascended to the heart of man what God has prepared for those who loved Him and kept His words, which is more excellent and more glorious than any glory; but the perfect will be those who will attain it, who have humbled and sanctified themselves and renounce this world and behold their Lord in heaven as in a mirror with their mind and imitate Him in all His humiliations. And departing from this world they will be with the Lord.


[p. 412] {#po.0.p412}


[p. 413] {#po.0.p413}


[p. 414] {#po.0.p414}
ܘܡܶܢ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܡܶܣܬ݁ܰܪܩܝܺܢ ܘܚܳܝܪܝܺܢ ܒܡܳܪܗܘܽܢ ܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܒܡܰܚܙܝܺܬ݁ܳܐ ܒܪܶܥܝܳܢܗܘܽܢ ܘܡܶܬ݁ܕ݁ܰܡܶܝܢ ܒܶܗ ܒܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܡܘܽܟܳܟܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ. ܘܐܶܡܰܬܝ ܕܥܳܢܕ݂ܝܺܢ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ܀ ܫܠܶܡ ܡܺܐܡܪܳܐ ܕܫܶܬܬܰܥܣܰܪ: ܕܥܰܠ ܕܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܝܳܪܶܒ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܡܶܢ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܶܐ ܪܰܘܪ̈ܒܳܐ܀
The sixteenth discourse on the manner by which one becomes greater than the great commandments ends.


[p. 415] {#po.0.p415}
ܡܺܐܡܪܳܐ ܕܫܰܒܥܰܬܰܥܣܰܪ: ܕܥܰܠ ܚܰܫܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܰܐܝܟܰܢ ܗܘܳܐ ܠܰܢ ܛܽܘܦܣܳܐ܀
SEVENTEENTH DISCOURSE ON THE PASSIONS OF THE LORD, BY WHICH HE BECAME AN EXAMPLE FOR US
ܚܰܫܽܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܕܡܳܪܶܢ ܕܰܗܘܳܐ ܠܢ ܒܗܘܿܢ ܚܰܘܪܳܐ ܀ ܀ ܥܰܠ ܚܰܫܽܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܰܗܘܳܐ ܠܢ ܒܗܘܿܢ ܚܰܘܪܳܐ ܕܒܺܝܗ ܢܶܬܕܰܡܶܐ: ܕܐܶܢ ܢܶܚܰܫ ܥܰܡܶܗ ܐܳܦ ܥܰܡܶܗ ܢܶܫܬܰܒܰܚ. ܡܳܐ ܗܳܟܝܽܠ ܕܩܳܪܶܐ ܐܰܢ݈ܬ ܒܕܺܝܰܬܝܺܩܺܐ ܚܕܰܬܳܐ: ܐܰܣܬܰܟܰܠ ܚܰܫ̈ܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܐܳܬ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܘܰܗܘܰܝܬ ܚܳܐܶܫ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܚܰܫ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕܬܶܫܬ݁ܰܒ݁ܰܚ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܫܬ݁ܰܒ݁ܰܚ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܥܰܡܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܚܳܐܶܫ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܐܳܦ ܝܰܘܡܳܢܳܐ ܐܶܡܰܬܝ ܕܚܳܐܶܫ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ: ܥܰܡܳܟ ܚܳܐܶܫ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܫܠܺܝܚܳܝܐ: ܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܕܚܰܫ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܐܶܬܥܰܠܝܰ: ܕܐܶܢ ܢܶܚܰܫ ܥܰܡܶܗ ܐܳܦ ܥܰܡܶܗ ܢܶܫܬ݁ܰܒ݁ܰܚ. ܠܳܐ ܗܳܐ ܝܺܕ݂ܝܺܥܳܐ ܕܟ݁ܶܣܝܳܐܝܺܬ ܚܳܐܶܫ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܥܰܡܰܢ܆ ܐܶܬܢܰܣܺܝ ܘܠܰܘ ܒܰܛܶܠ ܢܶܣܝܽܘ̈ܢܺܝܢ ܘܚܳܐܶܫ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܥܰܡ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܚܳܐܫܺܝܢ ܘܡܶܬܢܰܣܶܝܢ. ܚܳܙܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢ ܚܳܐܶܫ ܗܘ ܟܶܣܝܳܐܝܺܬ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܗܘܽ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕܡܰܢ ܕܰܠܟܘܽܢ ܡܨܰܥܰܪ: ܠܺܝ ܡܨܰܥܰܪ: ܘܡܢ ܕܰܠܟܘܽܢ ܡܝܰܩܰܪ: ܠܺܝ ܝܰܩܰܪ. ܓܰܠܝܳܐܝܺܬ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܡܶܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܗܰܘ ܙܰܒ݂ܢܳܐ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܦ݁ܰܘܠܳܘܣ ܚܳܫ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ. ܘܰܕ݂ܢܺܐܡܰܪ ܕܘܒ ܐܳܬܶܐ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܚܳܐܶܫ ܓܰܠܝܳܐܝܺܬ: ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܡܶܟܝܽܠ ܠܳܐ ܗܳܘܝܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢܗܘܽ ܕ݁ܰܚܢܰܢ ܝܳܗܒܺܝܢܰܢ ܢܰܦܫܰܢ ܠܚܰܫ̈ܶܐ: ܡܳܪܰܢ
1. On the passions of the Lord in which we have an example to be imitated, so that sympathizing with Him we may also be glorified with Him. When, therefore, you read the New Testament, distinguish the passions from the miracles and allow yourself to suffer as the Lord suffered, so that you may be glorified, just as the Lord was glorified, that is: you suffer with the Lord, for today also, when you have suffered, He will sympathize with you, as the Apostle said, after the Lord has suffered and been exalted: If we suffer with Him, we shall also be glorified with Him. Is it not clear that the Lord secretly sympathizes with us? He was tempted and did not abolish our temptations and He sympathizes with those who suffer and are tempted. You see how He suffers secretly, as the Lord Himself said: 'Whoever rejects you, rejects Me; and whoever honors you, honors Me.' He suffered openly indeed before that time which Paul spoke of; and for us to say that the Lord is still to come to suffer openly, this indeed will not happen, but if we have surrendered our soul to suffer, the Lord is faithful to sympathize with us secretly. If, therefore, you read that the Lord cleansed lepers, enlightened the blind, raised up the bent, strengthened the paralytics, calmed the gatherings of water, healed the sick, made the lame leap like deer, and extended the tongues of the mutes: these are miracles which the Lord performed for the sake of the unbelievers, so that they might believe; for the believer there is no need of miracles, but of passions, so that he may be perfected, suffer, progress, and be glorified. If, therefore, you believe that Jesus is God, you have no need of signs, nor do you inquire


[p. 416] {#po.0.p416}


[p. 417] {#po.0.p417}
ܗܳܟܝܽܠ ܕܩܳܪܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܕܰܟܺܝ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܓܰܪ̈ܒ݁ܶܐ ܘܰܦܬܰܚ ܣܡܰܝ̈ܳܐ ܘܰܦܬܰܚ ܟܦ̈ܝܳܐ ܘܚܰܝܶܠ ܡܫܰܪ̈ܝܳܐ: ܘܐܰܢܺܝܚ ܠܰܟܢܽܘܫܝܳܬ̈ ܡܰܝ̈ܳܐ: ܘܐܰܣܺܝ ܠܰܟܪ̈ܝܳܗܶܐ: ܘܩܰܦܶܨ ܚܓܺܝܪ̈ܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܐܰܝ̈ܠܶܐ ܘܰܦܫܰܛ ܠܶܫܳܢ̈ܶܐ ܕܦܺܐܩ̈ܶܐ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐܳܬܘ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܐܶܢܺܝܢ ܕ݁ܰܥܒ݁ܰܕ݂ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܗܰܝܡܶܝܢ ܕܰܢܗܰܝܡܢܽܘܢ: ܠܡܰܢ ܕ݁ܰܡܗܰܝܡܶܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܒ݁ܰܥܝܳܢ ܐܳܬܘ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܒ݂ܥܶܝܢ ܠܶܗ ܚܰܫ̈ܶܐ: ܕܢܶܬܓ݁ܡܰܪ ܘܢܶܚܰܫ ܘܢܺܐܪܰܒ݂ ܘܢܶܫܬܰܒ݁ܰܚ. ܐܶܢ ܗܰܝܡܶܢܬ ܗܳܟܝܽܠ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ: ܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܒܰܥܝܳܢ ܠܳܟ ܐܳܬܘ̈ܳܬܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܬܥܰܩܶܒ ܕܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܡܳܢܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܬܳܐ ܠܟ ܠܚܰܫ̈ܶܐ ܘܰܠܚܽܘܒܳܐ: ܘܗܳܐ ܐܶܬܓܠܺܝܬ ܠܳܟ ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܗܘܰܝ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ. ܐܶܢ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܠܰܡ ܣܶܒܰܪ ܕܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ: ܠܳܐ ܥܕ̣ܰܟ݀ܕܶܝܢ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܝܺܕܰܥ: ܐܰܝܟ ܡܳܐ ܕ݁ܘܳܠܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܠܡܶܕܰܥ. ܡܰܢ ܕܐܰܚܶܒ ܕܝܢ ܠܰܐܠܳܗܳܐ: ܗܳܢܳܐ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ. ܚܳܙܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܰܒܚܽܘܒܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܚܳܕ݂ܰܬ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܘܽܠܥܕ̇ܡ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܚܳܙܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܐܳܬܘ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܳܐ ܡܶܫܟܚܝܺܢ ܕܢܶܥܒܕܽܘܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ
how and why, but go to the passions and charity, and behold, it will become clear to you how and why these things were done. If anyone, He says, thinks he knows something, he knows nothing yet, as he ought to know. But he who loves God, this one knows. You see that a man knows everything through charity; for if you see the Lord performing signs, which men cannot do, if the matter displeases you because of


[p. 418] {#po.0.p418}


[p. 419] {#po.0.p419}
ܥܢܘܽܬܶܗ: ܐܶܢ ܡܫܰܟܪܳܐ ܠܳܟ ܨܒܘܽܬܳܐ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܡܘܰܟܳܟܶܗ: ܕܠܳܐ ܕܳܡܶܐ ܠܰܐܠܳܗܳܐ: ܡܶܢ ܐܳܬܘܳܬܶܗ ܕܰܥ ܕܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ: ܘܐܶܣܬܰܟܰܠ ܕܠܰܘ ܗܘ ܝܰܨܝܺܦ ܘܡܰܟܝܺܟ ܗܳܟ݂ܘܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܠܳܟ ܡܰܡܠܶܦ݂ ܕܬ݂ܶܬܡܰܟܰܟ ܘܬܶܬܟܫܺܛ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܶܗ: ܡܳܐ ܕܐܶܬܡܰܟܰܟܬ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܶܗ: ܬܶܬ݂ܪܰܡܪܰܡ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܬܬܪܝܺܡ ܗܘܳܐ. ܕܰܥ ܗܳܟܝܶܠ
His humility, that He is unlike God: know from the signs that He is the Lord and understand that He is not so vile and humble, but is teaching you to humble and despise yourself in His likeness, so that humbled in His likeness you may be exalted with Him, just as He Himself was exalted. Distinguish, therefore, the passions from the signs.
ܚܰܫ̈ܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܐܳܬܘܳܬܳܐ܀ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܚܰܫ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܝܳܗܶܒ݂ ܦ݁ܰܟܶܗ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܡܳܚܶܐ ܠܶܗ: ܘܰܡܡܰܠܶܠ ܠܶܗ ܫܠܳܡܳܐ ܒܥܰܝܢܳܐ ܘܰܡܨܰܠܶܐ ܥܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ. ܐܶܢ ܕܶܝܢ ܐܳܠܶܨ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܝܰܨܪܳܟ: ܘܰܡܨܰܠܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܥܰܠ ܡܰܢ݁ ܕܡܳܚܶܐ ܠܳܟ: ܘܡܶܫܬ݁ܺܝܰܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܥܰܡܶܗ: ܚܳܐܶܫ
2. Therefore, these are the passions of the Lord: When He gives His cheek to the one striking Him and speaks peacefully with him and prays for him. If, therefore, you compel yourself to pray for him who struck you, and enter into peace with him, you sympathize with the Lord and are glorified with Him.
ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܥܰܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܒ݁ܰܚ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܥܰܡܶܗ܀ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܢܳܐ ܚܰܫܳܐ. ܡܳܪܰܢ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܥܒ݁ܰܕ݂ ܘܰܡܫܝܰܓ ܪܶܓ݂ܠܶܐ ܕܡܰܢ ܕ݁ܰܡܙܰܒ݂ܰܢ ܠܶܗ: ܘܡܰܫܠܶܡ ܠܶܗ ܠܡܰܘܬܳܐ: ܘܗܳܘܶܐ ܚܰܒܪܳܐ ܠܩܳܛܘܽܠܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ: ܘܡܰܘܬܶܒ ܠܶܗ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܩܳܐܶܡ ܩܕ݂ܳܡܘܗ̱ܝ ܐܝܟ ܥܰܒܕ݂ܳܐ: ܘܰܡܫܝܰܓ ܠܶܗ ܪܶܓ݁ܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܠܗܰܘ ܣܳܢܬܶܗ ܡܶܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܕܰܢܫܝܓ ܠܪ̈ܰܚܝܡܰܘܗ̱ܝ. ܫܶܚܠܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܬܰܠܡܺܝܕ݂ܶܐ ܗܘܳܝܘܿ ܣܟܰܪܝܘܺܛܶܐ ܓܰܢܳܒܳܐ: ܘܫܶܡܥܘܿܢ ܪܝܺܫܳܐ: ܘܫܰܪܝܺ ܒܰܣܟܰܪܝܘܺܛܳܐ ܘܫܰܠܶܡ ܒܫܶܡܥܘܿܢ. ܐܶܢ ܗܳܟܝܽܠ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܡܰܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܰܫܠܡܳܢܰܝܟ ܘܰܡܙܰܒܢܳܢܰܝܟ ܘܚܰܒܪ̈ܶܐ ܕܩܳܛܘܽܠܰܝܟ: ܘܐܳܠܶܨ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܝܰܨܪܳܟ ܘܡܰܘܬܶܒ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܗܘܽܢ: ܘܰܡܫܝܰܓ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܗܘܢ ܪܶܓܠܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܘܡܰܫܘܶܝܬ ܠܗܶܝܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܪܶܓ݂ܠܶܐ ܕܚܰܒܪ̈ܳܬܳܟ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܰܘܕܰܥ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܕܣܳܢܰܝܟ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܠܳܐ ܦܰܪܣܝܳܗܝ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܠܣܟܰܪܝܘܽܛܳܐ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܐܶܡܝܪ ܕܚܰܕ݂ ܡܶܢܟܘܽܢ ܣܳܛܢܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܘܐܝܳܕ݁ܶܗ ܕܡܰܫܠܡܳܢܝ ܥܰܡܝ ܒܠܰܓܬ݁ܳܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܬܟܰܫܠܘܽܢ ܬܰܠܡܺܝܕܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܘܢܺܐܡܪܘܽܢ: ܕܰܐܝܟܰܢ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܕܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܡܰܢ ܡܰܫܠܶܡ ܠܶܗ ܠܡܰܘܬܳܐ ܘܢܶܛܥܘܽܢ ܡܳܐ ܕܰܗܘܰܝ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܘܐܰܪܚܶܩ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܒܰܦܔܰܪ. ܠܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܠܳܕܶܠ ܠܰܢ: ܘܠܳܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܡܶܬܟ݂ܰܫܰܠ ܒ݁ܗܳܕܶܐ ܕ݁ܠܳܐ ܡܦܰܪܣܶܐ ܐ݇ܢ̱ܬ ܠܡܰܫܠܡܳܢܰܝܟ. ܘܰܚܙܝܺ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܠܳܐ ܦܰܪܣܝܳܗܝ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܰܘܕܳܥܘܽ ܐܰܘܕ݁ܰܥ ܕܚܳܕ݂ܶܩ ܗܘ ܟ݁ܽܠܕ݁ܶܡ. ܐܳܦ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܡܳܐ ܕ݁ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܶܗ ܠܩܳܛܘܽܠܳܟ݂ ܕܠܳܥܶܣ ܥܰܡܳܟ݂ ܥܰܡ ܣܰܓܝܳܐܶܐ: ܐܶܢ ܐܶܡܰܪ̱ܬ ܕܩܳܛܘܽܠܝ ܠܳܥܶܣ ܥܰܡܝ: ܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܺܐܡܰܪ ܫܡܶܗ ܘܬܰܒܗܶܬܝܘܽܗ̱ܝ. ܘܰܚܙܝܺ ܟܡܳܐ ܐܠܨܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ ܬܰܠܡܺܝܕ݂ܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܕܢܺܐܡܰܪ ܠܗܘܢ ܫܡܶܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܠܡܰܚܝܣܶܝܢ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܐܰܠܨܶܗ ܗܰܘ ܒܰܪ ܪܳܐܙܶܗ ܕܩܰܕܶܡ ܥܰܠ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܒܪܳܐܙܶܗ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܚܰܒܪ̈ܰܘܗ̱ܝ: ܘܰܐܟܚܶܕ݂ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ
3. Another passion of the Lord is when, subjecting Himself, He washes the feet of the one selling and betraying Him to death, who became a companion of His murderers; and the Lord, assigning him a seat, stands before him, as a servant, and washes the feet of that enemy of His before His friends; for the figment of the disciples is Iscariot, the thief, and Simon the head; and beginning from Iscariot He ended at Simon. If, therefore, you know who your betrayers and sellers are and the companions of your murderers and you repress your spirit and, having assigned them a seat, you wash and dry their feet before the feet of your friends and do not indicate to them that they are your haters, just as the Lord did not slander Iscariot; but what He said: 'One of you is a devil and the hand of my betrayer is with me in the dish': lest His disciples should suffer scandal saying: 'How could He say, "I am the Lord," not knowing who was about to betray Him to death?' and fall into error by these deeds, with the Lord absent in the flesh. But no one reproaches us, nor is anyone scandalized that you do not slander your betrayers. And see that the Lord did not slander, but by indicating He indicated that He knew everything. You too, if you know your murderer is eating with you with others, if you say: 'My killer is eating with me,' do not betray his name and confuse him! And see how much the disciples solicited the Lord to tell them his name, but He did not say it even barely, when the companion of His secrets urged Him, to whom His secrets were familiar before his companions and in whom the Lord trusted, because he was like His heart; and He reluctantly betrayed the secret to him, until Judas himself had said: 'I am,' and betrayed himself, although the Lord did not betray him. If you do so to your sellers and betrayers, then you sympathize with the Lord and progress much.


[p. 420] {#po.0.p420}


[p. 421] {#po.0.p421}


[p. 422] {#po.0.p422}
ܥܠ ܘܟܗ̱ܝ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܐܚܝܟ ܠܝܟܗ ܗܘّ: ܘܰܠܡܰܚܣܶܢ ܐܰܘܕܥܶܝܗ ܒܪܳܐ: ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܐܳܦ݂ ܝܰܙܘܕܳܐ ܢܺܐܡܰܪ ܕܐܶܢܳܐ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ: ܘܦܰܪܣܝܺ ܗܘܽ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܟܰܕ ܡܳܚܰܢ ܠܳܐ ܦ݁ܰܪܣܝܶܗ. ܡܳܐ ܕܰܥܒܰܕܬ ܗܳܟܰܢ ܠܡܰܙܰܒܢܳܢܰܝܳܟ܂ ܘܰܠܡܰܫܠܡܳܢܰܝܺܟ: ܗܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܗ̱ܘ ܚܳܐܶܫ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܥܰܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܣܰܓܝ ܝܳܪܶܒ ܐ݇ܢ̱ܬ܀ ܬܘܒ ܚܰܫܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܺܢܳܐ. ܡܳܪܰܢ ܟ݁ܰܕ ܡܰܐܣܶܐ ܐܶܕ݂ܢܶܗ ܕܗܰܘ ܕ݁ܰܢܣܰܒ ܣܰܝܦܿܳܐ ܘܐܶܬܳܐ ܕܢܶܩܛܠܶܗ. ܐܶܢ ܐܳܠܶܨ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܗܳܟܝܶܠ ܢܰܦܫܳܟ ܘܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܫܰܦܝܪ
4. Likewise another passion: The Lord heals the ear of him who, taking the sword to kill Him, came. If you, therefore, compel yourself to do what is good to him who


[p. 423] {#po.0.p423}
ܠܡܰܢ ܕܨܳܒ݂ܶܐ ܠܡܰܡܩܛܠܳܟ: ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܡܶܬܓܰܡܪܰܐ܀
wants to kill you, you will be perfected in like manner.
ܬܘܒ ܚܰܫܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܢܳܐ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܟܰܕ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܒܰܨܠܘܽܬܳܐ: ܐܰܒ݁ܳܐ ܫܒܘܩ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܠܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܚܰܦܝܘ ܪܝܺܫܝ ܘܰܡܚܰܝܐܘܽܢܝ ܒܚܽܘܛܪܳܐ ܘܰܣܶܦܘ ܦܰܟܰܝ̈ ܒܒܘܽܙܳܚܳܐ: ܘܐܰܫܩܝܘܽܢܝ ܚܰܠܳܐ ܘܰܡܪܳܪܶܐ ܒܚܶܡܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܒ݁ܠܺܝܛܬ݁ܳܐ: ܘܡܰܡܬܚܘܽܢܝ ܥܰܠ ܙܩܝܼܦܳܐ ܒܪܘܰܓ݂ܙܳܐ: ܘܒ݁ܰܙܰܥܘ ܐܝܺܕ݁ܰܝ ܘܪܶܓ݁ܠܰܝ ܒ݁ܣܶܢܶܐܬ݂ܳܐ: ܘܕܰܩܪܘܽܢܝ ܒܪܘܰܡܚܳܐ ܒܰܝܒܥܶܠܕܒܳܝܒܘܽܬܳܐ. ܐܳܦ ܐܢܬ ܐܶܢ ܐܳܠܶܨ ܐܵܢ̱ܬ ܝܰܨܪܳܟ ܘܐܳܡܰܪ ܐܰܢܬ: ܡܳܪܝ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ: ܦܒܘܩ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܠܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܰܥܒܰܕ݂ܘ ܠܝܺ ܒܚܺܝ̈ܳܬܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ
5. Another passion: The Lord says while praying: 'Father, forgive those who covered my head, struck me with a reed, buffeted my cheeks with mockery, gave me vinegar and gall to drink with fury and curses, stretched me upon the cross with anger, pierced my hands and feet with hatred, and stabbed me with a lance with enmity.' You too, if you crush your mind saying: 'My Lord Jesus, forgive those who have done evil to me, just as they did to you yourself, Lord of both ages,' you will be greatly glorified with the Lord.
ܕܰܥܒܰܕ݂ܘ ܠܳܟ ܕܝܳܠܳܡ ܡܳܪܶܐ ܬܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܥܳܠܝܡܐ: ܣܰܓܝܺ ܡܶܫܬܰܒܚܰܬ ܥܰܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ܀ ܬܘܒ ܚܰܫܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܺܢܳܐ. ܡܳܪܰܢ ܟܰܕ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܠܬܰܠܡܺܝܕ݂ܰܘܗ̱ܝ: ܕܐܰܘ ܢܺܐܙܰܠ ܠܘܳܬ ܗܳܢܘܽܢ ܕܪܰܓܡܘܽܢܝ ܐܶܬܡܳܠܝ ܘܢܰܠܶܦ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܰܟܝܺܟܘܽܬܳܐ. ܐܳܡܪܝܺܢ ܠܶܗ: ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܝܺܗ̱ܘܽܕܳܢܶܐ ܒܳܥܶܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܕܢܶܩܛܠܘܽܢܳܟ. ܐܳܡܰܪ ܠܗܘܽܢ: ܬܰܘ ܘܠܳܐ ܬܶܬܕܰܟܪܘܽܢ ܡܶܝܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܒܝܫ ܕܰܥܒܰܕ݂ܘ ܠܟܘܽܢ ܒܕܰܡܫܳܐ ܠܨܰܦܪܳܐ ܘܐܶܬ݁ܕ݁ܰܡܝܽܘ ܒܶܗ ܬܰܠܡܺܝ̈ܕ݂ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܘܐܶܡܰܪܘ: ܕ݁ܢܺܐܙܰܠ ܢܡܘܬ ܥܰܡܶܗ ܕܢܺܚܝܐ ܥܰܡܶܗ. ܐܶܢ ܗܳܟܶܝܠ ܡܳܐܶܬ ܐܰܢܬ ܥܰܡܶܗ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܢܰܚܝܡܰܬ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܩܰܠܝܼܠ ܘܗܳܘܶܐ ܐ݇ܢܬ ܠܥܶܠ ܡܶܢ ܡܰܘܬܳܐ. ܥܕܰܡܳܐ ܘ̱ܘ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܠܡܰܘܬܳܐ ܡܶܬܐܳܠܶܨ܂ ܡܰܢ ܕ݁ܚܳܐܶܫ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܚܰܫ̈ܶܐ܀
6. Another passion: The Lord says to his disciples: 'Come, let us go to those who stoned me yesterday, and we will teach them humility.' They say to him: 'Lord, the Jews wanted to kill you.' He says to them: 'Come and do not remember any evil that they brought upon you in the evening, in the morning.' And the disciples, intending to imitate him, said: 'Let us go, let us die with him, that we may live with him.' If, therefore, you have died with him, you will also be resurrected a little later and will be above death: for he who suffers these passions is afflicted even unto death.


[p. 424] {#po.0.p424}
ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܚܰܫܶܐ ܘܕܳܡܶܝܢ ܠܗܘܿܢ. ܐܲܢ ܡܒܰܪܶܟ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܠܳܐܶܛ ܠܳܟ ܘܪܳܚܶܝܡ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܣܳܢܶܐ ܠܳܟ ܘܰܡܨܰܠܶܐ ܐܰܢ݈ܬ ܥܰܠ ܡܢ ܕܪܳܕ݂ܶܦ ܠܳܟ ܘܫܳܒܶܩ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܡܰܡܣܟܶܠ ܒܳܟ ܫܰܒܥܝܺܢ ܥܰܠ ܫܒܰܥ ܒܝܰܘܡܳܐ ܚܰܕ. ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܥܰܠ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕܟܽܠܳܟ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܪܓܰܙ ܥܰܠ ܡܰܢ ܕܚܳܛܶܐ ܒܳܟ. ܘܐܶܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܛܦܝܼܣ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ: ܕ݁ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܢܰܟܠܺܝܟ ܕܠܳܐ ܬܶܪܓ݁ܰܙ ܠܰܓܡܳܪ: ܐܶܡܰܪ ܕܰܫܒܘܽܩ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܟܽܠܗܶܝܢ ܣܰܟ݁̈ܠܘܳܬܳܐ ܒܝܰܘܡܳܐ ܚܰܕ݂: ܡܳܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܐܶܢ ܐܝܺܬ ܒܪܶܠܝܳܢܳܟ ܕܡܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܫܠܳܡܺܝ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐܰܪܒܰܥܡܳܐܐ ܘܐܶܫܥܝܺܢ ܣܰܟ݁̈ܠܘܳܢ ܬ݁ܶܪܓܰܙ ܥܰܠ ܡܰܡܣܟܠܳܢܳܐ: ܗܘܰܝܬ ܡܳܢܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܨܰܦܪܳܐ ܠܨܰܦܪܳܐ ܠܺܝܠܰܝ ܐܝܺܡܳܡ: ܘܐܶܢ ܐܰܣܟ݁ܶܠ ܒܰܪ ܒܶܣܪܳܟ ܐܰܪܒܰܥܡܳܐܐ ܘܐܶܫܥܝܢ ܣܰܟ݁̈ܠܘܳܢ: ܕܗܳܘܶܐ ܚܘܽܫܒܳܢܗܶܝܢ ܕܫܰܒܥܝܺܢ ܥܰܠ ܫܒܰܥ: ܐܶܢ ܐܶܫܟܰܚܬ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܡܰܡܣܟܠܳܢܳܐ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܟ݁ܽܠܗܶܝܢ ܣܰܟ݁̈ܠܘܳܬܳܐ ܠܰܝܠܺܝ ܐܝܺܡܳܡ: ܡܰܦ݁ܰܣ ܠܳܟ ܕܬܶܪܓܰܙ ܡܳܢܶܗ. ܐܶܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܐܳܚܶܕ݂ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܥܰܠ ܡܰܣܟ݁ܠܳܢܳܐ: ܐܳܦ݂ܠܳܐ ܚܰܡܫ ܐܰܘ ܥܣܰܪ: ܠܳܐ ܗܳܐ ܐܶܬܝܰܕ݂ܥܰܬ ܠܳܗ ܕܰܟܠܳܟ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܒܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܬܶܪܓܰܙ ܥܰܠ ܡܰܡܣܟܠܳܢܳܐ܆ ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ: ܡܳܐ ܕܰܪܚܶܡܬܳܝܗ̱ܝ ܘܰܦܪܰܥܬܳܝܗ̱ܝ ܛܳܒ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܚܠܳܦ ܒܧܝ̈ܫܳܬܳܐ: ܘܐܰܫܓܬ݀ ܠܶܗ ܪ̈ܶܓ݂ܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܘܨܰܠܝܺܬ ܥܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ: ܗܳܝܕ݂ܶܝܢ ܡܶܬܓܡܰܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܬܶܐܠܶܨ ܢܰܦܫܳܟ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܒܳܥܶܐ ܕܢܶܩܛܠܳܟ ܘܢܶܬܛܰܪܛܰܪ ܒܳܟ ܘܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܟܽܠ ܥܰܡ ܟ݁ܽܠ: ܘܰܡܬܰܠܡܶܕ݂ ܐܰܢ݈ܬ ܚܰܛܺܝ̈ܐܶܐ ܘܙܰܢܝ̈ܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܢܳܕ݂ܰܐ ܠܳܟ ܡܶܢ ܛܰܡ̈ܐܶܐ ܘܡܶܢ ܪ̈ܰܫܝܳܥܶܐ: ܘܡܶܢ ܐܰܝܠܺܝܢ ܕܐܝܺܬ
7. These are the passions, and those which are similar to them: if you bless him who curses you, and love those who hate you, and pray for him who persecutes you, and forgive him who sins against you seventy times seven in one day, concerning which the Lord said: do not be angry at all with him who sins against you. If, however, you cannot restrain yourself from being angry at all, he said: forgive all these offenses in one day. Therefore, if you have the will, having finished these four hundred and ninety offenses, to be angry with the delinquent: count from morning until morning, day and night; and if the son of your flesh has sinned against you four hundred and ninety times (which is the calculation of seventy times seven offenses): if afterwards you find him delinquent in all these offenses day and night: it is permitted for you to be angry with him. If, however, you do not even have five or ten offenses against the delinquent, is it not clear that the Lord by this word has forbidden you to be angry with the delinquent? That is: after you have loved him and repaid him with good for evil and washed his feet and prayed for him: then you will be perfect, handing yourself over to him who wants to kill you and harasses you; and you will be all things to all people and will teach sinners and harlots, nor will you abhor the unclean and the impious and those in whom the gangrene


[p. 425] {#po.0.p425}


[p. 426] {#po.0.p426}


[p. 427] {#po.0.p427}
ܒܗܘܢ ܙܰܚܠܺܝܬܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܚܛܝܳܬܳܐ ܘܡܰܐܣܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܟ݂ܽܠ ܕ݁ܐܳܬ݁ܶܐ ܠܐܝܺܕܰܝܟ: ܐܰܝܟ݁ ܐܳܣܳܐ ܛܳܒܳܐ܀
of sin is, and you will heal all who come to you like a skilled physician.
ܐܶܢ ܚܳܐܶܫ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܗܳܟ݂ܰܢ: ܛܘ̈ܒܶܝܗ ܠܢܰܦܫܳܟ݂ ܕܡܶܬ݁ܕ݁ܰܟܶܐ ܠܶܒܳܟ ܘܚܳܙܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ. ܗܳܟܰܢ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܥܒܰܕ݂ ܐܶܣܛܶܦ݁ܰܢܳܘܣ ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܒܰܨܠܘܽܬܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܛܰܒܰܥܘ ܟܺܝ̈ܦܶܐ܂ ܒܡܘܽܚܰܘܗܝ: ܕܠܳܐ ܬܶܬܚܫܶܒ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܚܛܝܺܬܳܐ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܕܡܶܛܠܳܬܝ: ܠܳܐ ܬܰܣܒܰܪ ܠܺܝ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܗ̱ܘ ܨܰܠܝܺ ܥܰܠ ܩܳܛܘܽܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂. ܘܰܫܠܝܺܚܶܐ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐܶܡܰܪܘ ܠܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܰܡܚܰܪܩܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܫܶܢܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ ܥܠܰܝܗܘܽܢ: ܓܰܒܪ̈ܶܐ ܐܰܚܰܝ̈ܢ: ܐܰܢ̱ܬ݁ܘܽܢ ܫܘܽܡܥܘܽܢ ܘܰܚܝܰܘ. ܚܠܳܦ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܢܰܢ ܒܳܥܶܝܢܰܢ ܡܶܢܟܘܽܢ ܕܬܶܐܛܦܝܼܣܘܽܢ. ܘܰܒܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܩܳܛܠܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܠܗܘܽܢ: ܡܨܰܠܶܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܥܰܠ ܩܳܛܘܽܠܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕ݁ܰܥܒܰܕ݂ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܠܥܰܝܢܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ. ܘܡܳܐ ܕܐܶܙܰܠܘ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܕܢܶܩܛܠܘܽܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܠܒܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܡܕ݂ܝܰܢ̱ܬܳܐ: ܩܳܝܡܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܘܡܰܪܬ݁ܶܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܠܗܘܢ ܕܢܺܚܘܽܢ: ܘܟܶܢ ܝܽܗܒܝܺܢ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܢܰܦܫܗܘܽܢ ܠܩܶܛܠܳܐ. ܘܡܳܐ ܕܰܬܠܰܘ ܐܢܘܽܢ ܒܰܙܩܝܺܦܳܐ: ܗܳܐ ܡܰܪܬ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܘܡܰܠܦܝܺܢ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܙܩܝܺܦܝܺܢ. ܫܘܽܒܚܳܐ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܡܫܝܺܚܳܝܐ: ܕܚܰܫ ܠܒܰܪ ܡܶܢܗܘܽܢ ܘܚܰܫܘ ܥܰܡܗ ܒܶܗ. ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܚܰܫ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܘܰܗܘܳܐ ܠܰܢ ܚܰܘܪܳܐ ܕܢܶܬܕܰܡܶܐ ܒܶܗ ܘܢܶܚܰܫ ܠܗ ܒܗ ܘܒܰܕܡܘܽܬܶܗ ܢܗܰܠܶܟ݂. ܫܘܽܒܚܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܕܝܺܠܶܗ ܘܛܘܽܒܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܠܗܘܽܢ. ܡܳܪܰܢ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܓܠܪܰܢ ܡܶܢܳܟ ܘܡܶܢ ܠܘܳܬܗܘܽܢ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܥܰܡܳܟ݂ ܘܥܰܡܗܘܽܢ ܢܶܚܕ݁ܶܐ ܒܦܰܪܨܘܽܦ݁ܳܟ܀
8. If you have suffered in this way, your soul will be blessed, because your heart will be cleansed and you will see the Lord. For thus did Stephen, saying in his prayer for those who were fixing stones into his brain: 'May this sin not be imputed to them on my account,' so that you might not think that only the Lord prayed for his murderers. And all the Apostles said to those who were gnashing their teeth at them: 'Men, you are our brothers. Hear us and live. We beseech you for God's sake to obey.' And until they killed them, they prayed for their murderers, just as the Lord did before them. And when they had come to kill them outside the city, standing, they exhorted them to live, and then they handed over their soul to them for slaughter. And after they had suspended them on the cross, behold, exhorting, they taught those who crucified them. Glory to the Lord Jesus Christ, who suffered outside of them, with whom they suffered, that is, who alone suffered, having become an example to us, that we might imitate him and suffer with him in him and walk after his likeness. Glory to him and blessedness to them. O Lord, would that we might not be separated from you and from them, but that we might rejoice with you and with them before your face!


[p. 428] {#po.0.p428}


[p. 429] {#po.0.p429}
ܐܶܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܨܳܒܿܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܬ݂ܶܕ݂ܰܥ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܪ̈ܳܐܙܶܐ: ܠܳܐ ܬ݂ܶܦܠܶܐ ܠܰܡܨܰܠܳܝܘ ܘܠܰܡܫܰܐܶܠܘ̈ ܠܟܽܠܢܳܫ: ܘܠܳܐ ܬܶܒ݁ܣܶܐ ܥܰܠ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ: ܕܰܟܒܰܪ ܗܰܘ ܕܒܳܣܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܥܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ: ܗܘ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܠܶܗ ܠܰܫܪܳܪܳܐ ܘܰܡܦܰܫܶܩ ܠܳܟ. ܘܰܗܘܰܝܬ ܡܶܬܡܰܟܟܰܟ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܘܡܶܬܪܟܶܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܘܰܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܓܰܒܪܳܐ ܕܐܳܙܶܠ ܠܰܐܰܬ݂ܪܳܐ ܪ̈ܰܚܺܝܩܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܠܰܡܕ݂ܝܺܢ̱ܬ݁ܳܐ ܦܠܳܢܝܺܬ: ܘܠܳܐ ܒܳܣܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܛܰܠܝܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܣܳܒܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܚܓܺܝܪܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܡܰܢ ܕܰܣܢܶܐ ܚܶܙܘܳܐ ܕܐܰܦ̈ܰܘܗ̱ܝ: ܘܠܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܬ݁ܳܐ ܒܳܣܶܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܫܰܐܶܠ ܠܟܽܠܡܰܢ ܕܦܳܓ݁ܰܥ ܒܶܗ: ܕ݁ܰܢܬ݁ܰܪܨܶܗ ܠܰܐܰܝܟܳܐ ܕܒܳܥܶܐ ܕܢܺܐܙܰܠ. ܗܳܟ݂ܰܢ ܐܳܦ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܒܳܥܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܬܺܐܙܰܠ ܠܰܡܕ݂ܝܺܢ̱ܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܶܒ݁ܣܶܐ ܥܰܠ ܚܰܕ݂ ܡܢ ܙܥܘܽܪܶܐ ܘܫܰܦܠܶܐ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܗܘܰܝܬ ܡܫܰܐܶܠ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܒܡܰܟܝܳܟܘܽܬܳܐ: ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܡܰܢ ܕܰܡܚܰܘܶܐ ܠܳܟ ܐܘܽܪܚܳܐ
9. If, however, you wish to know these mysteries, do not cease to pray and to ask everyone, nor despise anyone; for perhaps he whom you despise knows the truth and explains it to you. And humble yourself and bow down before God and before all men, like a man going into a distant region, or into some certain city, who does not despise a boy or an old man, nor a lame man or one foul of countenance, nor does he despise a woman, but asks all who meet him to direct him to where he wishes to arrive. Similarly you, who desire to arrive at the heavenly city, do not despise any of the least and vile, but with humility ask until you find someone who can show you the heavenly way, so that you may arrive at the heavenly home and enter to God, who will prepare joy for you.


[p. 430] {#po.0.p430}
ܫܡܰܝܡܳܝܬܳܐ: ܕܬ݂ܺܐܙܰܠ ܠܒܰܝܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ: ܘܥܳܐܶܠ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܘܳܬ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܰܡܚܰܕܶܐ ܠܳܟ܀ ܠܚܡ ܡܺܐܡܪܳܐ ܕܰܒܬ݂ܰܥܣܰܪ ܕܥܰܠ ܚܰܫܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܰܗܘܳܐ ܠܰܢ ܒܗܘܽܢ ܚܰܘܪܳܐ܀
The seventeenth discourse on the passions of the Lord, by which he became an example to us, ends.
