ܗܶܢܘܽܢ ܕܡܰܡܠܶܠ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܒܗܰܘ ܝܰܘܡܳܐ ܕ݂ܕ݂ܺܝܢܳܐ ܘܩܳܝܡܺܝܢ ܒܰܥܒܳܕܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ ܒܝ̈ܺܫܶܐ: ܥܰܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܛܰܪܘ ܦܘܽܩܕܳܢܰܘܗ̱ܝ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܠܒܶܫ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܗܰܘ ܓܰܝܒܪܳܐ ܡܢ ܨܶܐܬܳܐ: ܕܐܶܚܺܝܕܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܥܒܳܕ݁ܶܐ ܒܚ̈ܰܝܶܐ ܕܰܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ܀ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܫܡܰܥܘܽܢܝ ܘܰܢܛܰܝܶܒ ܠܰܢ ܥܒܳܕ݁ܶܐ ܛܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܕܐܝܬܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܢܰܚ̈ܬ݂ܶܐ ܕܡܶܬܩܰܒܠܝܺܢ ܠܳܒܫܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ ܒܶܝܬ ܡܳܪܰܢ. ܡܳܪܰܢ ܠܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܩܳܪܶܐ ܠܥܰܬܝܰܪܶܐ ܘܰܠܡܶܣܟܺܢܶܐ ܘܰܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܠܳܐ ܒܳܐܶܛ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܠܛܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܘܰܠܒܝ̈ܺܫܶܐ ܠܟܽܠ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܕܐܳܬܶܒ݂
17. Nevertheless, listen to me, and let us compare for ourselves the good works, which are garments; if anyone puts them on, they will be acceptable before the Lord. The Lord invites everyone: the rich and the poor, and He despises no one, but receives all men, good and bad, who


[p. 577] {#po.0.p577}
ܘܡܶܬܦܢܶܐ ܠܘܳܬܶܗ ܡܩܰܒ݁ܶܠ ܠܶܗ܂ ܝܰܘܡܳܐ ܪܰܒܳܐ ܕܕ݂ܺܝܢܳܐ ܐܝܺܬ ܒܶܝܬ ܓܰܙܶܗ ܕܨ ܠܟ݁ܽܠ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܐܝܟ ܥܒܳܕ݁̈ܰܘܗ̱ܝ܂ ܘܒܰܪ ܥܳܕ݂ ܥܳܢܶܐ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܢܳܛܰܪ ܡܶܠܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܘܒܳܥܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܐܰܝܟܰܢܳܐ ܕܦܰܪܦܶܫ ܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܕܩܘܽܕܫܳܐ ܒܕ݂ܰܘܝܰܕ݂ ܐܳܡܪܳܐ ܕܡܶܬܚܙܶܐ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܒܫܘܽܒܚܶܗ ܘܡܶܬܦܢܶܐ ܠ ܨܠܘܳܬܳܐ ܕܡܶܣܟܺܢܶܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܫܳܐܶܛ ܨܠܘܳܬܗܘܽܢ ܬܶܟ݂ܬ݁ܶܒ݂ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܠܕ݂ܳܪܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܝܳܐ: ܘܥܰܡܳܐ ܕܡܶܬܒܪܶܐ ܢܫܰܒ݁ܰܚ ܠܡܳܪܝܳܐ. ܡܶܛܠ ܕܐܰܕ݂ܚܺܩ ܡܶܢ ܡܪܰܘܡܳܐ ܕܩܘܽܕܫܶܗ: ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܠܰܐܪܥܳܐ ܐܰܒܰܩ: ܠܡܶܫܡܰܥ ܐܶܢܰܩܬܶܗ ܕܐܰܣܝܪܳܐ. ܘܰܠܡܶܫܪܳܐ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܡܰܘܬܳܐ. ܚܳܙܶܝܬ ܕܡܶܬܦܢܶܐ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܨܠܘܿܬܳܐ ܕܡܶܣܟܺܢ̈ܶܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܫܳܐܶܛ ܨܠܘܳܬܗܘܽܢ ܘܒܳܥܘܳܬܗܘܽܢ. ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܠܡܳܢ ܬܶܬܟܬܶܒ݂ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܘܢܶܚܙܘܳܢܳܗ ܠܕ݂ܳܪܳܐ ܐ݈ܚܪܳܢܳܐ ܘܢܶܒܥܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܫܪܳܪܳܗ. ܘܢܶܓܠܶܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܥܽܘܡܩܺܝܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܥܘܽܬܪܳܐ ܕܚܶܟܡܬܶܗ ܕܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܡܫܺܝܚܳܝܐ. ܘܰܢܗܰܝܡܢܘܽܢ ܒܶܗ ܘܢܺܐܡܪܘܽܢ ܗܳܟܰܢ: ܨܘܰܬ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܨܠܘܳܬܰܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܬܰܗܡܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܒܳܥܘܳܬܰܢ܂ ܫܡܰܥܰܝܢ ܘܰܥܢܰܝܢ ܘܐܶܬܦ݂ܰܢ ܠܰܓ݂ܥܳܬ݂ܰܢ ܘܰܫܡܰܥܰܝܢ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܒܥܶܠܕ݁ܒܳܒܰܢ ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܐܘܰܠܨܳܢܳܐ ܕܰܚܛܳܗܳܬܳܐ. ܘܢܰܓܪܘܽܢ ܪܘܽܚܗܘܽܢ ܘܢܺܐܡܪܘܽܢ: ܪܰܚܶܡ ܥܠܰܝܢ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܐܝܟ ܛܰܝܒܘܳܬܳܟ݂ ܘܐܰܝܟ ܣܘܺܓ݂ܐܳܐ ܕ݂̈ܰܚܡܰܝܟ ܥܛܺܝ ܚ̈ܛܳܗܰܝܢ. ܐܰܣܓ݂ܳܐ ܐܰܫܺܝܓ݂ܰܢ ܡܶܢ ܥܰܘܠܰܢ: ܘܡܶܢ ܚ̈ܛܳܗܰܝܢ ܕܰܟܳܢ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܣܰܟܠܘܳܬܰܢ ܝܳܕ݂ܥܺܝܢܰܢ ܐ̱ܢܰܚܢܰܢ: ܘܰܚܛܳܗܰܝܺܢ ܠܩܘܰܒ݂ܠܰܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܒܟ݁ܽܠܙܒܰܢ. ܠܳܟ ܗ̱ܘ ܡܳܪܝ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕܰܝܟ݁ ܚܛܺܝܢܰܢ ܘܒܝ̈ܺܫܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܩܕܳܡܝܟ ܥܒܰܕܼܢܰܢ: ܡܳܪܝ ܚܙܺܝ ܕܐܶܬܡܰܙܓܰܬ ܒܰܢ ܚܛܺܝܬܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܡܰܪܒ݁ܥܳܐ. ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕ݁ܺܝܢ ܒܩܘܽܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܨܒܰܝܬ: ܐܰܘܕܰܥܬܰܢ ܟ݁ܶܣܝ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܕܚܶܟܡܬ݁ܳܟ ܘܐܶܙܕܰܕܰܩܢܰܢ ܒܡܶܠܬܳܟ݂. ܪܘܽܣ ܒܶܗ ܘܚܰܘܪܰܢܝ ܛܳܒ ܡܶܢ ܬܰܠܓܳܐ. ܘܐܰܦܢܳܐ ܐܰܦܰܝܟ ܡܶܢ ܥܰܘܠܰܢ ܘܚܙܺܝ ܒܡܰܟܺܝܟܽܘܬܰܢ ܘܒܰܬܝܳܒܽܘܬܰܢ. ܘܰܫܠܺܝ ܣܰܟܠܺܘܳܬܰܢ ܘܗܰܒ ܠܰܢ ܒܘܰܣܳܝܡܺܝܟ ܘܚܰܕ݂ܘܳܬܳܟ݂: ܘܢܶܚܝܕܘܽܢ ܓܰܪ̈ܡܰܝܢ ܕܐܶܬܡܰܟܟܰܝܘ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܙܝܺܘܳܟ. ܘܢܶܬܡܰܟܰܟ݂ ܒܰܫܪܳܪܳܐ ܗܰܘ ܒ݁ܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܥܰܬܝܺܩܳܐ: ܕܐܶܬܚܰܒܰܠ ܒܐܰܪ̈ܓܝܺܓ݂ܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܛܘܽܥܝܳܝ: ܘܢܶܠܒܰܫ ܒܰܕ݂ܡܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܰܒܪܳܝܗ̱ܝ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܡܫܝܺܚܳܐ: ܘܢܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܓܰܕ̈ܡܰܥܝܢ ܡܰܒܟ̈ܝܳܢܶܐ ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܢܶܫܡܰܥ ܠܰܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܥܳܢܶܐ ܠܰܢ ܘܡܰܦ݁ܢܶܐ ܠܰܢ ܠܘܳܬܶܗ ܘܐܳܣܰܪ ܠܰܢ ܒܪܶܚܡܬ݁ܶܗ ܘܦܳܪܶܩ ܠܰܢ ܡܶܢ ܫܘܽܥܒܳܕ݂ܳܐ ܕܥܰܒܕ݂ܘܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܡܰܘܬܳܐ ܘܒܳܪܶܐ ܒܰܢ ܠܶܒܳܐ ܕܰܟܝܳܐ ܘܰܡܚܰܕܶܐ ܒܰܢ ܪܘܽܚܶܗ ܬܩܺܝܢܬܳܐ ܘܗܳܘܶܝܢܰܢ ܒܪܝܺܬ݁ܳܐ ܚܕ݂ܰܬܳܐ ܘܰܡܫܰܒܚܝܺܢܰܢ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܐܶܬ݂ܪܰܚܰܡ܂ ܥܠܰܝܢ ܒܕ݂ܳܪܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܝܳܐ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܐܰܕ݂ܚܺܩ ܡܶܢ ܡܪܰܘܡܳܐ ܕܩܘܽܕ݂ܫܶܗ ܘܰܫܡܰܥ ܐܶܢܰܩܬܰܢ ܕܐܰܣܝܪܝܺܢ
do penance and turn to Him; and on that great day of judgment, He has [treasures] in His treasury to render to each according to his works. And He will quickly grant the request of him who keeps His words and implores Him, as the Holy Spirit explained, saying through David: The Lord will appear in His glory and will turn to the prayer of the poor, and He does not despise their prayer. Let this be written for the last generation, and the people who shall be created shall praise the Lord, because He looked down from His high sanctuary: the Lord looked from heaven to earth, to hear the groaning of the prisoner and to deliver the children from death. You see the Lord turning to the prayer of the poor, and not despising their petitions and prayers; for these things are written down so that they may see them until the last generation and seek His truth from God, and He may reveal to them the depth of the riches of the wisdom of Jesus Christ, and those who believe in Him may say thus: Hear, O God, our prayer and do not neglect our petitions: hear us and answer us and turn to our cry and hear us because of our adversary and the tribulation of sin. And let them say patiently: Have mercy on us, O God, according to Thy grace: and according to the multitude of Thy mercy blot out our sins. Wash us more and more from our iniquity and cleanse us from our sins. For we know our iniquities and our sins are always before us. Against Thee, O Lord, alone have we sinned and done evil before Thee. See, O Lord, that sin is mingled with us from the womb: but Thou hast loved truth, Thou hast shown us the hidden things of Thy wisdom, and by Thy word we have been justified. Sprinkle us with the hyssop of Thy grace and cleanse us and purify us by its aid and whiten us above snow and turn Thy face from our iniquity and look upon our humility and our penance and blot out our iniquities and give us Thy delights and joys, and our bones, humbled before Thy splendor, shall rejoice. And let the old man, corrupted by the desires of error, be truly humbled, and let him put on the new man, renewed in good works after the likeness of Him whom the Lord Jesus Christ created; and let our bones be humble, until the Lord hears us and answers us and turns us to Himself and binds us with His charity and delivers us from the subjection of the servitude of death and creates a clean heart in us and renews His firm Spirit in us and we may be made

[p. 581] {#po.0.p581}
ܗ̱ܘܰܝܢ ܒܥܰܒܕ݂ܘܬܳܐ ܕܡܰܘܬܳܐ. ܘܣܳܡܰܢ ܠܰܒܢܰܝ̈ܳܐ ܘܦ݁ܰܪܩܰܢ ܡܶܢ ܦܘܽܥܒܳܕ݂ܳܐ ܩܰܫܝܳܐ ܕܡܰܘܬܳܐ ܘܦܰܢܝܺ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܳܐ ܠܰܬܚܘܽܡܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕܶܝܢ ܗܳܘܺܝܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܕܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܒܪܝܺܬܐ ܚܕ݂ܰܬܳܐ ܒܰܡܫܝܺܚܳܐ ܒܕܰܟܝܘܽܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܠܶܒܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܝܺܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ ܡܶܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܕܢܶܚܛܳܐ ܘܢܶܥܒܰܪ ܥܰܠ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܐ ܕܒܳܪܘܺܝܶܗ. ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܕܡܶܬ݁ܕ݁ܰܟܶܐ ܠܶܒܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܚܛܝܳܬܳܐ ܘܡܰܚܒܺܝܢ ܠܟܽܠܢܳܫ: ܒܢܰܝ̈ܳܐ
a new creature, praising the Lord, who had mercy on us in the last generation, because He looked down from the height of His sanctuary and heard our groaning, we who were prisoners in the servitude of death, and He adopted us as children and snatched us from the harsh servitude of death and brought the children back to their ends; that is: having become men, having become a new creature in Christ with purity of heart, just as Adam was, before he had sinned and transgressed the commandment of his Creator. These are they whose heart is clean from sin and who love everyone: the children who return to their ends.


[p. 582] {#po.0.p582}
ܕܦܳܢܶܝܢ ܠܰܬܚܘܽܡܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ܀ ܫܠܶܡ ܡܺܐܡܪܳܐ ܕܥܶܣܪܺܝܢ. ܕܥܰܠ ܡܰܣܳܩܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܩܰܫܝܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܐܝܺܬ ܒܐܘܽܪܚܳܐ
The twentieth discourse ends, concerning the arduous steps on the way to the city of the Lord.
ܕ݁ܰܡܕ݂ܝܺܢ̱ܬ݁ܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ܀ ܡܺܐܡܪܳܐ ܕܥܶܣܪܺܝܢ ܘܚܰܕ݂ ܕܥܰܠ ܐܺܝܠܳܢܳܐ ܕܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ܀ ® ‫݂ ܕܥܰܠ ܐܝܺܠܳܢܳܐ ܛܳܒܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܗ̱ܘ ܘܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܩܳܐܶܡ܂ ܘܥܰܠ
TWENTY-FIRST DISCOURSE, CONCERNING THE TREE OF ADAM


[p. 583] {#po.0.p583}
ܐܝܺܠܳܢܳܐ ܕܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܛܳܒܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܕܒ݂ܺܝܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܐܝܺܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܒ݁ܝܳܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܥܰܡܠܳܐ ܘܨܶܦܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܪܶܢܝܳܐ ܕܥܳܒܘܽܪ̈ܝܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܰܛܥܶܡܝܘ ܒܶܝܗ ܕܒܶܝܬ ܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ ܡܰܘܬܳܐ: ܒܗܳܝ ܕܒܶܗ ܝܰܕ݂ܥܘܽܗ ܠܒܺܝܫܬܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܝܳܕ݂ܥܺܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ. ܘܡܶܢ ܕܐܶܟܰܠܘ ܡܶܢܶܗ ܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܘ ܒܝܳܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܐܝܺܬܶܝܗ ܡܰܘܬܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܚܳܕ݂ܥܺܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܠܳܗ. ܘܡܶܢ ܕܐܶܫܬ݁ܡܰܥܘ ܠܒܺܝܫ̈ܳܝܐ ܘܚܰܙܰܘ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܰܚܙܰܘ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܐܝܺܬ ܒܳܗ ܘܪܰܚܡܘܽܗ̱ܝ: ܐܶܫܬܰܠܛܰܬ ܒܗܘܢ ܒܺܝܫܬܳܐ ܘܝܰܕ݂ܥܘܽܗ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܰܟܬܝܰܒ: ܕܰܒ݂ܝܰܘܡܳܐ ܕܬܶܥܒܪܘܽܢ ܥܰܠ ܡܶܠܰܬܝ ܘܰܒܡܰܘܬܳܐ ܬܡܘܽܬܘܽܢ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܛܳܒܬܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܐܰܠܶܦ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܰܕ݂ܒܶܝܬ ܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ ܟܰܕ݂ ܒܪܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ.
1. Therefore I shall begin to explain concerning the good tree, what it is and how it stands, and concerning the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, which is the Evil One and labor and solicitude and care for perishable things, through which the family of Adam tasted death; for through it they knew evil, which they had been ignorant of. And when they had eaten from it, they knew evil, which is death, which they had not known. And when they had obeyed the Evil One and had looked at the earth and seen what is in it, and had loved those things, evil took possession of them and they knew it, as it is written: On the day that you transgress My word, you shall die the death.

[p. 585] {#po.0.p585}
ܘܒܺܝܫܬܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܘ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ: ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܐܶܫܬܡܰܥܘ ܠܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ ܘܐܰܠܶܦ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܒܺܝܫܬܳܐ. ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܡܶܬܩܪܶܐ ܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ ܐܝܺܠܳܢܳܐ: ܕܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܘ ܒܶܗ ܕܒܶܝܬ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܒܺܝܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܛܳܒܬܳܐ. ܝܺܠܶܦ݂ܘ ܕܶܝܢ ܛܳܒܬ݁ܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܘܒܝܳܫܬܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ. ܗܘܰܘ ܠܰܡ܂ ܝܳܕ݂ܥܰܝ ܛܳܒܬܳܐ ܘܒܺܝܫܬܳܐ. ܘܡܶܢ ܬܰܡܳܢ ܩܶܛܪܰܬ ܣܺܝܥܶܬ݂ܳܐ ܕܦܳܝܦܘܽܪܘܽܬܳܐ ܒܳܐܕ݁ܳܡ ܘܰܒܚܰܠܺܕ݂ܰܘܗ̱ܝ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܗܘܿܢ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܕܡܶܢ ܐܝܺܠܳܢܳܐ ܕܺܝܕ݂ܰܥܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܛܳܒܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܕܒ݂ܺܝܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܐܟܠܘܿܢ. ܗܳܢܰܝܘ ܕܶܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܫܬܰܡܥܘܽܢ ܠܶܗ: ܕܗܘܰܝܘܽ ܡܰܡܠܶܦ ܠܟܘܽܢ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܒܺܝܫܳܢ: ܘܫܳܪܶܐ ܠܟܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܝ̈ܳܬܳܐ: ܘܡܶܢ ܒܰܣܺܝܡܘܽܬܳܗ ܕܒܳܪܘܳܝܟܘܿܢ. ܘܐܳܣܰܪ ܠܟܘܢ ܒܥܳܒܘܽܪ̈ܝܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܒܥܰܡܠܳܐ ܘܰܒܨܰܦ݂ܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܒܪܳܡܘܳܬܳܐ: ܘܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܠܟܘܢ ܕܬܶܟܦܪܘܽܢ ܒܒܳܪܘܰܝܟܘܽܢ ܘܬܰܚܪܒܘܽܢ ܚܰܕ݂ ܠܚܰܕ݂. ܘܬܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܠܰܘܛܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܒܢܰܝ̈ ܚܶܫܘܽܟܳܐ: ܘܗܳܘܶܐ ܠܟܘܢ ܡܳܪܳܐ: ܘܡܰܘܟܶܠ ܠܟܘܽܢ ܣܰܡܳܐ ܕܡܰܘܬܳܐ. ܘܗܳܐ ܝܰܘܡܳܢܳܐ ܐܳܟܠܺܝܢ ܝܰܠܺܝܕ݂ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܕܐܳܕܳܡ ܒܩܰܫܝܘܽܬ ܠܶܒܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢܶܗ ܕܗܳܢܳܐ ܐܝܺܠܳܢܳܐ ܡܰܘܕ݂ܰܥ ܒܝܶܫܬܳܐ ܘܰܡܠܰܦ ܠܗܘܿܢ: ܕܢܶܬܰܐܣܪܘܽܢ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܒܥܳܒܘܽܪ̈ܝܳܬܳܐ. ܡܶܬܰܐܣܪܝܺܢ ܕܶܝܢ ܘܡܶܬܚܰܢܩܝܺܢ ܒܨܶܦܬܳܐ ܘܰܪܢܝܳܐ ܕܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܥܳܒ݁ܪܳܢ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܡܰܟܟܺܝܢ ܘܡܶܬܩܰܕ݂ܫܺܝܢ ܘܡܶܣܬܰܪܩܺܝܢ: ܡܶܢ ܨܶܒܘ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܐܰܝܠܺܝܢ ܕܥܰܡ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܥܳܒܪܳܢ. ܘܟ݁ܽܠܶܗ ܕܐܰܣܝܺܪܝܺܢ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܶܣܬ݁ܰܪܩܺܝܢ ܡܶܢܳܗ: ܘܝܽܠܦܺܝܢ ܐܰܘ ܡܶܢ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܡܶܢ ܒ݁ܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܕܐܰܝܟܰܢܳܐ ܢܶܬܰܐܣܪܘܽܢ ܒܡܳܪܰܢ ܒܗܰܘ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܕܠܰܝܬ ܒܶܗ ܡܰܘܬܳܐ: ܘܢܶܐܟܠܘܽܢ ܬܰܡܳܢ ܡܶܠܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܐܝܺܬܰܝܗܶܝܢ ܚܰܝ̈ܶܐ ܡܰܚ̈ܰܝܢܶܐ: ܘܢܶܐܟܠܘܽܢܰܝ ܗ̱ܝ ܠܶܗ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܰܢܚܰܝܘܽܢ ܘܢܶܬܪܰܘܚܘܽܢ ܘܡܶܛܽܠܬܶܗ ܢܶܫܬܰܡܠܘܽܢ. ܐܰܡܺܝܢ܀
For God taught the family of Adam only good when He created them, nor did they know evil as long as they had not obeyed Satan, who taught them evil; and therefore Satan is called a tree, since through it the household of Adam knew evil and good. From God indeed they learned good, from Satan evil; they became, in fact, knowing good and evil. And from then on, the hatred of incredulity prevailed in Adam and in his progeny. Wherefore God said to them: of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil do not eat, that is: do not obey him; for he will teach you all evils and will draw you away from heavenly things and from the sweetness of your Creator and will bind you to perishable things and to labor and care and pride and will make you deny your Creator and bring ruin upon one another; and you will be children of cursing and children of darkness and he himself will be a master to you and will feed you with deadly poison. And behold, today the children of Adam, because of the hardness of their heart, eat from that tree which shows them malice and teaches them to bind themselves to the earth and to perishable things; but being bound, they are suffocated by the care and solicitude for things that pass away, for they do not humble themselves nor are they sanctified, nor do they empty themselves of things that pass away together with the earth. And the whole reason they are bound to the earth is that they do not renounce it, nor are they taught by God or by a man of God how to cling to the Lord in that age in which there is no death, and there eat the words of the Lord, which are life-giving life, and eating the Lord they may live and progress and be perfected for His sake.


[p. 586] {#po.0.p586}


[p. 587] {#po.0.p587}
ܘܢܺܐܚܘܽܢ ܘܢܺܐܪܒܘܽܢ ܘܢܶܬܓܰܡܪܘܽܢ ܡܶܛܰܠܳܬܶܗ܀ ܐܶܢ ܨܳܒ݂ܶܐ ܐܰܢ݈ܬ݁ ܗܳܟܝܽܠ ܕܬܰܚܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܡܰܡܘܳܬܳܐ ܕܐܝܰܠܳܢܳܐ: ܕ݁ܰܩܛܰܠ ܠܰܐܒ݂ܘܽܢ ܐܳܕ݁ܶܡ ܐܳܦ ܠܰܢ: ܘܬܘܒ ܠܳܐ ܬܡܘܽܬ: ܐܶܣܬ݁ܰܪܰܩ ܘܐܰܪܚܶܝܩ ܡܶܢ ܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ ܘܡܶܢ ܝܘܽܠܦܳܢܶܗ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ: ܡܶܢ ܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ ܘܡܶܢ ܟ݀ܽܠ ܕܒܺܝܫ ܘܡܶܢ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܘܡܶܢ ܨܶܦܬܶܗ ܘܡܶܢ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܕܐܶܬ݂ܦܰܪܰܩ ܡܶܢܶܗ: ܒܝܰܡܟܳܟܿܳܐ ܘܒܰܨܠܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܰܒܝܰܘܡܳܐ ܘܒܰܢܛܰܪܬܳܐ ܕܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܰܘܗ̱ܝ. ܘܐܶܦܰܫܶܩ ܬܘܽܒ ܡܳܢܰܘ ܝܘܽܠܦܳܢܶܗ ܕܒܺܝܫܳܐ ܕܢܳܩܰܦ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܠܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܰܠܒܺܝܟܺܝܢ ܒܗܳܢ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܒܥܳܒܘܽܪ̈ܝܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܪܰܚܝܺܩܝܺܢ ܡܶܢ ܓܡܝܳܪ̈ܶܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܐܰܣܝܳܪܝܺܢ ܒܪܘܽܚ ܒܗܰܘ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܕܢܘܽܗܪܳܐ. ܘܐܶܦܰܫܶܩ ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܦܰܩܕ݁ܶܗ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܐܕܳܡ ܡܶܢ ܩܕ݂ܺܝܡ: ܕܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܩܰܕ݂ܝܺܫܳܐ ܓܡܝܳܪܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܥܺܝܪ̈ܶܐ ܘܡܰܠܰܐܟ݁ܶܐ ܕܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܕ݁ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܟܰܕ݂ ܩܳܐܶܡ ܒܰܦܓ݂ܰܪ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ ܥܰܪܛܶܠܺܝ
2. If therefore you wish to be saved from the death of the tree which killed our father Adam and us also, and not to die anymore: empty yourself and distance yourself from Satan and his doctrine; that is, from Satan and from every evil thing and from the age and its solicitude and from all things which Jesus said must be renounced, with humility and prayer and fasting, observing His commandments. And I shall further explain what the doctrine of the Evil One is, which harms the just themselves, because in this age, being detained by perishable things, they become removed from the perfect, since they are bound to this age of light with [their] spirit. And I shall explain how God commanded Adam of old to be a holy perfect one, just as the watchers and angels in heaven, so that, established in body on earth, naked of all


[p. 588] {#po.0.p588}


[p. 589] {#po.0.p589}
ܡܶܢ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܕܐܺܝܬ ܒܳܗ: ܢܕ݂ܰܝܰܪ ܒܪܘܽܚ ܒ݁ܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܡܰܠܰܐܟ݁ܶܐ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܛܥܺܝܢ ܙܺܝܘܶܗ ܘܫܘܽܒܚܳܐ ܕܒܳܪܘܳܝܶܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܚܰܙܝܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܐܝܺܠܳܢܳܐ ܛܳܒܳܐ ܐܝܺܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܒܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܗܰܘ ܕܢܘܽܗܪܳܐ ܕܠܐ ܡܶܬܚܙܶܐ ܠܥܺܝܢ̈ܶܐ ܕܒܺܝܣܪܳܐ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܝܺܫܘܽܥ: ܘܗܘܺܝܘܽ ܐܝܺܠܳܢܳܐ ܕܚܰܝ̈ܶܐ ܘܰܠܚܺܝܐ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܒܦܺܐܪ̈ܰܘܗ̱ܝ: ܐܰܝܟ݁ܳܐ ܕܗܳܘܶܐ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ ܓܡܝܺܪܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟܰܢܳܐ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕܨܰܠܰܘ ܕܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܗܳܘܶܐ ܒ݁ܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ. ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܝܺܬ ܫܰܝܢܳܐ ܘܰܫܠܳܡܳܐ ܘܐܰܘܝܘܽܬ݂ܳܐ ܠܪܰܘܪ̈ܒ݁ܶܐ ܘܰܠܕ݂ܰܩܕ݁ܺܩܶܐ ܘܰܡܫܰܒܚܺܝܢ ܫܰܘܝܳܐܝܺܬ ܘܠܰܝܬ ܐܰܡܳܢ
things that are in it, he might dwell in spirit in heaven with the angels, clothed in mind with the glory of his Creator, nor would the visible earth become [a concern] to him. The good tree in that age of light, invisible to the eyes of the flesh, is the Lord Jesus, who is the tree of life giving life to all with its fruits, where the perfect will of God is done, as the Lord said: Pray that the will of God may be done on earth as it is done in heaven, that is: just as the greater and the lesser enjoy tranquility and peace and unanimity and glorify together, nor is there anyone there who is proud against one lesser than himself nor anyone who despises one greater than himself: so, pray that all men may become.
ܕ݁ܪܳܡ ܥܰܠ ܕܰܙܥܘܽܪ ܡܢܶܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܕܳܐܶܛ ܠܰܕ݂ܪܰܒ݂ ܡܶܢܶܗ: ܗܳܟܰܢ ܨܰܠܰܘ ܕܢܗܘܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܫ̈ܳܐ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ܀ ܐܝܺܬܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܦܺܐܪ̈ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܕܗܰܘ ܐܝܺܠܳܢܳܐ ܛܳܒܳܐ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܦܺܐܪ̈ܶܐ ܕܪܘܽܚܳܐ݀ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܫܠܺܝܚܳܐ: ܕܢܶܩܰܦ ܠܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܘܢܶܫܬܰܡܰܥ ܠܳܗ: ܘܠܳܐ ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܣܪ̈ܝܺܩܰܝ ܫܘܽܒܚܳܐ ܕܡܰܡܩܠܚܺܝܢ ܚܰܕ݂ ܥܰܠ ܚܰܕ݂ ܘܚܳܣܡܝܺܢ ܚܰܕ݂ ܒܚܰܕ݂ ܠܒܺܝܫܬܳܐ. ܘܟ݁ܽܠ ܕܡܶܬܕܰܡܶܐ ܒܶܗ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܟܺܝܬܳܪ̈ܶܐ ܝܳܗܶܒ
3. But the fruits of the good tree are the spiritual fruits which Paul reports: that we should cling to the Spirit and render obedience to Him, and not be vain in glory, despising one another and envying one another in evil; and whoever imitates these, rendering these fruits, is perfected. It is good, he says, to be envious in honest [things] always. But the fruits, he says, of the Spirit are these: to put on mercy and clemency and unanimity and peace and the glory of the Lord; that is: that we should be conformed to one another
ܒܫܰܦܝܰܝ̈ܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܒܟܽܠܙܒ݂ܰܢ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܦܺܐܪܶܐ ܠܰܡ ܕܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ: ܕܢܶܠܒܰܫ ܠܰܡ ܪܰܚܡܶܐ ܘܪܘܚܳܦܳܐ ܘܐܰܘܝܘܽܬ݂ܳܐ ܘܰܫܠܳܡܳܐ ܘܐܶܫܬܰܒܘܽܚܬܳܐ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕ݁ܢܺܫܬܰܡܰܥ ܚܰܕ݂ ܠܚܰܕ݂ ܒܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܦܺܐܪܶܐ ܕܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܒܚܘܽܒܿܳܐ ܘܰܒܢܰܓܝܳܪܘܽܬ݂ ܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܘܒܰܣܚܽܝܡܘܽܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܡܰܟܝܳܟܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܰܡܣܰܝܒܪܳܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܰܪܡܺܝܣܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܩܰܕ݂ܝܺܫܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܪܶܓܬܳܐ. ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܦܺܐܪ̈ܶܐ ܕܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܕܪܳܥܶܝܢ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܩܰܕ݁̈ܝܺܫܶܐ ܒܰܥܕܶܝܢ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܦܳܪܩܝܺܢ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܩܫ̈ܰܝܳܐ ܠܢܰܒܪ̈ܶܐ ܕܢܶܚܙܘܽܢ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܘܢܶܫܒܩܘܽܢ ܩܫ̈ܰܝܳܐ ܘܢܶܩܦܘܽܢ ܠܰܕܡܰܟܝܳܟܺܝܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܫܠܺܝܚܳܐ: ܗܘܰܝܬܘܽܢ ܓܳܒ݂ܶܝܢ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܡܰܟ݁ܺܝ̈ܟܳܢ ܘܢܳܩܦܝܺܢ ܠܗܶܝܢ. ܒܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܠܰܡ ܐܶܬܕܰܒ݁ܰܪ: ܦܰܩܕ݁ܶܗ ܒܳܪܘܳܝܶܗ ܠܐܕܳܡ: ܕܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܥܳܡܘܽܪܳܐ: ܘܰܓܪܳܐ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܐܰܟܣܢ̈ܳܝܳܐ ܘܐܰܘܬܳܒ݂ܳܐ. ܘܰܠܥܶܠ ܫܡܶܫ ܘܫܰܒܰܚ ܒ݁ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕ݁ܘܰܒܳܪܶܐ ܐܝܟ ܡܰܠܰܐܟܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܡܰܠܰܐܟ݁ܶܐ. ܘܰܕܗܳܢܰܢ ܗܘܰܝܬ ܡܶܢ ܩܕ݂ܺܝܡ ܣܳܗܶܕ݂ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܰܫܠܺܝܚܰܘܗ̱ܝ: ܕܗܶܢܘܽܢ ܐܶܬܰܘ ܘܚܰܘܝܽܘ ܠܰܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܕܢܶܥܒܕܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܕܐܶܥܰܠܬ ܗܰܘ ܡܰܝܢ ܕ݁ܰܐܪܰܥ ܣܚܺܝܦܳܐ ܕܰܒܥܶܠܕܒܳܒܝܘܽܬܳܐ ܒܿܗܘܽܢ ܒܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܘܰܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܩܳܐܶܡ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܒܰܝܢܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܠܰܒܢܰܫ̈ ܐܳܕܳܡ. ܘܒܰܕ݁ܶܩ ܫܠܺܝܚܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܐܳܡܰܪ: ܕܟܽܠ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܐܶܬܚܰܕ݁ܰܬ ܒܰܡܫܝܺܚܳܐ ܡܶܢܕܪܺܝܫ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܨܒܿܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܘܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܒܪܳܝܗ̱ܝ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܥܒ݁ܰܪ ܥܰܠ ܦܘܰܩܕ݂ܳܢܳܐ. ܘܦܳܚܶܡ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܝܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܗܰܘ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܳܐ ܕܐܶܡܪܶܬ ܕܗܳܟܰܢ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ. ܘܰܚܙܝܺ ܡܳܐ ܕܳܡܶܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܝܳܐ ܠܩܰܕܡܳܝܳܐ. ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܶܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܨܶܦܬܳܐ ܘܰܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܡܰܚܫ̈ܒܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܥܰܒܕ݁ܶܗ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܐܳܕܳܡ. ܘܰܐܚܪ̈ܳܢܶܐ ܗܳܟܰܢ ܦܰܩܶܕ݂ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܰܒܠܺܝܚܰܝܘܽܗ̱ܝ: ܕ݁ܰܗܘܰܘ ܕܠܳܐ ܨܶܦܬܳܐ ܘܰܕ݂ܠܳܐ
in these fruits of the Spirit: in charity and patience and meekness and humility and long-suffering and gentleness and holiness devoid of concupiscence. These are the fruits of the Spirit, which the saints in Eden consider, discerning the hard ones from these for the simple, so that having seen them they may leave the hard ones and follow the humble, as the Apostle said: Choose the humble things that are, and follow them. «In these things,» he says, «conduct yourself,» his Creator commanded Adam, «with your mind in heaven as an inhabitant and with your body on earth as a pilgrim and a stranger. And serve above and praise in that manner, just as an angel with the angels». That you yourself were once such is testified by the Lord and His apostles, who coming showed the children of Adam, so that... they might do, after He was exalted, who pierced the wall of enmity standing between Himself and the children of Adam with that same conduct. Which the Apostle regards, saying: All things have been renewed in Christ from the beginning, as He willed that Adam should be, and as he had been created, before he had transgressed the law. The latest will of the Lord was equal to the first, which I said was such. And attend to how similar the latest is to the first! The first, God made Adam without care and without evil thoughts; and the latest, the Lord and His apostles commanded thus: Be without care and without thoughts. The first


[p. 590] {#po.0.p590}


[p. 591] {#po.0.p591}


[p. 592] {#po.0.p592}


[p. 593] {#po.0.p593}
ܡܰܚܫ̈ܒܳܬܳܐ. ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܕܟܶܐ ܒܪܳܝܗ̱ܝ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܐܳܕܳܡ܂ ܘܰܐܚܪܳܝܳܐ ܗܳܟܰܢ ܦܩܰܕ݂: ܕܰܗܘܰܝܬܘܽܢ ܕܟܶܝ̣ܢ ܒܠܶܒܟܘܽܢ ܘܛܘܿܒܰܝܟܘܿܢ. ܠܳܐܕ݂ܳܡ ܗܳܟܰܢ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܥܰܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܢܶܥܒܰܪ ܥܰܠ ܦܘܰܩܕ݁ܳܢܳܐ: ܕܠܳܐ ܬܶܫܬ݁ܡܰܥ ܠܒܺܝܫܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܶܬ݁ܪܰܓ݂ܪܰܓ݂ ܠܰܐܪܥܳܐ ܘܰܠܟ݁ܽܠ ܕܐܝܺܬ ܒܳܗ. ܣܳܗܶܕ݂ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܝܳܐ ܕܡܶܢ ܠܥܶܠ: ܕ݁ܡܰܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܰܪܚܶܩ ܡܶܢ ܒܺܝܫܳܐ ܘܫܳܒܶܩ ܟ݁ܽܠ
God created Adam clean, and the latest commanded thus: Be clean of heart and you are blessed. To Adam He said thus, before he had transgressed the commandment: «Do not obey the Evil One nor desire the earth and the things that are in it». The latest will testifies above: He who has not departed from the Evil One and, having left all things on earth, has not looked into heaven crucified: will not attain that which Adam lost.
ܕܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܚܳܐܰܪ ܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܟܰܕ݂ ܒܨܠܺܝܒܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܡܰܕ݂ܪܶܟ ܠܗܰܘ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕ݁ܐܰܘܒܶܕ݂ ܐܳܕܳܡ܀ ܘܡܳܐ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܫܠܺܝܚܳܐ ܕܡܶܢܕ݂ܪܺܝܫ ܐܶܬܳܐ ܡܫܺܝܚܳܐ ܚܰܕܶܬ ܟ݁ܽܠܥܶܢܝܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܪܰܨܒܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܢܩܰܘܘܽܢ ܕܒܶܝܬ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܐܶܣܬܰܟܠ ܕܐܰܝܟ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܶܐ ܕܰܓܡܺܝܪܘܳܬܳܐ ܕܦܰܪܫܶܬ ܠܳܟ ܡܶܢ ܠܥܶܠ: ܘܐܰܝܟ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܦܺܐܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ݂ܪܘܺܚܳܐ ܕܦܰܪܶܫ ܫܠܺܝܚܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܕܒܺܝܣܪܳܐ ܨܒܳܝܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܢܶܬܕܰܒܪܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ: ܐܝܟ ܕܝܰܘܡܳܢܳܐ ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܨܳܒܶܐ. ܘܟܽܠܶܗ ܕܐܳܬܳܐ ܡܫܺܝܚܳܐ ܘܐܶܬܡܰܟܰܟ: ܕܢܰܠܦܰܢ ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܢܶܬܘܰܟ݁ܰܟ ܒܰܕ݂ܡܘܽܬܶܗ ܘܕܰܢܚܰܘܶܐ ܗܰܘ ܫܪܳܪܳܐ ܕܡܶܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ. ܘܕܰܟܬܝܺܝܒ ܕܰܩܪܶܒ ܘܐܶܬܢܰܣܝܰ: ܕܰܢܚܰܘܶܝܢ ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܐܶܬܢܰܣܝܰ ܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ܂ ܡܶܢܩܕܝܺܡ. ܘܕܰܟܬܝܺܒ ܕܰܙܟܳܝܗ̱ܝ ܠܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ: ܕܰܢܚܰܘܶܝܢ ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܐܶܠܘܽ ܨܒܳܐ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܒܡܶܠܬܳܐ ܣܳܚܶܦ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܣܰܚܦ݁ܶܗ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܒܝܳܬܳܝ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܐܶܫܬܡܰܥ ܠܶܗ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܥܳܕܶܠ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܕܰܢܚܘܽܪ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܪܰܓ ܥܘܺܬܪܳܗ ܕܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܦܘܽܦܪܳܗ ܥܳܒܘܽܪܳܐ: ܐܝܟ ܕܐܶܬܪܰܓܪܰܓ݁ܺܝܘ ܕܒܶܝܬ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܘܚܰܠܦܘ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܒܐܪܥܳܐ ܘܰܫܒܰܩܘ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܘܰܪܚܶܡܘ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܘܚܰܠܶܦܘ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܠܳܐ ܥܳܒܰܪ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܬܪܶܐ: ܘܰܩܢܰܝܘ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܥܳܒܰܪ ܘܡܶܫܬܪܶܐ:
4. And the Apostle saying: Christ came again renewing all things, as He willed the household of Adam to remain, understand God to have willed that men should dwell in such precepts of perfection, which I explained to you above, and in those fruits of the Spirit, which the Apostle distinguished from the [fruits] of the flesh, just as even today He so wills. And the whole reason why Christ came and humbled Himself was to teach us how we should be humbled after His likeness, and to reveal the pristine truth. And that which is written: He approached — and was tempted, to show us how Adam was once tempted. And that which is written that He Himself overcame Satan, to show us that Adam, if he had willed, could have driven him away by [a single] word, just as God drove him away with that word: «I will not obey him» when he wanted to seduce him, so that Adam might look at the earth, so that he might covet the riches of the earth and its perishable beauty, just as the household of Adam coveted, and exchanging heaven with earth they left heaven and loved the earth and, having exchanged perennial and indissoluble things, they acquired a fleeting and dissoluble thing, exchanging the perfect exemplar with an image, as Paul said: Whatever visible [thing] is an image of a [thing] which is neither visible nor perishable; just as neither the ministry which Moses showed to the children of Israel, nor the tabernacle of the covenant were the perfect exemplar, but an image, as it is written: The true tabernacle, into which Christ entered before us, so that we too might walk in His footsteps, that is, that which is in the lowest heights, as Paul said:


[p. 594] {#po.0.p594}


[p. 595] {#po.0.p595}
ܒܛܶܠܳܢܝܳܬܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܫܠܺܝܚܳܐ: ܕܟܽܠܥܶܢܝܢ ܕܡܶܬܚܙܶܐ ܛܶܠܳܢܝܳܬܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܕܗܰܘ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܚܙܶܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܥܳܒܰܪ ܠܶܗ. ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܕܐܳܦ݂ܠܳܐ ܬܶܫܡܶܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܚܰܘܝܽ ܡܘܽܫܶܐ ܠܰܝܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐܺܝܣܪܳܐܺܝܠ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܰܫܟܰܢ ܙܰܒܢܳܐ ܐܚܺܝܬܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܬܰܦܢܳܐ ܡܫܰܠܡܳܢܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܛܶܠܳܢܝܳܬܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܟܬܝܺܝܒ: ܕܗܰܘ ܡܰܫܟ݁ܢܳܐ ܫܰܪܝܺܪܳܐ ܕܩܰܕ݁ܶܡ܂ ܥܰܠ ܠܶܗ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܡܫܺܝܚܳܐ ܩܕ݂ܳܡܰܝܢ: ܕܰܒܥܶܩ̈ܒܳܬܶܗ ܢܶܥܘܽܠ ܠܶܗ ܐܳܦ ܚܢܰܢ: ܕܐܝܺܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܒܰܡܪ̈ܰܘܡܶܐ ܥܶܠܳܝ̈ܶܐ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܦܰܘܠܳܣ: ܕܝܺܝܕ݂ܰܥ ܐܰܢܳܐ ܓܰܝܒܪܳܐ ܕܐܶܬܚܛܶܝܦ ܠܥܶܠ ܡܶܢ ܬܠܳܬܳܐ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܠܦܰܪܕܰܝܣܳܐ ܪܘܽܚܳܢܳܐ. ܘܟܽܠܶܗ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܓܰܒܪܳܐ: ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܫܬܰܒܗܰܪ ܕܗܘܳܝܘܿ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܦܰܩܳܚ ܕܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܢܶܫܬܰܒܗܰܪ ܕܓܰܒܪܳܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ: ܐܳܦܝܠܳܐ ܟܰܕ ܓܰܒܪܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܢܚܰܫܶܒ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܥܰܡ ܚܰܛܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܩܕܳܡ ܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܘܢܰܙܥܰܪ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܡܶܢ ܟܽܠ ܕܐ̱ܝܺܬ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܬܬܪܝܰܡ ܘܢܶܦܶܠ ܐܰܝܟ ܐܳܕܳܡ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܗܳܕܶܐ ܨܳܒܶܐ ܗܰܘ ܡܰܢ ܕܰܕܪܰܫ ܠܰܢ
I knew a man, who was caught up above the three heavens into the spiritual paradise. And the whole reason why he said «a man» is so that he might not boast that it was he; for it is not expedient for a man to boast: «I am perfect», even if he be perfect; but let him condemn himself before all together with the sinners and make himself less than all on earth, lest being lifted up he fall like Adam. Nevertheless, not even now does He will, who paved the way for us


[p. 596] {#po.0.p596}


[p. 597] {#po.0.p597}
ܐܘܽܪ̈ܚܳܐ ܠܪܰܘܡܳܐ: ܕܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܒܬܶܛܠܳܢܝܳܬܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܠܬܰܠܡܺܝܕܳܝܐ ܗܰܘ ܡܫܰܠܡܳܢܳܐ ܢܶܩܰܦ. ܕܰܠܥܶܠ ܠܰܡ ܒܥܰܘ ܘܕܰܠܥܶܠ ܐܶܬܪܰܥܰܘ. ܐܰܬܰܪ ܕܰܡܫܝܺܚܳܐ ܝܳܬܶܒ ܒܰܡܪ̈ܰܘܡܶܐ ܥܶܠܳܝ̈ܶܐ܀
to the height, that we should remain in the image, but that we should follow the perfect exemplar. Seek the things that are above, he says, think of the things that are above, where Christ sits in the highest heights.
ܚܙܝܺ ܗܳܟܝܶܠ ܕܗܰܘ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܨܳܒܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܒܩܰܕܡܺܝܬܳܐ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ: ܗܘܽ ܨܒܳܐ ܐܳܦ ܒܰܐ̱ܚܪܳܝܬܳܐ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܐܶܢܳܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܩܰܕܡܳܝܳܐ: ܘܐܶܢܳܐ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܝܳܐ. ܘܗܳܢܰܘ ܕܰܦܩܳܕܳܐ ܪܰܒܳܐ ܘܰܓܡܝܺܪܳܐ ܩܰܕܡܳܝܐ ܘܰܐܚܪܳܝܳܐ: ܕܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܐܰܪܥܳܢܳܝܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܢܶܬܦܢܶܐ ܥܰܠ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܐ ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܘܰܢܡܽܘܬ ܡܶܢ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܪܶܥܝܳܢܶܗ. ܐܰܝܟ ܕܡܝܬ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܦܰܐܘܠܳܘܣ ܡܶܢ ܟܽܠ ܕܐܺܝܬ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܐܶܡܰܪ: ܐܶܢ ܡܝܬܬܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܚܘܽܒܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܕܥܳܠܡܳܐ: ܠܡܳܢܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܚܰܝ̈ܶܐ ܡܶܬܕܰܒܪܝܺܢ ܐܢܬܘܽܢ ܒܰܫܩܳܠܳܐ ܘܒܰܫܪܳܝܳܐ ܘܰܒܡܰܣܒܳܐ ܘܰܒܡܰܬܠܳܐ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܡܶܬܓܡܰܪ ܒܗܶܝܢ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܝܬ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܡܶܢ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ܆ ܘܐܶܢ ܐܳܡܪܝܺܢܠܶܗ: ܕܐܳܟܶܠ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܘܫܳܬܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܘܰܡܡܰܠܶܠ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ. ܐܳܡܰܪ ܠܗܘܽܢ: ܕܐܰܝܠܺܝܢ ܕܗܳܟܰܢ ܡܡܰܠܠܝܺܢ ܡܝܳܬܝܺܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ. ܣܰܝܒܳܪܬܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܘܰܠܒܘܽܫܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܝܰܬܝܰܪܘܽܬܳܐ ܢܶܬܝܰܗܒܳܢ. ܘܡܶܠܬܳܐ ܗܳܕܶܐ ܕܰܡܡܰܠܶܠ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ: ܠܰܘ ܠܰܡ ܐܶܢܳܐ ܚܰܝ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܚܰܝ ܒܝܺ ܡܫܝܺܚܳܐ ܗܰܘ ܕܰܡܡܰܠܶܠ ܒܝܿ. ܒܡܶܠܬܶܗ
5. See therefore the Lord willing the same thing at the end, which He willed at the beginning. Hence He said: I am the first and I am the last. And this is My great and perfect will, first and last: that no one should be earthly nor return to the earth, but having become heavenly in mind, let him die to the earth, just as Paul died to all things on earth and said: If you are dead to the use of the world, why do you conduct yourselves like the living in leisure and business, in buying and selling, by which no one is perfected, unless he dies to the age? And if they say to him: «You eat and drink and speak!» he says to them: «Those who speak thus are dead to the world»; food and clothing, indeed, are added. And as far as the utterance is concerned, which I speak, he says, it is not I who live, but Christ lives in me, who speaks in me. By the word of Christ, indeed, I stand and sit and eat and drink and sleep and wake and not by alien speech or senile conversation or narratives which are useless for perfection, or by the business of taking and giving, or by perishable gain: but, he says, Christ lives in me, who thinks of those things which are in heaven, not those which are on earth.


[p. 598] {#po.0.p598}
ܗܘܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܕܰܡܫܰܚܚܳܐ ܩܳܐܶܡ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ ܘܝܳܬ݂ܶܒ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ: ܘܐܳܟܶܠ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܘܫܳܬܶܐ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ: ܘܕܳܡܶܟ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ ܘܡܶܬܬܥܺܝܪ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ. ܘܠܳܐ ܒܡܰܡܠܠܳܐ ܢܘܽܟܪܳܝܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܒܫ̈ܘܽܠܝܳܬܳܐ ܦܰܪ̈ܢܘܽܟ݁ܳܫܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܒܫܰܪ̈ܒ݁ܶܝܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܚܰܝܠܺܝܢ ܠܰܓܡܝܰܪܘܽܬ݂ܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܒܥܰܪ̈ܒ݁ܶܐ ܕܡܰܥܣܒܳܐ ܘܡܰܡܬܠܳܐ: ܐܰܘ ܕܚܘܽܐܪ̈ܳܢܳܐ ܥܳܒܝܘܽܪ̈ܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܚܰܝ ܒܫܰܪܝܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܡܫܝܚܳܝܐ: ܕܡܶܬܪܰܥܶܐ ܕܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܕܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ܀ ܚܳܙܶܝܢ ܐܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܡܰܡܝܬܺܬ ܘ̱ܘܳܐ ܦ݁ܰܘܠܳܘܣ ܡܶܢ ܟܽܠ ܥܺܒܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܡܶܬܚܙܶܐ ܕܣܰܩܘܽܒܠܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܕ݁ܰܓ݂ܡܝܳܪܘܳܬܳܐ: ܗܳܝ ܕܪܳܗܛܳܐ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܚܙܶܐ ܠܥܰܝ̈ܢܶܐ ܕܒܶܣܪܳܐ. ܘܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܒܰܠܒܘܽܫܶܗ ܘܰܒܣܰܝܒܳܪܬ݁ܶܗ ܚܝܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ: ܒܗܳܝ ܠܳܐ ܝܳܕܶܥ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܕܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܡܶܬܚܙܶܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܡܶܬܪܰܥܶܐ ܕܰܠܥܶܠ: ܒܰܙܒܰܢ ܟܳܦܶܢ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܘܒܰܙܒܰܢ ܥܰܪܛܶܠܳܝ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܒܠܰܝ ܠܒܘܽܫ̈ܳܐ: ܐܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܰܒܟ݁ܽܠ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܡܕܰܪܰܫ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܒܟܰܦܢܳܐ ܘܰܒܣܰܒܥܳܐ ܘܰܒܥܰܪܝܳܐ ܘܰܒܥܰܪܛܶܠܳܝܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܒܐܝܺܩܳܪܳܐ ܘܰܒܨܰܥܪܳܐ ܒܢܶܓ݂ܕ݁ܶܐ ܣܰܓ̈ܺܝܐܶܐ ܟܰܕ݂ ܦ݁ܶܠܓ݁ܶܗ ܕ݁ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܠܳܐܶܛ ܠܰܢ ܘܦ݁ܶܠܓ݁ܶܗ ܡܒܰܪܶܟ ܠܰܢ
6. You see how Paul was mortified to all visible things contrary to perfection, who pursues that which is invisible to carnal eyes. But he did not live by his clothing and food either, for he had no care for visible things, but thinking of the things that are above, sometimes he was hungry, sometimes he was naked, sometimes he lacked clothing, as he said: In all things I have been exercised: in hunger and satiety, in cold and nakedness, in honor and ignominy, in many stripes, while half the world curses us and half blesses, in blessings and cursings, while we love all and are defrauded before all like seducers, yet truthful.


[p. 599] {#po.0.p599}


[p. 600] {#po.0.p600}
ܒܒܘܽܪ̈ܟ݁ܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܒܝܠܰܘ̈ܛܳܬܳܐ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܠܟ݁ܽܠܢܳܫ ܪܳܚܡܝܰܢ ܚ̱ܢܰܢ: ܘܰܠܥܰܝܢ ܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܡܶܬܓ݂ܰܠܙܝܰܢܰܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܡܰܛܥ̈ܝܳܢܶܐ ܠܰܡ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܫܰܪܝܰܪܝܺܢܰܢ܀ ܐܝܺܬ݂ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܗܳܟܝܶܠ ܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ ܡܳܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܐܰܝܟ ܨܶܒܬܳܢܶܗ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܓܡܝܺܪܳܐ: ܗܳܢܳܐ ܕܐܶܬܳܐ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܚܰܘܝܺ ܒܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܨܳܒܶܐ ܕܢܶܬܕ݁ܰܡܶܐ ܒܶܗ ܘܢܶܬܓܡܰܪ: ܘܚܳܐܪ ܒ݁ܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܘܚܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܥܶܠܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܥܶܠܳ̈ܝܶܐ: ܕܠܳܐ ܕܶܐܦܬܳܐ ܘܰܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܟܺܐܦܿܶܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܕܰܠܒܘܽܫܳܐ ܝܳܕܼܶܥ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܕܣܰܝܒܳܪܬ݁ܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܰܠܶܢ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܗ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ
7. Adam therefore was once perfect according to the will of God; this is what Jesus, coming, showed in Himself to him who wishes to imitate Him and be perfected and looks to heaven and not to the earth. And he rejoiced with the heavenly angels without care, without pain; nor did he have care for clothing or food, but God sustained him, as befitted


[p. 601] {#po.0.p601}
ܕܳܐܶܐ ܙܘܽܘܳܐ ܠܥܘܽܬܪܳܐ ܕܒܰܣܚܺܝܡܘܽܬܶܗ ܒܠܰܚܡܳܐ ܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܟܬܝܰܒ: ܕܠܰܚܡܳܐ ܕܡܰܠܰܐܟ݂ܶܐ ܐܶܟܰܠ ܒܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ. ܘܗܳܢܳܐ ܥܰܡܠܳܐ ܘܟܺܐܦܿܶܐ ܕܝܰܠܕ݂ܳܐ ܘܟܺܐܦ݂ܶܐ ܕܦܰܓ݂ܪܳܐ ܠܐ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܵܘ: ܐܰܚܟ݂ ܕܐܳܦ ܕ݁ܰܘܝܰܕ݂ ܦܰܪܰܫ: ܕܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܡܰܪܡܰܪܘ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐ݈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܶܗ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܗܳܝ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܗܘܿܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܬܶܥܒܪܘܽܢ ܥܰܠ ܦܘܽܩܕܳܢܰܘ̈ܗܝ: ܘܐܰܪܥܧܺܝܬ݁ܶܗ ܕ݁ܰܡܪܰܝܡܳܐ ܐܰܣܠܺܝܘ: ܗܳܝ ܕܨܳܒܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܕܐܝܟ ܡܰܠܰܐܟ݁ܶܐ ܢܶܙܘܘܽܢ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܬܒܰܪ ܒܥܰܡܠܳܐ ܠܶܒܗܘܽܢ: ܘܐܶܬܟܪܰܗܘ ܘܠܰܝܬ ܕ݁ܰܡܥܰܕܰܪ ܠܗܘܽܢ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܢܛܰܪܘ ܦܘܽܩܕܳܢܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܐܶܬܟܰܫܰܦܘ ܠܶܗ: ܘܐܶܬܪܰܥܺܝ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܐܰܒܳܐ ܒܰܒܪܶܗ: ܘܰܦܪܰܩ ܐܳܢܘܽܢ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܫ̈ܡܶܗ: ܘܰܒܚܘܽܒܶܗܘ ܕ݂ܡܳܪܰܢ ܝܶܫܘܽܰܥ ܡܫܺܝܚܳܐ. ܘܗܳܟ݂ܰܢ ܥܰܒ݁ܶܕ݂ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܗܘܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕ݁ܰܥܒܰܕ݂ ܠܚܰܘܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ: ܕܠܳܐ ܪܶܓ݁ܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܙܘܽܘܳܓܿܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܡܶܢ ܣܰܥܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ̈ܪܺܝܫܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܐܰܘ ܡܶܢ ܛܶܦܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ: ܐܶܢ ܨܳܒܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܗܘܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܳܐ: ܘܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܡܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܡܰܠܰܐܟ̈ܶܐ. ܘܡܰܢ ܕܰܒܪܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ: ܡܛܰܝܶܒ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܗܘܢ ܡܶܐܟ݂ܘܽܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܐܰܝܕ݂ܳܐ ܕܗܘ ܕܳܒ݁ܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܥܰܡܠܳܐ. ܘܗܘܽ ܫܳܩܶܠ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܛܰܥܢܗܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕܠܳܐ ܬܶܣܒܘܽܢ ܨܶܦ݂ܬܳܐ ܕܦܰܓܪܟܘܽܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܕܢܰܦܫܟܘܽܢ. ܕܗܰܘ ܡܰܢ ܕܰܒܪܳܟܘܽܢ ܣܰܓܺܝ ܒܛܺܝܠ ܠܶܗ ܥܠܰܝܟܘܽܢ. ܡܶܟܝܺܠ ܠܰܡ ܫܕ݂ܰܘ ܨܦܬܟܘܽܢ ܥܰܠ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܘܗܘ̈ ܢܬܰܪܣܶܝܟܘܽܢ ܘܰܢܢܝܺܚܟܘܽܢ ܘܰܢܢܰܛܰܪܟܘܽܢ. ܗܳܟܰܢ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܵܘ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܒܰܦܔܰܪ ܘܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܒܪܘܽܚ ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܠܶܐܡܰܬܝ ܕ݂ܫܳܦ݁ܰܪ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܒܳܪܘܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܕ݁ܰܢܥܰܠܶܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܠܪܰܘܡܳܐ. ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܢܳܟܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܗܘܿܢ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܠܳܐ ܪܰܚܫܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܚܰܝܘܰܬ ܫܶܢܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܗܘܽܢ ܠܳܐ ܨܒ݁ܳܐ ܕܢܶܫܬܰܡܥܘܽܢ ܠܪܰܚܫܳܐ ܘܰܠܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ. ܐ݀ܡܰܪ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܒܝܰܘܡܳܐ ܕܰܒܪܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ: ܕܕܶܚܠܰܬܟܘܽܢ ܘܙܰܘܥܰܬܟܘܽܢ ܐܰܪܡܶܐ ܥܰܠ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܕܐܝܺܬ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܘܐܺܝܕܳܗ ܕܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܘܐܺܝܕܶܗ ܕܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ ܟܰܒܳܫܳܝܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܕܐܝܺܬ ܒ݁ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܠܬܰܚܬ ܡܰܢܶܗ ܒ݁ܚܰܝܠܳܗ
the riches of His sweetness, with heavenly bread, as it is written: Man ate the bread of angels. Labor and the pains of childbirth and the pains of the body were not, just as David also explained: Because the children of men exacerbated the word of God, which said to them: «Do not transgress My commandments» and rejected the good pleasure of the Most High, by which He willed that they should become after the likeness of angels: therefore, he says, He crushed their heart with labor and they were weakened, nor is there anyone to help them, unless they keep the commandments of the Lord and beseech Him. And the Father was reconciled to them through His Son and saved them for His name's sake and through the charity of the Lord Jesus Christ. Even if the Lord had made them children, as He made Eve from Adam, without concupiscence and without coitus, whether from the hairs of the head or from their nails, if He had willed, He would have made children for them and they would have been men after the likeness of the Angels. And He who created them would have prepared for them food, whatever He had willed, without labor, and He Himself would have had care of them, as the Lord said: Do not be solicitous for your body nor for your soul, because He who created you has the greatest care of you. Hence, he says, commit your solicitude to the Lord and He Himself will nourish you and alleviate you and preserve you. By this reason men would have been in body on earth, in spirit in heaven, until it had pleased their Creator to assume them into the height; nor would anything on earth have harmed them: not the reptile, nor the biting beast, nor Satan, unless they had willed of their own accord to obey the reptile and Satan. For He said to them on the day He created them: I will send your fear and dread into all things that are on earth. And the hand of the Lord would have been over Adam and the hand of Adam would have subdued all things which were lower than him on earth, by the power of the Lord Almighty. And they were created without earthly desires; that is: let us not impute weakness to God, that He so willed, nor that His will was not effected, as He willed.


[p. 602] {#po.0.p602}


[p. 603] {#po.0.p603}
ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܐܰܚܝܺܕ݂ ܟܽܠ. ܘܰܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܪ̈ܓܝܺܓ݁ܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܰܪܥܳܐ ܐܶܬܒܪܝܺܝܘ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕܶܝܢ: ܠܳܐ ܢܣܺܝܡ ܡܚܺܝܠܘܽܬܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܗܳܟܰܢ ܨܳܒܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܘܳܐ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܨܒܳܐ܀ ܠܰܘ ܡܶܙܟܳܐ ܙܟܺܝܗ̱ܝ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܘܝܰܠܺܝܕ݂ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܠܰܐܠܳܗܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܒܛܰܝܒܘܽܬܶܗ ܘܰܒܒܰܣܺܝܡܘܽܬܶܗ ܝܰܗ̱ܒ݂ ܠܗܘܢ ܚܺܐܪܘܽܬ݂ܳܐ ܘܨܶܒܝܳܢܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܫܰܥܒ݁ܺܝܕ݂ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܐܰܟ ܫܰܪܟ݁ܳܐ ܕܒܶܪ̈ܝܳܬܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪ̈ܳܢܝܳܬܳܐ ܕܰܡܫܰܥܒ̈ܕ݂ܳܢ: ܘܠܰܝܬ ܠܗܶܝܢ ܚܺܐܪܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܐܳܕܳܡ ܐܺܝܬ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ: ܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܐܟܳܢ ܠܕ݂ܝܰܢܳܐ ܕܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܢܰܦ݂ܫܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ ܐܝܺܬ ܠܗܶܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܚܺܐܪܘܽܬܶܗ. ܐܶܢ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܨܳܒ݁ܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܕܢܶܚܒܘܽܫ ܚܺܐܪܘܽܬܗܘܽܢ: ܐܰܚܟ ܕ݁ܰܒܪܶܡܙܳܐ ܕܰܪܦܰܦ݂ ܥܰܝܢܳܐ ܡܰܝܬܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܠܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܝܰܗ̱ܒ݂ ܠܶܗ ܠܳܕ݁ܳܡ ܚܺܐܪܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܣܳܡ ܠܶܗ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܠܥܘܽܕ݂ܪܳܢܳܗ ܕܢܰܦܫܶܗ:
8. Adam and his descendants did not overcome God by overcoming, but by His grace and sweetness He gave them liberty and will, not wishing to subdue them, as the other remaining creatures, which are subdued and have no liberty, which Adam had, nor will they go to judgment, because they have neither a soul, as Adam had, nor his liberty. For if He had willed to restrict their liberty, as if by a nod and the blink of an eye He would have brought them to His will; yet He gave Adam liberty and proposed


[p. 604] {#po.0.p604}


[p. 605] {#po.0.p605}
ܕܠܳܐ ܢܰܪܦ݁ܶܐ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܘܢܺܐܪܰܬ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܡܶܢ ܥܰܡܠܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܘܡܶܢ ܨܶܦܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܡܶܢ ܒܝܺܫܬܳܐ ܟܠܺܝܝܗ̱ܝ: ܘܠܰܘ ܡܶܢ ܓܰܡܝܺܪܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܡܶܢ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ. ܘܰܕܬܶܫ݁ܰܪ ܠܟ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܚܰܙܝܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܕܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܥܰܪܛܳܠܺܝܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܦܰܓܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܝܳܕ݂ܥܺܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܟܬܝܺܒ: ܕ݁ܰܗܘܰܘ ܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ܂ ܘܚܰܘܳܐ ܥܰܪ̈ܛܶܠܳܝܺܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܚܰܙܝܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܥܰܪܛܶܠܳܝܘܽܬܗܘܿܢ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܕܐܶܟܰܠܘ ܡܶܢ ܐܰܝܠܳܢܳܐ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܶܢ ܕܰܫܒܰܩܘ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܘܰܪܚܶܡܘ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܘܐܶܬܳܐ ܪܶܥܝܳܢܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܠܘܳܐ ܦܰܓܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ: ܗܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܚܙܰܘ ܕܥܰܪ̈ܛܶܠܺܝܝܺܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ. ܐܝܺܬܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܒ݁ܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܡܗܰܠܟܝܺܢ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܘܰܡܡܰܠ̱ܠܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܡܶܢ ܦܰܓܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܚܰܘܝܺ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܒܗܳܢܳܐ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܝܳܐ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܐܶܬܝܺܬ ܕܐܶܥܒ݁ܶܕ݂ ܨܶܒ݂ܝܳܢܳܟ݂ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܗܰܘ ܕܡܶܢ ܒܪܝܽܫܝܺܬ ܐܰܘܒ݁ܶܕ݂ ܐܳܕܳܡ. ܐܳܡܰܪ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܥܰܠ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܕܶܒܝܳܢܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܝܳܐ ܕ݂ܕܳܡܶܐ ܠܗܰܘ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܳܐ: ܕܪܘܚܳܐ ܐܰܝܟܳܐ ܕܨܳܒܝܳܐ ܢܳܫܒܳܐ ܘܩܳܠܳܗ ܫܳܡܰܥ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܗܳܟܰܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܝܳܠܕ݂ܝܺܢ ܡܶܢ ܪܘܽܚܳܐ. ܘܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܕ݂ܪܘܺܚܳܐ ܩܳܠܳܗ ܗ̱ܘܳ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܫܳܡܰܥ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ: ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܐܰܝܡܟܳܐ ܐܳܬܝܳܐ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ: ܘܠܳܐ ܠܐܰܝܟܳܐ ܕܐܳܙܿܠ̱ܐ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ: ܗܳܟܰܢ ܩܳܠܳܐ ܕܐܳܕܳܡ ܘܰܕ݂ܚܰܘܳܐ ܡܶܫܬܡܰܥ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܦܰܓܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܪܶܥܝܳܢܗܘܽܢ ܒ݁ܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܩܕܳܡ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܩܳܐܶܡ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ. ܐܰܝܟ ܕܝܰܘܡܳܢܳܐ: ܕܐܺܝܬ ܐ݈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܕܰܒܪܘܰܚ ܕܰܡܡܰܠ̱ܠܝܺܢ ܥܰܡ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܟ݁ܰܕ ܚܳܝܪܝܺܢ ܒܪܰܒܘܺܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܟܡܳܐ ܐܶܬܡܰܟܟܰܬ: ܘܐܝܺܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܪܶܥܝܳܢܗܘܽܢ ܥܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܒ݁ܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܘܟܰܕ݂ ܡܨܰܠܶܝܢ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܐܳܙܿܠ ܩܳܠܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܦܰܓܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ: ܗܳܢܘܽܢ ܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܚܳܝܪܝܺܢ ܒܪܘܽܚ: ܒܗܰܘ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܝܺܠܝܳܕ݂ ܡܶܢ ܪܘܽܚܳܐ: ܘܕܳܡܝܺܢ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ ܒܡܰܟܝܺܟܘܽܬܳܐ. ܘܟܰܕ݂ ܐܝܺܬܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܗܳܟܰܢ ܒ݁ܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܐܶܬܡܰܟܰܟܘ ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܰܢܒܰܩܘ ܟܽܠܥܺܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܡܶܬܚܙܶܐ: ܕ݁ܰܠܥܶܠ
to him the law, as an aid to his soul, lest having left heaven he should gain the earth. For He restrained him from labor and care and from evil, not from perfection and heaven. And so that it may be certain to you that the earth was invisible to them, they did not even know their bodies to be naked, but as it is written: Adam and Eve were naked, nor was their nakedness visible to them; but when they ate from the tree (that is, after they had left heaven and loved the earth and their mind came down from heaven to their bodies) then they saw that they were naked. For they were in heaven, while they walked on earth, and they spoke from their body, as the Lord demonstrated them in His latest will saying: I came, that I might do Thy will, O God, which Adam lost from the beginning. For of this latest will, similar to the first, He said: The Spirit, where He wills, blows and you hear His voice. Such are they who are born of the Spirit. And just as you hear the voice of the spirit only, nor do you know whence it comes nor whither it goes: so the voice of Adam and Eve was heard from their bodies, their mind standing in heaven before God, just as today are spiritual men, who speak on earth with men, looking at the majesty of the Lord, how greatly it has been humbled; and their mind is with the Lord in heaven and they themselves, praying on earth and their voice proceeding from their bodies, contemplate in heaven in spirit that which is born of the Spirit, and they are similar to the Lord in humility; and by this reason, having been made in heaven (because they humbled themselves and because they left all visible things) they turn their sight and mind upward. Even if they wish to be exalted and return to the earth, so that they may possess it and use it, they remain and the gate being closed before their face they go out from the heavenly Jerusalem, just as Adam from the spiritual Eden, which is the spiritual Jerusalem, the city of God. Thus therefore, according to the demonstration which we have demonstrated, the mind of Adam was in heaven chastely, and sweetly in those fruits of the Spirit, which the Apostle explained.


[p. 606] {#po.0.p606}


[p. 607] {#po.0.p607}
ܢܰܦܢܘܽܢ ܚܰܕ݂ܪܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܘܪܶܓ݂ܠܰܝܗܘܽܢ. ܘܐܶܢܗܘܽ ܕܨܳܒ݂ܶܝܢ ܕܢܶܬܬܪܝܺܡܘܽܢ ܘܢܶܬܦܢܘܽܢ ܠܰܐܪܥܳܐ ܠܡܶܒܩܥܳܐ ܘܰܠܡܶܬܚܰܫܳܚܘܽ ܒܳܗ: ܦܳܝܫܺܝܢ ܠܗܘܿܢ ܘܡܶܬܬܚܺܕ݂ ܬ݁ܰܪܥܳܐ ܒܐܰܦܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ ܘܢܳܦܩܺܝܢ ܡܶܢ ܐܘܿܪܺܝܫܠܶܡ ܕܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܡܶܢ ܥܕܶܢ ܪܘܽܚܳܢܳܝܬܳܐ: ܕܗܝ݇ ܗ̱ܝ݇ ܐܘܽܪܺܝܫܠܶܡ ܕܰܒܪܘܰܚ ܡܕܰܒܪܳܢܺܝܬܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ. ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܗܳܟܝܶܠ ܒܰܕ݂ܡܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܬܰܚܘܝܺܬܳܐ ܕܚܰܘܝܺܢܰܢ: ܐܝܺܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܪܶܓ݂ܠܶܗ ܕܐܳܕܳܡ ܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܕܰܟܝܳܐܝܺܬ ܘܒܰܣܝܳܡܳܐܝܺܬ: ܒܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܦܺܐܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ݂ܪܘܺܚܳܐ ܕܦܰܪܶܫ ܫܠܺܝܚܳܐ܀ ̇ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܩܪܶܒ ܢܟܝܺܠܳܐ ܒܰܢܟܝܺܠܘܽܬܶܗ ܠܘܳܬ ܚܰܘܳܐ ܘܐܳܕܳܡ: ܫܰܕ݁ܶܠ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܠܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܥܳܕܶܠ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ: ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܠܟܿܳܪܘܽܝܳܐ ܕܟ݁ܽܠ: ܗܳܐ ܚܙܝܺ ܡܳܐ ܦ݁ܰܐܝܳܐ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܒܩܶܢܝܳܢܳܗ ܘܰܡܠܟܽܘܬܳܗ. ܩܢܝܺ ܘܐܰܡܠܶܟ݂ ܘܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܶܗܘܶܐ ܡܶܣܟܺܢܳܐ ܘܐܶܣܬ݁ܰܪܰܩ ܘܐܶܗܘܶܐ ܢܘܽܟܪܳܝܳܐ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕܙܶܠ ܠܳܟ ܠܒܶܣܬ݁ܰܪܝ ܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ. ܘܡܶܚܕ݂ܳܐ ܒܠܰܥ
9. But the crafty one, with his craftiness approaching Adam and Eve, flattered them, just as he flattered Jesus, saying to the Creator of all: «Lo, see how beautiful the earth is with its riches and kingdoms! Listen to me and possess and reign and do not be poor and emptied and become a pilgrim on earth». And the Lord said to him: Go behind Me, Satan. And immediately his struggle and temptation was crushed and consumed and failed


[p. 608] {#po.0.p608}


[p. 609] {#po.0.p609}
ܘܐܶܣܬܚܺܝܦ ܘܐܰܘܦܝܺ ܩܪܳܒ݂ܶܗ ܘܢܶܣܝܘܽܢܶܗ. ܗܳܟܰܢ ܐܳܦ ܠܳܐܕ݂ܳܡ ܫܰܕ݁ܶܠܶܗ ܒܢܺܝܟܠܳܐ: ܘܰܩܪܶܒ݂ ܠܘܳܬܶܗ ܐܰܝܟ ܚܳܨܘܽܦ݁ܳܝܐ ܘܒܳܩܶܠ ܛܰܥܢܳܐ ܘܡܰܠܟܳܝܗ ܠܚܰܘܳܐ ܕܬܶܡܠܶܟ݂ ܠܶܐܕܳܡ: ܘܦܰܩܕ݂ܳܗ ܕܬܺܐܡܰܪ ܠܶܐܕ݁ܳܡ ܕܢܶܩܢܶܐ ܢܶܟ݁ܣܶܐ ܘܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܡܰܠܟܳܐ: ܗܳܐ ܕܰܗܒܳܐ ܘܣܺܝܡܳܐ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܟܽܠ ܦܘܽܢܳܩ̈ܝܳܢ. ܩܢܰܘ ܘܐܶܬܒܰܣܰܡܘ ܘܐܰܡܠܶܟ݂ܘ ܘܰܟܒܰܪܘ ܘܰܣܓ݂ܰܘ: ܡܰܠܟܳܐ ܒܚܰܝܳܐ. ܘܰܦܕܰܘ ܡܶܢܟܘܽܢ ܥܰܢܘܳܝܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܰܡܣܰܪܩܘܳܬܳܐ ܘܩܰܕ݂ܝܺܫܘܽܬܳܐ ܐܳܦ݂ ܡܘܽܟܳܟܳܐ ܘܕܰܥܘ ܒܝ̈ܫ̈ܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܕܰܥܘ ܛܳܒ̈ܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܐܶܬܪܰܒܘ ܘܰܗܘܰܘ ܐܰܝܟ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܗܰܘ ܕܰܒܪܳܟܘܽܢ. ܘܡܰܠܟܰܝܬ ܚܰܘܳܐ ܠܳܐܕܳܡ: ܕܫܰܦܝܪ ܘܰܡܠܰܟܰܢ ܗܰܘ ܡܳܪܘܽܕܳܐ. ܐܶܢ ܡܳܐ ܡܶܛܺܝܠ ܕܩܰܕ݂ܡܺܝ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܡܶܢܰܢ ܘܩܰܫܺܝܫ ܡܶܢܰܢ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ. ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܠܚܰܘܳܐ: ܕܰܗܦܘܽܟܝ ܐܳܡܪܝ ܠܶܗ: ܕܦܰܩܕ݂ܰܢ ܒܳܪܘܽܝܰܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܫܬܡܰܥ ܠܳܟ: ܘܠܳܐ ܢܶܐܟ݂ܘܽܠ ܡܶܢܶܗ:
In that way also Adam was flattered with craftiness and, approaching him as a companion of counsel and aid, he persuaded Eve to give counsel to Adam, and commanded her to tell Adam to possess riches and become a king: «Behold gold and silver is on earth and all delights. Possess and delight and reign and grow and multiply», the Evil One persuaded, «and cast away from you continence and renunciation and holiness and even humility and know evils and know goods and grow and be like God, who created you». And Eve persuaded Adam: «That rebel gave us excellent counsel; since he is prior and older than we are, he himself knows». And Adam said to Eve: «Return and say to him: our Creator commanded us not to obey you nor to eat from it, lest we be detained in earthly things». This is: lest we should labor nor possess anything on earth. And twisting his tongue, he persuaded her: «Because He does not will nor acquiesce, lest you become like Him». And Adam said: «And if He does not will us to become such, will He not punish us, because we have acted boldly?» And the Evil One said: «When you are like Him, what is it to you?»


[p. 610] {#po.0.p610}
ܘܠܳܐ ܢܶܬܬܚܶܝܕ݂ ܒܐܰܪ̈ܥܳܢܳܝܬܳܐ. ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕܶܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܢܰܥܡܰܠ ܘܠܳܐ ܢܶܝܩܢܶܐ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܘܰܗܦ݁ܰܟ ܠܥܰܝܢܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܐܰܦܚܺܝܣܳܝܗ: ܕܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܨܳܒ݁ܶܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܢܺܝܝ ܕܬܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܶܗ. ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܘܐܶܢ ܠܳܐ ܨܳܒܶܐ ܕܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ ܢܶܙܗܘܶܐ: ܠܳܐ ܐܰܒܰܥ ܠܰܢ ܥܠ ܕܐܰܡܪܰܚܢܰܢ܆ ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܒܚܽܫܳܚܐ: ܡܳܐ ܕܰܗܘܰܝܬܘܽܢ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܶܗ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܚܳܝܒ ܠܟܘܽܢ& ܚܙܝ ܓ݁ܰܒܪܳܐ ܕܐܰܝܕ݂ܳܐ ܬ݁ܰܪܥܝܳܬܳܐ ܐܶܬܪܰܥܝ ܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ܂ ܥܰܠ ܡܰܢ ܕܰܒܪܳܝܗ̱ܝ ܡܶܢ ܥܰܦ݂ܪܳܐ ܘܚܰܠܛܶܗ ܥܰܡ ܡܰܠܰܐܟ̈ܶܐ ܫܡܰܝ̈ܳܢܶܐ. ܘܐܶܫܬܡܰܥ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܘܚܰܘܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܣܰܒܪܳܐ ܕܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܒܳܪܘܝܗܘܽܢ. ܐܳܡܰܪ
10. See, O man, what kind of thought Adam thought about Him who created him from dust and mingled him with the heavenly Angels! And Adam and Eve obeyed because of the hope that they would be like the Creator. For Paul says: The creatures were made subject to vanity. Not, he says, of their own will, but because of Him who subjected them


[p. 611] {#po.0.p611}
ܠܰܣܪܝܺܩܘܽܬܳܐ. ܠܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܒܨܶܒܝܳܢܗܶܝܢ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܡܰܢ ܕܫܰܥܒ݂ܶܕ݂ ܐܶܢܶܝܢ ܥܰܠ ܣܰܒܪܳܐ. ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܰܘ ܡܶܢ ܨܸܒܝܳܢ ܢܰܦܫܗܘܽܢ ܪܢܰܘ ܗܳܕܶܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܒ݀ܠܟܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܐܚܪ̈ܳܢܶܐ. ܫܰܪܟ݁ܳܐ ܕܶܝܢ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܳܐ ܐܝܺܬ ܠܳܗ ܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ: ܘܐܶܠܽܘ ܗܘܳܐ ܨܒܳܐ: ܐܰܠܦ ܫܢ̈ܝܳܢ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕ݁ܰܗܘܳܐ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܕܳܒܰܪ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܒܚܺܫܳܐ ܒܰܩܛܝܳܪܳܐ. ܐܶܬܛܦܝܺܣܘ ܗܳܟ݂ܝܽܠ ܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ܂ ܘܚܰܘܳܐ ܘܐܰܦܢܝܽܘ ܪܶܥܝܳܢܗܘܽܢ ܠܰܐܪܥܳܐ ܘܰܢܚܶܬܘ ܡܶܢ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ: ܘܰܗܘܳܐ ܪܶܥܝܳܢܗܘܽܢ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܦܰܓܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ: ܘܰܦܣܰܩܘ ܘܰܢܚܺܝܬܘ ܡܶܢ ܦܰܪܕ݁ܺܝܣܳܐ ܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܐ: ܕܐܚܺܝܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܬܰܦܢܳܐ ܡܫܰܠܡܳܢܳܐ: ܘܰܗܘܰܘ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܕܐܝܰܬܶܝܗ ܛܶܠܳܢܝܳܬܳܐ ܕܗܰܘ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܶܬ݂ܚܙܶܐ ܠܥܰܝ̈ܢܶܐ ܕܒܶܣܪܳܐ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܛܶܠܳܢܝܳܬܳܐ ܕܗܰܘ ܦ݁ܰܪܕ݁ܰܝܣܳܐ ܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܐ. ܘܰܢܚܶܬ݁ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܘܩܳܡ ܒܦܰܪܕܰܝܣܳܐ ܐܰܪܥܳܢܳܝܳܐ ܕܐܚܺܝܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܛܰܠܳܢܝܳܬܳܗ ܕܰܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܐ. ܘܰܗܘܰܘ ܡܶܣ̈ܟ݁ܺܢܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܥܘܽܬܪܳܐ ܥܶܠܳܝܳܐ ܘܐܰܩܶܦܘ ܠܥܶܡܪܗܽܘܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܥܘܽܬܪܳܐ ܬܰܚܬܳܝܳܐ: ܕܐܝܺܬ݂ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܥܳܒܰܪ ܘܡܶܫܬܪܶܐ ܒ݁ܰܚܕ݂ܳܐ ܫܳܥܳܐ. ܠܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ
because of hope. This is: not of their own accord did they think these things, but by the counsel of others. Otherwise Adam had a will; and if he had not willed, in those thousand years in which he was on earth, the Evil One would not have forced him by violence. Therefore Adam and Eve obeyed and, turning their mind to the earth, they descended from heaven and were made to use their mind and body on earth and, destitute of hope, they descended from the heavenly paradise, which is the perfect exemplar, and were made on earth, which is an image of [things] invisible to the eyes of the flesh; that is: an image of the heavenly paradise. And Adam descending stood in the earthly paradise, which is the image of heaven; and they were made poor of heavenly riches and followed the course after inferior riches, which are perishable things and dissoluble in one hour. Nevertheless, before God had cursed them, they did not labor


[p. 612] {#po.0.p612}


[p. 613] {#po.0.p613}
ܡܶܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܕܰܢܠܘܽܛ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܥܡܠܘ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܒ݁ܰܪܫܳܥܬ݂ܶܗ ܕ݁ܩܰܒ݁ܶܠܘ ܡܘܽܠܟܳܢܶܗ ܕܒܺܝܫܳܐ ܘܫܳܛܘ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܶܗ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܠܳܛ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܘܰܢܦܰܩܘ ܡܶܢ ܦܰܪܕ݂ܰܝܣܳܐ ܪܘܽܚܳܢܳܐ. ܘܗܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܦܠܚܘ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܕܐܶܬܒܪܝܽܘ ܡܶܢܳܗ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܥܘܽܬܪܳܐ ܕܥܳܒܰܪ. ܘܡܶܢ ܕܰܚܙܰܘ ܕܥܰܪܛܶܠܳܝܺܝܢ: ܡܶܢ ܕ݁ܰܠܒܶܫ ܪܶܥܝܢܗܘܽܢ ܗܰܘ ܫܘܽܒ݂ܚܳܐ ܥܶܠܳܝܳܐ ܐܰܩܶܦܘ ܠܡܰܐܨܰܦ ܕܰܠܒܘܽܫܳܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕ݁ܝܰܕ݂ܰܥܘ ܒܶܗܬܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܚܰܙܝܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܚܳܝܪܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܒ݁ܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ. ܘܰܚܙܰܘ ܕܐܶܬܟܠܺܝ ܠܰܚܡܳܐ ܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܐ ܘܐܰܩܶܦܘ ܠܥܰܡܠܳܐ ܒ݁ܙܰܪܥܳܐ ܠܣܰܝܒܳܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܙܗܘܰܘ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕܰܝܗܘܽܢ: ܘܐܶܬܓܠܶܙܘ ܡܶܢ ܡܰܠܳܐܟ̈ܶܐ ܘܡܶܢ ܡܰܫܪ̈ܝܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܪܰܘܪ̈ܒ݁ܳܬܳܐ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܰܟ̈ܝܺܟ݁ܳܢ ܠܢܳܛܪ̈ܰܝ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܠܰܐܝܠܺܝܢ ܕܫܳܛܝܢ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ. ܘܐܰܩܶܦܘ ܠܥܶܒܕ݁ܳܐ ܠܟܰܘܬܳܢܘܽܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܠܡܰܘܠܰܕ݂ ܐܰܝܟ ܚܰܝܘܳܬܳܐ. ܘܚܳܪܘ ܒܙܰܪܥܳܐ
on earth, but as soon as, having received the counsel of the Evil One, they had despised the word of God, He cursed them and they went out from the spiritual paradise: then at last they tilled the earth, from which they were created, because of perishable riches. And when they had seen that they were naked and their mind had put off the high glory, they immediately began to have care for clothing, because they knew shame, which did not appear to them while they were looking at heaven. And seeing the heavenly bread being withheld, they began to till the earth for the sake of food and they were desolate and excommunicated from the angels and from the great camps, which surround those who observe the commandments, not those who despise the word of God. And they began to covet coitus and generation like animals, and having looked at the earth they were assimilated to it, because they did not understand their high honor and connection and their charity toward the heavenly angels.


[p. 614] {#po.0.p614}
ܘܐܶܬ݁ܕ݂ܰܡܝܽܘ ܒܳܗ ܕܠܳܐ ܐܶܬܒ݂ܰܚܰܢܘ ܒܐܝܺܩܳܪܗܘܽܢ ܥܶܠܳܝܳܐ. ܘܰܒܚܘܽܠܛܳܢܗܘܽܢ ܘܰܒܚܘܽܒܗܘܽܢ ܕ݁ܰܠܘܳܬ ܥܶܠܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܥܶܠܳܝ̈ܶܐ܀ ܘܰܒ݂ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܟ݁ܽܠܗܶܝܢ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܘܚܰܘܳܐ ܨܒܰܝܘ ܘܐܶܫܬܰܦܰܠܘ ܒܚܰܕ݂ ܡܶܨܥܳܝܳܐ ܒܺܝܫܳܐ ܘܰܫܒܰܩܘ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܘܥܘܽܬܪܳܐ ܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܐ: ܘܰܪܚܺܝܡܘ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܟܽܠ ܕܒܳܗ. ܥܰܪܛܶܠܳܝܺܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܒܶܝܬ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܠܒܘܽܫܳܐ ܕܡܶܬܚܙܶܐ ܒܗܳܢܳܐ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ. ܗܳܟ݂ܰܢ ܐܝܺܬܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܕܒܶܝܬ ܐܳܕܳܡ܂ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܚܛܘܽܢ: ܘܠܰܘܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܠܳܐ ܝܳܕ݂ܥܝܺܢ ܚܛܰܘ ܒܡܳܪܘܽܕܘܽܬܗܘܽܢ. ܒܗܳܕܶܐ ܕܝܢ ܣܰܒܪܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ: ܕܰܣܒܰܪܘ ܕܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ. ܘܰܛܥܰܘ ܕܠܝܬ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕ݁ܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܕܢܶܙܗܘܶܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܒܳܪܘܽܝܳܐ ܕܥܳܠܡܶܐ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ: ܗܰܘ ܕܗܘܰܝܘ̈ ܒܳܪܘܽܝܳܐ: ܘܗܘܺܝܘ̈ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܡܫܺܝܚܳܐ. ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܶܝܢ ܚܳܙܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܘܡܰܥܠܶܡ: ܘܡܰܣܝܒܰܪ ܪܘܽܚܶܗ ܘܰܡܣܰܝܒܰܪ: ܟܰܕ݂ ܥܳܐܶܛ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܡܶܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ̈ ܘܫܳܪܶܐ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܘܒܳܥܶܐ ܕܢܶܚܛܘܽܦ ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܦܶܚܡܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܒܪܳܡܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܒܡܰܟܝܺܟܘܽܬܳܐ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܫܠܺܝܚܳܐ ܕܰܡܫܝܺܚܳܐ ܠܰܘ ܒܰܚܛܘܽܦܝܳܐ ܨܒܳܐ ܕ݁ܢܶܙܗܘܶܐ ܦ݁ܶܚܡܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܐܳܕܳܡ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܣܰܪܶܩ: ܐܳܦ݂ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܰܪܚܶܡ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܘܰܒܥܳܐ ܕܢܶܙܗܘܶܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܒܥܘܽܬܪܳܐ ܐܰܪܥܳܢܳܐ: ܘܰܕܡܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܥܰܒܕ݂ܳܐ ܢܣܰܒ: ܟܰܕ݂ ܗܘܳܐ ܒܰܕ݂ܡܘܽܬܳܗ ܕܗܳܝ ܘܰܒܚܘܽܒܶܗ ܘܰܒܡܰܟܝܺܟܘܽܬܶܗ: ܕܰܢܚܰܘܶܐ ܠܰܢ ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܰܚܳܐ ܘܰܒܪܳܐ ܘܝܳܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܩܰܪܝܰܒܳܐ: ܕܰܨܒ݂ܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܚܣܳܡܳܐ ܕܢܶܥܡܪܘܽܢ ܥܰܡܗ ܐܰܪ̈ܥܳܢܶܐ: ܕܡܘܽܬܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܕܥܰܒܕ݂ܳܐ ܢܣܰܒ ܕܢܶܫܬܡܰܥ ܠܰܐܒܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܥܰܒܕ݂ܳܐ. ܠܰܘ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܢܣܰܝܒ ܠܶܗ ܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ ܕܡܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܪܳܡܘܽܬ݂ܳܐ ܕܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܕܰܠܩܘܽܒܠܳܐ ܘܣܰܩܘܽܒ݁ܠܳܐ ܠܡܳܪܶܗ ܘܰܠܒܳܪܘܽܝܶܗ: ܘܢܺܬܶܒ ܠܩܘܽܒܠܶܗ ܘܢܶܠܨܺܝܘܗ̱ܝ. ܠܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܣܰܚܦܶܗ ܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ܂ ܒܚܰܘܡܳܐ ܕܰܢܦ݁ܰܠ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܪܳܡܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܰܨܒܳܐ ܕܢܶܙܗܘܶܐ
11. And all these things willing, Adam and Eve were prostituted through the Evil One and, having left heaven and heavenly riches, they loved the earth and all things that are in it. But the household of Adam were naked of visible clothing in this world. Such were the household of Adam, before they had sinned, nor yet did they sin in ignorance in their rebellion; yet they were foolish, thinking they would be like God, and they forgot that there is nothing that can be made like the Creator of all ages, who is the Creator and He Himself is the Lord Jesus Christ. But God saw and winked and bore it patiently, when Adam despised the words and broke His commandments, willing by way of robbery to become equal to God, by pride, not by humility. Therefore the Apostle said: Christ did not will to become equal to God by robbery, as Adam, but emptied Himself, even from that thing which Adam loved, God willing to become [rich] with earthly riches, and took the form of a servant, made in the likeness of the creature of the first man by his obedience, charity, and humility, to show us by what reason a man might become a brother and son and heir and neighbor, willing without envy for earthly ones to dwell with Him. He took, he says, the form of a servant, so that He might obey His Father like a servant. Not like Adam, He took the form of pride, so that He might become a contrary and adversary to His Lord and Creator and fix His seat opposite Him by rebelling. For Adam lost nothing on the day he fell, except pride, willing to become equal to God because of his pride,


[p. 615] {#po.0.p615}


[p. 616] {#po.0.p616}


[p. 617] {#po.0.p617}
ܦ݁ܶܚܡܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܒܪܳܘܡܘܽܬܶܗ. ܘܗܝܺ ܥܒܰܕ݂ܬ݁ܶܗ ܝܰܬܺܝܪܳܐ ܘܗܝܿ ܐܰܦܶܩܬ݁ܶܗ ܡܶܢ ܦ݁ܰܪܕܰܝܣܳܐ ܕܡܰܠܟܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܗܝܺ ܫܰܦܶܠܬܶܗ ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܠܰܐܪܥܳܐ. ܐܰܚܰܝ̈ ܢܶܥܪܘܰܩ ܡܶܢ ܪܳܡܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܡܶܠܚܳܐ ܕܦܰܟܗ ܛܰܥܡܳܗ: ܕܐܳܦ ܠܳܐ ܠܙܶܒ݂ܠܳܐ ܐܳܙܿܠ̱ܐ: ܕܠܳܐ ܛܰܥܡܳܐ ܐܝܺܬ ܒܳܗ ܕܢܶܡܠܘܽܚ ܡܶܢܳܗ ܕܶܒܚܶܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܚܰܩܠܳܐ ܡܶܙܕܰܒܠܳܐ ܡܶܢܳܗ ܘܡܰܟܫܪܳܐ ܡܶܢܳܗ ܚܶܛܬ݁ܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕܡܰܢ ܕܢܶܬܬܪܝܰܡ܂
which, rendering him superfluous, cast him out of the paradise of the kingdom and prostrated him even to the earth. Brothers, let us flee pride, lest we be salt made insipid in taste, which does not even go to the dung, since it has no savor to season victims, nor is any field manured with it, nor does wheat become better, as the Lord said: He who exalts himself — like Adam — shall be humbled; and he who humbles himself — like Jesus — shall be exalted, just as He was exalted.
ܐܰܝܟ ܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ: ܢܶܬܡܰܟ݁ܰܟ. ܘܡܰܢ ܕܢܶܬܡܰܟ݁ܰܟ݂ ܐܰܝܟ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܢܶܬܪܝܰܡ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܗܘ ܐܶܬܬܪܝܰܡ܀ ܒܪܳܡܘܽܬ݂ܶܗ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܕܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ ܐܶܚܰܕ݂ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܬܰܪ̈ܥܰܝ ܦܰܪܕܺܝܣܳܐ ܩܕܳܡܰܘܗ̱ܝ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܬ݁ܰܪ̈ܥܳܐ ܕܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ. ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܗܳܟ݂ܝܺܠ ܕܰܒܪܳܡܘܽܬܶܗ ܕܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ ܐܰܦ݂ܩܶܝܗ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܦܰܪܕܰܝܣܳܐ: ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܒܡܰܟܝܺܟܘܽܬܶܗ ܡܰܥܶܠ ܠܳܗ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܰܣܶܩ ܠܶܗ ܠܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܥܶܠܳܝܳܐ: ܠܰܐܬ݂ܰܪ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܥܳܡܰܪ ܘܡܶܬܚܙܶܐ ܠܳܗ ܬܰܡܳܢ. ܐܶܡܰܪ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ: ܕܰܒ݁ܡܰܢ ܡܪܰܥܶܝܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܠܝܽ ܡܶܢ ܒܳܬ݁ܰܪ ܕܐܰܪܓܶܙܬܘܽܢܳܢܝ܆ ܒܣܶܢܺܝܝܢܶܐ ܐܰܘ ܒܕܶܒ̈ܚܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܚܰܝ̈ܘܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܚܰܪ̈ܫܳܬ݁ܳܐܢ ܕܶܒܚܝ ܕ݁ܝܺܠܝ ܡܶܟܝܺܠ: ܘܐܰܪܥܽܘܬܝ ܘܨܶܒܝܢܝ ܘܰܢܝܳܚܝ ܐܝܺܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ: ܢܚܺܝܚܳܐ ܘܡܰܟܝܺܟ ܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܕܚܳܐܰܪ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܒܶܗ ܘܥܳܡܰܪ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܒܶܗ: ܘܗܘܽ ܒܝܽ ܣܳܠܳܩ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܣܳܠܶܩ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܠܰܐܬܪܳܐ ܕܰܢܝܳܚܝ. ܘܐܳܦ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܕܰܓܒܳܝܗ̱ܝ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܡܘ̈ܫܶܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܡܰܟܝܺܟ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ. ܡܰܟܝܺܟܘܽܬܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܟ݂ܽܠ ܐܶܬܬܰܩܠܰܬ݂ ܘܗܝܺ ܢܶܛܠܰܬ. ܬܰܩܠܶܗ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܡܘܽܫܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܫܶܬܡܳܐܐ ܐܰܠܦܺܝܢ ܐܳܣܪ̈ܰܝ ܣܰܝܦܳܐ ܘܥܰܡ ܢܶܫܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ ܘܥܰܡ
12. Because of the pride of Adam, God closed the gates of paradise before him; that is, the gates of heaven. Just as therefore because of pride God cast Adam out of paradise, so by His humility He introduces him, that is, He assumes him into the highest heaven, where God dwells and appears to him. For He said: With what thing will you appease Me, after you have provoked Me to anger? With riches or sacrifices of dumb animals? My sacrifice therefore is and My good pleasure and will and My rest is the meek and humble in spirit, whom I shall look upon and in whom I shall dwell; and he himself will ascend through Me, when I shall ascend into the place of My rest. Furthermore, He said that God had chosen Moses, because he was more humble than all men. Humility weighed against all things outweighs; for God weighed Moses with six hundred thousand girded with the sword together with their wives and their children and, that meek man being placed in one scale of the balance, the hardness and pride was lighter and humility and meekness outweighed. And the Lord said to him: Go out from this people and I will destroy them in one hour. And Moses said: If You blot them out, blot me out with them. And He said: By no means Moses; he who has sinned against Me, I will blot him out. And Moses said: Not at all, O Lord. If You will forgive them, just as You forgave them from Egypt until here, but if not — blot me out with them. By this reason Moses was magnified, because he counted himself with


[p. 618] {#po.0.p618}


[p. 619] {#po.0.p619}
ܓܰܒܪ̈ܰܝܗ ܕܡܰܥܣܰܪܬܳܐ: ܘܙܶܠܰܬ ܩܰܫܝܽܘܬܳܐ ܘܪܳܡܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܢܶܛܠܰܬ ܡܰܟܝܺܟܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܢܚܺܝܚܘܽܬܳܐ. ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ: ܦܘܽܩ ܠܳܟ݂ ܡܶܢ ܓܰܘܥܰܡܳܐ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܘܐܰܘܒܶܕ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܒ݁ܰܚܕ݂ܳܐ ܫܳܥܳܐ. ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܘܽܫܶܐ: ܐܶܢ ܥܳܛܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܥܛܝܢܝ ܥܰܡܗܘܽܢ. ܘܐܳܡܰܪ: ܐܳܘ ܡܘܽܫܶܐ. ܡܰܢ ܕ݁ܰܚܛܳܐ ܠܝܽ ܐܶܥܛܶܝܘܗ̱ܝ. ܘܐܳܡܰܪ ܡܘܫܶܐ: ܠܳܐ ܡܳܪܝ. ܐܶܢ ܫܳܒܶܩ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܫܒܰܩܬ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܡܶܨܪܶܝܢ ܘܰܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܠܗܳܫܳܐ: ܘܐܶܠܳܐ ܥܛܝܢܝ ܥܰܡܗܘܽܢ. ܘܰܒܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܚܺܝܶܒ ܡܘܽܫܶܐ: ܕܣܳܡ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܥܰܡ ܚܰܛܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܕܟ݁ܽܠ ܝܘܽܡ ܚܳܛܶܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ. ܫܒܽܘܩ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܠܰܡ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܫܒܰܩܬ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܓܵܘ ܡܶܨܪܶܝܢ ܘܰܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܠܗܳܫܳܐ. ܘܐܰܚܶܒ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܠܚܰܛܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܦܪܰܫ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܡܶܢܗܘܽܢ܀
the sinners, sinning all day. Forgive, he says, them, just as You forgave them from Egypt until today. And he loved the sinners, as himself, nor did he separate himself from them.


[p. 620] {#po.0.p620}
ܗܳܟܰܢ ܬܘܽܒ ܨܒܳܐ ܒܶܗ ܒܢܘܽܚ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕܰܘܗ̱ܝ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܠܰܡ ܕ݁ܠܳܟ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܚܙܝܺܬ ܕܬܰܡܚܺܡ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܘܡܰܟܝܺܟ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܡܶܢ ܟ݁ܽܠܳܗ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ: ܕܦܘܽܩ ܡܶܢ ܒܰܝܢܳܬܗܘܽܢ: ܕ݂ܥܳܛܶܐ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ ܠܟܽܠܒܣܰܪ ܕܰܒܪܝܺܬ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܚܰܒܶܠ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܒܣܰܪ ܐܘܽܪܚܶܗ. ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܢܘܽܚ: ܚܳܣ ܠܳܟ ܕܰܬܚܰܒܶܠܶܝܗ ܠܟ݁ܽܠܳܗ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ.
13. Furthermore, for the same reason, He was pleased with Noah alone, for He said: 'You alone have I seen to be pious and more humble than the whole earth.' And the Lord said to him: 'Go out from the midst of them, for I shall destroy all flesh that I have created, because all flesh has corrupted its way.' And Noah said: 'Far be it from You to destroy the whole earth.' And the Lord said to him:


[p. 621] {#po.0.p621}
ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ: ܗܳܐ ܣܳܐܶܡ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ ܠܳܗ ܠܟ݁ܽܠܳܗ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܒܡܰܣܰܐܬܳܐ ܥܰܡܳܟ. ܘܐܶܢ ܢܳܛܠܝܳܢ ܠܩܘܽܒܠܳܟ ܫܳܒܶܩ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܠܗܘܿܢ. ܘܰܬܩܰܠ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܠܰܥܡܶܗ ܘܰܢܛܰܠ ܢܘܽܚ ܒܡܰܟܝܳܟܘܽܬܶܗ ܛܳܒ ܡܶܢ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ. ܘܐܰܣܚܶܦ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܟܽܠܒܣܰܪ
'Behold, I will place the whole earth on the scales with you, and if they outweigh you, I will let them be.' And the Lord weighed them with him, and Noah outweighed them by his humility more than all of them together; and the Lord destroyed all flesh that was proud and wanton at that time.
ܕ݂ܪܳܡ ܘܙܰܠܚܶܠ ܒܗܰܘ ܙܰܒܢܳܐ܀ ܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ ܬܘܽܒ ܒܚܰܘ̈ܡܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܕܐܰܝܘܽܒ ܬܩܰܠ ܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܥܰܡܶܗ. ܘܰܢܛܰܠ ܐܰܝܘܽܒ ܒܡܰܟܝܺܟܘܽܬܶܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܐܶܫܬܟܰܚ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܶܗ ܒܚܰܘ̈ܡܰܘܗ̱ܝ. ܘܣܳܗܶܕ݂ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܚܳܐ ܡܰܢ ܥܰܒܕܝ ܐܰܝܘܽܒ: ܕܬܰܡܚܺܡ ܘܰܐܪܝܺܨ ܘܡܰܣܛܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܒܝܺܫܬܳܐ: ܘܠܰܝܬ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܶܗ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܘܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܥܰܠ ܘܰܥܣܰܐܬ݂ܳܐ. ܗܳܟܰܢ ܟܬܝܒ ܕܐܰܝܟ ܠܰܗܓܿܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܕܰܓܳܠ̈ܶܐ: ܕܰܒܡܰܣܰܐܬ݂ܳܐ ܬܩܝܺܠܝܺܢ ܘܰܣܕ݁̈ܝܺܩܝܺܢ ܐܰܟܚܕ݂ܳܐ. ܡܳܢܳܐ ܐܳܡܪܝܺܢܳܢܢ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܗܶܢܘܽܢ ܗܘܰܘ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܡܰܟ̈ܝ̈ܟܶܐ: ܕ݁ܰܠܡܳܐ ܡܶܬܕܰܒܪܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܠܪܳܡܘܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܠܬ݁ܰܙܝܰܙܘܺܬܳܐ ܕܰܡܠܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܬ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܟܠܳܗ̇ ܘܝܰܘܡܳܢ ܡܳܐ ܕܐܶܡܰܪܢ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܕܐܶܬܡܰܟܟ݁ܰܟ ܘܰܥܒܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܒܝܺܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܥܒܶܕ݂ ܛܳܒܬ݁ܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܩܰܕܡܳܝܶܐ. ܐܳܡܰܪ: ܕܠܰܝܬ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܕܥܳܒ݁ܶܕ݂ ܗܳܟܘܳܐ ܝܰܘܡܳܢܳܐ. ܘܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܘܐܶܢܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܗܳܘܶܝܢܰܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܢܘܽܚ ܘܐܺܝܘܽܒ ܘܕ݂ܳܢܝܺܐܶܝܠ: ܕܐܳܦ ܗܘܽ ܡܰܟܝܺܟ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܗܘܽܢ: ܕܥܰܡܗܘܽܢ ܣܳܡܳܗ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܡܢܳܬܶܗ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܰܝܬ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܐܰܝܟ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ. ܠܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܡܶܬܡܰܟܟ݁ܰܟ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ. ܐ݈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܡܰܟܝܺܟܝܺܢ ܘܰܡܝܰܬܪܝܺܢ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐܝܺܬ ܝܰܘܡܳܢ: ܚܰܕ݂ ܒܶܝܬ ܣܰܓܝ̈ܳܐܶܐ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܒܶܗ ܒܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܠܳܐ ܐܝܺܬ ܡܰܟܝܺܟܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܒܰܣܝܺܡܘܽܬܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܠܡܰܟ̈ܝܺܟܶܐ ܝܺܕ݂ܝܰܥ ܘܠܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܥܳܡܰܪ ܒܶܗ: ܘܠܳܐ ܦܪܳܪܳܐ ܘܰܕܪܶܡ܀
14. Likewise, even in the time of Job, He weighed everyone with him, and Job outweighed them by his humility, nor was anyone found like him in those days. And God testifies, saying: 'O, who is My servant Job, who is simple and upright and a stranger to evil, and there is none like him on the earth.' And what I said about the scales is written thus: 'As a vapor are all men liars, who, when weighed in the scales, are all together vanity.' What are we to say? Is it because these alone were humble that they were carried toward the pride and perversity with which the whole earth was filled? And if we say to anyone today: 'Humble yourself, depart from evil and do good, as the ancients did,' he says: 'There is no one who does so today.' Why are you and I not like Noah and Job and Daniel (for he too was humble like them, because the Lord placed his portion with them), if not because there is no one like them? 'I will not,' he says, 'humble myself.' Nevertheless, there are today men more humble and more excellent than them, a few among many. Yet, if humility and meekness are lacking in someone, he is not known to the humble, nor does God dwell in him, nor does he attain the truth.


[p. 622] {#po.0.p622}


[p. 623] {#po.0.p623}
ܐܳܦ ܦ݁ܰܐܘܠܳܘܣ ܕܶܝܢ ܣܰܓܺܝ ܪܰܒ: ܕܐܰܚܶܒ ܠܒܺܝ̈ܫܶܐ ܛܲܝܒ ܡܶܢ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܘܐܳܡܰܪ: ܕܣܳܗܶܕ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܝ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܕܨܳܒܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܺܝܬ ܕܐܶܡܽܘܬ: ܘܰܢܫܰܒܚܽܘܢ ܒܺܝ̈ܫܶܐ ܠܡܳܪܳܗ ܕܬܶܫܒܽܘܚܬܳܐ: ܐܶܢ ܨܳܒܶܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܰܢܩܰܒܠܰܢܝ: ܘܰܢܚܰܠܶܦ ܡܰܘܬܝ ܒܚܰܝܰܝ̈ܗܽܘܢ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܐܶܬ݁ܕ݁ܰܡܶܐ ܒܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܡܺܝܬ ܚܠܳܦ
15. Moreover, Paul is very great, because he loved the wicked more than himself and said: 'The Lord is my witness that I wished to die, so that the wicked might glorify the Lord of glory, if God had wished to take me and exchange my death for their salvation,' intending to imitate God, who died for sinners. And all the apostles died for sinners by various deaths: of scourges, of the sword, and of the cross. How then shall we attain them, we who do not even forgive sinners, and how greatly
ܐܰܦܺܝ̈ܢ ܚܰܛܳܝ̈ܶܐ. ܘܰܫܠܺܝܚܶܐ ܟܽܠܗܽܘܢ ܕܢܰܓܕ݁ܶܐ ܘܰܕܣܰܝܦܳܐ ܘܕܰܙܩܺܝܦܳܐ. ܚܢܰܢ ܗܳܟ݂ܰܢܳܐ ܐܰܝܟܰܢܳܐ ܡܰܕܪܟܺܝܢ ܚ̱ܢܰܢ ܠܗܽܘܢ: ܕܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܘܰܟܕܡܳܐ ܦܳܪܩܺܝܢܰܢ ܡܶܢ ܓܰܝܪܽܘܬܳܐ: ܕܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܕܢܰܦܫܰܢ ܝܳܨܦܺܝܢܰܢ. ܟܡܳܐ ܡܚܰܝܒܺܝܢܰܢ
we fall short of perfection, we who do not even take care of our own souls! How greatly shall we be condemned because we pursue them with persecution and kill ourselves, having become persecutors and not those who suffer persecution!


[p. 624] {#po.0.p624}
ܠܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܕܡܶܚܪܕܰܦ ܪܳܕܦܺܝܢܰܢ ܠܗܽܘܢ ܘܩܳܛܠܺܝܢܰܢ ܢܰܦܫܰܢ ܕܰܗܘܰܝܢ ܪܳܕܽܘܦ݁ܶܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܪܶܕܝܳܦܶܐ܀ ܬܘܒ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܰܠܰܐܟ݂ܳܐ ܠܡܰܪܝܰܡ. ܫܠܳܡ ܠܶܟܝ ܒܪܺܝܟܬܳܐ ܕܢܫ̈ܶܐ. ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܰܟܺܝܟܬܳܐ ܕܢܫ̈ܶܐ. ܡܳܪܝ ܥܰܡܟܝ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܡܰܟܺܝܟܽܘܬܶܟܝ. ܘܐܶܡܪܰܬ ܡܰܪܝܰܡ: ܡܰܘܕ݁ܝܳܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܠܰܐܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܚܳܪ ܒܡܽܘܟܳܟܳܐ ܕܐܰܡܬ݁ܶܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܒܫܽܘܦܪܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ
16. Furthermore, the angel said to Mary: 'Peace be to you, blessed among women.' That is, most humble among women. 'My Lord is with you'—because of your humility. And Mary said: 'I confess to God, because He has regarded the humility of His handmaid, not


[p. 625] {#po.0.p625}
ܒܠܽܘܬܪܳܐ. ܐܶܠܘܽ ܐܝܺܬ ܙܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ݁ܬ݁ܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܺܬܳܐ ܕܡܰܟܺܝܟܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܬ ܡܶܢ ܡܰܪܝܰܡ: ܡܶܢܳܗ ܡܶܬܝܺܠܶܕ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܡܫܺܝܚܳܐ: ܗܰܘ ܡܰܟܺܝܟܳܐ ܕܟܽܠܗܽܘܢ
however her beauty and riches.' For if there had existed another woman more humble than Mary, Christ would have been born of her, the most humble of all men, who is the friend of humility.
ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ: ܕܐܺܝܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܪܳܚܡܳܐ ܕܡܰܟܺܝܟܽܘܬܳܐ܀ ܡܶܟܺܝܠ ܘܗܳܐ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܐ ܗܘܳܐ ܬܰܚܬܳܝܳܐ: ܪܽܘܚܳܢܳܐ ܗܘܳܐ ܦ݁ܰܓܪܳܢܳܐ: ܢܦܰܫ ܚܰܝ̈ܶܐ ܗܘܰܬ ܛܰܥܡܰܬ ܡܰܘܬܳܐ. ܘܐܶܬܪܰܟܢܰܬ ܪܰܒܽܘܬܳܐ ܘܡܰܠ̱ܠܰܬ݂ ܥܰܡ ܐܳܕܳܡ. ܘܰܥܪܰܩܘ ܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ ܘܚܰܘܳܐ ܘܐܶܬ݁ܛܰܫܺܝܘ ܒܶܝܬ ܐܝܺܠܳܢ̈ܶܐ ܕܩܳܝܡܺܝܢ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܠܳܐܕܳܡ: ܐܰܝܟ݁ܳܐ ܐ݇ܢ̱ܬ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܕܠܳܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܒܶܝܬ ܥܺܝܪ̈ܶܐ ܥܶܠܳܝ̈ܶܐܢ ܘܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܩܳܠܳܟ݂ ܫܶܡܥܶܬ ܘܐܶܬܛܰܫܺܝܬ ܡܶܢ ܩܕܳܡܰܝܟ: ܕܒܺܝܗܶܬ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܕܐܶܚܙܶܝܟ݂ ܐܳܦ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܗܰܘ ܕܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܐܰܡܺܝܢܳܐܝܺܬ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܦܰܪܨܽܘܦ݁ܳܟ݂ ܩܳܐܶܡ ܗ̱ܘܺܝܬ: ܘܗܳܫܳܐ ܚܳܙܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܦܽܘܪܣܳܝܝ. ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܒܳܗܶܬ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܒܥܶܒܕܳܐ ܕܐܰܬܪܰܥܝܺܬ ܘܦܰܪܛܶܬ ܡܶܠܬܳܟ: ܘܠܳܐ ܝܶܕ݂ܥܳܬ ܕܠܳܐ ܥܰܦܪܳܐ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܓܳܒܽܘܠܶܗ: ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܕܢܶܥܡܰܪ ܥܒܺܝܕ݂ܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܥܳܒܽܘܕ݂ܶܗ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܒܪ̈ܰܚܡܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܢܶܬܡܰܟܰܟ. ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܠܳܐܕܳܡ: ܗܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕ݂ܙܰܗܰܪܬ݁ܳܟ݂ ܡܶܢܶܗ ܐܶܬܚܰܫܰܚܬ. ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܐܰܣܠܺܝܬ ܘܰܓܒܰܝܬ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܐܝܺܠܳܢܳܐ ܛܳܒܿܳܐ ܫܒܰܩܬ: ܠܗܰܘ ܕܠܐ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܗ̱ܘܰܝܬ ܒܶܗ ܒܺܝܫܬܳܐ: ܘܰܢܚܶܬܬ ܠܗܰܘ ܕܝܺܕܰܥܬ
17. Therefore, Adam was made on earth, he was made inferior to the heavenly, he was made bodily from spiritual, the breath of life was made the taste of death. And the Majesty condescended and spoke with Adam; and Adam and Eve, fleeing, hid themselves among the trees standing on the earth. And the Lord said to Adam: 'Where are you, Adam, that you are not among the watchers on high?' And he said: 'I heard Your voice and I hid myself, because I am ashamed to see You even on earth, I who stood constantly before Your face in heaven, and now You see my shame.' This is: I am ashamed of what I thought, having spurned Your word, not knowing that dust is not made like the One who fashions it, nor can the created dwell with its Creator, except through mercy, if it be humbled. And the Lord said to Adam: 'Behold, you have enjoyed the thing about which I warned you to beware'; that is: having rejected heaven, you chose the earth, namely, you left the good tree, in which you knew no evil, and descended to that through which you knew good and evil. This is, you fell from heaven to earth. Why did Adam say: 'Eve gave me counsel'? Eve said: 'The serpent gave me counsel'? The serpent said: 'The rebel deceived and sent me'? This is, namely, because God commanded Adam not to obey, neither he nor Eve, the one who rebelled against the word of his Lord, as we showed above how he rebelled: hence he sent the serpent, for he deceived him and he submitted himself to him.


[p. 626] {#po.0.p626}
ܒ݁ܶܗ ܒܚܺܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܛܳܒܬܳܐ. ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕܶܝܢ: ܢܦܰܠܬ ܡܶܢ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܠܰܐܪܥܳܐ. ܥܰܠ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܐܳܕܳܡ܆ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܕܚܰܝܘܳܐ ܡܠܰܟܬܰܢܝ ܥܰܠ ܚܰܝܘܳܐ ܐܶܡܪܳܐ ܕܚܶܘܝܳܐ ܡܰܡܠܟܰܢܝ܆ ܚܶܘܝܳܐ ܐܶܡܪ ܡܳܪܘܽܕܳܐ ܢܰܕ݂ܠܰܢܝ ܘܟܰܕܪܳܢܫ ܢܶܦܰܠ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܦܰܩܕ݁ܶܗ ܐܰܠܳܗܶܐ ܕܠܶܐ ܢܶܫܬܡܰܥ ܠܶܗ: ܠܳܐ ܗܘ ܘܠܳܐ ܚܰܝܘܳܐ: ܠܗܰܘ ܕܰܡܚܪܰܕ݂ ܥܰܠ ܡܶܠܰܬ݁ ܡܳܪܶܗ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܡܶܢ ܠܥܶܠ ܐܰܦܝܺܣܢܳܐ ܐܰܝܰܢ ܡܪܰܕ݂: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܫܰܕ݂ܰܕ݂ ܚܶܘܝܳܐ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܰܕ݂ܠܶܗ ܘܐܶܫܬܰܥܒ݁ܰܕ݂ ܠܶܗ܀ ܒܗܳܝ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܰܥܪܰܕ݂ ܘܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܣܰܝܦܶܗ: ܗܘܳܐ ܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ ܒܰܪ ܚܶܫܘܽܟ݁ܳܐ ܒܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ. ܘܐّܘܡܝܿ ܠܶܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܩܰܛܠܶܗ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܢܰܓ݁ܝܰܪܘܽܬ݂ ܪܘܽܚܶܗ: ܘܠܳܐ ܬܳܐܳܒ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܩܰܫܝܘܽܬܶܗ ܘܡܳܪܘܽܕܘܽܬܶܗ. ܘܰܚܠܳܦ݂ ܕܠܶܐ ܦܠܰܚ ܠܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܡܰܝܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕܰܟܬܝܺܒ ܗ̱ܘܵ ܕ݁ܰܠܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܟ݂ ܬܶܣܓܘܰܕ݂ ܘܠܶܗ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݁ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܬܶܦܠܘܺܚ ܘܐܶܬܟܰܫܰܦ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܕܰܠܩܘܽܒ݁ܠܳܗ ܕܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܒܶܪ̈ܝܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܢܝܳܬܳܐ ܫܰܕ݁ܰܠ ܘܰܡܪ̈ܰܕ݂ܝ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܠܚܺܝܘܝܳܐ ܘܠܳܐܕ݂ܳܡ ܘܰܠܚܰܝܘܳܐ ܐܰܠܶܦ݂ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܕܢܶܡܪܕܘܽܢ. ܘܰܢܦ݁ܰܠ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܡܶܢ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ: ܒܗܳܝ ܦܘܽܪܰܥܬܳܐ ܕܰܪܰܥ ܘܰܢܦܰܠ ܡܳܪܘܽܕܳܐ. ܡܳܪܘܽܕܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܥܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܣܶܠܩܰܬ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܡܰܡܚܫܰܒܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ. ܘܟܰܕ ܐܰܬܦܰܓܰܡ܂ ܠܶܗ: ܐܶܬ݂ܳܐ ܫܰܕ݂ܠܶܗ ܠܳܐܕ݂ܳܡ ܕܢܶܫܪܰܥ ܢܶܦܶܠ ܠܶܗ ܕ݁ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܒܪܳܐ ܘܬܰܠܡܝܺܕ݂ܳܐ. ܘܠܳܐ ܐܰܢܫܺܝܺܝܗ ܐܰܠܳܗܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܐܶܬ݁ܪܰܥܝ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܚܰܢܶܗ ܠܳܐܕ݂ܳܡ ܘܰܠܚܰܝܘܳܐ ܒܰܬܝܳܒܽܘܬܗܽܘܢ: ܘܣܺܝܡ ܠܗܘܢ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܕܐܶܢ ܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܠܶܗ
18. For this reason, because he rebelled and the Lord destroyed him, Satan became by his own will a son of darkness. And He neglected him and did not kill him because of His long-suffering; nor did he do penance because of his hardness and rebellious nature. And instead of serving the Lord (as God said: 'It is written: you shall worship the Lord your God and Him only shall you serve and supplicate'), he, on the contrary, also deceived other creatures and incited them to rebellion, just as he taught the serpent and Adam and Eve to rebel. And Adam fell by the same fall from heaven by which the rebel fell. For the thought occurred to the rebel to become God. And having been subverted, he seduced Adam, so that he might fall and become his son and disciple. But God did not allow him [to complete] what he had plotted, but had mercy on Adam and Eve because of their repentance and proposed a law to them on


[p. 627] {#po.0.p627}


[p. 628] {#po.0.p628}


[p. 629] {#po.0.p629}
ܒܰܪܢܳܫܳܝܐ ܚܳܫܶܐ ܒܶܗ. ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܕܐܶܬܚܰܒܰܠ ܗܘܽ ܘܚܰܒܶܠ ܠܰܐ݇ܚܪ̈ܳܢܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܚܳܣܳܝܐ ܚܰܡܬܺܝܢܶܗ ܕܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܥܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܘܒܰܝܰܠ ܚܘܰܒܶܠܶܗ ܘܥܰܠ ܬ݁ܰܫܢܝܩܶܝܗ: ܕܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕ݂ܚܰܒ݁ܶܠ ܡܶܬܚܰܒܰܠ: ܘܟܽܠ ܢܰܦܫܳܐ ܕܡܰܪܶܕ݂ ܘܐܰܘܒܶܕ݂: ܢܰܦܫܳܐ ܚܠܺܝܦ ܢܰܦ݂ܫܳܐ ܐܳܒܰܥ ܠܶܗ: ܘܟܽܠ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܚܺܛܺܦ ܡܶܢ ܒܰܪ̈ܝܳܬ݂ܳܗ ܬܳܒܰܥ ܠܶܗ: ܕܥܰܕ݂ܡܳܐ ܬܰܫܢܝܩܶܐ
earth, which if anyone did, he would be saved through it. And therefore, because he who is corrupt corrupted others, the right hand of Jesus will not spare him, nor his perdition and torments: but just as he destroyed, he will be cast down, and for every soul that he caused to rebel and destroyed, He will require 'soul for soul' from him, and whatever he snatched from His creatures, He will require from him, so that when the torments of all the impious are finished, his torments may remain for age upon age and be more cruel than all torments and lower than all.
ܕܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܪܰܫܝܺܥܳܝܐ ܘܐܰܫܢܚܺܝܩܶܗ ܕ݁ܝܽܠܶܗ ܢܶܝܗܘܶܐ ܩܰܝܺܡ ܠܥܳܠܰܡ ܥܳܠܡܺܝܢ: ܘܗܳܘܶܐ ܚܰܝܪܳܝܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܟܠ ܬ݁ܰܢ̈ܝܳܢ ܘܰܡܬܰܚܬܰܝ ܡܶܢ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ܀ ܚܳܣ ܠܶܗ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܢܶܫܓܘܽܪ ܓܺܗܰܢܳܐ ܕܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܐܝܟ ܕܝܽܠܶܗ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܚܰܒܶܝܠ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܶܗ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܪ̈ܘܚܶܐ ܛܰܢ̈ܦܳܬܳܐ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܰܗܘܰܝ ܠܶܗ ܒܰܢܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܡܫܰܥܒ݁̈ܕ݂ܳܢ ܠܶܗ: ܕܐܳܦ ܗܶܢܶܝܢ ܒܰܪ̈ܝܳܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܝ̈ ܠܬܶܫܡܶܫܬܳܐ: ܐܰܝܕ݂ܳܐ ܕܰܨܒܿܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕ݁ܢܶܒܪܶܐ ܐܶܢܶܝܢ. ܘܐܶܫܬ݁ܡܰܥܝ ܠܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܚܘܝܳܐ: ܘܐܶܬ݁ܛܰܢܰܦ݁ܺܝ ܘܰܗܘܰܝ̈ ܣܳܛܳܢܶܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܬܘܺܒ ܐܶܬܩܰܕ݁ܰܫܝ. ܟ݁ܽܠܢܳܫ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܐܰܪܫܰܥ ܒܕ݂ܳܪܕܳܪ ܡܰܡܪܡܰܪ. ܗܳܢܳܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܒܟܽܠ ܕܿܪ̈ܝܺܢ ܡܰܡܪܡܰܪ: ܟܡܳܐ ܕܗܳܘܶܐ ܗܳܢ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܡܰܡܪܡܰܪ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕ݁ܰܫܦ݁ܰܪ ܠܳܐܕ݂ܳܡ ܘܠܰܒܢܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܕܰܢܡܰܪܡܪܘܽܢ ܪܘܽܚܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܒܝܘܽܠܦܿܳܢܶܗ ܕܝܽܠܶܗ ܕܒܺܝܫܳܐ. ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܟܡܐ ܕܐܚܺܝܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܗܰܘ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܕܰܥܬܝܺܕ݂ ܡܶܬܡܰܪܡܰܪ ܘܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܢܰܩ ܒܛܰܘܦܳܢܳܐ ܕܢܘܽܪܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܬܳܐ ܛܘܽܦܳܢܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ ܕܡܶܠܬܳܐ
19. Far be it that God should kindle the Gehenna of men as much as that of him, because no one destroyed as much as he, except those unclean spirits who became his sons and submitted themselves to him; for these too were created for the ministry for which God willed to create them; and being obedient to Satan, like the serpent, they were polluted and became devils and were no longer sanctified. For whoever acts impiously exacerbates through individual generations; this one, however, exacerbates through all generations: as long as the world shall stand, he exacerbates, because it pleased Adam and his sons to exacerbate the Spirit of God with the doctrine of the Evil One. For which reason, as long as the age to come shall stand, he will be exacerbated and tormented by a deluge of fire, just as the deluge of waters came upon the sons of Adam because of his speech and seduction.

[p. 631] {#po.0.p631}
ܡܶܟܝܺܠ ܫܰܪܝܺ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܡܶܬܪܰܚܰܡܘܽ ܥܰܠ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܘܚܰܘܳܐ. ܘܰܥܒܰܕ݂ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܟܘܽܬܺܝܢܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܕ݁ܡܶܫܟ݁ܳܐ ܘܐܰܠܒܶܫ ܐܲܢܘܽܢ ܒܪ̈ܰܚܡܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܘܠܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܣܰܟܠܘܽܬܶܗ ܘܐܰܝܟ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ܂ ܕܐܶܬܪܰܥܝܺ ܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ ܥܒܰܕ݂ ܠܳܗ ܓܰܒܘܽܠܶܗ. ܐܶܠܘܽ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܐܰܝܟ ܣܰܟܠܘܽܬܶܗ ܡܣܳܦܝܳܐ ܡܝܬܰܪ ܗ݈ܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ: ܘܐܰܝܟ ܕܠܳܐ ܐܝܺܬ݂ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ ܒܚܺܐܪܘܽܬܶܗ ܓܒܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܥܰܡܠܳܐ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܐܝܺܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܣܰܩܘܽܒ݁ܠܳܐ ܕܰܓܡܝܳܪܘܳܬܳܐ: ܘܰܒܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ ܛܥܶܢ ܨܶܦ݂ܬܳܐ: ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܚܳܢܶܩ ܠܰܐܝܠܺܝܢ ܕܒܳܥܶܝܢ ܕܢܶܬܥܰܠܘܽܢ ܠܪܰܘܡܳܐ ܥܶܠܳܝܳܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܰܢܡܰܥ ܡܶܠܟܳܐ ܕܡܰܢ ܕܰܗܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܐܰܝܟ ܥܳܕܽܘܪܳܐ ܕܫܰܦܝܳܪܬ݁ܳܐ: ܘܓ݂ܰܠܙܶܗ ܡܶܢ ܦܘܽܪ̈ܫܶܐ ܦܰܫܺܝ̈ܛܶܐ ܘܐܰܣܪ݂ܶܗ ܒܫܘܽܦܪܳܗ ܕܐܰܪܥܶܐ. ܘܐܶܬܪܰܓܪܰܓ ܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ ܠܟܘܽܦܪܳܐ ܬܰܚܬܳܝܳܐ: ܘܐܶܬܓܠܶܙ ܡܶܢ ܫܘܽܦܪܳܐ. ܘܰܒܥܶܠܰܬ ܕܡܶܬܚܙܶܐ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܥܳܒܘܽܪܳܐ ܠܥܰܝܺܢܶܐ ܕܒܶܣܪܳܐ: ܣܰܓܺܝ ܚܰܒܺܝܒ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܠܝܬ ܠܶܗ ܥܰܝ̈ܢܶܐ ܕܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܕܰܢܚܘܽܪ ܒܫܘܽܦܪܳܐ
20. From then on, God began to have mercy on Adam and Eve and made them tunics of skin and, out of His mercy, clothed them; nor did his Fashioner act toward Adam according to his transgression and according to what he thought; for if He [had acted] toward him according to his transgression, He would have consumed him and rendered him as if he had not been. Nevertheless, Adam himself of his own accord chose for himself labor, contrary to perfection, and of his own accord took up care, which suffocates those who wish to be exalted to the highest height, having heard the counsel of him who showed himself to him as a helper for honest things and stripped him of heavenly beauty and bound him to the beauty of the earth. And Adam, having desired the lower beauty, was deprived of heavenly beauty; and since that perishable beauty is visible to the carnal eye, it is very dear to him who lacks the spiritual eye, with which he might behold heavenly beauty. And Adam, who had eyes, saw it: the Evil One blinded them, saying to him: 'You will grow even more and will be with your Creator.'


[p. 632] {#po.0.p632}
ܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܐ ܘܐܳܕܳܡ ܕܐܝܺܬ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܥܰܝ̈ܢܶܐ ܚܳܙܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ: ܥܰܘܰܪ ܐܶܢܶܝܢ ܒܺܝܫܳܐ: ܒܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܕܐܳܡܰܪܠܶܗ ܕܬܘّܒ ܝܳܙܶܒ݂ ܐܰܢ݈ܬ ܘܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܥܰܡ ܒܳܪܘܽܝܳܟ܀ ܘܫܠܶܡ ܡܺܐܡܪܳܐ ܕܟܐ܀ ܀ܕܥܰܠ ܐܝܺܠܳܢܳܐ ܕܐܳܕܳܡ܀
Discourse XXI on the tree of Adam ends.


[p. 633] {#po.0.p633}
SERMO VIGESIMUS SECUNDUS ܡܳܐܡܪܳܐ ܕܥܣܪܿܝܢ ܘܬܪܶܝܢ ܕܥܰܠ ܕܝܳܢ̈ܶܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܚܳܐܶܝܢ ܒܗܘܽܢ ܕܥܰܠ ܕܝܿܢ̈ܶܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܚܳܐܶܝܢ ܒܗܘܽܢ ܠܳܒ̈ܘܿܕܼܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܕܥܰܠ ܕܝܿܢ̈ܶܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܚܳܐܶܝܢ ܒܗܘܽܢ ܠܳܒ̈ܘܿܕܼܰܝܗܘܽܢ
TWENTY-SECOND DISCOURSE ON THE JUDGMENTS BY WHICH THOSE WHO DO THEM ARE NOT SAVED
ܢܦܰܪܶܫ ܡܶܟ݂ܝܺܠ ܕ݁ܚܰܝ̈ܶܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܚܳܫܶܐ ܒܙܘܘܿܢ ܡܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܢܛܰܪ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ. ܥܰܝܢܳܐ ܚܠܳܦ ܥܰܝܢܳܐ
1. We shall therefore explain the judgments by which, if they are observed, no one is saved. Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, cheek for cheek, stigma for stigma, bruise for bruise, soul for soul; this
ܫܶܢܳܐ ܚܠܳܦ ܫܶܢܳܐ. ܟܘܳܝܳܐ ܚܠܳܦ ܟܘܳܝܳܐ. ܨܘܰܠܦܬܳܐ ܚܠܳܦ ܨܘܰܠܦܬܳܐ. ܢܰܦܫܳܐ ܚܠܳܦ ܢܰܦܫܳܐ. ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕܝܢ ܠܰܝܡ ܟܽܠܥܽܒܕ݁ܶܡ: ܒܚܳܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܚܠܳܦ ܒܚܺܫܬܳܐ. ܪܚܰܡ܂ ܠܡ ܠܡܺܝܢ ܪܺܚܶܡ ܠܝܟ ܘܰܣܢܳܐ ܠܰܒܥܶܠܕܒܳܒܳܟ. ܘܐܶܢ ܡܳܚܶܝܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܰܐܒ݂ܘܽܟ: ܩܰܕܶܡ ܩܘܽܪܒܳܢܳܐ ܒܗܰܝܟ݁ܠܳܐܿ ܘܡܢ ܕܨܳܒܶܐ ܠܰܡ ܕܢܰܫܒܘܽܩ ܐܰܢ݈ܬ݁ܬܶܗ: ܢܶܬܶܠ ܠܳܗ ܟܬܳܒܳܐ ܕܕܘܽܠܳܠܳܐ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܠܳܐ ܓܳܪܰܐ:ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܠܳܐ ܫܰܦܝܰܪ ܠܳܐ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܠܰܒܢܰܫ݁ ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ. ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܦܘܽܩܕܿܳܢܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܫܰܦܝܪܝܺܢ: ܘܕܝܳܢ̈ܶܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܺܐܚܘܽܢ ܒܗܘܽܢ. ܘܰܠܡܳܢܳܐ ܝܰܗ̱ܒ ܐܳܢܘܽܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ܆ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܗܶܢܘܽܢ ܨܒܰܘ. ܘܥܰܠ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܐܰܦ݁ܣ ܠܗܘܢ ܕܢܶܦܪܥܘܽܢ ܒܚܺܫܬܳܐ ܚܠܦ ܒܚܺܫܬ݁ܳܐ:ܐܳܦ ܗܶܢܘܽܢ ܚܰܕ ܠܚܰܕ܆ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕ݁ܺܐܝܬ ܕܐܝܬ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܐܳܦ ܝܰܘܡܳܢ: ܕܒܳܥܶܝܢ ܕܢܶܡܪܕܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܬܚܝܬ ܦܘܽܩܕܳܢܳܐ: ܘܰܡܗܰܠܟܺܝܢ
is entirely evil for evil. Love him who loves you and hate your enemy. And if you have struck your father, offer a sacrifice in the temple. And he who wishes to dismiss his wife, he says, let him give her a bill of divorce even if she has not been an adulteress, which displeases both God and men. These are the precepts which are not good, and the judgments by which no one lives. And why did God give them if not because they themselves wanted them? And why did they set over themselves the worst judges? And why did He permit them to render evil for evil to one another? For even today there are men who, by rebelling, wish to withdraw themselves from the commandments and, walking in their own will, say that it is not justice which does harm to no one, but that, they say, is justice which does good to the good and harm to the wicked, as God will do on the day of judgment and correction.


[p. 634] {#po.0.p634}


[p. 635] {#po.0.p635}
ܒܨܶܒܝܳܢܗܘܽܢ ܘܐܳܡܪܝܺܢ: ܕܠܰܘ ܗܝ݇ ܗ̱ܝ݇ ܟܰܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܕܠܳܐ ܡܰܒ݁ܶܐܫܿܳܐ ܠܐ̱ܢܳܫ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܗܳܕܶܐ ܗܝ ܠܺܝܬ ܟ݁ܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܕܰܠܛܰܒ݁ܶܐ ܡܰܛܶܐܒ݂ܳܐ ܘܰܠܒܺܝܫ̈ܶܐ ܡܰܒ݁ܶܐܫܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܳܦ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܒܚܰܘܡܳܐ ܕܕܝܺܢܳܐ ܘܰܚܰܘܡܳܐ ܕܡܰܡܟܣܳܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܗܳܟܰܢ ܥܳܒܶܕ݂܀ ܐܶܢ ܡܶܢ ܟܬܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܣܬܰܟܠܝܳܢܰܢ: ܡܰܢܶܗ ܕ݁ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܡܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܡܠܰܓ݂ܢܺܝܢ ܚܰܕ݂ ܥܠ ܚܰܕ: ܠܳܐ ܝܳܕ݂ܥܝܺܢܰܢ ܠܳܗ ܠܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ܆ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܩܳܥܶܝܢ ܘܐܳܡܪܝܺܢ: ܕܒܳܥܶܐ ܕܢܰܪܡܶܐ ܥܠܺܝ ܦܠܳܢ ܚܘܽܒ̈ܠܶܐ ܒܺܝܫ̈ܶܐ: ܒܩܶܢܝܳܢܝ ܘܰܒܝܰܕ̈ܝܳܬܰܝܝ: ܘܐܳܡܰܪ ܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܕܠܰܘ ܟܺܐܢܳܐܝܺܬ ܥܒܺܕ݂ ܦܠܳܢ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܥܰܘܳܠܳܐܝܺܬ. ܗܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܩܳܥܶܐ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ: ܕܠܳܐ ܡܰܒܺܐܫܳܐ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ. ܘܐܰܝܢܳܐ ܕܐܰܒܺܐܫ ܠܐ̱ܢܳܫ: ܐܰܘ ܐܰܣܟܶܠ ܒܶܗ: ܐܰܘ ܕܒܰܪ ܩܶܢܝܳܢܶܗ: ܡܦܝܣ ܠܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܘܐܳܡܰܪ: ܕܐܰܣܟ݁ܠܶܬ ܫܒܘܽܩ ܠܝ ܘܦܳܪܰܥ ܐ̱ܢܶܐ: ܘܐܶܬ݂ܪܰܚܰܡ ܥܠܝ ܘܐܶܠܳܐ
2. If we do not understand from the Scriptures, do we not recognize justice from the world itself, with men shouting against one another? When they cry out and say: 'So-and-so wants to inflict the worst damages upon me in my wealth and possession!' everyone says: 'So-and-so does not act justly, but iniquitously.' Behold how everyone proclaims that justice does not do harm! And if anyone has done harm to another or has transgressed against him or has taken away his substance, he tries to persuade everyone by saying: 'I have sinned! Forgive me and I will repay and have mercy on me!' And if he does not wish to comply with him, everyone among the listeners says: 'Woe! So-and-so did not do as is right before God; for God said: Forgive one another seventy times seven. And unless you forgive, neither will I forgive you.' He sinned against him and


[p. 636] {#po.0.p636}
ܡܶܬܬܦܝܺܣ ܠܳܗ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܟܿܠ ܕܫܳܡܰܥ: ܘܳܝ ܠܰܘ ܐܝܟ ܕܳܐܶܐ ܠܰܐܠܳܗܳܐ ܥܰܒ݁ܶܕ݂ ܦܠܰܢ: ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܕܰܫܒܘܽܩܘ ܚܰܕ݂ ܠܚܰܕ: ܫܰܒܥܝܺܢ ܥܰܠ ܫܒܰܥ. ܘܐܶܠܳܐ ܫܳܒܩܝܺܢ ܐܵܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܐܶܢܳܐ ܫܳܒܶܩ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܠܟܘܽܢ. ܐܰܣܟ݁ܶܠ ܠܶܗ ܘܰܦܢܳܐ: ܡܶܛܺܝܠ ܡܰܣܟ݁̈ܠܳܢܶܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܢܰܢ ܕܛܘܽܒܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܠܰܡܪ̈ܰܚܡܳܢܶܐ ܕ݁ܰܥܠܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܢܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܪ̈ܰܚܡܶܐ. ܐܶܢ ܥܰܠ ܡܰܢ ܕܐܰܣܟ݁ܶܠ ܠܳܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܥܳܒ݁ܶܕ݂ ܪ̈ܰܚܡܶܐ: ܡܰܢ ܡܶܬܪܰܚܰܡ ܥܰܠ ܡܰܢ ܕܛܳܒ ܡܶܢܶܗ ܐܰܘ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܶܗ܆ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܡܶܬܪܰܚܡܰܬ ܥܠܰܝ܆ ܠܳܐ ܛܳܒ ܐܶܢܳܐ ܡܶܢܳܟ܆ ܘܐܶܢ ܐܳܡܰܪ: ܕܥܰܠ ܟܰܦ݁ܺܢܶܐ ܘܥܰܪ̈ܛܶܠܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܟܬܝّܒ ܕܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܢܶܬܪܰܚܰܡ:
he is converted: concerning those who transgress, God said: 'Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy'; if no one shows mercy to the transgressor, who has mercy on him who is better than himself or equal to him? For he says to him: 'Why do you have mercy on me? Am I not better than you?' And if he says that it is written that we should have mercy on the hungry and the naked: that statement includes not only the hungry and the naked, but also him who transgresses for any reason: if he has mercy and forgives, he does alms even in this. If anyone, therefore,
ܡܣܰܝܟܳܐ ܡܶܠܬܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܳܦ ܥܰܠ ܡܰܢ ܕܡܰܣܟ݁ܶܠ ܒܟ݁ܽܠ ܨܒܽܘ: ܐܶܢ ܡܶܬܪܰܚܰܡ ܘܦܳܒܶܩ: ܙܶܕܩ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܐܳܦ ܒܗܳܕܶܐ. ܡܢ ܗܳܟܝܽܠ ܕܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܒܗܳܢܳܐ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܡܰܣܟ݁ܠܳܢܳܐ ܪ̈ܰܚܡܶܐ: ܥܳܒܕܝܺܢ ܥܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܒܗܰܘ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܪ̈ܰܚܡܶܐ: ܘܫܳܒܩܝܺܢ ܠܶܗ ܣܰܟܠܶܘܳܬܶܗ ܘܰܚܛܺܝܗܰܘܽܗ̱ܝ. ܐܶܢ ܗܳܟܝܺܠ ܡܰܣܟܶܠ ܒܶܗ ܒܚܺܫܳܐ ܒܐ̱ܢܳܫ: ܢܰܕ݂ܢܰܚ ܥܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܚܘܽܒܶܗ:
shows mercy to transgressors in this age, he will obtain mercy in that age and his transgressions and sins will be forgiven. If, therefore, any wicked man has offended another, let him make his charity rise upon him, just as the Father makes His sun rise upon the wicked.


[p. 637] {#po.0.p637}


[p. 638] {#po.0.p638}
ܚܳܙܶܐ ܐܰܢ݈ܬ ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢ ܩܳܥܶܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܘܰܒܢܰܚܢܳܫ̈ܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܦܳܪܥܳܐ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܚܘܽܒ̈ܠܶܐ ܒܚܳܫ̈ܶܐ. ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܡܶܬܛܰܠܡܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܦܳܪܥܳܐ ܒܝܺܫܬܳܐ ܚܠܳܦ ܒܝܺܫܬܳܐ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܪܫܳܬ ܡܳܪܫܳܐ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܚܰܕ݂ ܐܰܘ ܬ݁ܪ̈ܶܝܢ ܐܰܘ ܬܠܳܬܳܐ: ܐܰܘ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܥܺܕ݂ܬ݁ܳܐ ܟܽܠܳܗ. ܘܐܶܠܳܐ ܕܳܒܿܶܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܕܢܶܬ݁ܶܠ ܠܳܟ: ܐܰܘܒ݁ܶܕ݂ ܕܚܺܠܳܟ ܘܠܳܐ ܬܶܦ݂ܶܠ ܒܒܚܳܫܬܳܐ ܘܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܕܚܺܢܳܟ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܥܒܶܕ݂ ܕܝܳܢܳܐ ܠܢܰܦܫܳܟ. ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܡܰܣܟܢܰܬ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܝ ܨܒܽܘ ܕܡܰܡܘܒܕܰܬ. ܘܐܶܢ ܐܝܺܬ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܕܐܳܡܰܪ: ܠܳܐ ܐܳܙܶܠ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܢ ܕܐܳܬܶܐ ܥܠܰܝ ܩܳܐܶܡ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ ܠܩܘܽܒܠܶܗ ܘܡܰܒܐܶܫ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܠܶܗ: ܘܠܳܐ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܐ݁ܝܰܬ݁ܶܝܗܿ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܒܝܺܫܬܳܐ. ܟ݁ܽܠܶܗ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܩܪ̈ܳܒܿܶܐ ܘܚܰܪ̈ܒ̈ܶܐ: ܥܰܠ ܕܩܳܝܡܝܺܢ ܓܰܒ̈ܶܐ ܬܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܚܰܕ݂ ܠܘܽܩܒܰܠ ܚܰܕ݂ ܐܳܡܰܬܝ ܕܡܶܫܬ݁ܰܥܠܶܐ ܓ݁ܰܒܪܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܚܰܒܪܶܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܙܒܰܢ ܚܰܕ݂ ܡܶܢܗܘܽܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܚܰܒܪܶܗ. ܡܶܛܰܠܗܳܢܳܐ ܥܳܒܪܳܐ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܬܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܓܰܒ̈ܶܐ: ܘܡܰܡܠܟܳܐ ܒܝܺܫܬܳܐ. ܠܳܐ ܠܰܥܠܝܺܒ̈ܶܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܘܠܳܐ ܠܥܳܠܘܽܦ̈ܶܐ ܦܰܩܶܕ݂ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܢܶܚܛܘܽܢ ܚܰܕ݂ ܒܚܰܕ. ܠܰܥܠܝܺܒܳܐ ܕܶܝܢ ܗܳܟܰܢ ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܐܶܢ ܬܩܰܘܶܐ ܒܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܬܶܥܒ݁ܶܕ݂ ܕ݁ܝܳܢܳܐ ܠܢܰܦܫܳܟ ܐܶܢܳܐ ܐܶܥܒ݁ܶܕ݂ ܕܝܳܢܳܟ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ. ܚܳܙܶܝܬ ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢ ܡܦܰܩܶܕ݂: ܕܐܳܦܝܠܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܝܕ݂ ܥܠܝܺܒܰܬ ܬܰܒܺܐܫ ܠܐ̱ܢܳܫ: ܕܠܳܐ ܬܶܦ݂ܽܠ ܠܝܺܟ
3. You see how God and men cry out that justice does not exact punishments for evil harms. For justice sustains injury, and does not render evil for evil, but if it reproves by vituperation, it does so only before one or two or three or before the whole church; and if anyone does not wish to repay you, lose your own; do not fall into evil and God will do your judgment, if you have not done judgment for yourself, nor will you be poorer for the lost thing. And if anyone says: 'I attack no one; but if anyone has attacked me, I will resist him and inflict evil,' not even this is justice, but wickedness. For the whole reason why wars and slaughters happen is that both parties rise up against one another, one against the other, when one is exalted against another and one does not bow before another. Therefore, justice departs from both sides and wickedness takes possession of things; for God commands neither the oppressed nor the oppressors to commit sin against one another. But to the oppressed He says thus: 'If you persevere in justice, and have not done judgment for yourself, I will do the judgment,' says God. You see how He commands that not even the oppressed should inflict evil on anyone, lest you fall from justice. But if there is someone who says: 'I imitate God, who exacts punishments from the iniquitous,' it is very wicked for you to imitate God and to equate yourself with God, who is without law, whom, even if He has sinned, no one corrects, since it is far from Him to commit iniquity. Do you therefore wish to be the judge of God? Therefore, be a creator, as He Himself is, and make for yourself a heaven and an earth, where He is not Lord, and create for yourself men, over whom the omnipotent Lord has no power, and do good to the good and evil to the wicked


[p. 639] {#po.0.p639}


[p. 640] {#po.0.p640}
ܡܶܢ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ. ܐܶܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܐܳܬܶܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܕܐܳܡܰܪ: ܕܒܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܡܶܬ݁ܕܰܡܶܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܕܬܳܒ݁ܰܥ ܠܥܰܘܳܠܶܐ: ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܛܳܒ ܒܺܝܫܳܐ ܕܒܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܡܶܬܕܰܡܶܐ ܐܢܬ ܘܰܡܦ݁ܰܝܶܡ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܢܰܦܫܳܟ ܠܰܐܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܐܝܺܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܳܡܘܽܣ: ܕܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܚܳܛܶܐ ܐܝܺܬ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܕ݂ܪܳܐܶܐ ܠܶܝܗ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܚܳܣ ܠܶܝܗ ܕܢܶܥܒܶܕ݂ ܥܰܘܠܳܐ. ܕܰܐܢܳܐ ܗܳܟ݂ܺܝܠ ܒܳܥܶܝܬ ܕ݁ܬ݂ܶܗܘܶܐ ܠܰܐܠܳܗܳܐ܆ ܡܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܘܰܗܘܺܝ ܒܳܝܪܘܳܝܳܐ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܶܗ: ܘܰܥܒܶܕ݂ ܠܳܡ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܘܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܐܰܝܟܳܐ ܕܠܰܝܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ: ܘܰܒܚܺܝܪ ܠܳܟ ܒܢܰܚܺܝܫܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ݁ܳܝܐ ܕܠܰܝܬ ܦܘܽܪܩܳܢ ܠܛܰܢܶܗ ܕܡܺܝܪܚܳܐ ܐܰܚܝܳܢ ܟ݁ܽܠ: ܘܐܰܛܶܐܒ ܠܛܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܘܐܰܒܺܐܫ ܠܒܺܝܫ̈ܶܐ ܡܳܐ ܕܰܗܘܰܝܬ ܐܝܺܬܝܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܥܒܺܝܕ݂ܳܐ: ܘܰܗܘܺܝܬ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܳܡܘܽܣ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܶܗ܀
after you have become an Aeon, not a created being, made without law like Him.


[p. 641] {#po.0.p641}
ܐܰܘ ܚܰܝܠܳܫܳܝܐ: ܐܶܬܕܰܟܪ ܠܳܐܕܳܡ ܐܰܒ݂ܘܽܟ݂ ܘܰܠܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ: ܕܥܰܠ ܕ݁ܐܶܬ݂ܪܰܥܝܽܘ ܕܢܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܐܰܠܳܗ̈ܶܐ: ܠܰܐܝܢܳܐ ܫܶܦܠܳܐ ܡܰܛܝܽܘ. ܘܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܠܳܐ ܛܥܰܝܬ ܓܰܠܝܳܐܝܺܬ: ܗܳܐ ܡܰܡܛܥܶܐ ܠܳܟ ܡܶܢ ܒܺܝܫܳܐ ܟܰܣܝܳܐܝܺܬ: ܕܬܺܐܡܰܪ: ܕܐܰܝܟ ܕܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ: ܕܬܺܐܬ݂ܶܐ ܠܰܡܚܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܰܐܣܝܳܐ. ܐܳܕܳܡ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܐܶܬܰܐܣܝܰܬ ܡܚܘܽܬܶܗ: ܚܙܝ ܕ݁ܰܠܡܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܰܐܣܝܳܐ ܡܚܘܽܬܳܟ ܕܝܳܠܳܟ. ܘܐܶܢ ܐܳܡܪܰܬ ܕ݁ܰܠܙܰܕ݂ܝܺܩܶܐ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܦܰܩܶܕ݂ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܕܢܶܬܢܰܩܡܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܥܰܘܳܠܶܐ: ܘܐܶܢܳܐ ܒܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܬ݁ܕ݁ܰܡܶܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܫܰܠܺܝܛ ܠܳܡ ܕܬ݂ܶܕ݂ܡܶܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ: ܘܠܳܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܳܟ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܠܗܘܽܢ. ܘܠܰܘ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕ݁ܚܳܛܶܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܚܰܕ݂ ܒܚܰܕ݂ ܚܪܰܒ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܒܰܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܳܡܪܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܡܳܐ ܛܳܒܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܝܳܐ. ܘܰܒܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܪܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ: ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܐܰܘܕܝܽܘ ܕܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܐܰܚܝܰܕ݂ ܟܽܠ. ܘܰܕܬ݁ܶܕ݁ܰܥ ܠܳܡ ܕܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ: ܚܙܝ ܕܡܶܢ ܝܰܘܡܳܐ ܕܐܰܘܕ݂ܝܽܘ ܠܳܐ ܡܫܰܕ݂ܰܪ ܥܠܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܠܰܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܠܳܐ ܨܳܒ݂ܶܝܢ ܬܳܝܒܝܺܢ: ܢܳܛܰܪ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܠܚܰܘܡܳܐ ܕܕܝܺܢܳܐ. ܝܰܘܡܳܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܡܥܰܕ݁ܰܪ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܠܰܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ. ܐܶܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܨܒܶܝܬ ܡܶܢ ܨܒܘܳܬ ܢܰܦܫܳܟ݂ ܕܬܶܗܘܶܐ ܩܳܛܽܘܠܳܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ݁. ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܣܢܝܳܬܳܐ ܬܶܦܘܽܩ ܡܶܢ ܦܘܽܡܳܟ. ܘܐܶܢ ܬܐܡܰܪ: ܕܰܒ݂ܕܰܝܳܢ̈ܶܐ ܡܶܬ݁ܕܰܡܶܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܕܠܰܝܬ ܫܘܽܠܛܳܢܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܗܘܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܗܽܘ: ܚܙܝ ܕܥܰܠ ܒܺܝܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܒܰܠܚܽܘܕ݂ܰܝܗܽܘܢ ܕܰܝܳܢ̈ܶܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܚܳܫܶܐ ܒܝܗܘܽܢ ܕܳܝܶܢܺܝܢ. ܘܰܚܙܝ ܕܕ݂ܰܝܳܢ̈ܶܐ ܒܺܝܫ̈ܶܐ ܕܳܝܶܢܺܝܢ ܠܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܒܺܝܫܳܝܐ. ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ
4. O miserable one! Remember your father Adam and Satan, who, because they wanted to become gods, to what humiliation they came! And you, who have not yet openly erred, Satan now seduces you in secret, so that you may say: 'As God does, I will do,' so that you may contract an incurable wound. The wound of Adam was indeed healed: you take care, lest perhaps your wound become incurable! And if you say: 'God commanded the just ancients to exact punishments from the iniquitous and I will imitate them': it is not permitted for you to imitate them, nor did God say that to you, as He did to them, nor would God have depopulated them through the prophets, because they sinned against one another, if they had not said: 'What is the fame of God?' Therefore He chastised them, until they confessed: 'The Lord is the omnipotent God.' And that you may know these things to be so, observe Him from the day they confessed, not having sent prophets against them, but if they do not wish to do penance, He reserves them for the day of judgment. Today, however, God sends no one as prophets. If, however, you wish to become a murderer of your own accord, you will have found out. For the Lord said: 'Let not even a shameful word come out of your mouth.' And if you say: 'I imitate the judges, since there is no power that is not from God, see them rule for evil and judge judgments by which no one lives.' And observe the bad judges judging the bad age. But that God established bad judges and gave bad judgments: so that the judges might not be justified, nor the judged enjoy peace; but that men also rebelled against justice, which are the precepts subsequent to our first rebellion of Adam our father: just as our father rebelled against the goodness of the heart and the simplicity of the mind and acquired a heart that knows evil by its own will: so we have rebelled against the justice which our Creator commanded us, which, although it knows evil by knowing, does not do it of its own accord.


[p. 642] {#po.0.p642}


[p. 643] {#po.0.p643}
ܕܝܢ ܕܐܰܩܺܝܡ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܰܝܳܢ̈ܶܐ ܒܝܺܫ̈ܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܚܳܝܣܺܝܢ ܕܗܶܢܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝܢܳܫ̈ܳܐ ܢܶܩܥܘܽܢ ܘܢܶܐܡܪܘܽܢ: ܘܠܳܐ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܡܶܬܕܝܺܢܺܝܢ ܢܶܬܬܢܝܳܚܘܽܢ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܶܝܢ ܕܰܡܪܰܕܘ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝܢܳܫ̈ܳܐ ܐܳܦ ܡܶܢ ܟܰܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܐܝܺܬܶܝܗ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܶܐ ܕܒܳܬܰܪ ܡܰܪܕܘܽܬܳܐ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܬܳܐ ܕܐܵܒܘܽܢ ܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ: ܕܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܡܪܰܕ ܐܰܒܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܛܰܝܒܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܠܶܒܳܐ ܘܡܶܢ ܫܰܦܝܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܪܶܥܝܳܢܳܐ: ܘܰܩܢܳܐ ܠܶܒܳܐ ܕܝܺܝܕ݂ܰܥ ܒܚܺܫܬܳܐ ܒܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ: ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢ ܡܳܪܕܺܝܢ ܐܳܦ ܚܢܰܢ ܡܶܢ ܟܰܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܦܰܩܕ݂ܰܢ ܒܳܪܘܳܝܢ: ܕܐܳܦܶܢ ܡܶܕ݁ܰܥ ܝܳܕ݂ܥܳܐ ܠܳܗ ܠܒܚܺܫܬܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܨܳܒܝܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܥܳܒܕ݂ܳܐ ܠܳܗ܀ ܡܶܢ ܕܰܚܙܳܐ ܗܳܟܝܶܠ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܰܡܪܰܕܢ ܠܰܢ ܐܳܦ݂ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܒܝܺܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܚܠܳܦ ܒܚܺܫܬܳܐ ܦܳܪܥܝܢܰܢ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܒܚ̈ܫ̈ܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܣܰܓ̈ܺܝܐܳܬܳܐ ܚܠܳܦ ܚܕ݂ܳܐ ܒܚܺܫܬܳܐ: ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܠܳܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܢܳܚ ܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܒܒܝܫܬܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܚܠܳܦ݂ ܒܝܺܫܬܳܐ: ܦܘܽܚܕ݂ܳܐ ܫܳܩܠܺܝܢ ܘܰܒܰܦ݁ܪܰܨܘܽܦܶܐ ܢܳܣܒܺܝܢ: ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܠܳܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ. ܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܒ݁ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܝܺܢ̈ܶܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܚܳܐܶܐ ܒܗܘܽܢ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܰܒܪܘܰܓ݁ܙܳܐ ܐܶܬܝܰܗܒܰܝ. ܐܶܡܰܪ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ: ܕܐܰܩܺܝܡ ܕܰܝܳܢ̈ܶܐ ܒܝܺܫ̈ܶܐ
5. After, therefore, God saw that we had rebelled even against this and not only rendered evil for evil, but many evils for a single evil (which the Lord did not say, nor is He pleased with evil rendered for evil)... they take a small gift and are respecters of persons (which the Lord did not say, for not even by these judgments is a man saved, because they were given with anger): for the Lord said: 'I will appoint the worst judges, who will not


[p. 644] {#po.0.p644}


[p. 645] {#po.0.p645}
ܠܳܐ ܚܳܝܣܺܝܢ: ܕܗܶܢܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝܢܳܫ̈ܳܐ ܩܳܥܶܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܘܐܳܡܪܝܺܢ: ܗܰܒ ܠܰܢ ܡܰܠܟܳܐ ܘܕ݂ܰܝܳܢ̈ܶܐ
spare, so that men themselves will be crying out and saying: Give us a king and judges, who will subdue us harshly.'
ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܰܡܫܰܥܒܕܝܺܢ ܠܰܢ ܩܰܫܝܳܐܝܺܬܳܐ܀ ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܠܰܫܡܘܺܐܶܝܠ: ܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܡܫܰܥܒܶܕ݂ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܡܰܠܟܳܐ: ܕܪܳܒܰܐ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ ܘܰܒܢ̈ܳܬܗܘܽܢ ܘܰܡܥܰܣܰܪ ܩܶܢܝܳܢܗܘܽܢ ܘܥܰܠܳܠܳܬܗܘܽܢ. ܘܰܩܥܰܘ ܕܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܪ̈ܰܝܳܢܶܐ ܐܳܙܠܺܝܢ ܠܰܢ ܕܩܳܛܠܺܝܢ ܒܣܰܝܦܳܐ ܠܟ݁ܽܠ ܕܡܰܥܣܟܶܠ: ܘܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܳܟܠܺܝܢ ܚ̱ܢܰܢ ܚܰܕ݂ ܠܚܰܕ. ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܰܣܠܺܝܘ ܦܘܽܩܕܳܢܝ: ܗܳܟ݂ܰܢܳܐ ܐܳܦ݂ ܠܝ ܐܰܣܠܺܝܘ. ܐܰܩܺܝܡ ܥܠܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܕܰܝܳܢ̈ܶܐ ܒܝܺܫ̈ܶܐ: ܕܥܰܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܥܰܘܳܠܶܐ ܢܶܬܢܰܩܰܡ: ܘܐܶܢܳܐ ܐܶܬܢܰܩܰܡ ܡܶܢ ܬܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ: ܕܠܳܐ ܕܰܝܳܢ̈ܶܐ ܡܶܫܟܚܺܝܢ ܚܳܐܶܝܢ ܒ݁ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܝܺܢ̈ܶܐ ܕܒܝܺܫܬܳܐ ܚܠܳܦ݂ ܒܝܺܫܬܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܥܳܒܺܕ݂ܰܝ ܒܝܺܫ̈ܳܬܳܐ: ܘܰܬܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܒܨܶܒܝܳܢܗܘܽܢ ܡܳܝܬܝܺܢ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܳܒ݂ܶܝܢ ܒܢܰܝܢ̈ ܐ݈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܕܰܝܳܢ̈ܶܐ ܘܥܳܒܺܕ݂ܰܝ ܒܝܺܫ̈ܳܬܳܐ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܪܳܚܡܝܺܢ ܟ݁ܶܣܦܳܐ ܘܐܝܺܩܳܪܳܐ ܘܫܘܰܒܚܳܐ ܥܳܒܘܽܪܳܐ: ܡܶܫܚܰܕ݂ ܫܳܚܕܝܺܢ ܘܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܗܶܓ݂ܡܳܘܢܶܐ ܘܟܳܢܫܺܝܢ ܥܘܽܠܛܳܢܳܐ ܕܣܰܝܦܳܐ: ܕ݁ܰܠܡܰܢ ܕܨܳܒ݂ܶܝܢ ܢܶܩܛܠܘܽܢ. ܘܰܒܫܘܽܚܕ݂ܳܐ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܣܦܘܽܩܠܰܛܪ̈ܶܐ ܕܢܶܗܘܘܽܢ
6. And the Lord said to Samuel: 'Tell them how the king will subdue them: for he will take their sons and daughters and will tithe their wealth and their produce.'
