ܕܥܳܬܝܕ݂: ܠܰܝܬ ܠܶܗ ܕܶܒ݂ܚܬ݁ܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܝܬܳܐ ܕܬܶܬ݂ܩܰܪܰܒ ܚܠܳܦ ܚܛܳܝܳܗܰܘܗ̱ܝ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܥܬܝܺܕ݂ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܚܣܳܡܳܐ ܕܢܘܽܪܳܐ ܕܐܳܟܠܳܐ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܗܘܰܘ ܣܰܩܘܽܒܠܳܐ ܠܢܰܦܫܗܘܽܢ ܘܠܵܐ ܬܳܒܘ. ܘܝܳܕ݂ܥܝܺܢܰܢ ܕܠܰܘ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܡܢ ܕܥܶܡܕ݂ ܡܶܢ ܟ݁ܰܕܘܽ ܩܰܒܶܠ ܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܰܫܪܳܪܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܚܰܕ݂ ܡܶܢ ܣܰܓ̈ܺܝܶܐܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܰܡܩܰܒܠܝܺܢ ܝܺܕܰܥܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܰܫܪܳܪܳܐ. ܠܰܘ ܗܳܟܝܶܠ ܕܠܰܝܬ ܠܗܘܿܢ ܬܝܳܒܘܽܬܳܐ ܐܰܡܰܪ ܫܠܝܺܚܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܕܶܒ݂ܚܬ݁ܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܝܬܳܐ ܠܰܝܬ ܠܗܘܿܢ. ܐܰܟ ܕܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܢܺܐܡܰܪ: ܕܠܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܺܢܳܐ ܐܝܺܬ ܠܒܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܕ݁ܰܚܛܰܘ ܠܶܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܬ݁ܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܝܬܳܐ: ܠܒܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܫܪܳܪܳܐ ܕܝܳܕܥܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܠܶܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܩܰܘܝܽܘ ܒܶܗ: ܘܠܰܝܬ ܠܗܘܿܢ ܕܘܰܟ݁ܬܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܐܰܬܪܳܐ ܕܢܝܽܙܳܚ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܕܢܐܙܠ̱ܘܽܢ ܢܕܰܒ݂ܚܘܽܢ ܠܶܗ ܕܶܒܚܬܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܝܬܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܬܳܒܘ ܠܘܳܬ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܗܰܝܡܰܢܘ ܒܶܗ ܒܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܬܳܐ ܘܕܰܒ݁ܰܚܘ ܠܶܗ ܗܝܺ ܗܳܝ ܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܬܳܐ ܘܐܰܘܕ݂ܝܳܬܳܐ ܕܡܰܕ݂ܒ݁ܚܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܡܶܢ ܩܕ݂ܝܳܡ. ܠܰܘ ܕܠܳܐ ܚܳܐܶܝܢ ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܕܠܰܝܬ ܠܗܘܿܢ ܦܘܽܠܚܳܢܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܺܢܳܐ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܫܪܳܪܳܐ ܕܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܘ ܘܰܣܛܰܘ ܡܶܢܶܗ. ܘܐܶܠܳܐ ܗܳܦܟܝ݁ܢ ܘܡܕܰܒܚܝܺܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܡܕܰܒܚܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܕܬ݂ܶܐܟ݂ܘܽܠ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܕܰܗܘܰܘ ܠܳܗ ܣܰܝܩܝܘܽܒܬܳܐ ܠܢܰܦܫܗܘܽܢ: ܘܐܶܡܰܪܘ: ܕܡܶܟܝܠ ܠܡ ܚܰܛܺܝܢ ܠܰܢ: ܠܳܐ ܡܩܰܒܶܠ ܠܰܢ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ. ܚܕ݂ܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܘܡܳܐܐ ܫܰܘܝܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ. ܘܗܺܝ ܒܚܺܫܬܳܐ ܡܰܡܠܟܳܐ ܠܗܘܢ ܕܢܺܐܡܪܘܽܢ ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ: ܕܠܳܐ ܢܬܘܽܒܘܽܢ ܘܢܺܚܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܐܰܠܦܰܬ ܠܰܣܟܰܪܝܘܽܛܳܐ ܘܰܚܢܰܩ ܢܰܦܫܶܝܗ. ܐܶܠܘܽ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܬܳܒ ܣܟܰܪܝܘܽܛܳܐ: ܡܩܰܒܶܠ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܒܳܥܶܐ ܒܡܰܘܬܳܐ ܕܐ̱ܢܳܫ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܕܰܢܬܘܰܒ ܘܢܺܚܐ. ܘܐܝܺܬ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܕܐܳܡܪܝܺܢ: ܕܐܶܢ ܡܶܣܬ݁ܕ݁ܶܩ ܢܰܚܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܡܶܬܡܰܠܚܐ ܕܘܽܟܬܶܗ: ܝܺܕܝܺܥܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ. ܘܐܶܢ ܡܶܬܬ݁ܰܪܥܳܐ ܐܶܣܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܡܶܬܒܰܢܝܳܐ: ܕܘܽܟܬ݁ܳܗ ܗܳܘܝܳܐ ܝܺܕܝܺܥܳܐ. ܘܐܳܡܪܝܺܢ ܠܶܒܳܐ ܕܐܰܝܳܦ̈ܶܐ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܟܽܠܰܢ ܐܰܝܳܦ̈ܶܐ ܚܢܰܢ. ܘܰܠܟ݁ܽܠܰܢ ܚܛܳܗܶܐ ܐܝܺܬ. ܒܦܘܽܪܫܳܢܳܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܢܡܰܠܠ ܥܰܡ ܟܽܠܢܳܫ: ܐܰܝܢܳܐ ܕܩܳܐܶܡ ܢܶܕܗܰܪ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܦܶܠ: ܘܐܺܝܢܳܐ
repentance. And we know that not all, where they have been baptized, receive the knowledge of the truth, but individuals are among the many who receive the knowledge of the truth. Therefore the Apostle does not say that they do not have repentance, but he says that no other sacrifice is given to them; as if you were to say that there is no other God besides Him against whom they have sinned, nor any other knowledge besides that truth which they knew and in which they did not persevere, nor do they have a place or space alien to this God, so that going away they may sacrifice another sacrifice to Him, unless they are converted to that God in whom they once believed and to whom they offered that knowledge and confession which they previously sacrificed. He does not say that they are not saved, but that no other worship is given to them besides that truth which they had known and from which they had fallen; and unless they are converted and sacrifice, as they once sacrificed, that the fire will devour them, who have become adversaries to themselves, saying: "from now on, because we have sinned, God does not receive us. For one and a hundred is the same," which malice teaches them to say, so that they may not be converted and be saved, just as it taught Iscariot, who hanged himself. For if Iscariot had been converted, the Lord would have received him, because He does not wish the death of man, but that he should be converted and live. And there are men who say: if a garment is torn and the place is patched, it remains known; and, if a wall is pierced and the place is rebuilt, it will be known. And they break the heart of the penitents, although we are all penitents and we all have sins. But let us speak discreetly with all;


[p. 714] {#po.0.p714}


[p. 715] {#po.0.p715}


[p. 716] {#po.0.p716}


[p. 717] {#po.0.p717}
ܕ݁ܢܶܦܶܠ ܠܶܗ: ܢܚܰܘܶܐ ܠܗ ܬܝܳܒܘܽܬܳܐ
he who stands, let him take heed, lest he fall; and to him who has fallen, let us show repentance and let us raise him up. If, He says, You should observe sins, O Lord, who will be able to stand?
ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ: ܡܰܢܘܽ ܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܠܰܡܩܳܡ ܆& ܚܙܰܝܬ ܐܰܝܟ݂ܰܢ ܐܶܡܪܰܬ ܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܕܩܘܰܕܫܳܐ: ܕܐܶܢ
2. You see how the Holy Spirit said: if the Lord should observe ancient sins, men will not be able to stand
ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܠܰܡܩܳܡ ܩܕ݂ܳܡܰܘܗ̱ܝ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܚܳܛܝܢ: ܘܒܰܬܝܳܒܘܽܬܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܡܶܬܩܰܒܠܝܢ. ܡܰܢܘܽ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܙܟ݂ܳܗ ܠܰܚܛܺܝܬ݁ܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܟ݁ܰܪܣܳܐ ܕܐܶܡܶܗ܆ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܚܳܛܶܝܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܘܐܳܦܶܢ ܙܳܟܶܝܢ ܠܳܗ ܠܰܚܛܺܝܬܳܐ: ܐܰܝܠܺܝܢ ܕܐܰܡܝ݁ܢܝܢ ܡܰܩܪܒܝܢ ܥܰܡܳܗ ܟܽܠ ܝܘܽܡ ܟܰܫܝܺܪܳܐܝܺܬ ܘܰܙܪܝܺܙܳܐܝܺܬ. ܠܳܐ ܕ̈ܝܢ ܢܶܬܡܰܬ݁ܰܠ ܒ݁ܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܬܰܝܺܒܳܐ ܒܢܰܚܬܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܒܐܶܣܬ݁ܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܢܡܰܬܶܠ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܒܥܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܥܳܐܶܠ ܠܢܘܽܪܳܐ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܰܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܒܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܥܳܡܕ݂ܝܺܢ ܕܐܚܺܝܬܶܝܗ ܚܘܽܒܳܐ ܘܰܫܪܳܪܳܐ. ܐܶܢ ܗܳܟܝܶܠ ܡܶܨܛܠܺܝܢ ܘܚܳܛܺܝܢ ܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܕܰܥܡܰܕ݂ܘ: ܟ݁ܳܠܥܳܕ݂ܳܢ ܕܰܢܬܘܽܒܘܽܢ: ܟܰܕ݂ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܗܘܢ ܚܘܽܒܳܐ ܕܢܶܥܡܕܘܽܢ ܒܿܗ ܘܢܶܬܕܰܟܘܽܢ. ܘܐܰܝܟܰܢܳܝܐ ܕܡܳܐܢܶܐ ܕܕܰܗܒܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܕܣܺܐܡܳܐ: ܐܰܘ ܕܰܢܚܳܫܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܕܰܙܓܘܽܓܝܳܬܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܕܦܰܪܙܠܳܐ: ܐܶܡܰܬܝ ܕܡܶܬܬܰܒܪܝܺܢ ܘܡܰܥܠܶܠ ܠܗܘܢ ܐܘܽܡܳܢܳܐ ܥܳܒܘܽܪܳܐ ܠܢܘܽܪܳܐ ܥܳܒܘܽܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܡܚܰܕ݁ܶܬ ܠܗܘܢ ܘܚܳܬܶܡ ܨܘܽܪܬܳܬܗܘܽܢ: ܘܡܶܬܩܪܶܝܢ ܚܰܕ݁ܬܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܕܰܒܠܰܝܘ: ܚܰܕ݂ ܟܡܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܐܘܽܡܳܢܶܝܗ ܗ̱ܘ ܕܐܘܽܡܳܢܳܐ: ܕܰܢܚܰܕ݁ܶܬ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܒܢܘܽܪܳܐ ܕܚܘܽܒܳܐ ܗܝܺ: ܘܪܘܽܚܶܝܗ ܫܪܳܪܳܐ ܘܡܰܝ̈ܘܗ̱ܝ ܗܰܝܡܳܢܘܽܬܳܐ. ܐܶܢ ܐܶܢܨܶܝܢ ܥܳܡܕ݁ܝܺܢܰܢ ܡܰܥܡܘܽܕܝܳܬܳܐ: ܘܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܒܰܢ: ܠܕܝܳܢܳܐ ܙܗ̱ܘ ܘܰܠܚܰܝܳܒܘܽܬܳܐ ܥܳܡܕܝܺܢ ܚ̱ܢܰܢ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܘܳܠܶܐ ܕܢܶܥܡܰܕ݂ ܘܢܶܩܢܶܐ ܚܘܽܒܳܐ ܘܰܫܪܳܪܳܐ ܘܗܰܝܡܳܢܘܽܬܳܐ. ܐܶܢܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܐܶܫܬܪܰܥܢ ܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܕ݁ܰܥܡܰܕ݂ܢ ܘܐܳܦܶܢ ܬܳܒܺܝܢܰܢ: ܚܘܽܒܶܗ ܗ̱ܘ ܕܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܕܐ̱ܚܺܝܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܢܘܽܪܳܐ ܚܰܝܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܡܳܕܶܟܶܐ ܠܳܐܬ݁ܳܢ ܘܫܘܽܚܬܰܢ: ܘܰܡܚܰܕ݁ܶܬ ܘܝܳܠܶܕ݂ ܠܰܢ ܡܶܢܕܪܝܰܫ: ܘܛܰܒ݂ܰܥ ܠܰܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܡܶܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ܂ ܐܳܦ ܗܰܘ ܚܳܬܡܳܐ ܕܝܰܗ̱ܒܘ ܥܰܠ ܟܳܗ̈ܢܶܐ: ܥܰܒ݁ܰܪ ܕܡܰܦܩܳܢܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܡܶܫܬܟ݁ܰܚ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܡܶܬܕܒܰܪ. ܘܐܶܢ ܗܰܠܶܟ݂ ܠܶܗ ܒܰܚܝܳܛܽܘܬܳܐ ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܠܡܰܦܩܳܢܳܐ: ܐܳܦ݂ ܪܘܰܫܡܳܐ ܕܝܰܗ̱ܒܘ ܠܶܗ ܟܳܗ̈ܢܶܐ: ܡܰܥܕ݂ܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܡܳܪܳܐ ܠܳܢ̈ܳܐ ܡܶܢܶܗ ܘܦܳܐܶܫ ܥܰܪܛܶܠ. ܡܰܢ ܕܐܺܝܬ ܠܶܗ ܠܰܡ ܢܶܬܝܰܗܰܒ ܠܶܗ ܘܢܶܬܬܰܘܣܰܦ ܠܶܗ: ܘܡܰܢ ܕܠܰܝܬ ܠܶܗ ܠܰܡ ܠܦܳܕܶܐ ܕܙܰܕܺܝܩܽܘܬܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܗܽܘ ܚܳܬܡܳܐ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂. ܐܳܦ ܗܰܘ ܠܰܡ ܕܐܺܝܬ ܠܶܗ ܢܶܫܬܩܶܠ ܡܶܢܶܗ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܗܰܘ ܕܩܰܒ݁ܶܠ ܟܶܣܦܳܐ ܕܢܶܬܬܰܓ݁ܰܪ ܒܶܗ: ܘܐܶܙܰܠ ܕܳܪܶܗ ܘܣܳܡܶܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܐܰܘܣܶܦ ܥܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ. ܘܰܩܪܳܝܗ̱ܝ ܡܳܪܶܗ ܥܰܒܕ݂ܳܐ ܒܺܝܫܳܐ. ܕܟܰܕ݂ ܝܺܕ݂ܰܥ ܗ̱ܘܰܝܬ݀ ܠܺܝ ܕܬܳܒ݁ܰܥ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܒܐܝܕܰܝ̈ܟ: ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܳܐ ܐܰܠܰܝܬ ܠܳܟ: ܫܩܰܠܬ ܩܳܠܝ ܒܦܘܽܡܳܝܟ: ܘܰܢܕܰܝܬ
before Him. For all sin and are received through repentance. For who is there who has overcome sin from his mother's womb? Nevertheless, men sin and do repentance and then overcome sin: those who struggle with it daily, assiduously, strenuously, and bravely. But a penitent man is not to be compared with a garment or with a wall, but should be compared with some thing which is cast into the fire; because men are baptized in the Spirit, which is charity and truth. If, therefore, they slip and sin, after they have been baptized, as often as they have done repentance, charity will be given to them, by which they may be baptized and purified. And just as a vessel of gold or silver or bronze or glass or iron, if it is broken, the craftsman, casting it into the falling fire, renews it, and its form being remade it is called new, after it had been worn out by use: how much more will God, who is the craftsman of the craftsman, renew them with fire, which is charity, and with His Spirit, which is truth, and with His water, which is faith? If, however, we are baptized and these are lacking in us, we are baptized to judgment and condemnation. Nevertheless, it behooves us to be baptized and to acquire charity and truth and faith. If, however, after we have been baptized, we slip and do repentance, the charity of Jesus, which is living fire, wipes away our stain and leprosy and conceives and regenerates us and dips us as of old. But not even the seal, which the priests have conferred upon us, passes away until our death. On the day of death, however, as each one shall be found, he will be taken; and if until death he walked in sin, even the sign, which the priests conferred upon him, the Lord of the sheep deletes from him, and he remains naked. He who has, He says, it will be given to him and it will be added to him; and, he who does not have — namely, the works of justice, but the seal only — even that which he has, He says, will be taken away from him, like him who received money, with which he might trade, and going away he bound it and put it away and did not increase it. And the Lord called him an "evil servant," who knew that I would exact from you the precepts which I delivered to you; you received my covenant with your mouth and cast


[p. 718] {#po.0.p718}


[p. 719] {#po.0.p719}


[p. 720] {#po.0.p720}


[p. 721] {#po.0.p721}
ܢܳܡܘܽܣܝ ܠܒܶܣܬܪܳܟ: ܘܐܶܬܚܬܰܡܬ݀ ܠܺܝ ܒܫܶܡܝ: ܘܰܥܒܰܪܬ ܥܰܠ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܰܝ. ܘܰܒܥܺܝܬ ܡܶܢܳܟ ܐܶܢܳܐ ܘܰܫܠܺܝܚܰܝ ܟܽܠܝܽܘܡ: ܘܠܳܐ ܬܳܒܬ. ܚܠܳܝܦ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܰܝܬ ܒܳܥܶܝܢܰܢ ܡܶܢܟܘܽܢ ܐܶܬ݁ܪܰܥܰܘ ܠܰܐܠܳܗܳܐ. ܣܰܒܘ ܠܰܡ ܡܶܢܶܗ ܗܰܘ ܟܶܣܦܳܐ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܗܰܘ ܚܳܬܡܳܐ: ܘܗܰܒܘ ܠܗܰܘ ܕܢܳܛܰܪ ܡܶܠܰܝ̈: ܘܰܠܥܰܒܕ݂ܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܒܺܝܫܳܐ ܐܰܪܡܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܠܚܶܫܘܽܟܳܐ ܘܰܠܚܘܽܪܳܩ ܫܶܢ̈ܶܐ. ܚܙܰܝܬ ܕܩܳܐܶܡ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܚܳܬܡܳܐ ܕܡܰܥܡܘܽܕ݂ܝܺܬܳܐ ܐܳܦ݂ ܥܰܠ ܥܰܘܳܠܶܐ ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܠܡܰܦܩܳܢܳܐ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܚܳܐܰܪ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܠܚܰܛܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܕܰܢܬܘܽܒܘܽܢ ܘܰܢܩܰܒ݁ܶܠ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܚܰܕ݂ܘܽܬܳܐ ܬܶܗܘܶܐ ܒ݁ܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܚܰܕ݂ ܚܰܛܳܝܳܐ ܕܬܳܐܶܒ ܝܰܬܺܝܪ ܡܶܢ ܬܶܫܥܺܝܢ ܘܬܶܫܥܳܐ ܙܰܕ݂ܝܺܩܺܝ̈ܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܣܢܺܝܩܺܝܢ ܥܰܠ ܬܝܳܒܘܽܬܳܐ܀
my law behind you and in my name you were signed and you transgressed all my commandments. And I besought you, I and my apostles, daily, and you were not converted. (For God, He says, we beseech you: be reconciled to God.) Take away, He says, from him the money, that is, the seal, and give it to him who keeps my words. And the evil servant, He says, cast into the darkness and into the gnashing of teeth. You see the baptismal seal remains even in the iniquitous until death, because Jesus was waiting for sinners, that they might be converted and He might receive them, as He said: There will be joy in heaven over one sinner doing repentance more than over ninety-nine just ones, who do not need repentance.


[p. 722] {#po.0.p722}
ܗܘܰܝܢ ܗܰܣܠ ܡܰܟܪܙܺܝܢ ܟܳܪܘܫܺܝܐܝܺܬ ܠܰܚܠܝ̈ܡܶܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܬܪܰܦܘܽܢ ܘܠܰܟܪ̈ܝܳܗܶܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܢܶܬܚܰܝܠܘܽܢ ܘܢܶܬܰܐܣܝܘܽܢ ܘܰܢܩܘܽܡܘܽܢ
3. Therefore with discretion let us exhort the healthy, that they may not fail, and the infirm, that they may recover and be healed and rise and not fall.
ܘܠܳܐ ܢܶܦܠܘܽܢ. ܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ ܬܘܽܒ ܟܬܝܼܒ ܠܙܘܰܘܳܓܳܐ: ܕܐܲܢ ܟܦܶܢ ܒܥܶܠܕܒܳܒܳܟ ܐܰܘܟܶܠܳܝܗ̱ܝ: ܘܐܲܢ ܨܗܶܐ ܐܰܫܩܳܝܗ̱ܝ. ܘܟܰܕ݂ ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܬܶܥܒܶܕ݂: ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܗ̱ܘْ ܝܳܪܶܒ݂ ܐܰܢ݈ܬ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܗܰܘ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܬܳܐܰܒ ܩܫܳܐ ܠܶܗ. ܠܰܓ݂ܡܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܰܝܬ ܠܗܘܢ ܒܥܶܠܕܒܳܒܳܝܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂: ܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܩܢܶܝܢ. ܠܳܐ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܗܝ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܕ݁ܰܠܙܘܽܘܳܓܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܐܶܬܡܰܪܰܚ. ܕܗܶܢܘܽܢ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܕܰܒ݂ܥܶܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܩܶܢܝܳܢܗܘܽܢ
4. Likewise it is prescribed for marriage thus: If your enemy is hungry, feed him; and if he is thirsty, give him to drink. And if you do so, you will progress before the Lord; and he, unless he is converted, will be hardened. The perfect, however, have no enemies, except Satan alone, nor do they possess anything. Is it not clear that these things were said to marriage, who because of their goods are prevaricators and have superfluous food, with which they may feed their enemies?


[p. 723] {#po.0.p723}
ܡܶܬܥܰܒܪܝܺܢ: ܘܰܠܗܘܽܢ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܐܝܺܬ ܣܰܚܒܳܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܡܫܰܪܬܚܳܐ ܕܢܰܘܟܠܘܽܢ ܠܰܒ̈ܥܶܠܕܼܒܳܒܰܝܗܘܽܢ܆ ܬܘܒ ܠܰܚܡ ܐܶܢ ܪܒܥ ܝܳܡܰܚܪܶܗ ܕܰܒܥܶܠܕܒܳܒܳܟ ܬܚܝܬ ܛܰܥܢܶܗ ܐܰܪܚܰܡ ܥܰܡܶܗ. ܘܐܶܢ ܛܳܥܶܐ ܬ݁ܰܘܪܶܗ ܘܐܲܢ ܚܙܰܝܬ ܡܶܕ݁݁ܡ ܕܐܰܒܝܰܕ݂
5. Item, if the donkey of your adversary, he says, succumbs under its burden, raise it up with him; and if his ox strays, and if you see any lost item of his property, gather it. And by doing these things you will be righteous and holy men to me. For thus does justice benefit
ܢܳܫܺܝܢ ܟ݁ܺܐܢܫܳܢ ܘܩܰܕ̈ܝܰܫܝܺܢ ܬܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܠܝ ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܡܰܬܶܛܰܐܒܿܳܐ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܠܟܠ ܕܡܰܟܺܐܫ ܠܳܗ. ܐܰܝܟ ܕܗܝ݇ ܨܳܒ݂ܝܳܐ ܕܢܶܛܶܐܒܘܽܢ ܠܳܗ ܐܳܦ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܐܰܬ݂ܥܰܒܪܰܬ ܘܐܰܒܺܐܫܰܬ ܠܗܘܿܢ. ܐܳܦ ܗܝ݇ ܐܝܬܳܝܗܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܒܺܝܫܬܳܐ ܘܡܰܬܳܛܐܒ݂ܳܐ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܡܰܒܶܐܫ. ܘܰܒܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܬܘܽܒ ܝܳܪܶܒ ܓ݁ܰܒܪܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܓܰܒܪܳܐ. ܗܰܘ ܕ݁ܰܡܪܰܚܶܡ ܥܰܠ ܒܥܶܠܕܒܳܒܶܗ ܘܰܡܚܰܥܶܡܠ ܩܶܢܝܳܢܶܗ ܡܳܐ ܕܰܛܥܳܐ ܘܡܶܬܪܰܥܶܐ ܠܶܗ: ܘܗܰܘ ܕܠܳܐ ܩܶܢܝܳܢܶܗ ܚܳܥܶܡܶܠ ܘܠܐ ܡܰܗܳܪܘܽ ܡܰܡܗܰܪ ܠܶܗ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܰܡܛܶܐܒ ܠܶܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܰܒܶܐܫ ܠܶܗ. ܫܰܦܝܺܪ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܕܪܳܡܶܐ ܥܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܚܘܒ݁ܳܠܶܐ ܒܝܺܫ̈ܶܐ. ܘܗܰܘ ܕ݁ܪܳܡܶܐ ܥܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܚܘܽܒ݁ܺܠܶܐ ܒܝܺܫ̈ܶܐ: ܦܟܝܼܚ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܬܰܫܢܺܩܶܗ ܡܶܢ
each one who inflicts evil upon himself, just as it wishes to be benefited by all, even by those to whom it has done evil through committed transgression. For it also turns away from evil and benefits the evildoer. In this matter, one is greater than another: he who pities his enemy and gathers his straying property and is reconciled to him, and he who neither gathers his property nor harms him by doing harm; but he who neither benefits nor harms is better than he who inflicts evil losses. And he who inflicts evil losses will undergo lighter torments than he who kills him by killing. Of all these, however, the righteous man is he who benefits him and is reconciled to him. All these also receive retribution according to their works, whether good or evil.


[p. 724] {#po.0.p724}
ܗܰܘ ܕܩܳܛܶܠ ܠܶܗ ܡܶܩܛܰܠ. ܕܶܝܢ ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕܡܰܡܬܶܐܒ ܠܶܗ ܘܡܶܬܪܰܥܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܟܺܐܢܳܐ. ܐܳܦ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ: ܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܐܰܝܟ ܥܒܳܝܕ݂ܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܡܶܬܦܪܰܥ: ܐܶܢ ܕܛܳܒ ܘܐܶܢ ܕܒܝܼܫܳܐ܀ ܬܘܳܒ ܐܰܝܢܳܐ ܕܪܳܓ݂ܶܙ ܡܶܪܓܰܙ ܐ ܦܫܝܚܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ ܣܰܟܠܘܽܬܶܗ ܡܶܢ ܕܗܰܘ ܕܡܳܚܶܐ ܡܶܡܚܳܐ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ.
6. Item, if anyone is angry by being angry, his offense is lighter than


[p. 725] {#po.0.p725}
ܘܗܰܘ ܕܡܳܚܶܐ ܡܶܡܚܳܐ ܠܒܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܦܘܚ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܬܰܒܢܺܝܚܶܗ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܕ݁ܩܳܛܶܠ ܠܶܗ ܡܶܩܛܰܠ. ܘܗܰܘ ܕܪܳܓ݁ܶܙ ܥܰܠ ܡܰܢ ܕܐܰܣܟܶܠ ܒܶܗ ܘܡܶܬܪܰܥܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܡܰܥܕ̈ܒ݁ܰܝ ܫܶܡܫܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܚܳܛܶܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܗܰܘ ܕܪܳܓ݁ܶܙ ܥܰܠ ܡܰܢ ܕܚܳܛܶܐ ܒܶܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܪܰܥܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܡܰܥܪ̈ܒܰܝ ܫܶܡܫܳܐ. ܐܶܢ ܪܳܓܙܺܝܢ ܐܰܢܬܽܘܢ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܚܛܘܿܢ. ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܫܰܠܺܝܛ ܠܟܺܐܢܳܐ ܢܶܪܓ݁ܰܙ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܕܢܶܟܒܘܽܫ ܚܶܡܬ݁ܶܗ ܘܰܢܣܰܝܒܰܪ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܡܰܟܺܝܫ ܠܶܗ ܘܢܶܬܥܠܶܒ ܠܶܗ ܩܰܠܺܝܠ: ܘܰܒܪܳܚܡܘܽܬܳܐ ܢܫܰܢܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܠܘܳܬܶܗ. ܘܗܰܘ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܪܰܥܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܪܰܡܫܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܡܰܒܶܐܫ ܠܰܒܥܶܠܕܒܳܒܶܗ: ܫܰܦܺܝܪ ܗ̱ܘܵ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܪܰܥܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܘܡܰܒܶܐܫ ܠܶܗ. ܘܗܰܘ ܕܡܰܥܒܶܕ ܠܶܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܪܰܥܶܐ ܠܶܗ: ܦܫܺܝܚ ̱ܘܵ ܡܰܘܬܶܗ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܪܰܥܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܘܩܳܛܶܠ ܠܶܗ. ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܕܶܝܢ ܡܶܢ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܪܚܺܝܩܺܝܢ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܶܝܢ ܬܪ̈ܶܝܢ ܚܰܝܳܒܺܝܢ ܡܰܘܬܳܐ: ܗܰܘ ܕܡܰܒܶܐܫ ܠܶܗ ܐܰܘ ܡܳܚܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܐܰܘ ܠܳܐܶܛ ܠܶܗ ܘܗܰܘ ܕܩܳܛܶܠ ܠܶܗ. ܬܰܫܢܺܝܩܶܗ ܕܶܝܢ ܕܩܳܛܘܽܠܳܐ ܒܝܼܫ ܗ̱ܘ̈. ܐܶܢ ܬܳܝܒܺܝܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܚܳܐܶܝܢ. ܘܐܶܢ ܪܳܗܛܺܝܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܶܐ ܪܰܘܪ̈ܒ݁ܶܐ: ܐܳܦ ܡܶܬܪܰܒܶܝܢ ܚܳܪܒܺܝܢ ܘܡܶܬܓܰܡܪܺܝܢ܀
that of him who strikes by striking another. And if anyone strikes another by striking, he will undergo lighter torments than he who kills him by killing. And if anyone is angry at one who sins against him and is reconciled to him before the setting of the sun, he does not sin as much as he who is angry at one who sins against him and is not reconciled to him by the setting of the sun. If you are angry, he says, do not sin; that is, it is not permitted for the righteous man to be angry, but he ought to suppress his anger and endure him who has done him evil, and force himself a little, and depart from him with friendship. And he who is not reconciled by evening, and does not inflict evil upon his adversary, is better than he who is not reconciled to him and inflicts evil upon him. And he who has done him evil, and has not been reconciled to him, will undergo a lighter death than he who is not reconciled to him and kills him. All, however, fall from justice. These two are indeed guilty of death: he who does him evil or strikes him or curses him, and he who kills him; but the torment of the murderer is the worst. If, however, they perform penance, all will live; and if they have followed the great commandments, they will even progress by progressing and will be perfected.


[p. 726] {#po.0.p726}
ܘܐܰܝܢܳܐ ܕܝܳܗܶܒ ܦܫܝܺܛܳܐܝܺܬ ܠܟܽܠ ܡܰܢ ܕܪܳܚܶܩ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܥܰܐܶܠ ܡܰܢ ܫܳܘܶܐ ܘܡܰܢ ܠܳܐ ܫܳܘܶܐ: ܪܰܒ ܗ̱ܘܵ ܚܘܽܒܶܗ ܡܶܢ ܕܗܰܘ ܕܰܡܓܰܒܶܐ ܘܝܳܗܶܒ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ. ܗܰܘ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܝܳܗܶܒ ܠܰܣܢܺܝܩܶܐ ܛܝܒ݁ܶܐ ܘܒܝܺܫܶܐ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܳܡܶܐ. ܐܰܝܟ ܕܡܰܕ݁ܢܰܚ ܫܶܡܫܶܗ ܘܡܰܚܶܬ ܡܶܛܪܶܗ ܥܰܠ ܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܘܥܰܠ ܥܰܘܳܠܶܐ ܘܥܰܠ ܛܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܘܥܰܠ ܒܝܺܫ̈ܶܐ: ܗܳܟ݁ܝܢܳܐ ܘܰܒܕ݂ܢܰܚ ܗܘܽ ܚܘܽܒܶܗ ܥܰܠ ܛܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܘܥܰܠ ܒܝܺܫ̈ܶܐ ܘܥܰܠ ܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܘܥܰܠ ܥܰܘܳܠܶܐ. ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܕܫܰܕ݁ܰܪ ܬܘܽܒ ܥܰܒܺܕ݂ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܦܰܩܶܕ݂ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ: ܕܙܰܡܶܢܘ ܠܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܠܛܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܘܰܠܒܺܝܫ̈ܶܐ: ܘܢܶܠܒܫܘ ܢܰܚܬܶܐ ܕܡܶܫܬܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܢܶܬܡܠܶܐ ܒܰܝܬܳܐ ܡܺܝܢܗܘܽܢ. ܗܰܘ ܕܶܝܢ ܕܥܰܠ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܘܰܒܕ݂ܢܰܚ ܚܘܽܒܶܗ: ܡܝܰܬܰܪ ܗ̱ܘ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܕܠܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܡܪܰܚܺܝܡ. ܘܗܰܘ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܪܰܚܰܡ ܥܰܠ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܰܒܺܐܫ ܠܐ̱ܢܳܫ: ܫܰܦܺܝܪ ܗ̱ܘܵ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܕܡܰܒܺܐܫ ܘܒܳܙܶܙ ܘܛܳܠܶܡ. ܘܗܰܘ ܕܡܰܒܺܐܫ ܘܒܳܙܶܙ ܘܛܳܠܶܡ: ܦܫܺܝܚ ܗ̱ܘܵ ܡܘܽܬܶܗ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܕܩܳܛܶܠ. ܗܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܰܒܶܐܫ ܠܐ̱ܢܳܫ: ܘܡܰܛܺܝܒ ܠܟܽܠܢܳܫ: ܗܘܺܝܘܽ ܟܺܐܢܳܐ ܕܒܳܬܰܪ ܓܡܺܝܪ̈ܶܐ. ܘܐܶܢ ܡܶܬܬ݁ܰܪܰܩ ܘܡܶܬܩܰܕ݁ܰܫ ܒܰܥܓܰܠ ܡܶܬܓܡܰܪ. ܡܰܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕ݁ܡܶܬܪܰܚܰܡ܂ ܗܘܺܝܘܽ ܒܪܺܝܟܳܐ: ܕܛܳܒ ܪܰܒ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܒܪܝܺܟ݁ܳܐ ܕܥܰܠ ܛܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܡܶܬܪܰܚܰܡ. ܘܗܰܘ ܕܡܶܬܡܰܟ݁ܰܟ݂ ܩܕܳܡ ܛܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܘܒܝܺܫ̈ܶܐ: ܘܚܳܫܶܒ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܡܝܰܬܪܝܺܢ ܡܶܢܶܗ: ܗܘܺܝܘܽ
7. And he who gives simply to every needy person, and does not ask who is worthy and who is unworthy, his charity is greater than that of him who chooses and gives to certain individuals. For he who gives to the needy, both good and bad, is like God; just as [He] makes His sun rise and sends His rain upon the just and the unjust and upon the good and the bad: he similarly makes his charity rise upon the good and the bad and upon the just and the unjust; just as furthermore God sent His servants and commanded them: Call together all men, good and bad, and let them put on wedding garments and let my house be filled with them. He, however, who makes his charity rise upon certain individuals, is better than he who pities no one. And he who pities no one and harms no one is better than he who does evil and plunders and inflicts injury. And he who does evil and pillages and inflicts injury will undergo a lighter death than he who commits homicide. He, however, who harms no one and benefits everyone, is righteous, the latter of the perfect; and if he empties himself and sanctifies himself, he will quickly be perfected. He, however, who pities all, both good and bad: this one is "blessed," much greater than that blessed one who pities only the good. And he who humbles himself before the good and the bad, and esteems them better than himself, this


[p. 727] {#po.0.p727}


[p. 728] {#po.0.p728}


[p. 729] {#po.0.p729}
ܓ݁ܰܒܪܳܐ ܕܪܰܒ ܒܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܕܦܰܪܰܩܠܺܝܛܳܐ: ܛܳܒ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܕܡܶܬܡܰܟ݁ܰܟ݂ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܛܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܘܒܝܺܫ̈ܶܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܚܳܫܶܒ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܡܝܰܬܪܝܺܢ ܡܶܢܶܗ܀
man is great through the Paraclete Spirit, greater than he who humbles himself before the good and the bad, and does not deem them better than himself.
ܛܘܽܒܰܢܗܘܰܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܰܡܪ̈ܰܚܡܳܢܶܐ ܕܡܶܬܪܰܚܡܺܝܢ ܘܫܳܒܩܺܝܢ ܠܟ݁ܽܠܢܳܫ ܕܡܰܣܟ݁ܶܠ ܒܗܘܢ ܕܰܥܠܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܪ̈ܰܚܡܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܠܘܳܬ݂ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܚܰܛܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܚܢܰܢ: ܘܐܶܢ ܫܳܒܩܺܝܢܰܢ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܐܰܣܟܶܠ ܒ݁ܰܢ: ܫܳܒܶܩ ܠܰܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܐܰܣܟܳܠܢܰܢ ܒܶܗ. ܐܶܢܰܢܩܰܕ݂ ܛܳܥܡܺܝܢܰܢ ܡܰܘܬܳܐ ܚܢܰܢ ܚܰܛܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܣܰܟ݁ܺܠܘܳܬܳܐ ܘܒܘܽܨܳܪܶܐ ܕܐܝܺܬ ܠܰܢ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܢܰܚܡܺܝܢܰܢ ܒܚܰܘܡܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ. ܡܰܘܬܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܚܛܳܗܶܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܘܣܰܟ݁ܺܠܘܳܬܳܐ ܘܒܘܽܨܳܪܶܐ. ܗܳܝ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܫܳܠܰܚ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܦ݁ܰܓ݁ܪܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܺܬܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ ܘܰܕ݂ܛܳܥܺܝܡ ܡܰܘܬܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܺܬܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ. ܒܚܰܘܡܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܕܬܐܶܥܒܰܪ ܥܰܠ ܡܶܠܰܬ݁ܝ ܡܰܘܬܳܐ ܬܶܛܥܰܡ: ܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܠܳܐܕ݁ܳܡ܂ ܒܳܪܘܳܝܶܗ: ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܒܚܰܘܡܳܐ ܕܡܰܣܟܶܠ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܗܳܘܝܳܐ ܠܳܟ݂ ܡܰܚܫܰܒܬ݁ܳܐ ܒܺܝܫܬܳܐ: ܘܰܡܳܐ ܕܥܳܒܰܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܥܰܠ ܡܶܠܰܬܝ ܡܶܣܓ݁ܳܐ ܣܰܓ݁ܝܳܐ ܘܡܳܐܶܬ݂ ܐܢ̱ܬ. ܦ݁ܰܓ݁ܪܳܐ ܓܝܪ ܫܠܰܚ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܒܗܳܝ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܒܳܬܰܪ ܕܰܛܥܶܡ ܡܰܘܬܳܐ. ܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܐܰܪܡܰܪܬ݁ ܡܶܠܰܬ ܦܘܽܡܳܝ: ܕܡܰܗܦܳܟ݂ܳܟ݂ ܘܐܰܘܦܟܳܟ݂ ܠܰܪܥܳܐ ܕܐܶܬܢܣܶܒܬ ܡܶܢܳܗ: ܒܗܳܝ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ: ܕܡܶܢ ܥܰܦܪܳܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܘܰܠܥܰܦܪܳܐ ܬܶܗܦܘܽܟ݂. ܘܐܶܢ ܬܬܘܒܥ ܬܺܚܶܐ ܘܐܶܬܢܰܚܰܡ ܒܡܶܠܰܬܝ ܐܰܝܟ ܡܳܪܳܐ ܘܠܰܘ ܐܰܝܟ ܣܰܟ݁̈ܠܘܳܬܰܢ ܗܳܟܰܢ ܪ̈ܰܚܡܰܘܗ̱ܝ. ܐܶܢ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܐܰܝܟ ܣܰܟ݁ܠܘܳܬܰܢ ܕܝܿܠܰܢ: ܐܰܝܟ ܬܶܢܳܢܳܐ ܡܣܰܝܦ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܰܢ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܬ݂ܪܰܚܰܡ ܥܠܰܝܢ: ܘܣܳܡ ܠܰܢ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܦܘܰܩܕ݁ܳܢܶܐ ܙܥܘܽܪܶܐ ܕܰܠܟܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܓܡܝܳܪܘܽܬܳܐ: ܒܚܰܘܡܳܐ ܕܰܥܒܰܪ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܥܰܠ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܶܗ ܘܰܢܦܰܠ ܡܶܢ ܓܡܝܳܪܘܬܳܐ: ܕܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܒܗܘܢ ܟܺܐܢܳܐ: ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܠܚܰܝܘܡܳܐ ܕܐܳܬܶܐ ܗܰܘ ܕܚܰܘܝܽ ܠܰܢ ܓ݁ܡܝܳܪܘܳܬܳܐ ܒܰܩܢܘܽܡܗ. ܐܶܡܰܪ ܐܰܠܳܨܺܝܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܢܰܦܫܟܘܿܢ ܕܬܺܐܬܘܽܢ ܠܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܓܡܝܳܪܘܬܳܐ: ܛܰܪܘ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܶܐ ܕܟܺܐܢܺܝܶܐ ܩܰܕ݁̈ܡܳܝܶܐ: ܘܚܳܐܶܝܢ ܐܵܢ݈ܬܘܽܢ ܚܰܝ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܰܠܥܳܠܰܡ܂ ܡܰܢ ܠܰܡ ܕܰܡܨܶܐ ܒܚܰܝܠܳܐ ܢܣܰܝܒܰܪ ܘܢܶܥܘܽܠ ܒܬ݁ܰܪܥܳܐ ܐܰܠܺܝܨܳܐ ܘܢܺܐܬ݂ܶܐ ܠܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܡܢܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܛܳܒܬܳܐ ܘܰܡܝܰܬܰܪܬ݂ܳܐ. ܘܐܶܢ ܠܳܐ ܫܳܒܶܩ ܟ݁ܽܠܡܕ݁ܶܡ
8. Blessed indeed are the merciful, who, moved by mercy, forgive all who sin against them, because they will obtain mercy from God. For we are sinners and, if we forgive those who sin against us, God will forgive us, against whom we have sinned. Even if we, sinners, because of the offenses and defects that are in us, taste death, we will be resurrected on the day of God. For sins and offenses and defects are death. For it is one thing to put off the body and another to taste death. On the day, he says, that you transgress my word, you will taste death, his Creator said to Adam; that is, on the day that you offend, you will contract an evil thought, and as often as you have transgressed my word, it will be multiplied by multiplication, and you will die. For Adam put off the body because of this word by tasting death. For God said to him, because he exacerbated the word of His mouth: By returning I will make you return to the earth from which you were taken; for He said to him: You are from dust and into dust you will return, and if you perform penance, you will live, and by my word, you will be resurrected as if by the Lord. Not like our offenses is His mercy; for if it were like our offenses, He would have destroyed us like smoke; nevertheless, having pity on us, He proposed to us those lesser precepts, closer to perfection, on the day that Adam transgressed His word and fell from perfection, so that by their help we might be righteous, until the day that He came who showed us perfection in His own person. For He said to those who cannot bear virtue: if you do not afflict yourselves nor reach this perfection: observe the precepts of the ancient righteous and you will live eternal life. For he who is strong in virtue, let him endure and enter through the narrow gate and he will reach this best and most excellent portion; and if he does not leave all that he has, let him remain in his affairs and do as is prescribed above for the righteous; and each one will receive retribution according to his works; if he is righteous, remaining with his children in his inheritance, he is blameless on the day of God. Otherwise, each one will receive retribution according to his works.


[p. 730] {#po.0.p730}


[p. 731] {#po.0.p731}


[p. 732] {#po.0.p732}
ܕܐܝܺܬ ܠܶܗ ܟ݁ܰܕܐܝܺܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܒܰܕܡܘܽܬ ܕܕܝܽܠܶܗ ܗ̱ܘܵ: ܢܶܥܒܶܕ݂ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܟܬܝܺܒ ܠܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܠܥُܠ. ܘܟܰܠܢܳܫ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܥܒَܳܕ݂ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܡܶܬܦܪܰܥ. ܐܶܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܟܺܐܢܳܐ ܟܕ ܐܰܚܺܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܥܰܡ ܒܢܰܝܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܘܰܒܚܳܪܬܘܽܬܶܗ: ܕܠܳܐ ܥܶܕ݂ܠܳܝ ̱ܗܘܵ ܒܝܰܘܡܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ: ܫܰܪܟ݁ܳܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܶܬܦ݁ܪܰܥ ܘܰܠܪܳܫ ܐܰܝܟ ܥܒَܳܕ݂ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܀ ܫܠܶܡ ܡܺܐܡܪܳܐ ܕܥܶܣܪܺܝܺܢ ܘܰܐܪܒܥܳܐ ܕܥܰܠ ܬܳܒܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܥܰܠ ܦܘܽܪܩܳܢܳܐ ܘܥܰܠ ܗܳܝ ܕ݁ܠܳܐ ܢܶܦܣܘܽܩ ܣܰܒܪܳܐ ܕܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܘܥܰܠ ܡܪܰܚܡܳܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܕܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܚܳܝܪܶܒ ܓܰܝܒܪܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܓܰܝܒܪܳܐ
The twenty-fourth discourse ends concerning penance and remission and concerning not taking away the hope of anyone and concerning mercy and concerning the manner by which one becomes greater than another by the help of his mercy and charity.
ܒܰܡܪܰܚܡܳܢܘܽܬܶܗ ܘܰܒܚܘܽܒܶܗ܀ ܡܺܐܡܪܳܐ ܕܥܶܣܪܺܝܺܢ ܘܚܰܡܫܳܐ ܡܺܐܡܪܳܐ ܕܥܶܣܪܝܺܢ ܘܚܰܡܫܳܐ ܕܥܰܠ ܩܳܠܳܐ
TWENTY-FIFTH DISCOURSE CONCERNING THE VOICE OF GOD AND SATAN


[p. 733] {#po.0.p733}
ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܘܰܕܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ ܩܳܠܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܘܰܕܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ ܀ ܀ ܐܳܦ ܝܰܘܡܳܢ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܣܳܥܰܪ ܒܢܺܝܫܳܐ: ܠܡܰܢ ܕܰܫܒܰܪ ܘܒܳܥܶܐ ܕܢܶܣܬ݁ܰܪܰܩ ܘܢܶܬܩܰܕ݂ܰܫ ܡܶܢ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܡܶܬܟܰܪܰܣ ܡܳܠܶܟ݂ ܠܶܗ ܐܰܘ ܒܟܶܣܝܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܒܓ݂ܶܠܝܳܐ. ܘܰܒܥܶܠܰܬ ܕܰܫܒܰܪ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܡܶܢ ܥܪܝܺܡܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܡܶܢ ܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܗܰܘ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܥܶܠܳܝܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܝܺܕ݂ܰܥ ܕܢܶܦܪܘܽܫ ܒܰܪ݈ܬ ܩܳܠܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܕ݁ܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ. ܘܡܰܡܛܥܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܒܝܺܫܳܐ ܒܡܶܠܟ݁ܶܐ ܣܰܓ̈ܺܝܶܐܐ ܕ݁ܡܶܨܛܰܢܰܥ ܡܳܠܶܟ݂ ܠܶܗ: ܘܟܽܠ ܝܰܘܡܳܐ ܕܐܝܺܬ
1. Today also the Evil One does this to him who is simple and wishes to empty and sanctify himself: he plots and gives him counsel either secretly or openly and, because he is simple in the prudence and knowledge of the higher age, he does not know how to distinguish the voice of God and Satan. And the Evil One seduces him with many counsels and astutely persuades him and daily changes snares for them and, if he recognizes another, he falls into others and, because he has not attained the truth by any reason, he seduces him and binds him to the earth and he thinks himself to be bound to heaven. For malice is accustomed—formerly and today also—under an apparently honest guise
ܒܰܐ̱ܚܪ̈ܳܢܶܐ. ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܐܰܕ݂ܪܶܟ݂ ܫܪܳܪܳܐ: ܒܚܰܕ݂ ܡܶܢ ܐܶܣܟܶܡܰܘܗ̱ܝ: ܡܰܛܥܶܐ ܘܐܳܣܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܒܚܺܫܳܐ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܘܣܳܒܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܗܰܘ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܕܗܳܐ ܒ݁ܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ
to cast Adam and his sons down from on high.


[p. 734] {#po.0.p734}
ܐܰܣܝܪ. ܡܥܺܝܕ݂ܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܒܝܺܫܬܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܩܕ݂ܺܝܡ܂ ܐܳܦ ܝܰܘܡܳܢ: ܕܰܒܦܰܪܨܘܽܦ ܫܰܦܝܳܪ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܕܡܶܬܚܰܙܝܳܢ ܬܰܚܬܰܝܘܗ̱ܝ ܠܳܐܕ݁ܳܡ܂ ܡܶܢ ܪܰܘܡܳܐ ܠܶܗ ܘܰܠܒܢܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ܀ ܡܶܢ ܩܕܝܺܡ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܐܰܚܬܬ ܠܳܐܕ݁ܳܡ: ܘܰܚܕܰܬ
2. For formerly he deposed Adam, and a few ascended to the place from which he descended, until God by His grace
ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܡܳܝܶܐ ܩܝܳܡܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܒܪ̈ܰܚܡܰܘܗ̱ܝ: ܘܒܰܦܝ̈ܺܝܣܶܐ ܣܰܓ݁ܺܝ̈ܐܶܐ ܐܰܦܢܝ̈ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܠܰܐܝܠܺܝܢ ܕܐܶܬܛܦܺܝܣܘ ܠܶܗ. ܒܟ݁ܽܠ ܦܘܽܪ̈ܣܝܳܢ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܐܶܬܦܰܪܰܣ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܰܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܢܺܐܚܘܽܢ: ܘܰܒܟ݁ܽܠ ܪ̈ܳܐܙܺܝܢ ܡܰܠܶܠ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܰܫܪܳܪܳܐ: ܘܰܒܟ݁ܽܠ ܦܺܝܠܳܐܢ ܨܳܐܪܶܗ ܒܐܚܺܝܕ݂ܳܐ ܕܰܢܒܺܝ̈ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܡܶܢ ܩܕ݂ܺܝܡ: ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܠܙܰܒܢܳܐ ܕܰܨܒܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܢܶܬ݁ܪܰܥܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܠܰܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ: ܘܫܰܕ݂ܰܪ ܠܰܒܪܶܗ ܘܐܶܬܳܐ ܥܒܰܕ݂ ܬܰܪܥܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܰܫܡܰܝ̈ܳܢܶܐ ܥܰܡ ܐܰܪ̈ܥܳܢܳܐ: ܘܚܰܘܝܳܗ ܠܰܓܡܺܝܪܘܽܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܠܩܰܕ݂ܝܺܫܘܽܬ݂ܳܐ ܕܰܒ݂ܪܝܺܬܶܗ ܕܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ܂ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܬܳܐ ܓܶܠܝܳܐܝܺܬ ܒܰܩܢܘܽܡܶܗ: ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܟܽܠܥܶܒܕܶܝܢ ܡܶܢܕ݂ܪܝܺܫ ܐܶܬܚܰܕ݁ܰܬ ܒܝܶܫܘܽܥ. ܚܳܙܶܝܬ݂ ܕܠܳܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܚܰܘܝܺ ܓܶܠܝܳܐܝܺܬ ܕܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܒܪܺܝܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܒܕܘܰܒܳܪ̈ܰܘܗ̱ܝ. ܡܰܢ ܕܨܳܒܶܐ ܗܳܟܝܽܠ ܕܢܶܝܣܰܩ ܠܦܰܪܕ݁ܰܝܣܳܐ: ܢܗܰܠܶܟ ܐܺܝܟ ܗܰܠܟ݁ܳܬܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܡܰܟܝܺܟ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܘܰܡܣܰܪ̈ܩܳܬܳܐ ܘܒܰܣܺܝܡ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܘܦܰܚ̈ܺܝܛܳܬܳܐ: ܕ݁ܰܗܘܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܛܳܒܳܝܐ: ܘܡܰܟܝܺܟܳܐܝܺܬ ܐܰܪܬܚܺܝ ܠܟܰܠܢܳܫ ܘܥܰܕܰܪ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ. ܐܶܢ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܠܺܝܬ ܠܶܗ ܦܘܽܠܚܳܢܳܐ ܕܰܪܥܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܕ݁ܰܚܙܳܐ ܗܳܟܝܶܠ ܕܗܳܟ݂ܰܢ ܪܚܶܡ ܐܳܕܳܡ: ܐܰܦܶܣ ܠܶܗ ܕܢܶܙܕ݂ܰܘܰܓ ܘܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܟܐܝܺܢ ܒܗܳܢܳܐ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܕܰܪܚܺܝܡ ܘܢܺܐܚܶܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܢܺܐܒ݁ܰܕ݂ ܠܶܗ ܘܽܠ ܕܐܳܦܶܢ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܒ݂ܰܝܚܺܝ̈ܛܶܐ ܪܰܓܢܳܝܗ̱ܝ:
called them and converted those obedient to Him with many persuasions. For God tried all ways for the sake of men, so that they might be saved; and God spoke the truth in all mysteries and formerly prefigured it through the prophets in all parables, until the day that He wished to be reconciled to men. And He sent His Son, who reconciled the heavenly and the earthly and showed the perfection and holiness of the pristine creature Adam manifestly in His own person, as He said: All things from the beginning have been renewed through Jesus. You see, no one showed manifestly how Adam was created, except Jesus by His conversation. Whoever, therefore, wishes to ascend to paradise, let him walk according to the humble, emptied, sweet, and despised ways of God, who showed himself kind to all and humbly warned and helped everyone. For if anyone does not exercise heavenly worship, he cannot be free from the worship of the earth. When, therefore, [God] had seen Adam loving such things, He permitted him to enter into marriage and in this world, which he loved, to become righteous and to live and not to perish entirely; and because of His mercy God made it so that, although we have sinfully desired these things, in them


[p. 735] {#po.0.p735}


[p. 736] {#po.0.p736}


[p. 737] {#po.0.p737}
ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܒܶܗ ܕܠܳܐ ܚܛܺܝ̈ܗܶܐ: ܐܶܢ ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܟܺܐܢܶܐ܀ ܐܶܢ ܗܳܟܝܽܠ ܠܰܘ ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢ ܗܺܝ ܨܒܘܽܬܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܪܶܐ ܗܳܝ ܕܡܶܢܩܕ݂ܝܺܡ: ܥܰܠ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܡܪܰܢ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܡܰܠܶܦ݂ ܠܰܢ ܩܰܕ݂ܝܺܫܘܽܬ݂ܳܐ ܘܰܓ݂ܡܝܳܪܘܽܬܳܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ: ܕܐܶܢ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܦܰܪܰܩ ܡܶܢ ܟܽܠ ܕܐܺܝܬ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܠܺܝ ܬܰܠܡܺܝܕ݂ܳܐ ܕܩܰܕܝܺܫܘܽܬܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܰܢ ܕܦܳܠܰܚ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܒܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܗܳܘܶܐ ܟܺܐܢܳܐ ܘܳܪܶܬ ܚܰܝ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܰܠܥܳܠܺܝܡ܂ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܓܡܝܪܳܐ܀ ܘܥܰܠ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܫܠܺܝܚ̈ܶܐ ܘܟܽܠ ܕܰܗܘܰܘ ܓܡܝܪ̈ܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܪܰܓܘ ܠܰܐܪܥܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܪܗܶܛܘ ܒܥܳܠܡܳܝܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܐܶܙܕܰܘܰܓܘ܆ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܦܰܩܶܕ݂ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܐܰܒܘܽܟܘܽܢ ܕܡܶܬܒ݁ܰܥܝܳܐ ܠܟܘܽܢ ܣܰܚܒܳܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܠܒܘܽܫܳܐ. ܐܰܢܬܽܘܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܬܰܐܨܦܘܽܢ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܐܶܢܳܐ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܠܟܺܐܢ̈ܳܐ ܕܦܳܠܚܺܝܢ ܒ݁ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܡܬ݁ܰܪܣܺܝܢ ܠܟܘܽܢ ܘܡܠܒܫܺܝܢ ܠܟܘܽܢ: ܘܚܳܐܶܝܢ ܚܰܝ̈ܶܐ ܕ݁ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܚܰܕ݂ܬܳܐ ܡܶܛܽܠܳܬܟܘܽܢ: ܘܥܳܒܕ݂ܺܝܢ ܠܟܘܽܢ ܗܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܥܰܡܠܗܘܽܢ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܠܳܐ ܡܰܒܶܐܫܺܝܢ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ. ܘܶܐܠܘܽ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܛܽܠܳܬܟ݂ܘܽܢ ܕܢܺܐܚܘܽܢ ܒܟܘܢ: ܐܶܢܳܐ ܡܰܥܡܶܕ݂ ܗ̱ܘܺܝܬ ܠܟܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܣܰܚܒܳܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܠܒܘܽܫܳܐ. ܘܐܶܠܘܽ ܐܳܬܝܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܬ ܟܽܠܳܗ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܒܳܬ݂ܰܪ ܓܡܝܪܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܩܰܕܝܺܫܘܽܬ݂ܳܐ܆ ܘܠܳܐ ܦܳܠܚܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܬ ܘܠܳܐ ܩܳܢܝܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܬ:/ܐܶܢܳܐ ܘܳܠܺܝܬ ܠܟ݁ܽܠܳܗ ܕܠܳܐ ܥܰܡܠܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܡܶܢܩܕܝܰܡ. ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܨܳܒ݁ܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܺܝܬ ܕܢܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ: ܘܐܳܕܳܡ ܐܰܒܘܽܟܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܬܝܺܟܘܽܢ ܠܗܳܢܳܐ ܥܰܡܠܵܐ. ܐܶܢܶܝܢ ܕܳܒܶܝܢ ܕܢܶܬܩܰܕܫܘܽܢ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ: ܐܶܢܳܐ ܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܙܘܳܓܳܬ ܠܗܘܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕ݁ܥܶܒܕ݁ܶܬ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܒ݁ܰܪܬܳܐ ܡܳܢܶܗ: ܕܠܳܐ ܙܘܽܘܳܓܳܐ ܘܰܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܐܶܓܬ݁ܳܐ. ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܟܳܠܝܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܥܶܕ݂ܠܳܝܳܐ ܕ݁ܶܐܕ݂ܰܝ ܠܳܐ ܢܶܗܘܶܐ
we may live without sin, if we are righteous. 3. If, therefore, the matter is not as I said it was formerly, why did God say, teaching holiness and perfection: Unless one separates himself from all that is on the earth, he cannot become my disciple of holiness, but he who cultivates the earth with justice becomes righteous and will inherit eternal life, yet he will not be perfect? And why did the Apostles and all the perfect not desire the earth nor run in the world nor enter into marriage, but God commanded them: Your Father knows that you have need of food and clothing? "Do not be anxious, because I will command the righteous, who work on the earth, and they will nourish you and clothe you and will live the life of your new age for your sake and they themselves will do [alms] for you from their labor, harming no one. And if not for your sake, so that they might be saved through you, I would not have made food and clothing rain down for you from heaven; and if the whole earth had followed perfection and holiness, and did not work nor possess, I would have preserved it all without labor as before. Thus I wished all men to be; and Adam, your father, led you to this labor. If, however, men had wished to be sanctified, I would have made children for them, just as I made a daughter for Adam from himself without marriage and concupiscence, provided that no one had an obstacle and reproach before me. If, however, they are righteous and work on the earth, let them inflict evil on no one and thus do for the needy as I commanded them, and they will inherit the kingdom, although they do not reach perfection."


[p. 738] {#po.0.p738}


[p. 739] {#po.0.p739}
ܐܰܢܳܫ. ܐܶܢܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܘܥܳܡܠܺܝܢ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܢܰܒܶܐܫܘܽܢ ܠܐ̱ܢܳܫ: ܘܢܶܥܒܕܘܽܢ ܠܰܣܢܺܝܩܶܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܦܰܝܩܕܶܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ: ܘܝܳܪܬܝܺܢ ܡܰܠܟ݁ܘܽܬܳܐ: ܐܳܦܶܢ ܠܰܓܡܝܳܪܘܳܬܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܡܳܛܶܝܢ܀ ܐܳܦ ܝܰܘܡܳܢܳܐ ܒܥܶܠܰܬ ܫܰܦܝܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܡܰܛܠܝܳܐ ܒܝܫܬܳܐ ܠܰܐܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܒܳܥܶܝܢ ܩܰܕܺܝܫܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܰܓ݁ܡܝܳܪܘܳܬܳܐ. ܘܟܳܠܝܳܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܠܘܳܬ ܓܰܐܝܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܣܳܠܩܺܝܢ ܠܰܓܡܝܳܪܘܽܬܳܐ: ܕܚܰܘܝ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ. ܡܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܐܳܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕܐܶܬܡܰܟܰܟܘ ܘܐܶܬܦ݂ܰܪܰܩܘ ܘܐܶܬܩܰܕܰܫܘ ܡܶܢ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܘܡܶܢ ܫܰܘܬܳܦ݂ܘܽܬ݂ܳܐ: ܘܰܪܚܰܡܘ ܠܟ݂ܽܠܢܳܫ ܘܐܶܬܰܘ ܒܳܬܰܪܝ: ܠܳܐ ܬܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܠܳܐ ܗܘܝܺܬ ܐܶܢܳܐ ܡܶܢܶܗ ܘܠܳܐ ܥܶܡܠܶܬ ܒܶܗ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܬܰܘ ܒܳܬܰܪܝ ܘܰܗܘܰܘ ܓܡܝܳܪ̈ܶܐ: ܐܳܬܶܐ ܒܝܫܳܐ ܘܰܡܚܰܘܶܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܐܰܪ̈ܥܳܢܳܝܳܬ݁ܳܐ: ܕܠܳܐ ܢܚܘܽܪܘܽܢ ܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܝܳܬ̈ܳܐ: ܘܢܶܬܪܰܥܘܽܢ ܕ݁ܰܠܥܶܠ ܘܢܶܙܟ݂ܘܽܢܳܝܗ̱ܝ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܐܰܚܘܶܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܒܐܰܪ̈ܥܳܢܳܝܬܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܟܰܚ ܡܰܝܬܶܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܓܡܝܳܪܘܬܳܐ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܟܳܠܶܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܥܶܠܰܬ ܥܰܡܠܳܐ ܕܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܕܕܡܳܐ ܕܩܳܝܡܺܝܢ ܒܥܰܡܠܳܐ ܕܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܢܶܥܒܶܕ݂ ܒܗܘܽܢ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܝܗ:
4. Even today malice seduces under a good pretext those who seek holiness and perfection and keeps them in pride, and they do not reach the perfection that God showed them. For while God says: humble yourselves and separate yourselves and be sanctified from the age and marriage and love all men and follow me; do not be of the world, just as I was not of it nor did I labor in it, but follow me and be perfect, the Evil One comes and makes them look at earthly things, so that they do not look at heavenly things and think of what is above and overcome. For unless he showed them earthly things, he could not depose them from perfection; but he keeps them under the pretext of righteous labor, so that while they stand in righteous labor he may fulfill his pleasure in them, although he cannot do everything, but only something. For after they had renounced and were sanctified and were contemplating heavenly things,


[p. 740] {#po.0.p740}
ܐܳܦܶܢ ܟܽܠ ܟܽܠܳܗ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܟܰܚ: ܒܪܰܡ ܒܡܕ݁ܶܡ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܡܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܐܶܣܬ݁ܰܪܰܩܘ ܘܐܶܬܩܰܕܰܫܘ. ܘܚܳܪܘ ܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܝܳܬܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܡܶܬܟܰܬܰܫ ܥܰܡܗܘܽܢ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܥܳܒܪܝܰܢ ܠܶܗ ܠܥܶܠ: ܘܦܳܐܶܫ ܠܶܗ ܗܘܽ ܠܬܰܚܬ ܡܶܢܗܘܿܢ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܝܰܠܺܝܛ ܗܘ ܕܢܶܥܒܰܪ ܪܩܺܝܥܳܐ: ܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܕ݁ܢܶܥܘܽܠ ܠܗܰܘ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܕܰܠܘܳܬ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܥܳܒܰܪ ܪܶܥܝܢܗܘܽܢ ܕܝܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܘܣܳܠܳܩ ܥܕܰܡܳܐ ܠܐܘܿܪܺܫܠܶܡ ܕܰܠܥܶܠ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܟܬܝܺܒ: ܕܗܘ ܢܕܰܒܪܰܢ ܠܥܶܠ ܡܶܢ ܡܰܘܬܳܐ. ܘܐܰܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܠܰܡ ܡܛܰܝܬܘܽܢ ܠܨܲܗܝܘܽܢ ܛܘܳܪܳܐ ܘܠܰܡܕ݂ܺܝܢܬܶܗ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ: ܠܘܳܬ ܘܰܒܥܕ݁ܺܝܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܡܰܠܰܐܟ݂ܶܐ:
he cannot contend with them, because they transcend him while he remains below them; since it is not permitted for him to pass through the firmament, nor to enter into that age which is with God, just as their mind passes through and ascends even to the supernal Jerusalem, just as it is written that He takes us from death: And you, he says, have reached Mount Sion and the heavenly city of God, to the camp of angels and to the spirits, he says, of the ancient righteous, who have fallen asleep in justice and have been perfected in Jesus and have entered into the spiritual paradise.


[p. 741] {#po.0.p741}
ܘܰܠܘܳܬ ܪ̈ܘܽܚܳܬܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܕܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܩܰܕ݁̈ܡܳܝܶܐ: ܕܰܒܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܫܟܶܒܘ: ܘܰܒܝܺܫܘܽܥ ܐܶܬܓܡܰܪܘ: ܘܥܰܠܘ ܠܦܰܪܕܰܝܣܳܐ ܪܘܽܚܳܢܳܐ܀ ܡܰܚܺܘܳܬܶܗ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ ܘܕܰܒܢܰܘܗ̱ܝ̈ ܒܗܳܕܶܐ ܡܶܬܬܰܐܣܝ̈ܳܢ: ܐܶܡܰܬܝ ܕܰܠܗܰܘ ܦܰܪܕ݁ܰܝܣܳܐ ܕܰܢܦ݁ܰܩ ܡܶܢܶܗ ܐܵܒܘܽܗܘܽܢ ܢܶܥܠܘܽܢ ܒܪܘܚ. ܐܳܦ ܗܳܟܝܶܠ ܝܰܘܡܳܢ ܕܐܶܬܕܰܪܫܰܬ ܐܘܽܪܚܳܐ ܠܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܒܡܫܺܝܚܳܐ ܒܚܰܕ݂ ܡܫܰܢܶܚܳܐ ܕܐܳܡܰܪ: ܕܰܫܒܘܽܩܘ ܟܽܠ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕ݁ܡܶܬܚܙܶܐ ܘܕܰܠܥܶܠ ܐܶܬܪܰܥܰܘ ܘܠܳܐ ܕܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܬܺܐܪܬܘܽܢ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ: ܘܗܳܐ ܙܟܰܝܬܘܽܢ: ܐܳܬ݁ܶܐ ܡܳܠܶܟܡ ܒܚܺܫܳܐ ܒܒܰܪܨܘܽܦ ܫܰܦܝܺܪܳܐ: ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܰܠܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܦ݁ܰܩܶܕ݂ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܡܶܨܛܰܕ݂ܳܐ ܒܶܗ ܒܰܓܡܺܝܪܳܐ ܘܐܡܪ ܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ: ܫܰܦܝܺܪ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܠܰܡ܂ ܬ݂ܶܩܢܶܐ ܩܰܠܺܝܠ ܒܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܡܶܣܰܬ ܢܚܳܚܳܟ ܕܝܽܠܳܟ ܘܰܕ݂ܡܰܢ ܕܐܳܬܶܐ ܠܘܳܬܳܟ݂. ܘܰܒܢܺܝ ܠܺܝܟ ܥܘܽܡܪܳܐ ܕܰܡܫܰܪܰܚ ܩܰܠܺܝܠ: ܕܐܳܬ݁ܶܝܢ ܐܰܟܣ̈ܢܳܝܶܐ ܘܡܶܬܬܢܺܝܚܺܝܢ ܒܶܗ. ܘܨܘܽܒ ܠܳܟ ܩܰܠܺܝܠ ܢܶܨܒ݂ܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܓܰܢܰܬ ܝܰܪܩܳܐ ܥܒܶܝܕ݂ ܠܳܟ: ܕܗܳܘܝܳܐ
5. For the wounds of Adam and his sons are healed then, when they enter by spirit into that paradise from which their father went out. Therefore even today, with the way to heaven opened through Christ, who said: Leave all visible things and think of what is above, not what is on the earth nor inherit on the earth, but in heaven, and behold you will overcome: the Evil One comes and proposes counsels under the guise of good [works], which God commanded only to the righteous, and mocking the perfect he says thus: "It is good, he says, for you to possess a little with justice for your own convenience and that of him who has come to you. Build for yourself a slightly more abundant dwelling, so that pilgrims coming to you may be relieved, and plant a small plantation for yourself and make a vegetable garden for yourself, for the healthy and the infirm." And under the pretext of the convenience of the afflicted he plots and deposes him from the sublime precept saying to the perfect: Do not even have care for your soul, and from that commandment: Think of what is above and not what is on the earth. And because he does not discern voice from voice, nor understands that these are precepts for earthly righteous, not for him who


[p. 742] {#po.0.p742}


[p. 743] {#po.0.p743}
ܕ݁ܰܡܛܰܪ̈ܦ݁ܶܐ ܡܶܬܦܰܪܰܣ ܘܡܰܚܶܬ ܠܶܗ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܡܶܢ ܗܰܘ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܳܐ ܪܳܡܳܐ ܕܐܳܡܰܪ ܠܰܓܡܺܝܪ̈ܶܐ ܕܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܠܢܰܦܫܳܟ ܬܺܐܨܰܦ: ܘܡܶܢܿ ܗܰܘ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܳܐ: ܕܕܰܠܥܶܠ ܐܶܬ݂ܪܰܥܰܝܘ ܘܠܳܐ ܕܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܘܰܒܥܶܠܰܬ݂ ܕܠܳܐ ܦܪܰܫ ܩܳܠܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܩܳܠܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܡܶܣܬ݁ܰܟ݁ܰܠ ܕܰܠܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܐܰܪܥܳܢܳܝܶܐ ܦܩܺܕ݂ܳܢ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ: ܘܠܳܐ ܠܗܰܘ ܕܒܳܥܶܐ ܫܡܰܝܳܢ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܘܰܓܡܺܝܪܘܽܬܳܐ: ܐܰܘܦܟܶܪܶܗ ܒܬܫܰܥܝܳܐ ܠܘܳܬ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܠܬܰܚܬ ܡܶܢ ܓܡܺܝܪܘܽܬܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܠܳܐ ܪܓܝܫ ܘܗܰܘ ܣܳܒܰܪ ܕܒܳܬܰܪ ܓܡܺܝܪܘܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܐܳܗܶܛ: ܘܐܶܫܬܟܰܚ ܠܬܰܚܬ ܡܶܢܳܗ. ܘܥܰܠܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܫܠܺܝܚܳܐ: ܕܐܶܠܳܐ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܘܦܳܪܶܫ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ ܚܰܝܠܶܗ ܕ݁ܩܳܠܳܐ ܕܩܳܪܶܐ ܘܡܰܡܣܶܩ ܠܝ ܠܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܩܳܠܳܐ ܕܡܰܚܶܬ ܠܝ ܠܰܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܠܳܐ ܐܰܪ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܟܳܬܶܫ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܓܰܒܪܳܐ ܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܪܓܺܝܫ ܥܰܠ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܪܳܗܶܛ. ܐܶܢܳܐ ܠܰܡ܂ ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܪܳܗܶܛ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ ܓܰܒܪܳܐ ܕܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܕܢܶܦܪܘܽܫ ܩܳܠܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܩܳܠܳܐ. ܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ ܗܳܢܶܝܢ ܡܥܰܕܶܠ ܡܰܘܦܶܟ݂ ܠܶܗ ܒܚܺܝܠܳܐ ܠܰܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܠܒܶܣܬܪܶܗ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܠܳܐܕ݁ܳܡ܂ ܐܳܦܶܢ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܫܰܦܝܺܪܳܢ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܥܰܡ̈ܡܶܐ ܕܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܒܳܥܶܝܢ ܠܗܶܝܢ. ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܙܶܕ݁̈ܩܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܢܚܳܡܳܝܐ ܕܰܡܛܰܪ̈ܦ݁ܶܝܐ: ܠܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܕܦܳܠܚܺܝܢ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܦܰܩܶܕ݂ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܢܶܥܒܕܘܽܢ ܐܶܢܶܝܢ: ܘܰܢܢܺܝܚܘܽܢ ܠܰܡܬ݂ܰܝܪ̈ܦ݁ܺܝܐ
seeks heavenly things and perfection: the Evil One bends him to justice, inferior to perfection, and he does not perceive it; and while he thinks he is following perfection, he is found below it. Therefore the Apostle said: Unless I know and distinguish the virtue of the voice, which calls and raises me to heaven, from the voice, which deposes me on the earth: I will be beating the air, like a man who does not know why he runs. I, he says, run in such a way, as a man who knows how to distinguish voice from voice. Therefore by flattering him the Evil One deceives him and makes him return to the earth, like Adam. For although these things are honest, yet the righteous nations of the earth seek them; for these are contrary to heavenly things. For God commanded all these things, alms and the relief of the afflicted, to the righteous,


[p. 744] {#po.0.p744}
ܘܢܺܐܚܘܽܢ ܒܗܶܝܢ. ܐܝܠܶܝܢ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܰܪܓܝܺܢ ܕܢܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܫܡܰܝ̈ܳܢܶܐ: ܢܚܘܪܘܽܢ ܒܰܫܡܰܝ̈ܳܢܶܐ: ܗܳܢܰܝ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܒܰܐܠܳܗܳܐ ܘܒܰܫܠܝ̈ܚܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܘܰܙܕܺܝ̈ܩܶܐ ܓܡܝܪ̈ܶܐ: ܘܰܢܚܘܽܪܘܽܢ ܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܝܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܢܶܬܬܰܚܕ݂ܘܽܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܒ݁ܰܚܕ݂ܳܐ ܨܒܝܘܽܬܳܐ
who cultivate the earth, so that they might do them and relieve the afflicted and be saved through them. For those who wish to become heavenly, let them look to heaven, that is, to God and His Apostles and the perfect righteous and let them gaze at heaven, not the earth, nor be detained by any earthly thing.


[p. 745] {#po.0.p745}
ܡܶܢ ܐܰܪܥܳܢܳܝ̈ܳܬܳܐ܀ ܠܰܝܬ ܠܰܡ ܦܘܽܪܣܳܐ ܕܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܕܢܶܦܠܘܽܚ ܠܰܐܠܳܗܳܐ ܒܪܘܽܚ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܡܕ݂ܰܘܰܕ ܒܨܶܒܘܳܬܳܐ ܕܥܳܠܡܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܠܗ̱ܰܘ ܡܰܢ ܕܰܓܒܳܐܝܗ̱ܝ ܢܶܣܬ݁ܰܦ݁ܰܝܣ ܕܢܶܫܦܰܪ. ܘܒܰܨܠܘܽܬܗܘܽܢ ܘܰܒܝܘܽܠܦܳܢܗܘܽܢ ܛܳܒ݁ܳܝܐ ܢܺܐܙܠ̱ܘܽܢ ܠܘܳܬ ܟܽܠܢܳܫ: ܛܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܘܒܺܝ̈ܫܶܐ ܘܢܰܛܶܐܒ݂ܘܽܢ ܠܟܽܠܢܳܫ
6. For there is no way given for one to be able to serve God in spirit, while he is disturbed by worldly things, unless he has adapted himself to please Him who chose him. And let these by their prayer and good doctrine approach everyone, good and bad, and benefit every afflicted person. For behold, He commands the heavenly to benefit everyone with heavenly things. For whence do you know, you who say that one ought not to speak with a vain and wandering man, that this one will not be righteous or perfect? Just as God said to Ananias:
ܕܒ݂ܰܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܝ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܢܰܛܶܐܒܘܽܢ ܠܟܠ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ. ܡܶܢ ܐܰܝܡܟ݁ܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܐܶܢ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܠܳܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܢܡܰܠܶܠ ܥܰܡ ܣܪܝܺܩܳܝܐ ܘܛܳܥܝܳܝܐ: ܕܙܰܕܺܝܩܳܐ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܓܡܝܪܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܟܺܐ݈ܢܳܐ~ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܠܚܰܢܰܢܝܳܐ: ܕܙܶܠ ܡܰܠܶܠ ܥܰܡ ܦܰܘܠܳܘܣ. ܘܐܳܡܰܪ ܚܰܢܰܢܝܳܐ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ: ܡܳܪܝ: ܓܰܒܪܳܐ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܒܺܝܫܳܐ ܘܫܶܡܥܶܬ ܕܐܘܰܠܨܳܢܳܐ ܐܰܣܒܶܠ ܠܩܰܕܺܝ̈ܫܶܐ ܕܒܐܘܪܺܫܠܶܡ. ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕܙܶܠ ܡܰܠܶܠ ܥܰܡܶܗ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܡܳܐܢܳܐ ܗܽܘ ܠܺܝ ܓܒܺܝܳܐ: ܘܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܳܐ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ. ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܗܳܟܝّܠ ܐܳܦ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ: ܕܐܺܝܬ ܠܳܟ݂ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܟܽܠܢܳܫ: ܡܰܠܶܠ: ܘܠܳܐ ܚܳܛܶܐ ܐܢ̱ܬ. ܕܰܘܩܳܐ ܠܰܡ ܒܒܰܕ݂ܬ݁ܳܟ݂ ܕܬܶܚܙܶܐ ܕ݁ܝܺܢܳܐ ܕܰܥܬܺܝܕ: ܘܰܬܙܰܗܰܪ ܠܚܰܛܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܠܘܽܩܕ݂ܰܡ ܘܟܶܢ ܠܙܰܕܺܝ̈ܩܶܐ. ܡܳܐ ܕܐܰܗܦܟ݁ܶܗ ܗܳܟܝܺܠ ܒܺܝܫܳܝܐ ܠܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܡܶܢ ܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܝ̈ܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܐܰܩܝܡܶܗ ܒܥܰܡܠܳܐ ܕܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܰܩܢܳܐ ܓܰܢ̈ܶܐ ܘܦܰܪ̈ܕ݁ܰܝܣܶܐ ܐܰܪ̈ܥܳܢܳܝܶܐ: ܘܩܢܳܐ ܙܳܐ ܘܒܶܢܝ̈ܳܢܶܐ: ܡܫܰܪܶܐ ܡܶܟܝܺܠ ܒܺܝܫܳܐ ܕܢܶܣܚܦܶܗ ܐܳܦ݂ ܡܶܢ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ. ܡܳܐ ܕܐܶܙܰܠ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܚܰܝܦܶܛ ܠܐܚܪܳܢܶܐ ܕܢܰܒܺܐܫܘܽܢ ܠܶܗ: ܥܰܠ ܐܶܬܳܐ ܥܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܕܟܺܐܢܳܐ ܕܦܿܳܫ ܡܶܢ ܓܡܝܪܘܽܬܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܕܰܢܕ݂ܰܠܚܶܗ ܘܢܶܥܒܕ݁ܶܗ ܒܺܝܫܳܐ. ܘܰܡܫܰܪܶܐ ܕܢܺܐܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ: ܕܒܰܫܬܳܟ݂ ܒܰܝܬܶܗܝ ܗܰܘ ܕܰܒܥܰܡܠܳܐ
Go, speak with Paul. And Ananias said to God: My Lord, this man is wicked. And I heard that he has inflicted tribulation upon the saints who are in Jerusalem. And God said to him: Go, speak with him, because he is a chosen vessel for me and you do not know. By a similar reason, therefore, you also, who have conversation with all, speak, and you will not sin. I have made you a watchman, he says, so that you may see the future judgment and exhort the sinners first, then the righteous. After, therefore, the Evil One turns someone away from heavenly things and places him in the labor of justice and he has acquired gardens and earthly paradises and wealth and houses, then the Evil One begins to cast him down even from justice. For while he is away, he excites others to inflict evil upon him; he himself comes upon the righteous man, who unknowingly resisted perfection, to disturb him and render him evil, and he begins to say: "Plunder your house, which you built with much labor!" He goes, argues, quarrels. Behold the first gain, which he collected! Furthermore he says to him: "Insatiable robbers have pillaged your plantation and vegetable garden!" And departing he fights. Behold another gain, which the Evil One persuaded him to do! Item he says to him: "They struck and slaughtered and led away your cattle, when they were grazing on your mountain." And clapping his hands he is disturbed. Behold another gain, which the Evil One persuaded the heavenly to possess and build.


[p. 746] {#po.0.p746}


[p. 747] {#po.0.p747}
ܣܳܓܝܳܐ ܒܢܰܚܬܳܝܗ̱ܝ. ܐܳܙܶܠ ܢܳܝܨܳܐ ܘܗܳܐܰܪ. ܗܳܐ ܚܰܝܕ݂ ܚܘܺܐܪܳܢܳܐ ܕܟܰܥܶܝܫ. ܬܘܽܒ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ: ܕܢܶܨܒܿܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܓܰܢܰܬ ܝܰܪܩܳܐ ܠܰܩܺܛܘ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܥܳܠܽܘܒ݁ܶܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܣܳܒܥܝܺܢ: ܘܐܳܙܶܠ ܡܶܬܟܰܬܰܫ. ܗܳܐ ܝܘܺܐܪܳܢܳܐ ܐ݈ܚܪܺܢܳܐ ܕܡܰܠܟ݁ܶܗ ܒܢܺܫܳܐ ܕܢܰܥܒܶܕ. ܬܘܽܒ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ: ܩܶܢܫܳܝܢܳܟ ܡܚܰܝܐܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܚܳܙܶܝܬ ܛܳܒ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܕܡܳܠܶܟ݂ ܒܚܺܫܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܗܳܘ̈ܝܳܢ ܠܗܶܝܢ ܒܺܝ̈ܫܳܬܳܐ. ܘܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܚܰܡܣܶܢ ܘܰܡܣܰܝܒܰܪ ܢܶܣܝܘܳܢܶܗ ܐܰܝܟ ܐܿܝܘܽܒ: ܐܳܦ݂ ܡܶܢ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܣܳܚܺܝܦ ܠܶܗ. ܡܶܬ݂ܺܝܠ ܕ݁ܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܡܰܒ݁ܶܐܫܝܺܢ ܠܐ̱ܢܳܫ. ܐܳܦܶܢ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܠܳܐ ܢܰܒܶܐܫ ܟܺܐܢܳܐ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ: ܚܳܢܶܩ ܠܶܗ ܒܺܝܫܳܐ ܒܥܰܝܡܬܳܐ ܘܰܨܶܦ݂ܬ݁ܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܫܳܒܶܩ ܠܶܗ ܕ݁ܢܰܕ݂ܪܶܟ݂ ܫܪܳܪܳܐ. ܘܐܶܠܳܐ ܢܶܬܬܢܚܰܚ ܘܢܶܥܒܶܕ݂ ܠܶܗ ܐܶܣܛܰܝܛܝ̈ܘܽܢܳܐ ܘܰܢܨܰܠܶܐ ܒܗܘܽܢ: ܘܢܶܥܒܶܕ݂ ܒܗܘܽܢ ܙܶܕ݂ܩܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܢܨܘܽܡ ܒܗܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܙܳܕ݂ܶܩ ܠܟܺܐܢܶܐ: ܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܕܢܰܕ݂ܪܘܺܝܗ ܠܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܐܰܩܢܳܐܝܺܬ. ܠܰܓ݂ܡܺܝܪܘܽܬܳܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܫܟ݁ܰܚ ܡܳܛܶܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ
7. You see, those good things, which the Evil One suggests, how they become evil. And unless he endures bravely, like Job, he is cast down even from justice, since the righteous inflict evil on no one. For although the righteous man inflicts evil on no one, the Evil One suffocates him with labor and anxiety, and does not allow him to attain the truth; and unless he refreshes himself, by making stations for himself,


[p. 748] {#po.0.p748}


[p. 749] {#po.0.p749}
ܫܰܒܩܳܗ ܠܰܐܪܥܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܦܰܩܕ݁ܶܗ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܘܰܫܩܰܠ ܨܠܺܝܒܳܐ ܘܐܶܣܬ݁ܰܪܰܩ ܘܐܶܬܡܰܟ݁ܰܟ݂ ܘܐܶܬܩܰܕܰܫ:ܘܰܗܘܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܥܰܒܕ݂ܳܐ ܒܟܶܢܫܬܰܡܥܳܢܘܽܬܶܗ: ܘܠܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܡܳܪܳܐ ܒܦܽܘܩܳܕܘܽܬܶܗ: ܘܢܶܪܚܰܡ ܠܚܰܛܳܝ̈ܶܐ ܘܰܠܙܰܕܺܝ̈ܩܶܐ: ܘܢܰܚܶܒ ܕܢܶܬܶܠ ܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܚܠܳܦ ܒܺܝ̈ܫܶܐ: ܐܰܝܟ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܐܰܝܟ ܫܠܺܝܚܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ. ܘܗܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܗ̱ܘ ܡܰܕ݂ܪܶܟ݂ ܪܰܘܡܳܐ ܘܥܘܽܡܩܳܐ ܘܐܘܽܪܟܳܐ ܘܰܦܬܳܝܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܩܰܕܺܝܫ̈ܶܐ: ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܩܰܕܺܝܫܳܐ ܒܟܽܠ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܐܰܕ݂ܪܶܟ݂ܘܽܗ̱ܝ: ܕܰܐܚܘܺܝ ܠܗܘܽܢ: ܒܚܽܘܒܳܐ ܘܒܰܚܢܳܢܳܐ ܘܒܰܫܠܳܡܳܐ ܠܘܳܬ ܟܽܠܢܳܫ: ܛܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܘܒܺܝ̈ܫܶܐ. ܘܥܘܽܡܩܳܐ ܘܐܘܽܪܟܳܐ ܘܰܦܬܳܝܳܐ ܥܰܝܡ ܩܰܕ݂ܝܺܫ̈ܶܐ:
in which he may pray and do alms and fast, as befits the righteous, he cannot solidly attain justice. To perfection, however, he cannot reach, unless he leaves the earth, as God commanded him, and unless he takes up the cross and empties and humbles and sanctifies himself and becomes as a servant by his obedience, not as a master by his command, and loves sinners and righteous and willingly hands over his soul for the bad, as God and as His Apostles; and then he will comprehend the height and depth, length and breadth with those saints, who comprehended the Holy One in all things, which He showed them: in love, charity, peace towards all, good and bad.


[p. 750] {#po.0.p750}
ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܐܰܕܪܟܘܽܗ̱ܝ ܠܩܰܕ݂ܝܺܫܳܐ ܒܟ݁ܽܠܡܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܚܰܘܝܺ ܠܗܘܽܢ: ܒܪܶܚܡܬܳܐ ܘܚܘܰܒܳܐ ܘܰܫܠܳܡܳܐ ܕܰܠܘܳܐ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ: ܛܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܘܒܺܝ̈ܫܶܐ܀ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܗܳܟܝܶܠ ܨܶܢܥ̈ܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܡܶܨܛܰܢܥܳܢ ܒܚܺܫܳܐ ܠܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܕܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܝܺܚ̈ܺܝܕ݂ܳܝܶܐ: ܘܒܳܥܶܝܢ ܕܢܶܫܒܩܘܽܢ ܟܽܠܥܶܒܕ݁ܶܡ ܘܢܶܬܥܰܠܘܽܢ ܠܪܰܘܡܳܐ ܒܥܶܩ̈ܒܳܬܳܐ ܕܗܰܘ ܕܐܶܬܥܰܠܝܽ ܩܕܳܡܰܝܗܘܽܢ. ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܓܝܪ ܕܰܓܒܰܘ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܥܘܽܡܪܳܐ ܕܟܰܐܢܘܬܳܐ ܘܙܘܽܘܳܓ݁ܳܐ: ܗܶܢܘܽܢ ܢܶܥܒܕܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܐܰܪ̈ܥܳܢܳܝܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܙܶܕ̈ܩܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܫܰܦܝܺܪ̈ܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܰܩܢܶܝܢ: ܘܢܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܟܺܐܢܶܝܢ ܒܕ݂ܘܰܒܳܪ̈ܰܝܗܘܽܢ. ܘܐܶܢ ܨܳܒ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܢܶܫܒܩܘܽܢܳܗ ܠܰܐܪܥܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܩܰܝܣܶܝܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܘܢܶܪܕܘܽܢ ܒܥܶܩ̈ܒܳܬܳܐ ܕܡܰܟܺܝܟܘܽܬܶܗ: ܒܓ݁ܰܠ ܣܳܠܩܝܢ ܠܰܓܡܝܺܪܘ̈ܬܳܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕ݁ܠܰܘ ܣܰܓܺܝ ܪܰܚܝܩܺܝܢ ܡܶܢܶܗ. ܓܡܝܺܪ̈ܶܐ ܓܶܝܪ ܐܰܟ ܡܰܠܰܐܟܳܝܶܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕܐܰܝܠܺܝܢ ܕ݁ܰܠܗܳܺܝ ܩܝܳܡܬܳܐ ܫܳܘܶܝܢ: ܠܰܡܡܳܬ ܬܳܢܝܳܐ ܡܶܫܟܚܝܰܢ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܝܟ ܡܰܠܰܐܟ̈ܶܐ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ. ܡܶܟܝܺܠ ܕܰܟܕܰܒܠܰܐܦ݂ܳܝܶܐ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ: ܒܗܘܽܢ ܒܡܰܠܰܐܟ݂ܶܝܶܐ ܙܳܕ݁ܶܩ ܕܢܶܬ݁ܕܰܡܶܐ ܡܢ ܕ݂ܨܳܒܶܐ ܕܢܶܬܓܡܰܪ. ܢܶܚܙܶܐ ܡܳܢܰܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܦܘܽܠܚܳܢܳܐ ܕܡܰܠܰܐܟܳܝܶܐ܆ ܡܰܠܰܐܟܳܝܶܐ ܠܳܐ ܦܳܠܚܺܝܢ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܠܳܐ ܡܰܠܒܫܝܿܢ ܥܰܪܛܶܠܳܝ̈ܶܐ. ܠܳܐ ܡܣܰܒܥܺܝܢ ܟܰܦ݁̈ܢܶܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܡܩܰܘܶܐ ܪܶܥܝܢܗܘܽܢ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܒܶܡܠܬܶܗ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܡܰܪܬܶܝܢ ܠܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܣܳܦܶܩ: ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܕܰܩܕ݁ܰܡܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܐܰܡܝܢܝܢ ܘܰܠܪܰܒܘܽܬܶܗ ܡܫܰܡܫܝܢ: ܘܠܳܐ ܝܺܨܦܝܳܢ ܕܣܰܝܒܳܪܬܗܘܽܢ: ܕܡܳܪ݂ܰܢ ܒܳܕ݂ܶܩ ܕܚܺܝܠܗܘܽܢ ܘܰܕ݂ܟܽܠܢܳܫ. ܙܳܕ݂ܶܩ ܠܗܘܿܢ ܠܰܐܝܠܺܝܢ ܕܐܰܟ ܡܰܠܰܐܟܳܝܶܐ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ: ܕܰܠܗܘܽܢ ܠܡܰܠܰܐܟ݂ܶܐ ܢܶܬܕܰܡܘܽܢ܆ ܘܡܶܠܬ݁ܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܢܰܟܪܙܘܽܢ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܦܰܩܶܕ݂ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ: ܕܠܳܐ ܬܰܐܨܦܘܽܢ ܕܣܰܝܒܳܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܕܰܠܒܘܽܫ̈ܳܐ: ܐܳܦܠܳܐ ܕܢܰܦܫܗܘܽܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܕܐܰܚܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ: ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܝܳܨܶܦ݂ ܕܺܝܠܗܘܽܢ ܘܰܕܟܽܠܢܳܫ: ܘܠܶܗ ܒܛܺܝܠ ܥܰܠ ܒܪܝܺܬܶܗ ܕܰܢܕܰܒܪܳܗ. ܘܰܒܚܰܕ݂ ܟܺܝܳܢܳܐ ܙܿܐܶܢ ܠܰܣܬܺܝܩܶܐ: ܘܗܶܢܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܡܰܠܰܐܟ݁ܶܐ ܗܘܰܘ ܐܰܡܺܝܢܺܝܢ ܩܕ݂ܳܡ ܪܰܒܘܽܬܶܗ. ܘܐܶܠܘܽ ܨܳܒܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܟ݁ܽܠܢܶܫ ܕܢܶܫܬܰܦܰܠ ܠܰܐܪܥܳܐ ܘܢܺܚܬܘܽܢ ܠܰܓ݂ܡܺܝܪܘܳܬܳܐ: ܡܳܪܰܢ ܠܳܐ ܟܳܠܶܐ ܠܗܘܢ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܣܰܝܒܳܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܠܒܘܽܟܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܗܘ ܡܰܡܚܶܝܬ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܡܰܛܢܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܰܚܺܬ ܠܰܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐܺܝܣܪܳܐܝܶܠ
8. These are the deceits, by which the Evil One lies in wait for those who become anchorites and, having left all things, wish to be raised to the height in the footsteps of Him who was exalted before them. For those who have chosen the life of justice and marriage, let them do alms from the earthly things which they possess and good works from those which they possess; and they will be righteous in their conversation. Even if they wish to leave the earth, as God commanded, and proceed in the footsteps of His humility, they quickly ascend to perfection, because they are not far from it. For the perfect are like angels, as God said: Those who are worthy of this resurrection will not be able to die, but will be like angels. Therefore, since they are like angels, it befits him who wishes to be perfected to become like the angels. Let us see, what is the ministry of the angels? Angels do not cultivate the earth, do not clothe the naked, do not satisfy the hungry, nor does their mind remain on the earth, but by the command of God they exhort everyone, as they are capable, so that they may be assiduously in His sight serving His majesty, nor are they anxious for food, because God has care of them and of everyone. It befits those who are like angels to imitate the angels and to announce the word of God, as He commanded them: Do not have care for food and clothing, nor for your soul, nor for your brothers, because God has care of them and of all and He himself is anxious for His creature, so that He may direct it. And through the righteous He preserves the needy, who like angels are assiduous before His majesty. And if all men had wished to leave the earth and tend toward perfection, God would not have kept them for the sake of food and clothing, but would have sent down Manna for them, as He sent to the sons of Israel in the vast desert


[p. 751] {#po.0.p751}


[p. 752] {#po.0.p752}


[p. 753] {#po.0.p753}
ܒܡܰܕ݂ܒ݂ܪܳܐ ܚܰܪܒ݁ܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܙܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܚܨܳܕ݂ܳܐ ܐ݈ܝܺܬ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܒܶܗ. ܘܗܘّ ܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܬܘܽܢܝܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܥܒܰܕ݂ ܠܶܐܕܳܡ ܘܰܠܚܰܘܳܐ ܒܗܰܘ ܝܰܘܡܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܚܛܰܝܘ ܡܶܚܛܳܐ. ܚܰܕ݂ ܟܡܳܐ ܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܠܰܢ ܒܚܰܘܡܳܐ ܕ݁ܡܶܬ݁ܪܰܥܶܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܝܢ ܕܢܶܪܗܰܛ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܓܡܺܝܪܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܢܺܐܙܰܠ ܒܳܬܪܶܗ ܘܢܶܥܒܶܕ݂ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ ܪܰܒܳܐ: ܗܰܘ ܕ݁ܨܳܒܶܐ ܕ݈ܗܳܢܰܢ ܬܶܗܘܶܐ ܒܪܝܺܬܶܗ ܟ݁ܽܠܳܗ ܐܰܝܟ
lacking seed and harvest, and would have made tunics for them, as He made for Adam and Eve on the day that they sinned by sinning. How much more would He have done for us on that day, on which we took counsel, by following perfection to follow Him and to do His great will, by which He wished all His creatures to become like angels in heaven?


[p. 754] {#po.0.p754}
ܡܰܠܰܐܟܝܶܐ ܕܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ܆ ܓܡܺܝܪܘܳܬܳܐ ܓ݁ܺܝܪ ܠܥُܠ ܡܶܢ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ
9. For perfection is above heaven and justice is below on the earth, which stands on the border of evil, from which the righteous
ܕ݁ܩܳܝܡܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܬܚܘܽܡܳܐ ܕܒܺܝܫܬܳܐ: ܘܰܠܫܳܥ
are always beaten, because they are its borders and their neighbors are cursed. Cursed, he says, is the earth because of you;


[p. 755] {#po.0.p755}
ܬܚܘܽܡܳܗ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܘܒܰܪܹܐ ܬܚܘܽܡܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ ܠܺܝ̈ܛܳܐ.
for God said to Adam: "Therefore, because you loved those things which are on the earth, and hated heavenly things, behold they are given to you, provided that you do not fall
ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܳܐܕ݂ܳܡ: ܕܕܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܰܪܚܶܡܬ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ: ܘܰܣܢܰܝܬ ܡܺܕ݂ܶܡ ܕܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ: ܗܳܐ ܝܺܗܝܺܒ ܠܳܟ. ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܫܬ݁ܰܪܓ݁ܰܠ ܬܶܚܘܰܬ ܠܳܟ݂ ܠܬܰܚܬ ܡܶܢ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܘܐܶܚܬܳܐ ܠܰܫܝܘܽܠ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܢܚܶܬܬ ܡܶܢ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܠܰܐܪܥܳܐ. ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܢܦܰܠܬ ܡܶܢ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܩܰܒܶܠܬ݁ܳܟ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܕܡܶܫܟܚܰܬ ܚܳܝܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ݁ ܒܳܗ: ܐܳܦܿܢ ܠܰܓ݂ܡܺܝܪܘܳܬܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܡܳܛܶܐ ܐ݇ܢ̱ܬ: ܡܳܐ ܕܥܳܡܠ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܒ݁ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܦܘܽܪܥܳܬܳܐ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܬܳܐ. ܛܥܶܡܬܳܝܗ̱ܝ ܠܡܰܘܬܳܐ ܡܶܬܛܥܰܡ: ܗܳܫܿܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܢܳܦܶܠ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܡܶܢ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܡܶܣܬ݁ܰܚܦ݁ܰܬ ܒܰܫܝܘܽܠ. ܘܢܳܦܶܠ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܡܶܢ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ. ܘܝܳܪܶܬ݂ ܐܰܢ݈ܬ ܬܰܢܚܽܘܡܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܕܐܶܬܓ݁ܠܶܙܬ݂ ܡܶܢ ܐܝܺܠܳܢܳܐ ܛܳܒܳܐ ܕܚܰܝ̈ܶܐ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܰܛܥܶܡܬ ܡܰܚܫܰܒܬ݁ܳܐ ܒܺܝܫܬܐ: ܘܝܺܕܰܥܬ ܒܺܝܫܬ݁ܳܐ: ܘܰܢܦܰܠܬ ܡܶܢ ܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܠܰܐܪܥܳܐ. ܐܶܢ ܕܝܢ ܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܡܶܥܒ݁ܰܕ݂ ܒܺܝܫܬܳܐ: ܡܶܢ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܠܰܫܝܘܽܠ ܢܳܦܶܠ ܐܢ̱ܬ܀
beneath the earth and descend into Hades, as you descended from heaven to earth. For when you had fallen from heaven, the earth received you, in which you will be able to live, even if you do not reach perfection, while in this first fall you apply yourself to labor. By tasting you tasted death: now, if you fall from the earth, you will be cast into Hades and you will fall from justice and you will inherit torments, just as you were deprived of the good tree of life, because you tasted an evil thought and by knowing evil you fell from heaven to earth. If, however, by perpetrating you perpetrate evil, you will fall from the earth into Hades."


[p. 756] {#po.0.p756}
ܫܠܶܡ ܡܐܡܪܳܐ ܕܟܗ܀
The twenty-fifth discourse ends.


[p. 757] {#po.0.p757}
ܟܘ ܡܺܐܡܪܶܐ ܕܥܳܣܪܝܰܢ ܘܶܫܬܿܐ ܥܰܠ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ
TWENTY-SIXTH DISCOURSE ON THE SECOND LAW WHICH THE LORD IMPOSED UPON ADAM
ܐ ܕܰܬ݁ܪܶܝܢ ܕܣܳܡ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܠܐܕܳܡ ܀ ܀ ܀ ܥܰܠ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܕܣܳܡ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܠܐܕܳܡ ܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܕܐܶܟ݂ܰܠ ܡܶܢ ܐܺܝܠܳܢܳܐ ܡܶܟܺܝܠ ܗܳܐ ܣܳܐܶܡ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ ܠܳܟ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܒܗܳܢܳܐ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܰܪܚܶܡܬ ܕܗܳܢܳܐ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܕܣܳܐܶܡ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܠܳܟ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܬܰܥܒܪܝܽܘܗ̱ܝ ܢܶܒܠܺܝܟ ܡܶܢ ܫܝܘܽܠ ܘܢܶܬ݁ܶܠ ܠܳܟ ܚܰܝ̈ܶܝܐ ܕ݁ܰܠܥܳܠܰܡ ܘܚܘܽܪܬܳܢܐ ܘܢܶܚܡܬܳܐ. ܘܐܶܢ ܬܰܡܪܰܚ ܥܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܥܰܠ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܳܐ ܬܶܚܙܶܝܗ ܠܰܫܝܘܽܠ ܘܐܶܫܬܰܢܰܩ. ܐܶܢ ܬܶܛܰܪ ܗܳܟܝܶܠ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܕܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܬܶܪܗܰܛ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܚܘܽܒܿܳܐ ܘܒܳܬܰܪ ܓܡܺܝܪܘܳܬܳܐ: ܠܚܰܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܦܢܳܝܳܐ ܕܗܳܢܳܐ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܡܶܬܓ݂ܠܶܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܘܓ݂ܳܡܰܪ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ ܠܳܟ ܘܰܠܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܕܙܳܗܛܝܺܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܚܘܽܒܳܐ ܘܒܳܬܰܪ ܓܡܺܝܪܘܽܬܳܐ. ܘܥܳܐܠܺܝܢ ܐ݇ܢܸܬܘܽܢ ܠܦܰܪܕ݁ܰܝܣܳܐ ܪܘܽܚܳܢܳܐ ܕܰܢܦܰܩܬ ܡܶܢܶܗ. ܘܰܡܚܰܘܶܐ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ ܠܟ݁ܽܠ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܚܳܐܶܝܢ ܒܡܶܐܬܝܺܬܝ ܘܒܳܬ݂ܰܪ ܡܶܐܬܝܺܬܝ: ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܒܪܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܰܝܬ ܐܰܝܟ ܡܰܠܰܐܟ̈ܶܐ: ܘܐܰܝܟ݂ܰܢ ܢܺܐܬܘܽܢ ܠܗܳܝ ܒܪܝܺܬ݁ܳܐ ܩܰܕ݁ܺܝܫܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܰܒ݁ܪܶܐ ܗ̱ܘܰܝܬ. ܘܐܶܢܳܐ ܐܶܠܒܰܫ ܕܡܘܽܬܳܟ݂ ܘܐܰܚܰܘܶܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ܂ ܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܥܳܢܶܕ݂ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ: ܛܳܥܶܝܢ ܠܳܗ ܝܰܠܺܕ݂ܰܝܟ݂ ܠܰܒܪܝܺܬܳܟ݂ ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܗܘܳܐ ܘܡܰܢܘܰܐܝܺܠܳܢܳܐ ܕܐܶܟܰܠܬ ܡܶܢܶܗ: ܘܰܠܟܽܠ ܨܒܘܽܢ ܢܕܰܡܘܳܢܳܗ ܠܰܒܪܝܳܬܳܟ݂ ܐܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܘܠܰܐܝܠܳܢܳܐ ܕܐܶܟܰܠܬ ܡܶܢܶܝܗ: ܘܠܳܐ ܢܶܕܥܘܽܢ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܚܰܕ݂ܚܕ݁ܳܢܝܺܢ: ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܐܺܬܶܐ ܘܐܰܚܰܘܶܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܓܰܠܝܳܐܝܺܬ ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܐܺܝܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܝ ܡܶܢ ܒܪܝܳܬܳܐ. ܐܶܬܛܥܘܽܢ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܝܰܠܺܕ݂ܰܝܟ ܘܢܶܦܠܘܽܢ ܐܳܦ ܡܶܢ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܰܡܦܰܩܶܕ݂ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܠܳܟ ܝܰܘܡܳܢܳܐ܀
1. Concerning the law which the Lord imposed upon Adam after he had eaten from the tree. — Therefore, behold, I set a law for you concerning that very thing which you have loved, which law, once I have set it for you—unless you shall have transgressed it—will keep you from Hades and will give you eternal life, an inheritance, and resurrection. And if you act boldly against it, just as you did against the first, you will see Hades and be tormented. If, therefore, you keep this law of justice and have pursued charity and perfection, at the end of the years of this world I will appear and will perfect you and all who have pursued charity and perfection, and you will enter into the spiritual paradise from which you went out. And to all who live at my coming and after my coming, I will show how you were created in the likeness of the angels and how they may arrive at that holy creature in which you were created. And I will put on your likeness and show them everything. For after you have departed from this age, your progeny will forget your creature, what it was like and what the tree was from which you ate, and they will liken your creature to all things, as to what it was, and the tree from which you ate; nor will they know, except for certain individuals, until I come and show them manifestly what my will was from the beginning. For your offspring will wander and will fall even from the justice which I command you today.


[p. 758] {#po.0.p758}


[p. 759] {#po.0.p759}


[p. 760] {#po.0.p760}
ܘܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܳܐܕܳܡ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܣܳܡ ܠܶܗ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܝܳܐ: ܒܗܰܘ ܝܰܘܡܳܐ ܕܰܥܒܰܪ ܥܰܠ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܳܐ. ܗܳܐ ܩܶܢܝܳܢܳܐ ܕܰܪܚܶܡܬ ܘܠܳܐ ܐܶܬܒܰܚܰܢܬ݁ ܒܐܝܺܩܳܪܳܟ. ܩܢܝܳܐ ܟܡܳܐ ܕܰܒܥܰܝܬ: ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܟܺܐܢܳܐܝܺܬ ܬܶܗܠܶܟ. ܘܗܳܐ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܕܰܪܚܶܡܬ ܝܺܗܝܰܒܳܐ ܠܳܟ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܣܰܒ ܕܚܰܒܪܳܟ. ܗܳܐ ܥܰܡܠܳܐ ܕܰܒܥܰܝܬ ܝܺܗܝܺܒ ܠܳܟ݂ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܥܰܠ ܥܰܡܠܳܐ ܕܚܰܒܪܳܟ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܬܝܰܥܰܢ. ܗܳܐ ܙܘܰܘܳܓ݁ܳܐ ܕܰܒܥܰܝܬ ܒܢܶܡܠܟܶܗ ܕܒܺܝܫܳܐ ܝܺܗܝܺܒ ܠܳܟ: ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܰܬ݂ ܚܰܒܪܳܟ݂ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܪܰܓ ܘܠܳܐ ܬܶܣܰܒ ܬ݁ܰܪܬ݁ܶܝܢ ܢܶܫܝ̈ܰܢ: ܘܠܳܐ ܢܶܙܢܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܟ ܘܠܳܐ ܒܢܳܬܳܟ݂ ܢܶܗܘ̈ܝܺܢ
2. And God said to Adam, when He imposed upon him the final law, on the day he transgressed the first: Behold the riches which you loved and did not understand your honor. Possess whatever you wish, provided that you walk justly. And behold the earth, which you loved, is given to you, provided that you do not take the property of your neighbor. Behold the labor which you sought is given to you, provided that you do not greedily desire the labor of your neighbor. Behold the marriage which you sought by the counsel of the evil one is given to you, provided that you do not covet the wife of your neighbor, nor take two wives, nor do your sons commit fornication,


[p. 761] {#po.0.p761}
ܙܳܢܝ̈ܳܬܳܐ. ܘܦܰܩܶܕ݂ ܠܰܒܢܰܝ̈ܟ ܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܪܳܟ: ܘܰܒܢܰܝ̈ܟ ܢܶܦܩܕܘܽܢ ܠܰܒܢܰܝ̈ܗܘܽܢ ܥܰܕ݂ ܐܳܬܶܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܘܗܳܘܶܐ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ ܠܟܘܿܢ ܚܰܘܪܳܐ ܕܰܓܡܝܳܪܘܽܬܳܐ܀
nor do your daughters become harlots. And command your sons after you, and your sons will set the precept for their sons, until I come, and I will show myself to you as an example of perfection.
ܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܡܳܐ ܕܩܳܢܶܝܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ: ܠܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕ݁ܰܠܥܳܠܰܡ ܐܶܩܢܘܽܢ ܘܐܶܛܥܘܽܢܳܢܝ. ܘܡܳܐ ܕܒܳܢܶܝܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܕܝܳܕ݂ܥܝܺܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܕܠܰܘ ܠܥܳܠܰܡ ܗܳܪܟܳܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܘܢ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܗܘܰܝܬܘܽܢ ܝܳܕ݂ܥܝܺܢ ܕܡܰܥܒܰܪ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܠܳܗ ܠܰܐܪܥܳܐ ܘܰܠܟ݁ܽܠ ܕܐܝܺܬ ܒܳܗ̇. ܘܕ݂ܝܺܢܳܐ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܘܰܢܝܳܚܬ݁ܳܐ ܗܳܘܝܳܐ. ܘܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܐܰܝܟ ܥܒܳܕܼܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܡܶܬܦܪܰܥ. ܟܰܕܘ ܠܟܘܢ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܘܚܰܘܳܐ ܕܰܢܦܠܬܘܿܢ ܡܶܢ ܒܬܘܽܠܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܡܶܢ ܓܡܝܺܪܘܬܳܐ. ܠܳܐ ܬܘܰܒ ܬܶܦܠܘܽܢ ܠܟܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܬܪܝܰܨܘܺܬܳܐ ܘܡܶܢ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ. ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܕܐܝܺܬ ܣܰܩܘܰܒܠܳܐ ܠܰܓ݂ܡܝܺܪܘܽܬܳܐ: ܟ݁ܽܠܶܗ ܫܘܦ݂ܪܳܐ ܕܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܕܡܶܬܚܙܶܐ ܠܥܰܝ̈ܢܶܐ
3. And He said to them: When you possess, do not possess as if for eternity, forgetting me. And when you build, do so as men who know that you are not to remain here forever. But know that I will cause the earth to pass away and everything in it. And there will be judgment and there will be rest, and each one will receive retribution according to his works. It is enough for you, Adam and Eve, to have fallen from virginity and perfection: do not fall further from uprightness and justice. For just as the entire beauty of the earth visible to the eyes of the flesh is opposed to perfection, so is every evil harmful or saddening to man opposed to justice, and to everything that has a soul.


[p. 762] {#po.0.p762}
ܕܒܶܣܪܳܐ: ܗܳܟ݁ܰܢܳܐ ܐܝܺܬ ܣܰܩܘܽܒܠܳܐ ܠܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܟܽܠ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܒܺܝܫ ܘܢܳܟܶܐ ܠܒܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܡܠܰܚܶܩ ܠܰܐܝܕ݂ܳܐ ܕܐܝܺܬ ܒܳܗ̇ ܢܰܦܫܳܐ܀ ܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܗܳܟܝܶܠ ܦܘܽܩܕ݁ܳܢܳܐ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܳܐ ܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ ܘܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܟܺܐܢܶܐ ܩܰܕ̈ܡܳܝܶܐ ܐܰܩܺܝܡܘ ܥܰܠ ܗܳܝ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܕ݂ܰܦܩܰܕ݂ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܳܐܕܳܡ: ܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܕܰܥܒܰܪ ܥܰܠ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܰܗܘܳܐ ܐܰܪܥܳܢܳܐ. ܫܰܪܟ݁ܳܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܰܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ: ܐܶܠܘܽ ܩܰܘܝܽܘ ܒܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܰܟܬܝܰܒܳܐܝܬ ܕܐܳܕܳܡ ܘܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ ܪܕܰܘ ܒܳܗ̇: ܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܝܰܗܶܒ݂ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܢܳܐ: ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܐܳܬܶܐ ܡܳܪܳܐ ܘܝܳܗܶܒ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܣܒܰܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܝܰܘܡܳܢ ܗܳܟܳܐ. ܐܶܡܰܪ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܦܰܘܠܳܐ: ܕܢܳܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܡܰܣܛܝܳܢܘܽܬ݁ܳܐ ܐܶܬܬܰܘܣܰܦ: ܗܳܢܳܐ ܕܰܒܝܰܕ݂ ܡܘܽܫܶܐ ܐܶܬܝܳܗܶܒ. ܣܰܒܪܘ ܠܶܗ ܗܳܟܝܶܠ ܠܗܳܢܳܐ ܫܰܝܢܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܒ݂ܝܰܕ݂ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܐܳܕ݁ܳܡ܂ ܘܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܟ݁ܺܐܢܶܐ ܘܰܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ ܘܙܰܕ݁ܺܝ̈ܩܶܐ: ܘܰܕܡܶܟܝܘ ܥܰܠ ܗܳܢܳܐ ܣܰܒܪܳܐ: ܕܐܳܬܶܐ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܥܳܒܶܕ݂ ܫܰܝܢܳܐ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܘܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܩܪܶܒ ܙܰܒ݂ܢܳܐ ܗܰܘ ܕܰܨܒܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܒܶܗ ܢܶܬ݂ܓ݁ܠܶܐ ܘܢܶܥܒܶܕ݂ ܬܰܪܥܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܫܰܝܢܳܐ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ: ܒܥܳܬ ܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܚܠܳܦ ܟ݁ܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐ݈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܛܳܒ̈ܶܐ ܘܒܺܝܫ̈ܶܐ ܘܐܶܡܪܰܬ ܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ: ܥܶܗܰܕ݂ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܳܟ݂ ܠܥܰܒܕ݂ܳܟ ܗܳܝ ܕܐܰܬܟܠܰܬ ܠܳܐܕ݁ܳܡ܂ ܘܰܠܟ݁ܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܟܺܐܢ̈ܶܐ: ܘܒܳܗ̇ ܐܶܬܒܰܝܐܝܘ
4. Therefore, after the first commandment, Adam and all the ancient just ones stood in the justice which God commanded Adam after he had become earthly, having transgressed the first word. But to other men, if they had persevered in that prescribed justice in which Adam and the just walked, no other law would have been given until the Lord had come, giving that Gospel which He has now given. For the Apostle said: The law was added because of transgression, given through Moses. Therefore, Adam and all the just and the prophets and the upright, awaiting the peace [made] by the Lord, slept relying on that hope, that the Lord was to come and to make peace on earth. And when the time had approached in which God willed to appear and to make reconciliation and peace on earth, the Spirit, imploring for all men, good and evil, said thus: Be mindful of your word to your servant, which gave hope to Adam and to all the just and by which they were comforted in their humility, because your word gave them life. And He came, whose promise is truthful and whose covenant is faithful, and He perfected those who, having left all things, did His will, and pursuing charity and perfection before His coming, they fell asleep, and He introduced them into the spiritual paradise, as He had promised, and to the latest ones He manifestly showed what Adam had once been. And he was taken up from them into the promised paradise, so that they, having left the earth, might follow Him.


[p. 763] {#po.0.p763}
ܒܡܘܽܟܳܟܗܘܽܢ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܡܺܐܡܪܳܐ ܐܰܝ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܘܐܶܬܳܐ ܗܰܘ ܕܫܰܪܝܳܪ ܫܘܽܘܪܳܝܳܗ ܘܡܘܽܠܟܳܢܶܗ ܡܗܰܝܡܢ ܘܓܰܡܰܪ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܠܰܐܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܰܫܒܰܩܝܘ ܟܽܠܥܶܡܕܶܡ ܘܰܥܒܰܕܘ ܨܶܒܝܳܢܶܗ ܘܰܪܗܶܛܝܘ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܚܘܽܒܳܐ ܘܒܳܬܰܪ ܓܡܝܪܘܽܬܳܐ. ܘܰܫܟܶܒܘ ܩܕܳܡ ܡܶܐܬܝܺܬܶܗ: ܘܐܰܥܶܠ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܠܦܰܪܕܰܝܣܳܐ ܪܘܽܚܳܢܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܫܬܰܘܕܝ: ܘܚܰܘܝܺ ܠܰܐܚܪܳܝܶܐ ܓܰܠܝܳܐܝܺܬ: ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܗܘܳܐ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܡܶܢ ܩܕܳܡ. ܘܰܡܠܰܟ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܦܰܪܕܰܝܣܳܐ ܘܐܶܬܥܰܠܝ ܡܶܢ ܠܘܳܬܗܘܽܢ: ܕܗܶܢܘܽܢ ܢܶܫܒܩܘܽܢ ܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܘܢܺܐܙܠ̱ܘܽܢ ܒܳܬܪܶܗ܀ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܣܒܰܪܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܝܰܗ̱ܒ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ: ܗܝܺ ܗ̱ܝ ܕ݁ܰܥܠܶܝܗ ܥܒܰܪ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܘܰܢܦܰܠ. ܘܗܳܝ ܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܝܰܗ̱ܒ ܘܡܘܽܫܶܐ ܘܰܢܒܺܝ̈ܶܐ ܗܝܺ ܗ̱ܝ ܕܐܶܬܬܣܺܝܡܰܬ ܥܰܠ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܡܶܢ ܒܳܬܰܪ ܕܰܥܒܰܪ ܥܰܠ ܦܘܽܩܕ݂ܳܢܳܐ
5. But the Gospel which Jesus gave is that which Adam transgressed and fell from; and the justice which Moses and the Prophets gave is that which was imposed upon Adam after he had transgressed the first


[p. 764] {#po.0.p764}


[p. 765] {#po.0.p765}
ܩܰܕܡܳܝܐ. ܘܰܗܘܳܐ ܢܶܡܘܽܣܳܐ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܳܝܳܐ ܘܰܐܚܪܳܝܳܐ ܩܰܕܡܳܝܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕ݁ܰܗܘܰܘ ܐ̱ܚܪ̈ܳܝܶܐ ܩܰܕ̈ܡܳܝܶܐ ܘܩܰܕ̈ܡܳܝܶܐ ܐ̱ܚܪ̈ܳܝܶܐ. ܡܢ ܕܰܓܡܝܪܘܽܬܳܐ ܕ̈ܝܢ ܒܳܥܶܐ ܘܩܰܕ݂ܝܺܫܘܽܬܳܐ ܪܳܚܶܡ: ܒܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܗܳܘܝܳܐ ܩܰܕ݂ܝܺܫܘܽܬܳܐ ܕܠܶܒܳܐ: ܝܳܗܶܒ ܠܶܗ ܟܠ ܕܐܝܺܬ ܠܶܗ ܠܰܣܢܺܝܩܶܐ ܘܡܶܬܥܰܠܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܡܶܢ ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܡܶܬܚܙܶܐ: ܘܗܳܘܶܐ ܥܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܚܶܪܝܳܢܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܕܳܐܢ ܠܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܘܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܳܒ݁ܰܥ ܠܐ̱ܢܳܫ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܡܰܚܶܒ ܠܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܐܝܟ ܩܰܕ݂ܝܺܫܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܡܰܕ݁ܢܰܚ ܚܘܽܒܶܗ ܠܘܳܬ ܟ݁ܽܠܢܳܫ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܫܶܡܫܶܗ ܕܐܰܒܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܟܽܠ
commandment: and the first law became the last and the last the first, just as the last became first and the first last. But he who seeks perfection and loves holiness, the holiness of the heart consists in these things: let him give all that he has to the needy and lift himself above visible things and, having made contention for himself, let him judge no one, nor seek penalties from anyone, but love all, as a holy one of the Lord, since He makes His charity rise over all men, just as the Father makes His sun rise over all who are on the earth, over the good and the bad and over the just and the unjust.


[p. 766] {#po.0.p766}
ܕܐܝܺܬ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܛܳܒ݂ܶܐ ܘܥܰܠ ܒܺܝ̈ܫܶܐ ܘܥܰܠ ܟܺܐ̱ܢ̈ܶܐ ܘܥܰܠ ܥܰܘܳܠܶܐ܀ ܠܳܡ܂ ܡܐ݈ܡܪܳܐ ܕܟܘ܀
The twenty-sixth discourse ends.

### TWENTY-SEVENTH DISCOURSE CONCERNING THE HOSTS
ܡܺܐܡܙܳܐ ܕܟܙ܀ ܡܺܐܡܙܳܐ ܕܟܙ ܘܫܰܒܥܳܐ ܕܥܰܠ ܫܰܪܒܳܐ ܕܓ݂ܰܝ̈ܣܶܐ
ܟ݁ܽܠ ܐܰܝܠܶܝܢ ܕܚܳܙܶܐ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܥܰܡܠܗܘܽܢ ܕܡܶܬܕܰܡܶܝܢ ܒܚܰܫ̈ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܡܫܰܕܰܪ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܡܰܢ ܕܰܡܚܰܘܶܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܐܘܽܪܚܳܐ ܕܩܘܽܫܬܳܐ. ܘܐܶܢ ܚܳܝܪܝܺܢ ܒܚܰܫܰܘܗ̱ܝ̈ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܒܳܠܥܝܺܝܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܒ݁ܠܰܥ ܘܰܡܨܰܠܶܝܢ ܥܰܠ ܡܰܢ ܕܡܳܚܶܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܨܰܠܝܺ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܥܰܠ ܡܰܢ ܕܰܡܚܳܝܗ̱ܝ: ܘܥܰܠ ܡܰܢ ܕ݁ܰܩܪܳܝܗ̱ܝ ܚܰܪܳܫܳܐ ܘܒܰܪ ܓܰܘܪ̈ܶܐ ܘܡܰܛܥܶܐ ܥܰܡܳܐ: ܐܶܢ ܝܺܗܒܝܺܢ ܫܠܳܡܳܐ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܡܰܫܠܶܡ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܠܡܰܘܬܳܐ ܘܰܡܫܺܝܓܝܺܢ ܠܶܗ ܪܶܓ݂ܠܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܥܒܰܕ݂ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܠܰܣܟܰܪܝܘܽܛܳܐ. ܐܶܢ ܥܳܒܕܝܺܢ ܗܳܟܰܢ ܘܡܶܬ݁ܕܰܡܶܝܢ ܒܚܰܫܰܘܗ̱ܝ: ܗܘܽ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܡܰܠܦܳܢܳܐ. ܘܰܡܚܰܘܶܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܐܘܽܪܚܶܗ
1. To all whose labor God sees, who imitate His passion, He sends someone to show them the way of truth. And if, contemplating the passion of the Lord, they are scourged, just as He himself was scourged, and they pray for the one striking them, just as the Lord prayed for him who struck Him, and for him who called Him a poisoner and a son of adultery and a seducer of the people, if they greet him who delivers them to death and wash his feet, just as the Lord did to Iscariot: if they do so, imitating His passion: the Lord Himself becomes their teacher and shows them His way and His door,


[p. 767] {#po.0.p767}


[p. 768] {#po.0.p768}


[p. 769] {#po.0.p769}
ܘܬܰܪܥܶܗ: ܘܗܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܓ݁ܰܒܪ̈ܶܐ ܘܐܳܙܠܝܺܢ: ܗܳܘܶܝܢ ܠܶܗ ܠܚܰܝܠܰܘܳܬ݂ ܟܳܪ̈ܘܽܙܳܐ ܘܡܰܠܦܳܢܶܐ ܠܘܳܬ
and then they become men and, going forth, will be preachers of Jesus and teachers among all men.
ܟܽܠܢܳܫ܀ ܡܳܐ ܕܰܚܙܰܠ ܕ݁ܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܢ ܫܪܳܪܳܐ ܘܚܘܽܒܳܐ ܘܡܰܟܝܺܟܘܽܬܳܐ: ܗܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܙܳܕ݂ܶܩ ܠܰܢ ܕܢܺܐܙܰܠ ܡܶܢ ܡܕܺܝܢ̱ܬܰܢ ܠܰܐܬ݂ܪܳܐ ܐ̱ܚܪܺܢܳܐ. ܐܶܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܳܐ ܡܶܬܚܰܣܠܝܺܢ ܡܶܢ ܚܰܠܒܳܐ ܘܗܳܟܰܢ ܢܳܦܩܝܺܢ ܡܶܢ ܡܕܺܝܢ̱ܬܗܘܽܢ: ܐܳܙܠܝܺܢ ܡܶܣܬ݁ܰܢܩܝܺܢ ܥܰܠ ܡܪܰܒܝܳܢܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܢܘܽܟܪܳܝܬܳܐ. ܘܰܟܒܰܪ ܠܳܐ ܡܪܰܒܝܳܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܬܰܩܢܳܐܝܺܬ. ܘܰܟܒܰܪ ܠܳܐ ܫܳܠܡܳܐ ܠܥܺܕ݂ܬܳܐ: ܘܥܳܒܕ݂ܳܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܕ݁ܶܚ̈ܠܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܡܶܢ ܟܳܦܘܽܪ̈ܶܐ: ܘܗܿܢܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܫܰܒܪ̈ܶܐ ܡܶܬܕܰܒܪܝܺܢ: ܘܛܳܥܶܝܢ ܘܡܺܝܬܝܺܢ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܠܳܐ ܝܳܕܥܝܺܢ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܟܡܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܛܠܶܝܢ ܒܰܡܕܺܝܢ̱ܬܗܘܽܢ ܢܶܗܘܘܽܢ: ܐܰܘ ܓܰܒܪܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܬܳܐ: ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܡܶܬܬܰܟܠܝܺܢ ܥܰܠ ܢܰܦܫܗܘܽܢ ܕܐܳܙܠ݈ܝܢ ܘܐܳܬܶܝܢ: ܕܠܳܐ ܢܺܐܙܠ̱ܘܽܢ ܘܢܺܐܒܕܘܽܢ ܠܗܘܽܢ. ܐܝܺܬ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܡܪܰܒܝܳܢܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܛܳܒܬܳܐ: ܕܰܡܪܰܒܝܳܐ ܛܳܒ ܡܶܢ ܐܶܡܳܝܐ. ܘܐܝܺܬ ܡܪܰܒܝܳܢܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܒܝܺܫܬܳܐ ܕܐܰܘ ܥܒܰܕ݂ܬܶܗ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܥܰܒܕ݂ܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܚܛܺܝܬܳܐ: ܐܰܘ ܥܒܰܕ݂ܬܶܗ ܥܰܒܕ݂ܳܐ ܠܰܒܢܰܝܗܿ. ܐܳܦ݂ܠܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܝܳܠܦܝܺܢܰܢ: ܕܰܟܡܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܛܠܺܝܢ ܒܺܝܢܰܝܗܘܽܢ ܠܳܐ ܫܳܒܩܝܺܢ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܕܢܺܐܙܠ̱ܘܽܢ ܒܐܘܰܪܚܳܐ: ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܐܰܫܠܶܡܘ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܠܡܰܢ ܕܰܡܩܰܒ݁ܶܠ ܠܗܘܢ ܘܡܰܝܬ݁ܶܐ ܠܗܘܽܢ܆ ܘܡܳܐ ܕܰܗܘܰܘ ܓܰܒܝܪ̈ܶܐ ܗܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܶܬܬ݁ܰܟ݁ܰܠܝܺܢ ܥܠܰܝܗܘܽܢ: ܘܰܡܫܰܕܪܝܺܢ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕܰܝܗܘܽܢ: ܘܐܳܙܠ݈ܝܢ ܘܐܳܬ݂ܶܝܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܐܳܒܕܝܺܢ܀
2. Therefore, having known the truth and charity and humility, it behooves us to go from our city to another place. But if they are not weaned and thus go out from their city: going forth, they need a foreign nurse. And [she] perhaps will not educate them soundly. Perhaps she is not in conformity with the Church and renders them sectarians or infidels, and they, as little children, are seduced and wander and, being ignorant, they die. Nevertheless, while they are little children, let them remain in their native city, whether they be men or women, until they can trust in themselves and go and return, lest they perish while going out. For there is a good nurse who educates better than a mother, and there is a bad nurse who makes a man either a slave of sin or a slave of her children. Do we not learn even from the world, which, while children are small, does not allow them to go on the road unless it has handed them over to someone who will receive them and lead them? And after they have become men, then they trust them and let them go alone, and they go and return and do not perish.


[p. 770] {#po.0.p770}
ܘܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܒܪܺܝ ܐܳܡܰܪ ܠܳܟ: ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܓ݁ܰܒܪܳܐ ܘܩܰܝܡܶܬ ܠܢܰܦܫܳܟ: ܘܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܘܐܳܙܶܠ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܘܐܳܬ݂ܶܐ ܐ݇ܢ̱ܬ: ܘܠܳܐ ܢܳܦܶܠ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܬܰܪܡܘܽܛܳܐ ܥܰܠ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ: ܟܶܢ ܬܶܥܘܽܠ ܘܬܶܦܘܽܩ ܒܐܘܰܪܚܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ. ܕܠܳܐ ܡܳܐ ܕܰܢܦܰܩܬ ܡܶܢ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ: ܢܶܓܢܒܳܟ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܘܢܶܥܒܕ݂ܳܟ ܥܰܒܕ݂ܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܚܛܺܝܬܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܕܰܒܢܰ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ. ܐܶܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܒܺܝ̈ܫܶܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܐܰܒܳܗܰܝ̈ܟ݂ ܘܰܩܫܰܝ̈ܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܐܰܒܳܗܰܝ̈ܗܶܝܢ ܕܐܶܩܠܳܐ܆ ܐܰܟܘܳܬܳܗ ܕܬܶܩܠܳܐ ܥܒܶܕ݂ ܕ݁ܰܡܚܰܐܘܽܗܿ ܘܐܶܫܬ݁ܰܢܰܕ݂ܘ ܒܳܗܿ ܘܐܰܪܡܝܽܘܗܿ ܒܢܘܽܪܳܐ: ܘܠܳܐ ܡܨܰܥܰܪܬ ܥܰܪ̈ܝܳܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ: ܘܠܳܐ ܨܶܒ݂ܝܳܢܳܐ ܒܝ̈ܫܳܝܐ ܕܡܰܠܦ݁ܺܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܠܳܗܿ ܥܶܒܕ݂ܰܬ. ܝܰܘܡܳܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܝܳܬܶܒ݂ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܘܰܡܟܰܘܶܢ ܠܰܢ ܘܐܳܡܪܝܺܢ: ܗܳܟܳܐ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܟܪܝܺܣܛܝܳܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܢܰܦܶܩ ܒܪܰܢ ܐܰܘ ܒܪܰܬܰܢ: ܕܡܳܐ ܕܐܶܡܰܪܢ ܠܗܘܢ ܐܳܦܶܢ ܕ݁ܐܰܘ ܠܥܶܣܘ ܨܰܠܝܽܘܗܝ: ܘܥܰܠ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܚܕ݂ܳܐ ܩܫܺܝܬܳܐ ܕܐܳܡܪܝܺܢܰܢ ܠܗܘܿܢ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܐܰܒܳܗܳܬܳܐ: ܕܢܶܝܒܣܽܘܗܝ ܐܶܢ ܐܺܝܬ ܒܗܘܢ ܡܣܰܝܒܪܳܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܝܽܘܒܠܳܢ ܠܰܢ ܠܶܝܣܝܪܳܐ ܦܶܬ݂ܓ݁ܳܡ̈ܺܝܢ ܒܺܝ̈ܫܺܝܢ. ܘܕܰܠܡܳܐ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܰܒ݂ܢܰܝ̈ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܚܢܰܢ ܠܳܐ ܝܳܕܥܺܝܢܰܢ ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܐܰܠܶܦ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܠܬ݁ܰܠܺܝ̈ܡܺܝܕ݁ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܡܰܟ݂ܝܺܟ݁ܽܘܬ݂ܳܐ ܘܰܒܝܺܗܺܝܠܘܽܬܳܐ܆ ܘܐܳܡܪܝܺܢ ܕܚܳܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܝܢ ܕܢܶܦܠܚܽܘܢ ܢܬܰܪܣܶܐ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܰܒܛܰܠܝܘܽܬܗܘܽܢ: ܘܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂ ܦܺܐܪܶܐ ܕ݁ܰܓ݂ܡܝܪܘܽܬܳܐ ܢܶܬܚܙܘܽܢ ܘܰܢܗܘܽܘܢ ܒܗܘܿܢ. ܚܙܰܝܬ ܕܥܰܠ ܩܰܫܝܘܽܬ݂ܰܢ ܪܳܛܢܝܢ ܐܰܒܳܗܰܝ̈ܢ ܘܠܰܘ ܥܰܠ ܡܰܟܝܺܟ݁ܘܽܬܰܢ܂ ܘܡܳܐ ܕܛܳܒ ܩܫܶܝܢ ܐܰܒܳܗܰܝ̈ܟ݂ ܘܒܺܝ̈ܫܺܝܢ: ܚܰܘܳܐ
3. And to you, my son, I say: until you are a man and have raised yourself and known and gone and returned, and are not sluggish to fall upon another: then enter and go out on the way of the Lord, lest someone steal you, after you have gone out from the world, and make you a slave of sin or of men. But if your parents are wicked and harsh, like the parents of Thecla, do as Thecla, whom they struck and tortured and threw into the fire, and she did not reproach them by reproaching, nor did she do the evil will which they were teaching her. But today the world, sitting, corrects us and it is said: "We will now cast out our son or daughter because of Christianity; for if we say to them even 'go, eat,' they afflict us with insults, and for a single harsh word, which we say to them as parents to test whether they have patience, they return ten evil words to us. And perhaps, because we [are] children of the world, we do not know how Jesus taught his disciples humility and modesty?" And they say: "We would gladly labor to nourish them as in the time of their infancy, provided that the fruits of perfection had appeared in them." You see our parents murmuring because of our hardness, not because of our humility. And the harsher and worse your parents are, show


[p. 771] {#po.0.p771}


[p. 772] {#po.0.p772}


[p. 773] {#po.0.p773}
ܠܗܘܢ ܕܰܟܝܺܟ݁ܘܽܬܳܟ ܫܰܢ̱ܬ݁ܳܐ ܐܰܘ ܝܰܪܚܳܐ. ܐܰܘ ܐܳܦܶܢ ܥܶܣܪܳܐ ܝܰܘ̈ܡܺܝܢ: ܘܟܶܢ ܬܶܦܘܽܩ. ܣܳܒ݂ܰܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܳܡ ܕ݁ܡܳܐ ܕܰܢܦܰܩܬ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܠܳܐ ܡܰܟܝܺܟ݂ ܐܢܬ ܙܟ݂ܰܝܬ݁ܳܗ ܠܒܺܝܫܬܳܐ& ܗܰܘ ܗ̱ܘܰ ܥܶܕ݂ܳܢܳܐ ܣܳܓ݁ܝܳܢ ܩܪ̈ܳܒܰܝܟ ܡܳܐ ܕܰܢܦܰܩܬ ܡܶܢ ܠܘܳܬ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܰܝ̈ܟ. ܘܐܶܢ ܡܰܟܝܺܟ݁ܘܽܬܳܐ ܠܝܬ ܒܳܟ ܡܚܰܒܠܳܐ ܠܳܟ ܚܛܺܝܬܳܐ. ܐܶܢ ܣܳܐܶܡ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܒܪܶܥܝܳܢܳܟ ܕ݁ܰܡܣܰܝܒܰܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܟ݁ܽܠ ܕ݁ܐܳܬܶܐ ܒܠܰܚܡܳܐ: ܕ݁ܰܓܳܠܘܽܬܳܐ ܘܰܥܫܽܘܩܝܳܐ ܘܰܛܠܽܘܡܝܳܐ: ܟܰܕ݂ ܐܳܡܪܝܺܢ ܠܳܟ ܕ݁ܓ݁ܰܪܬ ܘܐܰܘܠܶܕ݂ܬ: ܘܫܰܬܝܺܩ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܐܰܝܟ ܟܺܐܦܳܐ ܛܳܒܬܳܐ: ܕܒܿܳܠܥܳܐ ܡܳܐܐ ܣܰܩܽܘܪ̈ܝܳܢ ܠܳܐ ܡܡܰܠ̱ܠܳܐ: ܘܐܶܠܳܐ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܦܘܽܩ: ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܛܰܠܝܳܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܕ݂ܰܟܝܺܠ܀
them your humility for a year or a month or at least ten days, and then go out. Do you perhaps think, after you have gone out and are not humble, that you have overcome evil? At that time your battles will be multiplied, after you have left your relatives; and if you do not have humility, sin will corrupt you. But if you have proposed in your mind to bear all things, whatever may come upon you: lying, force, injury, if they say to you "you have committed adultery and begotten," and you are silent like a good stone, which is struck by a hundred splinters and does not speak, — but if not, do not go out, for you are still an infant.


[p. 774] {#po.0.p774}
ܓܰܒܪܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܡܣܰܝܒܰܪ ܕ݂ܪܰܘܪ̈ܒܳܢ ܡܶܢ ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܘܰܒܝܺܫܳܬ݂ܳܐ. ܥܕ݂ܰܡܳܐ ܕܐܶܢ ܓ݁ܳܪܝܺܢ ܠܶܗ ܘܰܡܢܰܓ݁ܕ݂ܝܺܢ ܠܶܗ ܘܙܳܩܦܝܺܢ ܠܶܗ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܰܠܫܠܝܺܚܶܐ: ܡܣܰܝܒܰܪ ܟܰܕ݂ ܫܰܬ݁ܝܺܩ: ܘܰܒܚܰܝ̈ܘܳܬܶܗ ܠܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܘܰܠܡܳܪܶܗ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܫܘܒܗܳܪܶܗ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܬܶܦܘܽܩ. ܢܶܡܚܘܽܢ ܐܰܒ݁ܳܗܰܝ̈ܟ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܝܘܽܠܦܳܢܳܐ ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܐܶܙܰܠܬ ܫܡܰܥܬ ܘܐܶܬܰܝܬ ܘܰܢܠܘܽܛܘܽܢܳܟ݂: ܣܰܝܒܰܪ ܐܶܢܘܽܢ ܘܰܣܓܘܽܕ݂ ܠܗܘܽܢ ܥܕܰܡܳܐ ܕܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܓܰܒܪܳܐ. ܘܡܶܢ ܗܳܪܟ݁ܳܐ ܒܳܩܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܢܰܦܫܳܟ: ܐܶܢ ܡܨܰܝܬ ܡܣܰܝܒܰܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܠܢܘܽܟܪܳܝܶܐ ܘܐܳܙܶܠ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܠܳܐ ܨܶܦ݂ܬܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܡܶܫܬܰܒ݂ܗܰܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܒܰܝܢܰܝܟ ܘܰܠܡܳܪܰܢ: ܘܐܳܡܰܪ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܕܰܠܡܳܐ ܐܶܢ ܡܳܚܶܝܢ ܠܝܺ ܐܰܝܟ݁ܳܐ ܕܐܳܙܶܠ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ: ܛܳܒ ܡܶܢ ܕܰܡܚܰܐܘܽܢܝ ܐܰܒܳܗܰܝ̈ ܘܰܒܢܰܝ̈ ܡܕܝܰܢ̱ܬܝ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܝܘܽܠܦܳܢܳܐ ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܡܰܟܝܺܟܘܽܬܳܐ ܡܳܚܶܝܢ ܠܝܺ: ܘܗܳܟ݂ܰܢ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܓ݁ܰܒܪܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܳܩܶܠ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܛܰܥܢܳܐ ܕܢܰܦܫܳܟ݂ ܘܟܳܚܶܬ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܪܶܥܝܳܢܳܟ݂ ܒܝܘܽܠܦܳܢܳܐ ܘܰܒܫ̈ܘܳܐܠܶܐ ܕܡܶܠܬܳܐ. ܟܡܐ ܕܡܰܟܝܺܟ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܗܳܟܰܢ ܝܳܪܶܒ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ. ܘܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܺܐܡܰܪ ܕܟܳܠܶܐ ܠܝܺ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܕܬܰܘ ܒܳܬܰܪܝ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܡܣܰܪܩܝܺܢ ܐ݇ܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܡܶܢ ܡܶܕ݁ܶܡ ܕܡܶܬܚܙܶܐ: ܠܰܘ ܡܶܟܝܳܠ ܟܳܠܶܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܠܳܟ݂. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܬ݁ܶܦܘܽܩ ܬ݁ܰܐܒ݁ܰܕ݂ ܕܳܚܶܠ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܳܢܳܐ ܚܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ: ܕ݁ܝܰܘܡܳܢ ܬܰܐܠܰܦ ܘܠܡܚܳܪ ܬܠܰܡܶܕ ܐܰܒܳܗܰܝ̈ܟ. ܘܰܠܚܰܝܘܡܳܝܐ ܐ݈ܚܪܳܢܳܐ ܬ݁ܶܗܘܶܐ ܡܰܟܝܳܟܘܽܬܳܟ݂ ܠܟܳܗ̈ܢܶܐ ܘܰܠܚܰܘܡܳܐ ܕܐܰܪܒܥܳܐ ܘܰܠܚܰܘܡܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܚܡܶܫܬܳܐ ܬ݁ܶܗܘܶܐ ܒܪܝܺܬܳܐ ܚܕ݂ܰܬܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܐܳܕ݂ܳܡ ܘܬܶܬܰܓܰܪ ܘܬܶܬܺܝܕ݂ܰܥ ܡܰܟܝܺܟܘܽܬܳܟ݂ ܠܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ. ܘܰܠܫܰܘܡܳܐ ܕܫܰܒܥܳܐ ܬܶܬܢܫܶܐ
4. For a man bears greater and worse things; until he is dragged and scourged and crucified like the Apostles, he suffers in silence and his boasting remains between him and his Lord. But [if] you have gone out [and?] your parents have struck you because of the doctrine and because of the word of God, because you heard while going and returned, and they have cursed you: sustain and adore them, until you become a man. And from then on you will test yourself: if you know how to sustain strangers and if you go without anxiety, boasting between you and the Lord, and say: "Perhaps where I am going, if they strike me more than my parents and fellow citizens struck me, they will strike me because of doctrine and humility." And you will be a man to the extent that you carry your burden and wear down your mind with doctrine and the investigation of the word. The more humble you are, the more you will progress. But do not say: "He is holding me back," (as the Lord said: follow me, emptied of visible [things]) I am not holding you back by holding you, but I fear lest you perish by going out; nevertheless, I rejoice that you are learning today and will teach your parents tomorrow, and the day after tomorrow exercise your humility toward priests, and on the fourth day toward the clergy, and on the fifth day toward the young, and on the sixth day be a new creature, like Adam, and extend and make known your humility to all men, and on the seventh day be recreated by Him who called you into the heavenly Jerusalem. The impediment is on your part, by which you are less humble and do not know the truth and become a father to others. I, indeed, out of charity give you counsel, so that you may know what is expedient for you; I do not judge you in indicating it. Be a son of wisdom and know all things and pray for me through the charity of the Lord Jesus Christ.


[p. 775] {#po.0.p775}


[p. 776] {#po.0.p776}
ܠܘܳܐ ܡܰܢ ܕܰܩܪܳܟ݂ ܒܐܘܽܪܺܝܡ ܥܶܠܺܝܬܳܐ. ܟܳܠܝܳܐ ܡܶܢܳܟ ܗ̱ܘ ܕܬܶܬܡܰܟ݁ܰܟ݂ ܘܐܶܕܰܥ ܫܪܳܪܳܐ ܘܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܰܢ̱ܬ ܐܰܒܳܐ ܠܰܐ̱ܚܪ̈ܳܢܶܐ. ܐܶܢܳܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܡܶܢ ܚܘܽܒܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܡܳܠܶܟ݂ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ ܠܳܟ ܕܬ݂ܶܕ݂ܰܥ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܐܳܙܶܠ ܠܳܟ: ܠܰܘ ܡܶܕ݂ܶܡ ܕܳܐܶܢ ܐ݈ܢܳܐ ܠܟ ܗ̱ܘܰܝ ܒܪܳܐ ܕܚܶܟܡܬܳܐ: ܘܕ݂ܰܥ ܟ݁ܽܠܥܶܡܕܶܡ ܘܨܰܠܳܐ ܥܠܰܝ: ܒܚܘܽܒܶܗ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܡܫܺܝܚܳܐ܀ ܐܝܺܬ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܡܰܠܦܳܢܶܐ ܝܰܘܡܳܢ: ܕܡܳܐ ܕܐܙܰܠܘ ܡܬܰܠܡܕ݁ܝܺܢ ܠܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܟܰܕ݂ ܠܳܐ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ:
5. For there are teachers today who, going, take to themselves as a disciple an ignorant man, saying to him: "Go,


[p. 777] {#po.0.p777}
ܐܳܡܪܝܺܢ ܠܶܗ ܬ݁ܳܐ ܦܘܽܩ. ܘܡܳܐ ܕܰܢܦܰܩ ܐܳܡܪܝܺܢ ܠܶܗ ܙܰܠ ܒܥܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ. ܘܠܳܐ ܡܰܟܪܝܺܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܘܠܳܐ ܡܳܢܰܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܝܘܽܠܦܳܢܳܐ ܫܳܒܩܝܢ ܠܶܗ ܕܢܺܐܠܰܦ. ܘܐܶܢ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܠܳܐ ܡܥܰܕܰܪ ܠܶܗ ܡܰܠܦܳܢܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܕܘܽܟ: ܥܳܒܕ݂ܝܺܢ ܠܶܗ ܒܰܛܝܳܠܳܐ: ܕܠܳܐ ܢܨܰܠܶܐ ܝܺܕ݂ܰܥ: ܘܠܳܐ ܡܺܐܠܰܦ ܫܳܒܩܝܺܢ ܠܶܗ ܕܢܺܐܠܰܦ. ܘܗܳܘܶܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܬ݁ܰܓܳܪܳܐ ܗܶܕ݂ܝܘܽܛܳܐ: ܕܠܳܐ ܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܕܢܶܬܕܰܒܰܪ: ܡܶܕܶܡ ܕܰܡܟܰܢܶܫ: ܡܰܘܒܶܕ݂ ܠܶܗ ܒܗܶܕܝܘܽܛܘܽܬܶܗ. ܘܰܟܒܰܪ ܬܺܐܡܰܪ: ܕܰܓ݂ܒܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܠܗܶܕܝܽܘܽܛܶܐ ܕܢܰܒܗܶܬ ܒܗܘܢ ܠܚܰܟܺܝܡܶܐ. ܗܳܠܶܝܢ ܗܶܕ݂ܝܘܽܛܶܐ ܕܰܓ݁ܒܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܒܐܰܪ̈ܥܳܢܳܝܬ݁ܳܐ ܗܶܕ݂ܝܘܽܛܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܘܚܰܟܺܝܡܝܺܢ ܗ̱ܘܰܘ ܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܝ̈ܳܬܳܐ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܰܟܬܝܰܒ: ܕ݁ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܠܳܐ ܝܶܕ݂ܥܶܬ ܣܳܦܪܘܽܬܳܐ: ܐܶܥܘܽܠ ܒܚܰܝܠܳܐ ܕܡܳܪܝܳܐ. ܗܳܢܰܘ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܠܰܡ ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܐܰܣܠܺܝܬ ܚܶܟܡܬܳܐ ܐܰܪܥܳܢܳܝܬܳܐ: ܐܳܩܢܶܐ ܚܶܟܡܬܳܐ ܫܡܰܝܳܢܳܝܬܳܐ. ܐܶܢܳܐ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܐ̱ܢܳܐ. ܕܝܰܠܰܦܘ ܚܰܫܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ ܘܡܰܟܺܝܟܘܽܬܶܗ: ܘܗܳܟ݂ܰܢ ܬܶܬܰܐܣܪܘܽܢ ܒܚܰܫܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܩܳܝܡܝܺܢ ܐܵܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ: ܘܟܰܕ݂ ܝܳܬܒܝܺܢ ܐܵܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ: ܬܶܬܰܐܣܪܘܽܢ ܒܡܳܪܰܢ ܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܘܠܳܐ ܬܺܐܙܠ̱ܘܽܢ ܬܶܬܰܐܣܪܘܽܢ ܒܟܘܽܪܳܟܐ ܐܰܝܟ ܒܥܺܝܪܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܝܺܕ݂ܥܝܺܢ ܐܵܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܡܺܝܕ݁ܶܡ: ܘܬܶܬܰܐܣܪܘܽܢ ܠܟܘܢ ܒܐܰܪܥܳܐ. ܐܶܠܳܐ ܐܶܬܰܐܣܰܪܘ ܟ݁ܽܠܥܶܕ݂ܳܢ ܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܒܡܳܪܰܢ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܡܕܰܒܚܝܢ ܐܵܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܕܶܒܚܶܐ ܕܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܬ݁ܳܐ: ܒ݁ܰܙܒ݂ܰܢ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܩܳܝܡܝܺܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ: ܘܒܰܙܒ݂ܰܢ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܒܳܪܟܝܺܢ ܐܵܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ: ܘܒ݁ܰܙܒ݂ܰܢ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܡܗܰܠܟܝܺܢ ܐܵܢ̱ܬܘܿܢ: ܘܒܰܙܒ݂ܰܢ ܟܰܕ݂ ܙܳܡܪܝܺܢ ܐܰܢ̱ܬܘܽܢ ܒܪܘّܚ ܩܘܽܕܫܳܐ. ܘܠܳܐ ܐ݈ܢܳܫ ܡܬܘܳܡ ܢܶܬܦܰܠܰܓ݂ ܥܰܠ ܥܺܕ݂ܬܳܐ ܘܥܰܠ ܟܳܗܢܳܝܶܗ. ܘܡܶܢ
go out!" And when he has gone out, they say: "Pray to the Lord!" when he does not know who the Lord is, nor do they allow him to learn what the doctrine is; and if the Lord does not send him a teacher from somewhere, they render him idle, because he does not know how to pray, nor do they allow him to learn by learning, and he becomes like a foolish merchant who does not know how to dispose of [his goods], wasting because of his foolishness what he has collected. And perhaps you will say: "God chose the foolish, so that through them He might confound the wise." The foolish, whom God chose, were foolish in earthly things and wise in heavenly things, as it is written: Because I have not known literature, I will enter into the power of the Lord; this is: "because I have rejected earthly knowledge, I will acquire heavenly wisdom." But I say: learn the passion of the Lord and His humility and so bind yourselves to His passion that, standing and sitting, you may adhere to the Lord in heaven. And do not, by going away, give yourselves to wandering, like cattle, utterly ignorant, lest you be bound to the earth, but at all times bind yourselves to heaven, to the Lord, offering sacrifices of knowledge, sometimes standing, sometimes kneeling, sometimes walking, sometimes singing in the Holy Spirit. And let no one ever doubt about the Church and its priests, because all knowledge of the truth proceeds from the Catholic Church. And let him love sects also and infidels, although the Catholic Church is greater in our eyes.

[p. 779] {#po.0.p779}
ܥܺܕܬܰܐ ܙܘ̱ܘ ܩܰܬܳܠܺܝܩܺܝ ܡܶܬܝܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܟ݁ܽܠܶܗ ܫܪܳܪܳܐ. ܘܐܳܦ ܠܕ݂ܶܚܠ̈ܬܳܐ ܘܰܠܟܳܦܘܽܪܶܐ ܢܰܚܺܝܒ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܪܰܒ݁ܳܐ ܒܥܰܫ̈ܢܰܝܢ ܥܺܕ݂ܬ݁ܳܐ ܩܰܬܘܽܠܺܝܩܺܝ܀ ܡܳܐ ܕܝܺܕܰܥܬܘܽܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܬܶܫܒܩܘܽܢ: ܗܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܬܨܰܠܘܽܢ ܘܬܺܐܡܪܘܽܢ: ܐܵܒܘܽܢ ܕܒܰܫܡܰܝܳܐ ܫܒܘܽܩ ܠܰܢ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܐܳܦ ܚܢܰܢ ܫܒܰܩܢ ܠܚܰܝ̈ܒܰܝܺܢ. ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܕܝܶܫܘܽܥ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܐܠܦܰܢ ܕ݁ܢܰܚܶܒ ܚܰܕ݂ ܠܚܰܕ: ܘܰܠܟ݁ܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܝܰܠܺܝܕ݂ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܕܐܳܕܳܡ. ܘܡܳܐ ܕܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܢܰܢ ܕܢܶܥܒܶܕ݂ ܗܳܟܰܢܳܐ ܘܢܶܫܒܘܽܩ ܗܳܟܰܢ: ܢܺܐܙܰܠ ܢܨܰܠܶܐ: ܕܠܳܐ ܠܚܰܝܳܒܘܽܬܳܐ ܩܳܪܶܝܢܰܢ ܠܶܗ ܠܡܳܪܰܢ. ܗܳܟܰܢ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܥܒܰܕ݂ܘ ܬܰܠܡܺܝܕ݂ܰܘ̈ܗ̱ܝ ܕܡܳܪܰܢ: ܘܟܶܢ ܐܶܙܰܠܘ ܨܰܠܺܝܘ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܠܗܘܿܢ: ܕܨܰܠܰܘ ܥܰܠ ܟܽܠܗܘܽܢ ܒܢܰܝ̈ܢܳܫܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܥܠܘܽܢ ܠܢܶܣܝܘܽܢܳܐ: ܘܐܰܝܟ ܕܰܟܬܝܺܒ: ܕ݂ܡܶܠܳܐ ܣܰܢܝܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܦܘܽܡܟܘܢ ܠܳܐ ܬܶܦܽܘܩ܆ ...ܠܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܫ ܢܶܫܡܰܥ ܡܶܢ ܦܘܳܡܰܢ ܡܶܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܣܢܝܳܐ: ܠܳܐ ܒܰܡܕܝܺܢ̱ܬ݁ܰܢ ܘܠܳܐ ܒܒܰܝܬ݁ ܐܰܒܳܗܰܝ̈ܢ. ܘܢܰܪܟܶܢ ܪܺܫܰܢ ܘܢܶܣܓܽܘܕ݂ ܠܟܽܠܢܳܫ. ܘܰܢܗܘܶܐ ܚܰܝܳܒܺܝܢܰܢ ܕܢܰܚܶܒ ܠܟ݁ܽܠܢܳܫ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܫܠܺܝܚܳܐ: ܡܶܕܶܡ ܠܳܐ ܬܚܘܽܒܘܿܢ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܚܰܕ݂ ܠܚܰܕ݂ ܕܢܶܬܬܚܰܒ. ܘܢܶܕܰܥ ܡܳܢܳܐ ܚܰܝܳܒܺܝܢܰܢ ܠܶܗ ܡܶܢܰܢ: ܠܡܰܢ ܕܐܺܝܩܳܪܳܐ ܐܝܰܩܳܪܳܐ. ܘܰܠܡܰܢ ܕܕ݂ܶܚܠܬܳܐ ܕ݁ܺܚܠܬܳܐ. ܘܰܠܡܰܢ
6. But after you know how to forgive, pray and say: Our Father, who art in heaven, forgive us, as we have forgiven our debtors, just as Jesus the Lord taught us to love one another and all the sons of Adam. And after we know how to act thus and so to forgive, going, let us pray: without guilt we will invoke the Lord. For thus did the disciples of the Lord, and then, going, they prayed, as He said to them: Pray for all men, that they may not enter into temptation, and as it is written: Let no foul word come out of your mouth; [this is]: let no one hear a foul word from our mouth, not in our city, nor in our father's house; and let us bow our head and adore all, and let it be ours to love all men, as the Apostle said: Owe nothing to anyone, except to love one another. And let us know what we owe to each: to whom honor, honor; to whom fear, fear; to whom greeting,

ܕܫܠܳܡܳܐ ܫܠܳܡܳܐ. ܘܰܠܡܰܢ ܕܣܘܰܥܪܳܢܳܐ ܣܘܽܥܪܳܢܳܐ. ܘܰܠܡܰܢ ܕܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܬ݁ܳܐ ܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܬ݁ܳܐ. ܠܡܰܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܐ݈ܝܰܩܳܪܳܐ ܚܰܝܳܒܺܝܢܰܢ ܠܶܗ: ܘܪܰܒ ܗ̱ܘܽ ܡܶܢܰܢ: ܠܳܐ ܢܶܬܶܠ ܠܶܗ ܝܘܽܠܦܳܢܳܐ ܕܢܶܙܕܰܥܰܡ ܘܢܺܐܡܰܪ: ܕܐ݇ܢܸܬ ܡܰܠܦܰܬ ܠܝܳ܆ ܘܡܰܢ ܕܕ݂ܶܚܠܬ݁ܳܐ ܚܰܝܳܒܺܝܢܰܢ ܠܶܗ ܠܳܐ ܢܶܬܶܠ ܠܶܗ ܚܘܽܒܳܐ ܦܫܺܝܛܳܝܐ ܘܰܢܨܰܥܰܪ. ܘܰܠܡܰܢ ܕܚܘܽܒ݁ܳܐ ܦܫܺܝܛܳܐ ܚܰܝܳܒܺܝܢܰܢ ܠܶܗ: ܠܳܐ ܢܚܰܘܶܐ ܠܶܗ ܟܡܺܝܪܘܳܬ݂ܳܐ ܘܰܢܥܰܩܶܡ ܦܰܪܨܘܽܦܰܘܗ̱ܝ. ܘܡܰܢ ܕܣܘܽܥܪܳܢܳܐ ܚܰܝܳܒܺܝܢܰܢ ܠܶܗ ܠܳܐ ܢܶܬܶܠ ܠܶܗ ܫܠܳܡܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܪܘܽܚܩܳܐ ܘܢܶܬܪܰܥܰܡ ܥܠܰܝܢ. ܘܰܠܡܰܢ ܕ݁ܰܫܠܳܡܳܐ ܚܰܝܳܒܺܝܢܰܢ ܠܶܗ: ܠܳܐ ܢܶܫܬ݁ܰܘܚܰܪ ܠܘܳܬܶܗ ܘܢܰܛܥܢܰܢ ܚܘܽܩܪܳܐ ܒܫܰܪ̈ܒܰܝܘܗ̱ܝ. ܘܰܠܡܰܢ ܕܝܺܕ݂ܰܥܬ݁ܳܐ ܚܰܝܳܒܺܝܢܰܢ ܠܶܗ: ܠܳܐ ܢܶܦܣܘܽܩ ܡܶܢ ܠܘܳܬܶܗ ܥܰܕ݂ ܡܶܫܬܰܪܰܪ: ܕܠܳܐ ܢܶܬܟ݂ܫܶܠ ܠܶܗ ܘܢܺܐܒܰܕ܀
greeting; to whom love, to whom visitation, visitation; to whom knowledge, knowledge. But to whom we owe honor and he is greater than we, let us not wish to give him doctrine, lest, becoming inflamed, he say: "You teach me?" And to whom we owe fear, let us not wish to show him simple charity, lest he reproach us. And to whom we owe simple charity, let us not wish to show him gloominess and sadden him. And to whom we owe visitation, let us not greet him from afar, lest he complain about us. And to whom we owe greeting, let us not linger with him, lest he burden us with his histories and narrations. And to whom we owe knowledge, let us not depart from him until he is persuaded, lest, scandalized, he perish.

ܢܶܗܘܶܐ ܬܡܝܼܡܶܐ ܒܗܳܢܳܐ ܥܳܠܡܳܐ ܠܒܺܝ̈ܫܳܬ݁ܳܐ ܘܚܰܟܺܝ̈ܡܶܐ ܠܟ݁ܽܠܗܶܝܢ ܛܰܒ̈ܳܬܳܐ ܠܡܶܥܒܰܕ݂. ܘܰܢܫܰܝܢ ܠܟܽܠܢܳܫ ܘܢܺܐܬ݂ܰܪ ܡܶܢ ܟܽܠܢܳܫ: ܘܢܰܘܐܰܪ ܠܟ݁ܽܠܢܳܫ ܘܢܶܝܕ݂ܰܥ ܟܽܠ ܩܳܠܳܐ ܕܰܓܡܝܼܪܘܽܬܳܐ. ܡܶܢ ܕܟܰܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ: ܘܰܕܟܺܐܢܘܽܬܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܕܣܳܛܳܢܳܐ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܗܳܕ݂ܶܐ ܘܽܘ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܡܳܪܰܢ: ܕܰܗܘܰܝܬܘܽܢ ܥܪܝܽܡܝ̈ܢ: ܕܢܳܕ݂ܰܥ ܝܘܽܠܦܳܢܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܝܘܽܠܦܳܢܳܐ ܘܡܶܠܬܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܡܶܠܬܳܐ: ܠܰܘ ܕ݁ܢܶܛܪܘܰܕ݂ ܒܺܝ̈ܫܶܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܒܚܳܫ̈ܶܐ ܡܶܢ ܒܶܝܬ ܛܳܒ̈ܶܐ. ܝܘܽܠܦܳܢܳܐ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܒܺܝܫܳܝܐ ܢܳܟ݁ܶܐ ܠܰܢ: ܠܳܐ ܒܢܰ̈ܝ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܒܺܝ̈ܫܶܐ. ܘܐܶܢ ܩܳܛܠܝܢ ܠܰܢ ܡܶܩܛܰܠ: ܝܘܽܬܪܳܢܳܐ ܗ̱ܘ ܠܰܢ܀ ܫܠܶܡ ܡܰܐܡܪܳܐ ܕܥܶܣܪ̈ܝܺܢ ܘܫܰܒܥܳܐ ܕܥܰܠ
7. Let us be simple in this world toward evil things and prudent toward doing all good things. And let us pacify all and from all let us profit and all let us make gain and let us distinguish all the voices of perfection from the [voice] of justice and the voice of justice from the voice of Satan; for this reason the Lord said: Be prudent, so that we might distinguish doctrine from doctrine and word from word; not so that we might expel the bad from the midst of the good. For bad doctrine is harmful to us, not bad men; and if they kill us, it will be a gain for us.

ܡܺܐܡܪܳܐ ܕܥܶܣܪܝܺܢ ܘܰܬܡܳܢܝܳܐ ܕܥܰܠ ܢܰܦܫܳܐ ܕܒܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܕܠܳܐ ܗܘܳܐ ܕܡܳܐ ܢܺܐܡܰܪ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܥܰܠ ܫܰܪܒ݁ܳܐ ܕܪܳܪܡܚܺܝܢ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܕܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܒܪܝܺܬܳܐ ܐܝܺܬ ܒܶܗ ܒܒܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܘܢܰܦܫܳܐ

### TWENTY-EIGHTH DISCOURSE, THAT THE HUMAN SOUL IS NOT BLOOD
ܒܪܝܺܬ݁ܳܐ. ܘܥܳܒܕܝܺܢ ܠܳܗ ܠܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܕܒܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܕܡܳܐ ܐܰܝܟ݁ ܕܚܰܝ̈ܘܳܬ݂ܳܐ: ܘܒ݁ܶܗ ܠܰܡ ܒ݁ܦܰܓ݁ܪܳܐ ܡܺܝܬ݁ܳܐ ܢܰܦܫܳܐ ܘܢܳܦܩܳܐ ܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܚܰܝܳܐ. ܡܚܰܘܶܝܢܰܢ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܠܳܐ ܡܳܝܬ݁ܳܐ ܢܰܦܫܳܐ ܥܰܡ ܦܰܓ݁ܪܳܐ ܐܶܠܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ ܚܰܝܳܐ ܢܳܦܩܳܐ ܡܶܢܶܗ. ܕܶܬܝܺܕ݂ܰܥ ܕܗܳܝ ܢܰܦܫܳܐ ܡܶܬܩܰܪܝܳܐ ܒܰܙܒܰܢ ܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܘܒܰܙܒܰܢ ܢܰܦܫܳܐ. ܘܦ݁ܰܓܪܳܐ ܘܢܰܦܫܳܐ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܒܰܪ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܟܰܝܳܢ ܒܪܝܺܬ݁ܶܗ ܒܰܠܚܘܽܕ݂: ܘܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܕܩܘܽܕ݂ܫܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܕܐܳܬܝܳܐ ܥܳܡܪܳܐ ܒܶܗ: ܐܶܡܰܬܝ ܕܢܳܛܰܪ ܦܘܽܩܕܿܳܢܶܐ ܕܒܳܪܘܺܝܶܗ: ܐܰܝܟ݁ܰܢ ܕܡܶܢ ܝܰܘܡܳܐ ܩܰܕ݂ܡܳܝܳܐ: ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܒܪܳܐ ܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ ܦܰܓܪܶܗ ܘܢܰܦܫܶܗ ܕܐܳܕܳܡ. ܗܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܢܦܰܚ ܒܶܗ ܡܶܢ ܪܘܽܚܶܗ ܕܩܘܽܕ݂ܫܳܐ ܗܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܢܦܰܚ ܒܺܝܗ ܡܶܢ ܪܘܺܚܶܗ ܕܩܘܽܕ݂ܫܳܐ
1. We will institute a discourse concerning the proposition about which some move a discussion, that the created spirit and the created soul are in man, and making the human soul blood like that of animals, they say that the soul dies in the body and the living spirit goes out. But we will demonstrate that the soul does not die with the body, but goes out alive from it, so that it may be known that the soul is sometimes called spirit, sometimes soul, and that man by the nature of his creation is body and soul only, and the Holy Spirit of God coming to dwell in him, when he observes the commands of his creator, as from the first day, when God created the body


[p. 786] {#po.0.p786}


[p. 787] {#po.0.p787}
ܘܟܶܢ ܗܘܳܐ ܐܪܳܡ ܢܦܰܫ ܚܰܝܳܝܐ. ܐܶܡܪ ܓ݁ܶܝܪ ܐܶܫܰܥܝܳܐ: ܕ݁ܰܒ݂ܪܳܐ ܪܘܽܚܶܝܗ ܕܒܰܪܢܳܫܳܐ ܒܓܰܘܶܗ. ܘܠܳܐ ܐܶܡܰܪ ܕܰܢܦ݁ܰܚ: ܕܢܰܘܕ݁ܰܥ ܕܡܰܡܦܘܽܚܬܳܐ ܡܶܢ ܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ ܕܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܘܠܰܘ ܒܪܝܺܬ݁ܳܐ ܗ̱ܝ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܳܦ ܝܳܕ݂ܥܝܺܢܰܢ ܝܰܘܡܳܢܳܐ: ܕܐܶܡܰܬܝ ܕܪܘܽܚܶܝܗ ܕܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܠܰܝܬ ܒܟܰܝܠܳܐ ܐ̱ܢܳܫܳܐ ܡܰܚܣܝܠܰܝ ܗ̱ܘ: ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܶܡܰܪ ܦ݁ܰܘܠܳܘܣ. ܐܶܡܰܬܝ ܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܕܥܳܡܪܳܐ ܒܶܗ ܗܳܝ ܡܰܡܦܘܽܚܬܳܐ: ܗܳܝܕ݁ܶܝܢ ܗܳܘܶܐ ܢܦܰܫ ܚܰܝܳܝܐ: ܐܰܝܟ݂ ܕܰܒܗܰܘ ܝܰܘܡܳܐ ܕ݁ܰܢܦ݁ܰܚ ܒܶܗ ܡܳܪܝܳܐ ܟ݁ܰܕ݂ ܒܪܺܝܗ̱ܝ: ܐܰܝܟܰܢ ܕܰܢܦ݁ܰܚ ܡܳܪܰܢ ܪܘܽܚܶܗ ܒܐܰܦ̈ܶܝܐ ܕܬܰܠܡܝܺܕ݁ܰܘܗ̱ܝ: ܕܢܶܗܘܘܽܢ ܐܰܝܟ ܕܐܺܝܬܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܗ̱ܘܳܐ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܥܰܕ݂ܠܳܐ ܢܶܚܛܶܐ. ܡܶܛܽܠ ܕܟܽܠ ܐܶܡܰܬܝ ܕܚܳܛܶܐ ܐܳܕܳܡ ܘܝܰܠܕ݂ܰܘܗ̱ܝ ܡܫܰܢܝܳܐ ܠܳܗ ܡܶܢܗܘܽܢ ܗܳܝ ܡܰܡܦܘܽܚܬܳܐ ܕܐܝܺܬܶܝܗ ܪܘܽܚܳܐ ܕܐܰܠܳܗܳܐ: ܘܐܶܡܰܬܝ ܕܬܳܝܒܺܝܢ
and the soul of Adam. Then He breathed into him the Holy Spirit and then Adam became a living soul. For Isaiah says: He created the spirit of man in his midst. He did not say: "breathed" so as to signify that the breath is from the Spirit of the Lord, nor that it is a creature; just as also today we know that man, when the Spirit of the Lord is not in him, is reprobate, as Paul says. But when the breath dwells in him, then he becomes a "living soul," just as on that day when the Lord breathed into him, when He had created him, just as the Lord breathed His Spirit into the face of His disciples, so that they might be such as Adam was, before he sinned; for as often as Adam and his sons sin, the breath, which is the Spirit of God, recedes from them and, when they do penance, coming, it dwells in anyone as in that one, according to the measure of the charisms of Christ, according to the diverse charisms.


[p. 788] {#po.0.p788}
